[biomaRt](/packages/biomaRt)
-------

                       Changes in version 2.70.0                        

NEW FEATURES

- More functions have gained a `useCache` argument, which defaults to
  `TRUE`,
  to reduce the load on the upstream server.

BREAKING CHANGES

- The deprecated Ensembl mirrors ("asia" and "useast") have been
  removed.

- This package now defaults to https://jun2026.archive.ensembl.org
  where it
  was previously defaulting to https://www.ensembl.org/. The June 2026
  (Ensembl
  116) release is the last release to include the Biomart utility.

- Modification of SSL settings via `setEnsemblSSL()` is now deprecated
  and
  will be removed in the next biomaRt release. Please get in touch if
  your
  workflow depends on this feature.

MINOR IMPROVEMENTS

- Unnecessary call to `listEnsemblArchives()` in `getBM(useCache =
  FALSE)`
  has been removed.

- A complete static dataset of previous Ensembl releases is now shipped
  with
  this package. This solves an issue where the upstream Ensembl website
  stopped
  listing all releases on their page. The dataset is directly
  accessible to
  users via `data("ensembl_releases")`. It is also possible to get the
  list of
  Ensembl archives without an internet connection via
  `listEnsemblArchives(fetch = FALSE)`.

INTERNAL CHANGES

- Vignettes now run again on continuous integration to ensure they stay
  up
  to date.

- Unused internal functions have been removed.

- Code duplication across functions have been reduced.

[biotmle](/packages/biotmle)
-------

                       Changes in version 1.37.1                        

- Removal of the `superheat` dependency, which has been archived on
  CRAN. The
  heatmap drawn by `heatmap_ic()` is now built directly with `ggplot2`.

- `heatmap_ic()` gains a `row_dendrogram` argument, which restores the
  row
  dendrogram previously available through `superheat`. Biomarkers are
  ordered
  by hierarchical clustering whether or not the dendrogram is drawn, so
  this
  argument affects only the display. It defaults to `FALSE`, matching
  the
  default of the `superheat` argument it replaces. Drawing the
  dendrogram
  introduces dependencies on `ggdendro` and `patchwork`.

- `heatmap_ic()` now returns a `ggplot` object, which can be stored and
  further
  modified in place, rather than drawing to the active graphics device
  as a
  side effect.

- `heatmap_ic()` gains a `scale` argument controlling whether each
  biomarker's
  contributions are standardized across observations before plotting;
  this
  replaces the argument of the same name previously forwarded to
  `superheat`.

- Arguments passed to `heatmap_ic()` via `...` are now forwarded to
  `ggplot2::geom_tile()` rather than to `superheat::superheat()`. Calls
  that
  relied on `superheat`-specific arguments (e.g., `left.label`,
  `clustering.method`, `row.dendrogram`) must be updated.

[BreastSubtypeR](/packages/BreastSubtypeR)
--------------

                       Changes in version 1.5.14                        

Performance

- sspPredict() avoids repeated ranking by computing Spearman
correlations in one matrix call per eligible panel. Panels with
non-finite values, constant columns or unsupported classes retain
the existing scalar calculation and its warning and error behavior.

                       Changes in version 1.5.13                        

API compatibility

- BS_ssBC() uses PatientID as a unique sample lookup key, not a
repeated biological-patient identifier. For ER, ER.v2, TN and TN.v2,
exactly one original column and one exact converted PatientID column
must provide the same complete, nonempty, unique labels as the assay
names in order. This intentionally tightens compatibility even for
excluded/empty rows and contradictions whose numerical results
agree. The converted-key check prevents metadata flattening or
partial matching from changing the key actually used. Supported
storage must satisfy both boundaries; the existing empty four-class
restrictions still apply. Guard refusals use
bsr_patientid_mismatch_error. Manual BS_Multi() propagates that
error when dispatch reaches ssBC; earlier preconditions such as a
missing PatientID column can still give an unclassed error. AUTO
routing and its early order check are unchanged, but selected
ssBC/ssBC.v2 wrappers can newly refuse duplicate original columns or
ambiguous converted keys that pass that precheck. Existing TSIZE
metadata preparation errors in .nc_pheno() occur first; this is not
a priority promise for missing clinical columns, invalid s, NODE
errors or missing receptors. No identifiers are realigned or
overwritten. Reconcile source records; internally consistent keys
cannot detect an upstream sample mix-up. Other standalone NC
wrappers are unchanged.

- Four-class (Subtype = TRUE) ssBC with s = "ER", "ER.v2" or "TN" no
longer stops with "undefined columns selected" when no sample
belongs to any selected receptor subgroup and the input is otherwise
well formed. Standalone BS_ssBC(), manual BS_Multi() and the AUTO
mixed-cohort route with no recognized ER/HER2 pair return the
existing five-class empty result plus missing BS.Subtype,
Call.Subtype and predictions.FourSubtype. This needs at least one
represented PAM50 gene, unique plain-vector receptor columns and a
single character or factor PatientID column whose labels are
identical to the assay column names in assay order. Other inputs
remain errors, with identity diagnostics as described above.
Receptor labels are matched literally and are not normalized;
alias-coded AUTO inputs still fail, now with the same error as the
corresponding five-class call. TN.v2, all five-class results and the
other methods' results, summaries and entropy are unchanged.

- For evaluated patients with invalid binary TSIZE, clinical NC
methods mask ROR-C, original ROR-PC and experimental 18-gene ROR-PC
scores and groups. The mask applies even at NODE >= 4. Subtype
calls, genomic ROR and other patients' valid results are preserved.
Previously, finite codes such as 2 or 25 could produce scores and
groups.

- Invalid codes raise one bsr_invalid_tsize_warning per public call.
Its patient_ids field contains the affected evaluated IDs. This
replaces generic coercion warnings such as "NAs introduced by
coercion" and also flags codes that used to pass silently. With
options(warn = 2), an unhandled warning stops the call.

- Iterative cIHC ignores missing iteration votes. Patients with no
usable votes retain averaged calibrated expression and have missing
calls, centroid similarities and numerical ROR scores. Valid binary
TSIZE and NODE >= 4 still yield the experimental high-risk group.
Missing or invalid TSIZE withholds that group. ssBC singleton
subgroups retain their no-call behavior.

- Clinical scoring checks TSIZE missing-value declarations before row
selection, including on ordinary factors and vectors and on layered
Hmisc/haven labels. Haven validates SPSS codes and ranges, including
declarations wrapped in labels or AsIs. Conflicting or residual
declarations stop clinical scoring. Resolve their missing values to
NA before converting to ordinary binary codes. Clinical calls now
accept the labelled output of haven::zap_missing() directly. An
unknown extra class on a haven column or an unlisted attribute,
including custom provenance, stops the whole clinical call. Opaque
numeric classes outside the haven family retain per-patient masking
and a warning. Genomic-only and SSP-only calls are unaffected.

- Clinical scoring respects SPSS user-missing codes and ranges,
including declared 0 and 1, and requires haven for SPSS-labelled
TSIZE. Genuine and declared missing values are excluded from the
invalid-code warning.

- TSIZE accepts binary codes in S4Vectors Rle and base AsIs wrappers
and stored numeric/integer codes with Hmisc/expss-style label
metadata. Unverified labelled missing-value declarations require
explicit conversion. Unsupported numeric classes mask the same six
fields and warn even when the storage contains 0/1. Other S4 classes
and unsupported Rle storage raise an input error. Metadata matching
requires one clinical record per predicted ID. BS_ssBC additionally
checks every input PatientID, including excluded rows, as described
above.

- Shiny recognizes a whole TRUE/FALSE or T/F column as logical in CSV
and TSV uploads, including quoted fields. In mixed text, only exact
numeric binary labels are usable. Blank, NA and NaN upload markers
retain the cohort-wide clinical downgrade. Numeric integer64 codes
use their actual integer values, correcting the earlier
interpretation of their storage bits.

- Standalone and multi-method ssBC/ssBC.v2 now report a no-call for a
one-tumor receptor subgroup. The patient remains in the output with
missing calibrated expression, subtype and risk metrics, including
the experimental NODE-dependent group even with four or more
positive nodes. Other evaluated NC cases retain the existing NODE
rule. The warning now identifies the stratum and patient and says
"no subtype or risk estimate" in place of the earlier low-confidence
fallback label.

- Vis_pie() displays "No assigned subtype calls" for a nonempty table
of missing calls. It requires a nonempty data frame with a Subtype
column.

- Align internal four-class ssBC/ssBC.v2 predictions to input sample
order and retain matrix dimensions for singleton internal outputs
(#234). Per-sample calls, numerical results, calibration and
existing missingness are unchanged. This complements the AUTO
coverage restoration in #233.

- In BS_Multi(methods = "AUTO"), restore every existing
sample-indexed
ssBC/ssBC.v2 component to input assay IDs/order after calculation
(#233). score.ROR, predictions, correlation matrices and calibrated
testData now have full input coverage, as BS.all already did. Added
payloads are typed NA; no score, risk group or calibrated expression
is invented. Existing values/missingness, model metadata, absent
fields and method eligibility are preserved. This is an API
dimension change, not a classifier change.

- Plotting helpers report and omit entirely unavailable expression
columns or correlation rows from plot copies, retaining missing
calls with available measurements. External PCA/clustering consumers
must similarly filter unavailable calibrated columns and align
annotations by ID. No imputation or new partial-missingness policy
is introduced. Manual/standalone ssBC behavior remains unchanged;
standalone ordering/singleton issue #234 remains separate.

Documentation and regression coverage

- Document PCA-PAM50's inherited locale-sensitive character-key
ordering before both cohort-calibration sampling stages (#232).
Preserve the original PCAPAM50 1.0.4 algorithm and
reference-compatible behavior within each locale; no sorting,
sampling, calibration or scoring calculation changes. Identical
seeds alone do not guarantee identical subtype or numerical ROR
outputs across locales. Document effective LC_COLLATE, exact IDs,
R/RNG/seed and package/source/dependency provenance; no locale
forcing or ID-case normalization is introduced.

- Add offline original-reference fixtures and regression coverage for
both sampling stages, selected identities, medians and calls, sample
permutations, character/factor IDs, clinical alignment and caller
RNG/locale preservation. Alternate-locale comparisons skip only when
the locale is unavailable; expectations verify effective collation
and allow justified numerical roundoff without requiring universal
cross-locale equality.

- Document the already available BS_sspbc(..., ssp.name = "ssp.ror")
pathway (#131), its native categorical ROR-bin labels and model
posterior probabilities. Correct the documented matrix/list return
types and sample alignment, and add a research-use vignette example
with CSV export using Mapping(include_ssp_ror = TRUE)$se_SSP_ROR.
Distinguish categorical bins from continuous/Parker-derived scores,
recurrence probabilities and clinical Prosigna outputs; explain the
OSLO protocol-adjusted training-scale limitation.

- Add regression coverage for packaged SSP-ROR model availability,
single and multiple samples, sample identity/order, native-output
parity for both expanded public datasets (296 genes, 361 evaluable
rules per sample), invalid model names and preservation of both
SSPBC subtype models. Prediction code, fitted models and native
missing-rule handling are unchanged.

New features

- Add opt-in Mapping(include_ssp_ror = TRUE) preparation of a
separate
se_SSP_ROR input (#131). Required Entrez IDs come from the bundled
ssp.ror gene-pair rules (currently 296 genes and 361 rules). Default
Mapping outputs and the existing NC/SSP gene sets remain unchanged;
#131 does not alter packaged data.
- SSP-ROR uses the existing duplicate resolution and SSP expression
scales: linear FPKM for raw counts, or 2^x for nonraw log2 input
(FPKM+1 for log2(FPKM+1)). Optional KNN includes represented SSP-ROR
genes as protected targets, using the same original donors and
estimator. Absent genes are never synthesized; unsupported requested
genes can fail an opt-in call.
- Existing subtype results, normalization and RNG behavior are
preserved. BS_sspbc() already executes ssp.ror with its native
output; model-output APIs, BS_Multi(), Ensemble voting and the
four-model InputCoverage() report are unchanged.

Example data and reproducibility

- Expand OSLO2EMIT0obj to 569 genes x 102 samples on the existing
log2(protocol-adjusted FPKM + 1) scale, preserving all original 356
rows, values, annotations and sample metadata (#199). Append 213
verified genes; no unadjusted expression matrix is introduced.

- Expand TCGABRCAobj to 5,350 genes x 100 samples, preserving all
original 5,000 rows/counts and metadata and appending 350 verified
model genes. Retain recount3 G026 base-pair coverage sums and GTF
gene-sum lengths; no count transformation or variance reranking is
performed.

- Retain public object names and the se_obj, data_input and res
structure. Regenerate Mapping/AUTO results under pinned source
cb7a7c70, with recorded seeds and versions. The expansion leaves
OSLO mapped inputs and complete method results unchanged under the
same code; TCGA normalization changes and 64 method calls change
across 40 samples. Comparisons separately retain historical stored
results and recomputation from historical inputs; earlier
corrections such as #198 are not attributed to dataset expansion.
Original save-event build/seed provenance is incomplete.

- Keep historical regression fixtures self-contained, including
incomplete TCGA proliferation coverage and frozen
AUTO/entropy/reference results. Synchronize the six Shiny input
tables, dataset documentation and examples, and add relocatable
generation scripts and versioned manifests.

- Keep default Mapping, model files, algorithms and public APIs
unchanged. Both examples map to 50 NC and 339 SSP genes; complete
source-gene coverage does not establish native SSP-ROR preparation
or training-input compatibility. SSPBC training used unadjusted
StringTie FPKM; equivalence with adjusted OSLO expression is
unestablished. The separately merged #131 opt-in prepares SSP-ROR
input; normalization research remains #208.

- The scoped author and public-source/field-level redistribution
review was completed, and PR #228 merged the #199 integration.
Source attribution and reuse conditions continue to apply. The
package was at version 1.5.12 when the examples were integrated.

- Validate #199 against merged #131 at f878f58c: default mapped
inputs
and complete results retain the approved Stage 3A values. Optional
SSP-ROR preparation covers 296 genes and 361 rules in each expanded
example without changing legacy components; it is not added to
stored data_input.

- Compact historical test fixtures by sharing only independently
hash-verified assay prefixes with the public objects. Historical
metadata, mapped inputs and results remain independently frozen;
reconstructed complete objects are identical to the originals.
Public data bytes and scientific expectations are unchanged.

Bug fixes

- Shiny expression uploads preserve probe and sample labels and parse
sample measurements as numeric values. Malformed measurements are
reported with their input line, probe and sample before mapping
(#246).

- In mixed cohorts with no recognized ER/HER2 pair, five-class
BS_Multi(methods = "AUTO", Subtype = FALSE) retains the empty
ssBC.v2 result. Patients remain in input order with missing ssBC.v2
calls, and the other selected methods still contribute to the
summary (#247).

- Mapping() uses the labels of factor-valued probe annotations to
select assay rows. This corrects mapping when the factor's integer
codes point to different rows (#250).

- Resolve the original research ROR-S, ROR-P, ROR-C and ROR-PC
exact-boundary defect (#172) with the author-approved (med, med)
package convention: low below the lower cutoff, medium at or between
both cutoffs, and high above the upper cutoff. The unscaled pairs
remain -0.15/0.10, -0.25/0.10, -0.10/0.20 and -0.20/0.20,
respectively. No rounding, tolerance or classification from
displayed/reverse-scaled scores is used. Only the eight equality
assignments change from numeric text to med; numerical scores,
coefficients, normalization, subtype predictions, nonboundary
groups, missing/nonfinite handling, output schemas and the separate
NODE-dependent ROR-PC output are preserved. Add exact IEEE-754
boundary, adjacent-value, clinical/no-clinical and preservation
regressions.

- Document #172 as an author-approved convention supported by Nielsen
et al. (2010, doi:10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-10-1282) and Martin et al.
(2016, doi:10.1007/s10549-016-3725-z), not historically proven
equality semantics of the original distributed code. Published
scaled cutpoints do not replace the package's raw constants. These
are research ROR results, not clinical Prosigna results. This
supersedes the historical #172 deferrals recorded in earlier release
entries below.

- Resolve duplicate probes with method = "stdev" or "iqr" using the
first maximum among statistics that are not NA/NaN (#218). The
existing sample SD and type-7 IQR calculations, expression-row tie
order and infinite-statistic ordering are retained; singleton probes
pass through unchanged. Groups with defined statistics retain
identical numerical results. Mixed defined/undefined groups now
select a defined maximum instead of an undefined probe.

- Duplicate groups with no defined statistic now raise
BreastSubtypeR_duplicate_undefined, identifying the Entrez ID,
method and probe count. This intentionally rejects zero-sample
duplicate groups for both methods and one-sample duplicate groups
for stdev; defined zero IQRs still select the first tied probe. No
fallback method is substituted.

- Optional KNN propagates these errors for protected required genes
and excludes recognized unsupported background groups with
diagnostics. Existing max error handling and propagation of
unrelated errors are preserved. The default max method, raw-count
processing, KNN estimator, RNG behavior and output schemas are
unchanged.

                       Changes in version 1.5.12                        

Interpretation and compatibility

- Identify the existing additional 18-gene research score and its
group as Experimental 18-gene ROR-PC and Experimental 18-gene ROR-PC
group (#221). Their prognostic performance and risk-category
thresholds have not been independently validated; this calculation
differs from the published Lien implementation and is not a clinical
Prosigna result. The original 11-gene Parker ROR-PC remains a
distinct output.
- Retain the exact ROR-PC (Subtype + Clinic + Prolif.Subtype) and
ROR-PC Group (Subtype + Clinic + Prolif.Subtype) data columns, types
and values. Correlations, proliferation processing, coefficients,
thresholds, missing-value handling and the independent NODE >= 4
rule are unchanged.
- Signal the classed bsr_experimental_ror_pc_warning once per
relevant
top-level public NC call, and once for BS_Multi() when returned
component results contain the experimental columns. Package loading,
Mapping(), clinical-off and AIMS/SSPBC-only calls do not emit this
notice. Expert handlers can target this class without suppressing
other warnings; options(warn = 2) intentionally treats it as an
error.
- Show the notice and display labels for relevant selected Shiny Full
metrics and record them in its existing TSV provenance comments.
Preserve the comment-line count and tabular schema; Calls-only and
AUTO exports are unchanged. Labeling and reproducibility do not
establish prognostic or clinical validation.

Bug fixes

- Correct original Parker-derived ROR-P and ROR-PC proliferation
scoring (#198). After existing PAM50 selection and method-specific
calibration, RORgroup() standardizes a separate copy of the
represented PAM50 expression within each sample, then averages the
original 11-gene panel. This chosen PAM50-only convention matches
the complete 50-gene Perou Lab executable example; it is not
equivalent to running the distributed script on arbitrary expanded
gene sets. For cIHC.itr, only the final averaged matrix used for ROR
scoring is standardized. Classifier predictions, correlations,
calibration, sampling, consensus, Confidence, RNG, sample axes and
outList are unchanged. ROR-S, ROR-C and the distinct
unstandardized 18-gene research ROR-PC are unchanged, including its
NODE-dependent groups. Existing original coefficients, cutoffs,
transformations and deferred exact-boundary behavior (#172) remain.
Undefined sample standardization gives missing original
proliferation-dependent scores/groups; matrix dimensions and
finite-or-NA handling (#206) are retained without imposing a new
panel coverage threshold.

- Compatibility: original ROR-P/ROR-PC scores and risk groups can
change substantially, including for complete inputs. Historical
saved scores are not automatically equivalent to newly computed
scores. Record implementation, gene coverage, calibration and input
provenance when comparing results. Bundled datasets, historical
outputs and manuscript/Ensemble analyses have not been recalculated.
These remain research scores, without commercial Prosigna
equivalence or clinical validation; method-specific extensions and
incomplete panels require separate interpretation.

- RORgroup() keeps both proliferation panel subsets as matrices and
no
longer fails when exactly one 11-gene or 18-gene panel gene is
represented (#206). Represented genes are still averaged with
mean(..., na.rm = TRUE) without any gene-count threshold; absent
genes are never synthesized. A sample with no observed panel value,
or a nonfinite panel estimate, now receives a missing proliferation
score instead of NaN or Inf, so ROR-P, original ROR-PC and the
additional ROR-PC score and groups are missing for that sample
rather than the literal text "NaN" or an apparently valid high/low
category. Every exported numerical ROR score is now finite or NA: a
NaN or infinite result, including overflow in the final 100 * (score + 0.35) / 0.85 scaling or an infinite tumor-size covariate, is
reported as NA with a missing group for ROR-S, ROR-P, ROR-C,
original ROR-PC and the additional subtype-specific ROR-PC score.
This missing-value correction alone preserved finite complete-input
scores, subtype calls, calibration, correlations, coefficients,
cutoffs, the exact-equality limitation (#172), the correlation
choice (#156) and the independent NODE >= 4 high-risk rule.
Incomplete panels are documented as a compatibility limitation, not
a validated score.

                       Changes in version 1.5.11                        

Mapping

- Mapping() now defaults to impute = FALSE; primary examples and
Shiny
explicitly opt out. Duplicate resolution precedes optional
imputation and complete required outputs bypass donor preparation.

- Optional nonraw imputation uses the fixed-k=10 pure-R estimator
over
the full eligible gene-level donor input, targeting only original
holes in represented genes selected for existing NC/SSP outputs.
Exact ties retain donor row order; estimates use one to ten
available original contributors per coordinate among those ten
selected profiles. Unsupported/partial targets and nonfinite newly
projected estimates error with internal diagnostics. Absent rows are
not created and observed/nontarget values, RNG state, output
structure and expression scales are preserved.

- Optional KNN no longer uses legacy row/column missingness cutoffs.
Unusable background donors are excluded with diagnostics, required
genes remain protected, and diagnostic capacity is checked before
estimation.

- Reject missing raw counts with either setting and never impute
raw-derived expression. Full-count normalization and library-size
handling are unchanged. Remove unused impute imports/dependency
after replacing the legacy backend.

- Infinity rejection applies when optional KNN runs, not to disabled
or complete output bypasses. This revision differs from the original
published pipeline; incomplete-input estimates and downstream
predictions may change even with explicit impute = TRUE.

Bug fixes

- AIMS and the SSPBC subtype models now return missing calls and
probabilities for samples with zero evaluable model rules (#212, PR
#215). Observed FALSE comparisons still count as evidence; supported
samples and model definitions are unchanged.

                       Changes in version 1.5.10                        

Bug fixes

- Preserve all Shiny reference-median labels under C and UTF-8
locales
(#210, PR #211). Construct the four non-ASCII option names at
runtime; all option values, ordering and defaults remain unchanged.
Regression tests compare the rendered UI and HTTP option labels
across locales.

- Load Shiny server and UI regression-test sources explicitly as
UTF-8
(PRs #209 and #211). This fixes locale-dependent test-source parsing
without weakening the citation assertions or changing prediction
logic.

- BS_Multi() restores AUTO ssBC and ssBC.v2 subcohort results by
character PatientID labels after checking complete, unique
identities (#202). Factor levels no longer cause eligible calls to
be lost during restoration. Intended missing calls, valid
character-ID results, AUTO eligibility, prediction algorithms and
ROR formulas are unchanged.

- BS_cIHC.itr() now converts PatientID values to character before
selecting expression columns in each iteration (#201). Factor
labels, including unused levels, select the intended ER-balanced
centering samples and values. Missing, empty, duplicated and
unmatched identifiers produce informative errors. Valid character-ID
results, both subsampling policies, iteration counts, RNG behavior
and numerical ROR formulas are unchanged.

- BS_cIHC() now converts PatientID values to character before
name-based indexing (#200). Factor labels, including those with
unused levels, select the intended ER-balanced centering samples and
expression values. Missing, empty, duplicated and unmatched
identifiers produce informative errors. Valid character-ID results,
balancing rules, RNG behavior and numerical ROR formulas are
unchanged.

- BS_PCAPAM50() now converts PatientID values to character before
name-based indexing (#197). Factor labels, including those with
unused levels, select the intended expression samples and centering
values. Missing, empty, duplicated and unmatched identifiers produce
informative errors. Valid character-ID results, sampling order,
output order, RNG behavior and numerical ROR formulas are unchanged.

- BS_PCAPAM50() now orders complete intermediate rows by character
PatientID before second-stage sampling, matching the PCAPAM50 1.0.4
first-step merge under the caller's collation (#195). Selected sets,
centering medians, calls and derived scores may change. First-step
calculations and final input-order restoration are preserved. This
does not resolve the separate ROR expression-standardization
investigation.

- BS_PCAPAM50() now restores all sample-indexed outputs to input
order, including score.ROR and the prediction, distance and
expression components of outList. Internal calibration and sampling,
and per-sample values for the same input, seed and environment, are
unchanged.

- Report an informative error from Mapping(method = "max") when every
probe of a multi-probe Entrez ID has an undefined row total (NA, NaN
or Inf - Inf), naming the Entrez ID and the number of candidate
probes, instead of failing with an unrelated dimnames error. This
changes only the diagnostic: no probe is selected, imputed, averaged
or dropped for such a group, and selection and results for every
group with a defined total are unchanged. Follows the singleton
preservation of #178; the duplicate resolution review of #177
remains open.

Interpretation and documentation

- Declare S4Vectors and htmltools in Suggests for their direct use in
tests and the optional Shiny application.

- The factor-identifier corrections (#197, #200, #201 and #202) can
change affected sample selections, predictions, derived scores or
restored calls. The PCA-PAM50 intermediate-order correction (#195,
PR #196) can change results even with valid character identifiers.
Unchanged ROR formulas do not imply unchanged scores when their
inputs change. Output-axis restoration (PR #193) preserves
per-sample values but can affect downstream positional joins. These
fixes do not resolve the separate ROR scientific questions or
establish that manuscript results are unaffected.

- Clarify current version and installation-channel wording in the
README and vignette. Earlier release notes are retained.

                        Changes in version 1.5.9                        

Bug fixes

- RORgroup() now requires finite nonnegative integer-valued NODE
counts for ROR-PC Group (Subtype + Clinic + Prolif.Subtype) (#187).
Negative, fractional or infinite numeric values previously left the
unscaled score as numeric text in the group column or were silently
classified; they now give one warning per call and a missing group.
The column is consistently character, including all-missing batches.
NA/NaN NODE, all numerical ROR scores, the original Parker groups
and the valid-count rules from #157 are unchanged. The
exact-equality limitation in #172 remains deferred.
- Preserve singleton gene rows under Mapping(method = "max") without
ranking them (#178). In the nonraw impute = FALSE path, remaining NA
and NaN measurements are retained instead of causing a dimension
error. Selection among multiple probes and all other mapping methods
are unchanged.
- Reject mixed AUTO/manual selections and duplicate method names in
BS_Multi() before accessing input data or executing classifiers
(#188). AUTO must be the only entry; manual selections must contain
at least two distinct methods. Valid method selections and their
execution order are unchanged.

                        Changes in version 1.5.8                        

Bug fixes

- Correct PAM50 Confidence gene alignment, Spearman-test handling and
two-decimal rounding; undefined values remain missing. Earlier code
could lose centroid gene names when extracting a data.frame column,
fail to pair genes and return false zeros. This defect is verified
in the Bioconductor 3.23 version 1.4.1 and 3.24 version 1.5.7 source
archives. GitHub revisions sharing a version number can differ: the
Confidence fix was already in GitHub commit 6f68e09 (version 1.5.7).
Users of affected builds should recompute Confidence summaries and
downstream uses of those summaries. A legitimately computed
Confidence can still be zero. This finding alone does not invalidate
subtype calls or numerical ROR scores, which the fix does not
change. Confidence is not a calibrated subtype probability.
- Correct the additional NODE-dependent ROR-PC Group (Subtype +
Clinic + Prolif.Subtype) boundaries (#154): NODE = 0 uses <= 40 / > 40
through 60 / > 60, and NODE = 1--3 uses <= 15 / > 15 through 40 / > 40; at least four positive nodes remain high risk with nonmissing
tumor size. Scores are not rounded for grouping.
- Represent an undefined numerical NaN score as an actual missing
category in the additional NODE-dependent ROR-PC group for NODE = 0
or 1--3, instead of the literal text "NaN". Numerical scores,
finite/infinite categories, clinical missing-value handling and the
independent NODE >= 4 high-risk rule are unchanged. Original Parker
grouping is unaffected.

Reporting and presentation

- Resolve Shiny preprocessing through the installed package namespace
when launched with BreastSubtypeR::iBreastSubtypeR(). Empty
intentional Shiny aborts clear stale results without blank error
callouts; meaningful validation and ordinary error messages remain
visible.
- Remove the unused ggrepel import without changing plot geometry.
Clarify NODE error wording, OSLO sample-subset provenance and .txt
TSV exports.
- Add descriptive InputCoverage() and Shiny coverage reporting for
PAM50, AIMS and SSPBC, using bundled-model gene/rule denominators.
Reporting does not change method eligibility, imputation,
predictions or scientific reliability, and does not assess every ROR
component.
- Refresh the five visualization functions' typography, spacing,
legends and annotations while retaining the established subtype
colors. Display the already calculated heatmap row dendrogram. These
are presentation changes: scaling, clustering, displayed order,
calls, counts, PCA values, boxplot statistics and raw entropy remain
unchanged.
- Update the local Shiny presentation, public OSLO2-EMIT0 README
screenshot, installation/channel guidance, input and export
documentation, and Editor's Choice links. Clarify ssBC.v2
reference-quantile provenance.
- Keep strict package-error/warning CI gates while excluding account
checks only from the GitHub CI BiocCheck invocation. Mailing-list
subscription, Support Site registration and watched-tag registration
require separate maintainer verification; skipped checks are not
reported as successful.

Scientific clarification and known limitation

- Clarify research Spearman correlations versus commercial Prosigna
Pearson correlations (#156). Shared coefficients do not establish
equivalent preprocessing, calibration or clinical validation.
Calculations are unchanged; these are research outputs, not clinical
Prosigna results.
- Temporarily defer the known original Parker-derived ROR-S, ROR-P,
ROR-C and ROR-PC (Subtype + Clinic + Prolif) categorical-output
defect at exact equality to unscaled cutoffs. Strict comparisons can
leave numeric text instead of low, med or high. The unscaled cutoff
pairs are -0.15/0.10, -0.25/0.10, -0.10/0.20 and -0.20/0.20,
respectively, before 100 * (score + 0.35) / 0.85. Numeric-text
labels are invalid categories, not scientifically accepted
assignments. Primary evidence does not conclusively define equality
assignments; a separate scientific review is required. Preserve all
four grouping implementations, scores, coefficients and thresholds.
The separate NODE-dependent correction above remains in place.

                        Changes in version 1.5.7                        

Bug fixes and documentation

- Fixed BS_AIMS() for a single mapped sample while retaining the
exact
sample identifier and matrix dimensions. Historical multi-sample
calls, probabilities and other returned components are unchanged.
- Corrected the AIMS return-value documentation: calls and
assigned-call probabilities are sample-by-one-column matrices;
all.probs is a named list containing the five-subtype probability
matrix.
- Fixed stale results in iBreastSubtypeR(). Input replacement,
example
reload and relevant parameter changes invalidate dependent
predictions, plots and exports. Mapping is retained when only
prediction settings change.
- Added server-side download checks for absent, failed or outdated
predictions. Download controls appear only for supported current
results; unavailable full metrics are explained rather than replaced
with calls.
- Invalid Shiny inputs now produce actionable, recoverable errors.
Correcting prediction settings permits a rerun without remapping
valid inputs or reloading the session. Failed predictions cannot
expose previous results.
- Clarified the cIHC.itr ER-positive : ER-negative target ratio
(default 54 / 64): it must be finite and strictly positive, and
target mode permits values above one. The Shiny iteration control
retains default 100, minimum 10 and step 10; other whole numbers of
at least 10 are accepted.
- Added AIMS and Shiny regression tests. Validation also included
real-browser checks covering input invalidation, downloads, error
recovery, uploaded sample identifiers and independent sessions.
Synchronized installation, workflow and output documentation without
changing scientific algorithms or the public API.

                        Changes in version 1.5.6                        

Bug fixes (behaviour change)

- cIHC.itr (BS_cIHC.itr()) now balances ER groups towards the ER+ :
ER- target ratio (default 54 / 64, the ER distribution of the UNC
PAM50 reference set). In every iteration the ER group that is
over-represented relative to the target is subsampled without
replacement, to ceiling(ratio * n_ERneg) ER+ or ceiling(n_ERpos /
ratio) ER- samples, and the other group is kept in full; a cohort
already at the target is used in full. Previously the numerically
larger ER group was always subsampled, to ceiling(ratio * n_smaller)
samples, so the balancing subset followed the target only when ER+
samples were at least as many as ER- samples and was inverted
otherwise (for example, 54 ER+ and 64 ER- samples were subsampled
to 54 : 46 instead of being used in full).
- The ceiling() rounding convention is kept, so with the default
ratio
results are identical to 1.5.5 whenever ER+ samples are at least as
many as ER- samples. With the default ratio = 54 / 64, the balancing
subset can change for cohorts or subsets in which ER- samples
outnumber ER+ samples, that is, cohorts with an ER-negative
majority. This can affect the calls, scores and ROR values of
BS_cIHC.itr(), and the cIHC.itr and entropy columns of BS_Multi():
in manual calls that include "cIHC.itr", and in AUTO calls that
select cIHC.itr under the existing routing and size gates. AUTO
selects cIHC.itr in both branches of the eligible mixed cohort (at
least 15 ER+ and 18 ER- samples, outside the TN-only and HER2+
routes), with ten methods when the ER+ fraction is strictly
between 0.39 and 0.69 and with eight methods otherwise, so eligible
cohorts with an ER+ fraction of 0.39 or less are included. A changed
balancing subset need not change the subtype call of every cohort or
sample. AUTO method selection, its thresholds and all other methods
are unchanged.
- New argument er_subsample in BS_cIHC.itr() and BS_Multi() (passed
to
cIHC.itr only). er_subsample = "larger" restores the previous rule,
sampling order and outputs exactly, to reproduce results obtained
with BreastSubtypeR 1.5.5 and earlier; the default is "target".
- ratio must be a single finite positive number (write 54 / 64, not
54:64). 54:64 and ratio = 0, which previously gave a base-R error or
centred on the smaller ER group only, now stop with an informative
error. With the default er_subsample = "target" any such ratio is
feasible.
- Regression tests compare both modes with outputs retained from
BreastSubtypeR 1.5.5 and check that BS_Multi() changes no other
method.

                        Changes in version 1.5.5                        

Bug fixes

- Fixed standalone reading of inst/CITATION without package metadata.
The citation file now uses an ASCII-only comment and generates the
package-manual entry only when package metadata is available. The
published article citation and the metadata-derived manual entry are
preserved during normal installed-package use.

                        Changes in version 1.5.4                        

Documentation

- The URL and BugReports fields in DESCRIPTION, the README and the
vignette now point to the development repository
https://github.com/JohanHartmanGroupBioteam/BreastSubtypeR and its
issue tracker instead of the former personal repository, which
redirects there. The mirroring workflow
.github/workflows/sync-to-org.yml, obsolete since the repository
moved to the organization, was removed. No code changes.

                        Changes in version 1.5.3                        

Maintainer

- Emmanouil G. Sifakis (emmanouil.sifakis@ki.se) is the package
maintainer from this version on; Qiao Yang remains an author. The
public repository moved to
https://github.com/JohanHartmanGroupBioteam/BreastSubtypeR (the
previous address redirects). No code changes.

                        Changes in version 1.5.2                        

AUTO routing

- AUTO now decides whether a cohort is HER2+ from the HER2 column
alone: the HER2+ branch requires at least one evaluable HER2 value
and every evaluable HER2 value to be HER2+. Previously the branch
was entered whenever the joint ER/HER2 counts held no HER2-negative
sample, which had two consequences. A cohort with HER2 entirely
missing, or coded with unrecognized values, was routed as HER2+ and
ran AIMS and sspbc only; such cohorts now follow the ER-based rules
(for example a 60/40 ER cohort gets the balanced mixed panel, with
ssBC.v2 returning NA). And a HER2-negative sample whose ER value was
missing was left out of the joint counts, so one such sample did not
end the HER2+ classification while an otherwise identical sample
with a known ER value did; the classification no longer depends on
whether ER was recorded. Missing values and equivocal codes such as
"2+" are treated alike, as not evaluable, and AUTO now reports how
many samples had no evaluable HER2 value and therefore took no part
in the decision. Cohorts with complete HER2 information are routed
exactly as before. Added tests, including regression tests for the
size-gated ER/HER2-defined cohorts.
- AUTO sample subsetting for ssBC and ssBC.v2 now uses the same
inclusive minimums as method selection (>=). Previously a subgroup
whose size was exactly the minimum (ER+ 15, ER- 18, HER2
subgroups 8/9) was accepted by the selection step but excluded from
the subset, so its samples received NA from ssBC/ssBC.v2 while the
method was reported as running. The packaged OSLO2-EMIT0 example is
such a case (18 ER- tumors): with the strict comparison a fresh
BS_Multi(methods = "AUTO") run did not reproduce the packaged frozen
result OSLO2EMIT0obj$res, which carries ssBC calls for those tumors;
with >= it does. A regression test asserts this. Note that the
pseudocode in the supplementary methods of the published paper (Yang
et al. 2025, NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics,
doi:10.1093/nargab/lqaf131) records the strict comparison in this
subsetting step while using >= for method selection; the package now
applies >= in both, and the shipped example is the behavior the
package reproduces.
- README and vignette: the AUTO bullet for ER/HER2-defined cohorts
now
states the size gating (ER group minimum and HER2 subgroup minimum;
smaller cohorts run AIMS and sspbc only), the HER2+ cohort detection
rule, and the treatment of cohorts without evaluable HER2 values.

Bug fixes

- Fixed the ROR-C Group (Subtype + Clinic) column in the ROR output
of
the nearest-centroid methods when hasClinical = TRUE: it was a copy
of the ROR-PC Group (Subtype + Clinic + Prolif) column instead of
the risk group derived from the ROR-C score (thresholds -0.1
and 0.2). The ROR-C score and all other columns are unchanged. Added
a synthetic regression test.
- Fixed the AUTO-mode sample subsets passed to ssBC and ssBC.v2:
samples with a missing ER (or HER2) value produced NA sample names
in samples_ER.icd / samples_ERHER2.icd, which either failed the
SummarizedExperiment subsetting in BS_Multi() ("index out of bounds:
NA") or, when the padded vector was as long as the cohort, silently
skipped the intended subsetting. Missing values are now dropped with
which(), matching makeCalls.ssBC(). Cohorts without missing ER/HER2
values are unaffected. Added regression tests.
- AUTO now reports when no cohort rule matches the ER/HER2 subgroup
sizes and it falls back to the single-sample predictors AIMS and
sspbc (previously a silent fallback). The selected methods are
unchanged.
- Mapping() now accepts a SummarizedExperiment with a single sample.
duplicate_genes(), prepare_nc_matrix() and the probe filter dropped
the matrix dimensions of one-sample input and failed with "dim(X)
must have a positive length". The collapsed gene-by-sample matrix is
now built explicitly; results for multi-sample input are identical
for all method values. Present in 1.4.0 and 1.5.1. Added regression
tests.
- Phenotype tables with factor ER, HER2 or TN columns are now
normalized exactly like character columns; previously unmatched
factor levels were replaced by their integer codes (for example
"Unknown" -> "3") on the BS_Multi() / get_methods() path, which
bypasses the factor conversion in Mapping(). Added regression tests.
- Mapping(RawCounts = TRUE, impute = TRUE): the FPKM matrix is now
checked for missing values itself before imputation (the guard
tested the already imputed log-CPM matrix, so the FPKM matrix was
never imputed).
- BS_Multi(): the warning issued when PCAPAM50 fails now includes the
underlying error message (it previously ended after "failed in this
iteration: ").
- iBreastSubtypeR(): the launcher's dependency helper called
requireNamespace() with unsupported arguments, so it failed silently
and loaded nothing (the app still started because shiny::runApp()
attaches shiny itself). The helper (.load_app_dependencies()) now
loads the requested namespaces and stops with a clear message if a
package is missing or cannot be loaded. Added a test.
- Shiny app: the cohort preflight reported "ready" when only one of
the ER and HER2 columns (or only TN) was present, and the AUTO run
then failed with "requires both 'ER' and 'HER2' columns". The
preflight now names the missing column(s) and blocks the run. Added
tests.
- Documentation: the @return sections of BS_cIHC(), BS_cIHC.itr(),
BS_PCAPAM50() and BS_ssBC() now describe the list that is actually
returned (BS.all, score.ROR, mdns/mdns.fl, outList, and for
BS_cIHC.itr() the per-iteration call matrices); they previously
described a character vector, a data.frame or non-existent elements.
The BS_cIHC.itr() ratio argument is now documented as applied to the
larger ER group relative to the smaller one, and the alphabetical
tie-break of its consensus call is stated. No code changes.
- Documentation: Mapping(method = "mean") and "median" were described
as keeping "the probe with the highest mean/median expression"; the
implementation collapses the duplicate probes of a gene into their
per-sample mean or median, exactly as collapseIDs() in the original
PAM50 bioclassifier code (Parker et al., 2009), from which the
"mean", "median", "iqr" and "stdev" options derive. The help text
now says so and notes that "max" (largest row sum) is an addition of
this package. No code or mapped values changed.
- The per-sample entropy reported by BS_Multi() is now NA when no
executed method returned a call for that sample. table() drops
missing values, so such a row previously gave -sum(numeric(0)), that
is 0 - the same value as unanimous agreement. Rows with at least one
call are unchanged, and the statistic itself (raw, unnormalized
Shannon entropy in bits) is untouched. The situation cannot arise in
AUTO, whose panels always include AIMS and sspbc; it arises in
manual runs of nearest-centroid-only method sets, where a sample
with unknown ER/HER2 status receives no call. Note that Vis_Multi()
orders by entropy, so such samples now sort last instead of
appearing among the unanimous ones. The entropy column is also
documented in ?BS_Multi for the first time. Added tests.
- BS_PCAPAM50() no longer treats samples with an unknown ER status as
ER-negative. The IHC label is derived from the ER column, so a
missing or non-canonical ER value yields NA, and the reference test
!grepl("^L", IHC) is TRUE for NA; such samples were therefore
counted as ER-negative in the PC1 axis check, in the
misclassification-minimizing cutoff search and in the ER-balanced
gene-centering set. They are now excluded from those three steps, a
message reports how many were excluded, and they are still
classified. Cohorts with a complete ER column are unaffected: the
packaged OSLO2-EMIT0 example reproduces its stored PCAPAM50 calls
exactly. This also aligns BS_PCAPAM50() with BS_cIHC() and
BS_cIHC.itr(), which already exclude unknown ER from their
balancing. Added tests.
- BS_cIHC(), BS_cIHC.itr() and BS_PCAPAM50() now stop with a clear
message when the cohort lacks one of the two ER (or
luminal/non-luminal IHC) groups needed for ER balancing, instead of
failing with "undefined columns selected" or "arguments imply
differing number of rows". Cohorts with both groups are unaffected.
Added tests.

Tests

- tests/testthat.R now calls test_check("BreastSubtypeR"), so the
files under tests/testthat/ run during R CMD check. Previously the
file held a single inline test and test-tn-cohort-detection.R was
never executed. The inline BS_Multi() test moved to
tests/testthat/test-bs-multi-manual.R. testthat edition 3 is
declared (Config/testthat/edition), and the Suggests entry requires
testthat >= 3.2.0.

                        Changes in version 1.5.1                        

Bug fixes

- Fixed TNBC cohort detection in cohort-specific method selection
(#133). Cohorts are now classified as TNBC only when all evaluable
non-missing TN annotations indicate TN. Mixed cohorts containing
both TN and nonTN samples are no longer routed to the TNBC-specific
branch solely because some samples are TN.

Tests

- Added synthetic phenotype-table tests for TN-only, mixed, UNC-like
mixed, and missing or partly missing TN annotations.

                        Changes in version 1.5.0                        

Highlights (from v1.1.3 onward)

- Paper published in NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics (2025), Editor's
Choice (DOI: 10.1093/nargab/lqaf131).
- Support for raw RNA-seq counts (requires gene lengths).
- iBreastSubtypeR refresh: cleaner UX, smarter AUTO guidance,
consistent exports.

Enhancements

- ssBC/ssBC.v2: singleton subgroup robustness: Subgroups with n=1 no
longer error:
- Keeps matrix shape (drop=FALSE) and hardens dimnames/types.
- Primary path: original sspPredict(). Fallback: nearest-centroid
(Spearman) when needed.
- If there are 0 common PAM50 genes, returns NA labels with shaped
distances/dist.RORSubtype to avoid downstream errors.
- ROR computation guarded for incomplete inputs.
- SSPBC output now "full": BS_sspbc() and Shiny "sspbc" runs return a
full metrics table (not calls-only).
- Exports map core label columns to the standard names
(Call_5class / Call_4class when applicable).
- Shiny: "Load example data..." button
- One-click load of a small demo dataset from inst/RshinyTest/ to
explore the UI without uploads.
- Shows a notification on success; users can immediately run
Preprocess & map and analyses.
- AUTO preflight UI (Shiny): Now detects cohort kind (TN, ER/HER2,
ER-only, HER2-only) and shows compact stats:
- ER/HER2 subgroups: ER+/HER2-, ER-/HER2-, ER+/HER2+, ER-/HER2+
- TN cohorts: TN vs nonTN
- Readiness uses the same minimums used by AUTO (sourced
programmatically; no duplicated thresholds).
- Shorter notifications.
- Routine toasts (e.g., "Step 1 complete. Proceed to Step 2.") now
auto-dismiss sooner to reduce UI clutter.
- Phenodata normalization (Mapping): Accepts flexible ER/HER2/TN
encodings and normalizes to canonical forms (ER+/ER-, HER2+/HER2-,
TN/nonTN). Ambiguous HER2="2+" remains as-is and raises a warning.

Bug fixes

- TN cohorts + ssBC: BS_Multi() now respects TN cohorts when methods
are specified manually; ssBC/ssBC.v2 switch to s = "TN" / "TN.v2"
when a TN column indicates a TN cohort. Falls back to s = "ER" /
"ER.v2" otherwise.
- AUTO: Fixed a crash in BS_Multi(methods = "AUTO") when ER and/or
HER2 contained missing values (NA).
- AUTO internals: fixed variable name typo (samples_ERHER2.icd).
- Mapping(): Robust ENTREZID coercion (from as.character() to
as.integer() with suppressed warnings).
- cIHC.itr: outList$distances now returned as numeric matrix.

Shiny

- Surface method warnings as toasts:
- Runs are wrapped in a warning handler; package warnings (e.g.,
ssBC.v2 singleton fallbacks) appear as yellow notifications.
- Warnings include subgroup, n, and example sample IDs for quick
triage.
- Shiny preflight reset:
- Fixed a stale cohort summary after switching data sources
(manual uploads <-> example). The preflight panel now
revalidates once inputs change.

Developer notes

- Added lightweight internal logger ._msg() and replaced scattered
message() calls in AUTO to standardize package output without
affecting CRAN/Bioc checks.

Documentation

- README/vignette: brief note on the example-data button and expected
file locations.
- Mapping(): Column metadata clarified. Added explicit requirements
for receptor fields used by AUTO and ER/HER2/TN-dependent methods
(ssBC, cIHC/cIHC.itr, PCAPAM50) and for ROR covariates (TSIZE, NODE
as numeric 0/1). Documented preferred coding and automatic
normalization behavior.

Compatibility Notes

- SSPBC "full" output keeps previous columns for calls; additional
metrics may appear.

Upgrade Notes

- Raw RNA-seq counts are supported from v1.1.3 onward (requires gene
lengths).
- If you previously parsed BS / BS.Subtype, switch to Call_5class /
Call_4class.
- Package API unchanged.

[CAGEr](/packages/CAGEr)
-----

                       Changes in version 2.19.2                        

BUG FIXES

- Fix plotReverseCumulatives(group = "sampleLabels"), which failed
with 'by' must specify a uniquely valid column since
S4Vectors 0.51.8 stopped de-duplicating column names in
as.data.frame() of a DataFrame: the sampleLabels column was selected
twice.
- Remove the utils::data import, which clashed with the new data()
generic of BiocGenerics and caused a replacing previous import
warning at load time. importPublicData() now calls utils::data()
explicitly.

                       Changes in version 2.19.1                        

BACKWARDS-INCOMPATIBLE CHANGES

- In aggregateTagClusters(), tpmThreshold now only selects the tag
clusters that define the boundaries of the consensus clusters. Two
erroneously applied filters are removed: the one that kept only the
CTSSs with a normalised signal above tpmThreshold in at least one
sample, and the one that dropped the CTSSs whose normalised signal
summed over all samples was not above tpmThreshold.
- The excludeSignalBelowThreshold argument of aggregateTagClusters()
is deprecated. It was erroneously discarding the individual CTSSs
below tpmThreshold in every sample.
- CustomConsensusClusters() no longer drops the CTSSs whose
normalised
signal summed over all samples is 1 or less. Its threshold and
nrPassThreshold arguments still apply.

BUG FIXES

- Fix vignette build with recent S4Vectors, whose table() method for
Rle objects does not accept the useNA argument anymore.

OTHER CHANGES

- Accelerated paraclu() ~10×, and distclu() and
aggregateTagClusters()
2–4×, with unchanged results. Clusters that do not overlap any CTSS
now stop the computation with an explicit error message.
- Accelerated exportToTrack() 10–30× when qLow and qUp are given,
with
unchanged results.

                       Changes in version 2.26.0                        

New features

gene
fusion) data. The endpoint is listed only in the 'internal' group of
the cBioPortal OpenAPI v3 specification and is therefore called

phosphoprotein) and the corresponding entity identifiers (stableId)

profiles to the new functions based on molecularAlterationType
- Add genericAssayStableIds argument to fetchData

Bug fixes and minor improvements

- fetchData uses all molecular profiles in the study (excluding
'GENERIC_ASSAY') when molecularProfileIds is not specified (NULL or
NA). Previously, no profiles were downloaded when using the default
molecularProfileIds in cBioPortalData and getDataByGenes.

structural variant and generic assay data) as is rather than
attempting to join gene metadata
- cBioPortalData excludes 'STRUCTURAL_VARIANT' and 'GENERIC_ASSAY'
profiles, which are not indexed by gene, and warns when they are
explicitly requested

avoid the 'service version differs from validated version' warning;
AnVIL now validates the specification with SHA-256 rather than MD5
- Remove the version constraint on AnVIL in DESCRIPTION

profile routing

[CellMentor](/packages/CellMentor)
----------

                 Changes in version 1.1.2 (2026-05-22)                  

Bug fixes

- calculate_performance() now passes as.factor(true_labels) and
as.factor(clusters) to aricode::NMI(). As of aricode 1.1.0
(currently shipping in Bioconductor 3.24), NMI() routes mixed-type
inputs through sort_pairs(), which calls as.integer() on character
labels — turning cell-type names such as "alpha" into NA and
aborting with "NA are not supported.". Coercing both sides to factor
keeps the computation well-defined and restores compatibility with
the Bioconductor build farm. This was the underlying cause of the
vignette failure that 1.1.1 surfaced but did not fix.

                 Changes in version 1.1.1 (2026-05-19)                  

Bug fixes

- cluster_nmf() now falls back to k-means clustering when the NMF
embedding has too few features or cells for SNN (variable-feature
selection on low-dim embeddings was failing under Seurat 5.x). The
number of k-means / hclust centers is now clamped to a feasible
range, so grid search no longer fails silently on small reference
splits.
- CellMentor() now stops with a clear message if every parameter
configuration in the grid search fails, instead of cascading to a
cryptic switch() error during final-model training.
- evaluate_params() warnings now include the underlying error
message,
so build logs surface the real cause of failures.
- initialize_wh() validates that method is a single character string
and reports a helpful error if not.

Documentation

- Updated citation to the published Nature Communications paper
(Hevdeli et al., 2026, doi:10.1038/s41467-025-67088-7).
- Added inst/CITATION so citation("CellMentor") returns a structured
bibliographic entry.

[ChIPseeker](/packages/ChIPseeker)
----------

                       Changes in version 1.49.5                        

- test-txdb.R no longer pins the tx_id -> gene mapping of
TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene. That mapping is annotation data
rebuilt for each Bioconductor release, and tx 70455 changed from
ENST00000487630.1_3 to ENST00000959756.2_2/3554 in BioC 3.24,
failing R CMD check on both Linux builders. Expected values are now
derived from the installed TxDb at test time. (2026-11-12, Thu)

                       Changes in version 1.49.4                        

- The vignette no longer evaluates the KEGG compareCluster() example
at build time. It calls enrichKEGG(), which fetches rest.kegg.jp
live; a transient outage of that endpoint aborted R CMD build on the
Bioconductor Linux builder (nebbiolo1, Bioc 3.23) while building the
vignettes. The example is kept as eval = FALSE with a precomputed
figure (figures/compareCluster_KEGG.png), consistent with the other
cached figures in the vignette. (2026-11-03, Tue)
- annotatePeak() keeps annotation, geneChr/geneStart/geneEnd, geneId
and transcriptId consistent with each other at transcript level
(issue #252). The transcript id of an exon/intron/UTR hit was taken
from names(genomicRegion)[subjectIndex], indexing the unlisted
ranges with the names of the GRangesList; this mostly returned NA
and occasionally a wrong transcript, so a peak could be reported
with the metadata of an unrelated transcript (even on another
chromosome). The ids are now expanded before indexing, and the
Promoter branch writes the feature id reset into anno instead of a
stale local variable, so promoter peaks keep the nearest-TSS
transcript. The same alignment is now applied at level = "gene": the
gene of the overlapping exon/intron/UTR is resolved with TXID2EG()
and used instead of the nearest gene, so
geneId/geneStart/geneEnd/distanceToTSS follow the annotation there
as well. (2026-10-01, Thu)
- seq2gene() no longer fails with $ operator is invalid for atomic
vectors when none of the queried regions overlaps an exon
(getGenomicAnnotation.internal() returns NA then); host-gene
extraction is skipped and the nearest/flanking genes are still
reported (issue #248). (2026-10-01, Thu)
- getTagMatrix()/plotPeakProf2() no longer fail with Error in
cursor:(cursor + seq - 1) : result would be too long a vector when
type = "body" is used with a flank extension shorter than 1kb (issue
#250). The share of bins of a flank is derived from its actual
length (500bp now contributes 5% of the bins instead of being
rounded down to zero), a non-empty flank always gets at least one
column, and the binning loops were replaced by edge-based averaging
of equal-width bins. This changes numbers slightly: the old code
divided the last bin of a section by count-1 instead of count
(about 10% too high for a 10 bp bin), and it put all leftover
positions of a section into its last bin instead of spreading them,
which can move that bin considerably (up to ~40% for a 7 bp
remainder in a 300 bp bin). The x-axis breaks of plotPeakProf2() are
derived from the same column layout. (2026-10-01, Thu)
- downloadGEObedFiles()/downloadGSMbedFiles() rewrite the ftp:// urls
of gsminfo$supplementary_file to https:// before downloading and
report the underlying download error when a file cannot be fetched
(issue #254). (2026-10-01, Thu)
- An empty input is now handled: annotatePeak(GRanges(), ...) returns
an empty csAnno instead of failing with "Error: invalid subscript"
or "replacement has 1 row, data has 0". The root cause
(follow()/precede() returning a SortedByQueryHits object instead of
indices for an empty query) is guarded in
getNearestFeatureIndicesAndDistances(), which also makes seq2gene()
return character(0) for an empty input. (2026-10-01, Thu)
- Documented the distance definition of flank_gene_distances reported
by annotatePeak(..., addFlankGeneInfo = TRUE): a distance of 0 means
that the peak overlaps the feature range - at level = "transcript"
the feature is the whole transcript, which is why most entries can
be 0 - while non-overlapping peaks get the signed distance to the
feature TSS (issue #235). (2026-10-01, Thu)
- annotatePeak() no longer fails with Error: invalid subscript when
every peak is dropped, which typically happens because none of the
seqlevels of the peaks matches TxDb (chr1 vs NC_000001.11).
getGenomicAnnotation() no longer hands the SortedByQueryHits object
returned by follow() for an empty query to features[], and
annotatePeak() now reports the seqlevels mismatch together with how
to align the chromosome names (seqlevelsStyle()). (2026-10-01, Thu)
- plotAvgProf()/plotMultiProf() now state which xlim matches the tag
matrix instead of stopping with "please specify appropreate
xcoordinations...". xlim defines the x-axis coordinates, so its
width has to match the number of columns of the tag matrix; the typo
is gone and both valid forms (c(1, nc) and, for a matrix with one
column per bp, c(-(nc-1)/2, (nc-1)/2)) are shown (issue #240).
(2026-10-01, Thu)
- enrichPeakOverlap() accepts a single GRanges as targetPeak again:
it
was passed on unwrapped while the permutation test works on a list
of target peak sets, so the call failed with "GRanges objects don't
support [[, as.list(), lapply()". The documentation of
enrichPeakOverlap()/enrichAnnoOverlap() now also states the
direction of the test - the observed ratio is the fraction of target
peaks covered by the query peaks and the target is the shuffled set
- which explains why N_OL is identical in both directions while
the p-value is not, and that N_OL of enrichAnnoOverlap() counts
genes and can exceed the number of input peaks (issue #84).
(2026-10-01, Thu)
- enrichPeakOverlap() gained an opt-in symmetric argument. With
symmetric = TRUE the mirrored direction (query and target exchanged)
is computed as well and the two one-sided permutation p-values are
combined as min(1, 2*min(p, p_rev)) (Hedges), so the result no
longer depends on the order of the arguments. The default stays
FALSE (one-sided) and all existing numbers are unchanged; the
mirrored test doubles the number of permutations and raises the
smallest reportable p-value to 2/(nShuffle+1). enrichAnnoOverlap()
needs no such argument, its hypergeometric p-value is already
exactly symmetric (issue #84). (2026-10-01, Thu)
- upsetplot(vennpie = TRUE) can be drawn again with ggplot2 >= 4.0.
The vennpie sub-view is embedded as an annotation_custom() layer,
which ggplot2 only supports below coord_cartesian(), so the sub-view
no longer uses coord_fixed(). No replacement for it is added:
ggplotify rasterises the grob with the aspect ratio of the device,
and forcing a square panel distorted the venn diagram further
(measured anisotropy 1.43 without versus 1.50 with
theme(aspect.ratio = 1), against 1.41 for the undistorted drawing).
Before, the plot failed with `annotation_custom()` only works with
`coord_cartesian()`. Note that ggupset 0.4.1 itself still maps the
deprecated size aesthetic, so drawing the plot may print "Please use
linewidth instead"; the warning comes from ggupset
(https://github.com/const-ae/ggupset/issues) and can be ignored.
(2026-10-01, Thu)

                       Changes in version 1.49.2                        

- annotatePeak() now reports geneChr and geneStrand as characters
instead of factor codes. as.data.frame() returns 'seqnames'/'strand'
as factors and assigning a factor into mcols() dropped the class, so
both columns came out as integers (e.g. geneStrand = 1/2 instead of
+/-, and a wrong geneChr whenever the seqlevels were not in numeric
order) (issues #233, #247). (2026-09-15, Tue)
- annotatePeak() now warns when peaks are dropped because no feature
of TxDb can be found for them (e.g. peaks on contigs/scaffolds
without genes, or a seqlevels style mismatch). Previously they
disappeared silently (issues #251, #258). (2026-09-15, Tue)
- annotatePeak(..., sameStrand = TRUE) no longer assigns a peak to a
feature on the opposite strand. Overlap detection in
getNearestFeatureIndicesAndDistances() was calling findOverlaps()
with unstrand(features), which bypassed sameStrand and overrode the
strand-aware nearest-feature result (issues #257, #258). Peaks with
ambiguous strand (*) are unaffected and still match features on any
strand. (2026-09-14, Mon)
- plotAnnoBar() no longer uses the deprecated ggplot2::aes_string()
(issue #268). It follows the tidy evaluation idiom already used by
plotDistToTSS(). (2026-09-14, Mon)
- upsetplot() no longer uses the deprecated ggplot2::aes_(); the x
aesthetic is now mapped with .data$anno, the same tidy evaluation
idiom used by plotDistToTSS(). (2026-09-17, Thu)
- dropped unused @importFrom directives that have no call site in the
package (ggplot2::geom_text, ggplot2::geom_segment,
ggplot2::scale_fill_brewer, ggplot2::scale_fill_hue), so the
generated NAMESPACE imports less. (2026-09-17, Thu)

                       Changes in version 1.49.1                        

- Fixed bug in getNearestFeatureIndicesAndDistances() where results
for overlap == "all" were silently overridden by the overlap ==
"TSS" branch, causing the two modes to behave identically.
(2026-09-07, Mon)
- Comprehensive documentation updates for core functions
(annotatePeak(), getGenomicAnnotation(), getTagMatrix() and related,
readPeakFile(), seq2gene(), dplyr verb extensions, plotting
functions, etc.).
- Simplified redundant logic in seq2gene() by merging the promoter
and
flanking-gene extraction into a single condition (no behavior
change).

                         Changes in version 1.3                         

Change in 1.3.5

ggplotChromatogramsOverlay().

Chromatograms(spectra), peaksData() and [ no longer re-validate the
wrapped Spectra on every call (which re-stated every backing file),
so they no longer scale with the number of files.

- Improve performance of peaksData() for ChromBackendSpectra with
overlapping chromatogram windows (e.g. from chromExtract()): each
spectrum is aggregated once and shared across the windows it falls
in, instead of once per window. Results are unchanged; the speed-up
grows with the number of overlapping windows.

are
located by scanning outwards from it rather than scanning the whole
chromatogram. Results are unchanged.

sort

methods.

first, avoiding a spurious failure when input data is already
sorted.
