[clusterExperiment](/packages/clusterExperiment)
-----------------

                       Changes in version 2.33.1                        

- `getBestFeatures` with `DEMethod="limma-voom"` (and functions that
  call it, such as `mergeClusters` and `RSEC` with count data) now uses
  `limma::voomLmFit` instead of `voom` followed by `lmFit`, following
  the limma authors' recommendation of `voomLmFit` over `voom`.
  `voomLmFit` reduces the residual degrees of freedom for genes that
  have zero counts in all of the samples in a cluster, so results for
  such genes can be noticeably different (typically less significant)
  than in previous versions. Because the shared variance estimates are
  affected, the results of other genes in the same analysis can also
  change. If no gene has zero counts in all of the samples of a
  cluster, results are the same as in previous versions. Requires limma
  (>= 3.99.3).

[clusterProfiler](/packages/clusterProfiler)
---------------

                       Changes in version 4.21.6                        

mechanism evidence: correctness and limits

- Pathway and mechanism reports show ledger-derived support,
conflict,
mixed, undetermined and noncomputable evidence before legacy grades,
with attempted/computable denominators and incomplete-coverage
flags; A/B/C rules and discovery scores are unchanged (2026-11-11,
Wed)
- Added an offline paired replay of frozen perturbation responses
across historical/fixed code and 8/4 versus 5/2 caps: it
distinguishes corrected coverage diagnoses from cap sensitivity
without claiming improved accuracy (2026-11-11, Wed)
- adjudicate() retains explicit mixed measurements and does not
select
a programme half when collection directions disagree; incomplete
half-statistics return unknown rather than crashing (2026-11-11,
Wed)
- interpret() preserves a supplied method-normalized effect even when
raw perturbation responses are mixed, without inventing an effect
when it is missing (2026-11-11, Wed)
- adjudicate() reads every measured perturbation row instead of the
first: row order no longer changes the effect; raw response
directions and method-normalized effects are summarized separately,
and opposing normalized effects yield no single effect (2026-11-11,
Wed)
- pathway_evidence() reports whether dataset resolution returned
data,
found nothing usable, or failed; a network outage or a machine
without the suggested gpsadb previously printed "No usable
perturbation data found in GPSAdb" and reason no-dataset, which is a
false statement about the database. Failures are now lookup-failed
with the error text in the dataset_lookup attribute, and a partial
failure is disclosed even when another candidate resolves
(2026-11-11, Wed)
- pathway_evidence() distinguishes missing fold changes from members
that are absent from them: with direction supplied by
pathway_direction or NES and no signed list, the row now says
no-fold-changes instead of claiming the members were not found
(2026-11-11, Wed)
- Subsetting pathway_evidence() by columns keeps the retained
evidence
ledger; a pure column reorder used to strip the attributes while
keeping the class, so mechanism_report() saw no candidate/dataset
evidence (2026-11-11, Wed)
- pathway_evidence() falls back to the other removal spellings GPSAdb
records (CRISPRi, knockout, siRNA, shRNA) when the legacy literal
"knockdown" query returns nothing; STAT1, recorded as CRISPRi plus
knockout only, had been reported as having no data. The search stops
at the first spelling that yields datasets, so methods are not
united; overexpression stays excluded (2026-11-11, Wed)
- pathway_evidence() counts supporting cell lines within a driver,
applies the member-support floor before promotion, maps all Entrez
members, and retains every candidate/dataset outcome in attr(x,
"perturbation_tests"), including conflicts and failures (2026-11-10,
Tue)
- mechanism_reproduction() requires enough finite members per
dataset,
rejects conflicting experiment identities and does not count unknown
biosamples as independent replication; mechanism_preflight()
distinguishes zero coverage from unavailable coverage (2026-11-10,
Tue)
- mechanism_report() exposes perturbation_tests and per-candidate
support/conflict summaries; its classes are now supported,
conflicting and undetermined rather than excluded. Nonsignificance
is not disproof; target-overlap neighbourhoods and perturbation
breadth are descriptive flags, not causal equivalence or specificity
tests (2026-11-10, Tue)
- adjudicate() honours explicit coverage overrides and fingerprints
actual evidence and decision settings; measured-only evidence
reaches interpret(), whose adjudicated prompt now carries exact
identity, direction and writable-strength constraints. These
constraints do not guarantee model compliance or establish causality
(2026-11-10, Tue)
- Corrected the 4.21.5 benchmark claims: all 17 expected drivers were
scorable, with default signed hit counts 6/17, 10/17 and 13/17 at
ranks 1/5/10. Earlier 14-driver denominators and module PPV gains
were invalid; the frozen, study/driver-stratified audit reports set
size with module coverage and keeps historical verification separate
from current grading. No target-count weight is introduced;
conflicting duplicate network weights now error (2026-11-10, Tue)

                       Changes in version 4.21.5                        

interpret()

- interpret() takes prior: another tool's answer (a SingleR or scGPT
label, a TF-activity ranking), sent after the evidence as a claim to
check rather than as evidence. The record adds conclusion,
prior_verdict and prior_rationale. On PBMC 10k with SingleR
labels, 12 of 14 verdicts on misassigned subtypes were Corrected
and 1 of 14 on correct ones (2026-11-02, Mon)
- reduce_redundancy() defaults to 0.7, the default of the simplify()
it calls, and its documentation now describes what simplify() does
rather than the earlier greedy selection. Cisplatin GO ORA keeps 81
of 141 terms (0.5: 40), geneList GO ORA 76 of 195; KEGG lists are
kept whole (2026-11-02, Mon)

GO annotation cache

- The built GO gene-set object is cached per (organism, ont, keytype)
on top of the annotation cache: 1.4 s of a 2.8 s warm BP call, and
compareCluster() pays it once per cluster (13 clusters: 39.5 s
against 19.7 s, results identical). Up to three objects are kept,
least recently used first out, and an evidence-filtered annotation
is never cached (2026-10-29, Thu)

pathway-level mechanism evidence

- pathway_evidence() tests enriched pathways against measured
perturbation data instead of hunting for transcription factors.
Given candidate drivers it resolves each to its knockdown datasets
and reports A/B/C with a statement column holding the claim a
perturbation experiment could refute. Candidates are supplied by the
caller on purpose: picking them automatically carried no usable
signal (2026-10-30, Fri)
- Level A requires replication across two cell lines, a direction
that
agrees with the pathway, and a pathway direction that does not come
from the pathway's own members. Before this, a member-derived
direction earned B on a tautology (the agreeing fraction is at
least 50% by construction) and significance alone earned A even when
the perturbation moved the pathway the way it was already running
(2026-10-30, Fri)
- reason records why a pathway stopped short of A --
single-cell-line,
direction-conflict, no-dataset, too-small, not-significant,
no-test-completed, member-derived, low-support and the input-side
cases -- so "nothing found" is distinguishable from "nothing could
be looked at". A failed GPSAdb call is no-test-completed with a
warning, not weak evidence, and a timeout no longer reads as "no
perturbation test identified a driver" (2026-10-31, Sat)
- mechanism_preflight() decides before a run whether the data can
carry a driver claim, and returns the numbers behind the decision.
On eleven real datasets it blocked 7 of 7 that gave no usable answer
and 0 of 4 that did, and every reason was visible in advance
(2026-11-03, Mon)
- mechanism_report() turns reason into "what to do next" and gives
the
candidate's full inventory, separating data, analysis and "no
experiment would change this". It stops recommending experiments
when the preflight says attribution is not supported, because adding
a cell line cannot rescue a dataset with 23 differentially expressed
genes, and it resolves aliases so a report on GR finds NR3C1's
dataset (2026-11-03, Mon)
- mechanism_report() gains network, min_overlap and global_effect_de.
module groups drivers whose regulator-target sets overlap, because
paralogues, subunits of one complex and parallel pathway arms cannot
be told apart by an expression experiment: on 17 benchmark datasets
this covers the true driver 7/10 against 6/10 for the single top-1
and lifts module-level PPV from 19% to 54%, recovering HIF1A-EPAS1,
STAT1-IRF1, XBP1-ATF6, TP53-TP73 and NR3C1-AR with no prior
annotation. global_effect_reason marks a driver whose knockdown
moved more than global_effect_de genes (default 3000), since such a
perturbation drags any pathway of this size and a supported verdict
on it says "large perturbation", not "specific driver". Neither
field changes the A/B/C class (2026-11-08, Sat)
- mechanism_reproduction() reports how many of a driver's independent
perturbation datasets move the pathway the same way, and
pathway_evidence(reproduction = ) uses it to word a single-cell-line
row. The majority sign is the mode of the per-dataset signs rather
than sign(sum(shift)), so one dataset with a large effect cannot
overturn two smaller ones that agree, and datasets whose members are
all NA are dropped before k is counted (2026-11-07, Sat)
- mechanism_discover() ranks candidate transcription factors for a
profile, so pathway_evidence() gets a shortlist instead of
searching 265 candidates at 1-2 s per query. On 17 experiments the
true driver ranked first in 43%, the top five in 71% and the top ten
in 93% (median 2) among the 14 drivers a typical network contains;
the other three are absent from CollecTRI. The shortlist is not a
verdict: verifying the top five let 70% of true drivers through but
also 40% of the decoys, a positive predictive value near 19%, and
the decoys that pass are the driver's neighbours -- ATF4 and ATF6
beside ER stress, EPAS1 beside HIF1A, IRF1 downstream of STAT1. The
score also rises with the number of annotated targets, even among
candidates that are not the driver; n_targets and share report this
rather than correcting it (2026-11-07, Sat)
- The attribution route explored on branch mechanism-decompose is not
merged. Five statistics over one reference matrix landed on the same
recall/precision trade-off, the best pointing at the true driver
in 6 of 9 datasets against 6 of 9 for this implementation, with two
failure modes no reweighting fixed.
dev_docs/mechanism-attribution-postmortem.md records the five things
not to try again (2026-11-03, Mon)
- Fixes: a level-B row now says a single-cell-line limit is the data
rather than the evidence, while a direction conflict keeps its own
wording; a member-derived direction no longer reads "100% of members
moved up, below the support floor of 50%"; reason reports too-small
ahead of low-support; coherent-refuted is separated from
coherent-untested; an empty result, an outage and an unreachable
level A each warn instead of passing as findings; print() runs for
pathway_evidence and a column subset no longer breaks it; empty and
NA tokens are not counted as members; alias lookup runs in both
directions, so drivers = "GR" finds NR3C1 (2026-10-31, Sat)

mechanism analysis: collect, adjudicate, write

- evidence() grades a gene list against upstream collections and
returns an evidenceBundle whose $regulators carries evidence_kind
(measured, predicted, observed or none) and a level. supported
requires one measured source corroborated by a second: counting
sources is not counting evidence when two predictions agree
(2026-10-25, Sun)
- adjudicate(), formerly consensus(), decides which claims survive a
change of evidence type and returns verdicts, the evidence behind
them, diagnostics, parameters and a provenance fingerprint;
interpret() requires an adjudication, so that decision cannot be
skipped on the way to prose (2026-10-28, Wed)
- upstream = "perturbagen" asks GPSAdb which measured perturbation
moves the input genes -- the only source that reaches level A.
upstream = "tfunion" adds ENCODE ChIP-seq, ChEA 2022,
TF_Perturbations and TRRUST: 2869 sets naming 315 factors C3:TFT has
no set for, including EPAS1, NFKB1, TP53, CTCF, ESR1, JUN and FOS
(2026-10-27, Tue)
- mechanism_writable(), mechanism_xref(), collapse_findings(),
mechanism_graph() with plot_mechanism(), mechanism_sets(),
consensus_findings(), mechanism_significant() and
mechanism_alias_regulator() are exported, and simplify() removes
redundancy from any collection rather than only GO
(#743, 2026-10-26, Mon)
- Fixes: perturbation_effect no longer calls an activator a repressor
when the caller's own contrast knocks that factor down, and
measured_direction now reads the same gene set it does;
unsupported_claims() no longer drops real symbols such as P53 and
P300, no longer exempts a rejected regulator because its symbol was
also an input gene, and no longer excuses one whose symbol prefixes
an unrelated gene; print() reports coverage and a failed source
instead of silence, and no longer counts aliases against candidate
regulators (2026-10-29, Thu)

                       Changes in version 4.21.4                        

fixes

- The headline verdict could be produced by a symbol collision.
TRANSFAC's NF1 is Nuclear Factor I while the HGNC symbol NF1 is
neurofibromin, and matched on the string the motif term and a
knockout dataset "agreed". A collided label can no longer reach
supported (2026-10-25, Sun)
- A protein name that maps to a gene is no longer treated as a family
label. TRANSFAC names nuclear receptors by their protein -- GR, PXR,
FXR, HIF2A -- none of which are HGNC symbols, so the perturbation
channel skipped them as families and GR could not reach supported on
a glucocorticoid experiment, where it is the one answer that is
certain (2026-10-26, Mon)
- Regulators are looked up in perturbation databases under every name
they are known by, in both directions: the collections say GR where
the database says NR3C1, and HIF1 where it says HIF1A. Querying one
spelling returned nothing, which is indistinguishable from "never
perturbed" (2026-10-27, Tue)
- mechanism_is_family_label() no longer reads a hyphenated symbol as
a
family: TRANSFAC writes NKX2_5 where HGNC writes NKX2-5, which also
stripped those genes of their measured evidence kind (2026-10-25,
Sun)
- The perturbation sweep no longer runs concurrently: GPSAdb returns
different data when queried in parallel and reports nothing unusual,
so the supported set flipped between runs.
options(clusterProfiler_perturb_workers = 4) takes the trade
knowingly (2026-10-26, Mon)
- A p-value tie between two datasets for one regulator is settled by
system match, then p-value, then genes moved, then dataset id -- the
last unique, so the ordering is total rather than dependent on
arrival order (2026-10-26, Mon)
- Corroboration now requires the sources to cite different datasets,
not merely different source names: perturbagen and biotrigger are
two views of one GPSAdb experiment, so when both cited the same
dataset the server was agreeing with itself (2026-10-26, Mon)
- evidence_similarity() and evidence_biotrigger() are exported but no
longer part of the bundle, after measuring what they contribute:
biotrigger raised the supported count without adding a transcription
factor, and the additions were genes with no bearing on the system
under study (2026-10-26, Mon)
- microRNA collections are no longer tested by default. Predicted
seed
matches gave 7 significant miRNAs among the up-regulated genes and
none among the down ones, the opposite of what a repressor predicts,
so the direction that would make the result interpretable is absent
(2026-10-25, Sun)
- upstream = also accepts "cellstate" (C8) and "tissue" (C4:CGN),
whose set identifiers already name the entity and are passed through
unchanged rather than through the transcription-factor rules, which
would turn a cardiac signature into the gene HPX (2026-10-25, Sun)
- network = TRUE is documented as informational: $ppi carries the
edges but nothing consumes them into a verdict, so the channel is
reference material rather than corroboration (2026-10-28, Wed)
- evidence_ppi() grades STRING edges by the channel behind them:
escore or dscore at 0.4 or above gives B, anything else C, and no
STRING channel measures a perturbation so an edge never reaches A.
pscore is deliberately unused -- it is 0 even for NFKB1-NFKBIA,
which carries escore = 0.999 (2026-10-25, Sun)
- The session cache directory is no longer forced to tempdir() on
attach, which overwrote a directory set in .Rprofile and made
downloaded collections miss their cache (2026-10-25, Sun)
- Switching ontology no longer evicts the GO annotation cache. The
cache was keyed on the ontology and stored only the last call's
annotation, so BP then MF then BP rebuilt it every time: five
alternating enrichGO() calls took 85.5 s of which the enrichment
itself is 0.4 s, and now take 11.6 s, with identical results
(2026-10-27, Tue)
- A gseaResult is now tested with GSEA, not re-tested with ORA.
Taking
the union of core_enrichment and running enricher() on it discarded
the ranking and the sign, so the "GSEA path" was the ORA path with a
different input and the two agreed against ground truth because they
were the same test (2026-10-27, Tue)
- The two front ends can legitimately disagree: on the airway list
GR_Q6 has ORA padj 0.0002 and GSEA padj 0.166, both correct, because
one asks about over-representation among significant genes and the
other about moving monotonically with the phenotype. Use ORA for the
first question, GSEA for the second (2026-10-27, Tue)
- An interrupted Enrichr download no longer poisons the cache: the
union libraries count as cached only when a .meta marker sits beside
the GMT, as the MSigDB files already did. A truncated file used to
be reused, shrinking the collection and grading every regulator
outside it absent instead of failed (2026-10-28, Wed)
- tft combined with upstream = "tfunion" is an error rather than a
silent no-op. tft = "gtrd" is how a caller escapes the family and
consensus labels no perturbation dataset can answer for, and
dropping it turned a 504-set search into a 2869-set one without a
word (2026-10-28, Wed)
- enrichDAVID() applies qvalueCutoff row by row: an NA q-value means
Storey estimation failed for that row, so it bypasses this cutoff
instead of switching the cutoff off for every term
(clusterProfiler#710, #584, #614, #332, 2026-10-27, Tue)
- gseKEGG() reports the same category / subcategory columns as
enrichKEGG(); a reader that filtered on category silently behaved
differently depending on which function produced the result
(#787, 2026-10-26, Mon)

interpret()

- $pathways carries pathway_padj, the pathway's own enrichment
p-value, beside padj_within_pathway, which is the attribution's. The
two answer different questions and without the first the narrative
context could only order by attribution strength: on the hypoxia
contrast that put "carbohydrate metabolic process" above "response
to hypoxia" (2026-10-28, Wed)
- An adjudicated run now adds one fixed sentence to its system
prompt:
only supported findings may be stated as mechanisms, single_source
is a hypothesis, absent is not "does not exist", and untested is not
an absence. It is appended rather than substituted, so the four
legacy input types keep the prompt they had byte for byte -- a test
compares the strings rather than trusting it (2026-10-28, Wed)
- The pathway layer now reaches the narrative.
interpret(adjudication)
lists which regulator explains each enriched pathway, in its own
prompt section marked as context, and only for entities the
adjudication already graded -- so an attribution can never introduce
a regulator or make a claim sound stronger. The "context, not
evidence" instruction travels inside that section rather than in the
system prompt, which would have changed the bytes of the four legacy
input types (2026-10-28, Wed)
- network = TRUE is documented as reference material: $ppi carries
the
graded STRING edges but nothing turns an edge into a corroboration,
so it changes no verdict. A test pins that, so the assumption cannot
creep back (2026-10-28, Wed)
- fix interpret() reverting a caller's adjudication. It re-ran
adjudicate() with the default min_independent in three places -- the
prompt builder and the two post-hoc evidence tables -- so a caller
who adjudicated at a stricter setting had it silently overridden,
which is the one thing making adjudication a separate step exists to
prevent. The carried verdict table now travels through the whole
call (2026-10-28, Wed)
- interpret() gains evidence_status(), a deterministic grounding
check: every gene symbol the interpretation names is classified as
observed or out_of_evidence. No model is called, so unlike a second
model the check is exact (2026-09-26, Sat)
- interpret(), interpret_agent() and interpret_hierarchical() stamp
their results with an execution record, read back with provenance():
the model actually addressed, the decoding parameters and whether
the response confirmed them, digests of the prompts and response,
token usage and finish_reason. A remote model is not a versionable
dependency, and without the record a transport failure arrives as an
ordinary result (2026-09-03, Thu)
- interpret() reads per-gene statistics through gene_stats, a
differential-expression table whose gene, log fold change and
adjusted p-value columns are recognised by name or row names, and
lists the genes of the enriched terms with those values (2026-10-18,
Sun)
- interpret() no longer truncates the genes it sends: every input
gene
is listed, every fold change of the sent terms' genes is given, and
an agent cluster without enriched terms lists every input gene.
n_pathways stays NULL, because on five public lists a lower cap
named fewer themes; lower reduce_threshold instead (2026-10-11, Sun)
- interpret() now interprets an enrichment result and nothing else,
so
its task and prior arguments are removed; combining enrichment
evidence with other tools moves to interpret_agent(prior = ), whose
Synthesizer returns conclusion and prior_verdict (2026-09-30, Wed)
- reduce_redundancy() and reduce_go_redundancy() are exported and
interpret() takes reduce / reduce_threshold, so every significant
theme reaches the model once: GO by Wang semantic similarity, other
collections by Jaccard overlap (2026-09-20, Sun)
- interpret() and interpret_agent() take reasoning, passed through to
the provider and recorded in the execution stamp; left NULL the
request is byte-identical to one made before the argument existed
(2026-09-20, Sun)
- interpret_agent() gains an optional Reviewer agent (review = TRUE)
that audits the draft, reporting grounding separately from it
(2026-09-03, Thu)
- interpret() and interpret_agent() warn when add_ppi = TRUE and the
STRING query fails, instead of silently interpreting without PPI
evidence (2026-09-30, Wed)
- fix interpret() to read gene names from the object's symbols rather
than from a mismatched identifier column; an unparsed model response
is reported instead of returning NULL (2026-09-26, Sat)
- digest is now in Suggests, used for the prompt and response digests
of provenance() (2026-10-23, Fri)

                       Changes in version 4.21.3                        

- fix get_kegg_species() and kegg_taxa() for KEGG's retirement of the
organism special database name: https://rest.kegg.jp/list/organism
now answers HTTP 400 while the rest of the REST API keeps working,
so the weekly "Update KEGG Data" workflow and any user calling
search_kegg_organism(use_internal_data = FALSE) failed with "cannot
open URL ... HTTP status was '400 Bad Request'". Both now read
/list/genome, which returns the same organisms as <T
number>\t<code>; <scientific name> (<common name>); the species list
is parsed from the name and code of that single column. An organism
without a common name keeps its scientific name in common_name, as
it did before (2026-10-18, Sun)
- restore_hybrid_result() and restore_entrez_result_ids() map a gene
set's IDs back to the source keyType with one vectorized pass
instead of one labels[ids] + unname() per set. On a BP result
(~5,900 tested sets, 390k ID slots) that loop cost 7.5 s per call
and compareCluster() calls it once per cluster; the vectorized form
takes 0.2 s and is byte-identical, including list names, empty sets
and geneID order (pinned by a test). hybrid_ids_for_input() likewise
replaces a per-id mapping$source == id scan with a single split and
named lookup (negligible wall time at cluster-sized inputs, but no
longer quadratic in the mapping size). Measured on the
PBMC 10k 13-cluster SYMBOL compareCluster() together with the
enrichit fixes: 140 s -> about 70 s (run-to-run 69-78 s), with 7,489
rows, p-values (difference 0), Counts and geneID sets identical
(2026-10-18, Sun)
- enrichGO() caches the hybrid GSON it builds for a non-ENTREZID
keyType when some input IDs cannot be mapped to Entrez. Without a
universe, that build reads every key of the OrgDb and therefore
depends only on (organism, ont, keyType), but compareCluster() calls
enrichGO() once per cluster and rebuilt it every time (7.7 s per
call on human GO BP, PBMC 10k, 13 clusters, 2026-10-18). The hybrid
path itself is unchanged and still fires ONLY when an input ID has
no Entrez mapping -- an all-mappable input keeps the existing fast
path and never builds hybrid data -- while a universe-scoped or
evidence-filtered call neither reads nor writes this cache
(2026-10-18, Sun)
- read.gmt.pc() now reads the fields of a Pathway Commons gene set
description by their labels rather than by splitting the string at
every "; ". A pathway name that holds a semicolon, such as
Phospholipase C-mediated cascade; FGFR2, is no longer cut short and
its datasource, organism and idtype stay in their own columns;
previously the extra pieces were merged into the last field, so the
fields were shifted one to the left and nothing said so. A
description that declares fewer fields than expected returns NA for
the missing one instead of failing the whole read, and enrichPC()
and gsePC() take the species from the first gene set that declares
an organism (#789, 2026-10-08, Thu)
- fix enrichGO() with a non-ENTREZID keyType when some source IDs
cannot be mapped to Entrez: the memory-saving Entrez annotation
remains the fast path, while unmapped source IDs are added through
direct native-key annotations and analyzed in one hybrid GSON; when
universe is omitted, the effective annotated hybrid background is
constructed and reported by message instead of silently dropping IDs
(#829, 2026-10-03, Sat)
- restore the original source keyType consistently after the Entrez
optimization and readable conversion, including result metadata and
projected gene-set memberships (#829, 2026-10-03, Sat)

                       Changes in version 4.21.2                        

- enrichMKEGG() and gseMKEGG() accept a GSON object for organism, as
enrichKEGG()/gseKEGG() already did, so KEGG module enrichment can
run against a locally built annotation (gson_KEGG()) when KEGG is
unreachable; they also now stop with "organism should be a species
name or a GSON object" instead of an unrelated error from the
organism mapper. The organism documentation for the KEGG functions
now mentions the GSON option at all (2026-09-22, Tue, #623)
- enrichGO() takes an evidence argument to restrict the GO annotation
by evidence code before the analysis, e.g. evidence = c("IDA",
"IPI", "IMP") to keep manually supported annotations or evidence =
"IEA" for electronic ones only; dropping IEP is the usual way to
avoid circular reasoning when the gene sets come from co-expression
clustering. Because the annotation (and hence the background)
changes, the result is not simply a subset of the unfiltered run,
and filtered runs are not cached (2026-09-22, Tue, #160)
- enrichGO() no longer aborts with missing value where TRUE/FALSE
needed when an OrgDb's organism cannot be identified — an
AnnotationHub OrgDb, for example. The cached-GO-data check compared
the cached organism against get_organism(OrgDb) in a bare if(), and
that comparison is NA for such an OrgDb, so the second call in a
session failed with an error that named none of this; an
unidentifiable organism is now treated as "not cached" and the
annotation is rebuilt (2026-09-22, Tue, #232)
- Gff2GeneTable() now reads Ensembl/GTF-style GFF3 as well as
NCBI/RefSeq files: it accepts a gene_id= attribute (Ensembl) in
addition to GeneID= (NCBI) and takes the gene symbol from
Name=/gene_name= when gene= is absent. Previously an Ensembl file
left every key NA, and merging two all-NA key columns is a cartesian
product — useful-looking but wrong on a small file and negative
length vectors are not allowed on a real genome. A file with neither
identifier style now stops with a message saying what is expected
(2026-09-22, Tue, #193)
- add_go_level() appends a level column giving the GO level of every
enriched term (1 = the ontology root), so results can be kept to a
band of levels with e.g. subset(res, level >= 3 & level <= 6); the
level is taken from the ontology the term itself belongs to, so ont
= "ALL" and compareCluster() results are labelled term by term
(2026-09-22, Tue, #793)
- simplify() now infers the ontology from the GO IDs when the result
object does not carry one, instead of refusing: this covers a
gseaResult whose @setType holds a collection name rather than an
ontology (MSigDB C5, a gson GO file, a TERM2GENE built from GO
annotations) as well as an enrichResult from enricher(), which
previously required assigning x@ontology by hand; results spanning
several ontologies are simplified as GOALL, and non-GO gene sets are
still rejected with a message that says so (2026-09-22, Tue, #753,
#369)
- compareCluster() now warns when a non-character universe is
supplied: it wraps each per-cluster call in suppressMessages(),
which used to swallow the underlying enrichment function's "universe
is not in character and will be ignored" message, so a numeric
universe appeared to be accepted while having no effect (2026-09-22,
Tue, #654)
- gsePC() and gseWP() now expose an eps argument and forward it to
GSEA() (and on to enrichit::gsea_gson()), matching GSEA(), gseGO(),
gseKEGG() and gseMKEGG() (2026-09-22, Tue)
- fix gson_cpd() to use the compound KEGG REST endpoint;
enrichKEGG(organism = 'cpd') had been failing since KEGG retired
/link/cpd/pathway, which now returns HTTP 400 (2026-09-22, Tue,
#828)
- kegg_rest() now reports a failed download where it happens, telling
an unreachable network apart from an HTTP error status and from an
empty response; previously these surfaced much later as an obscure
error (2026-09-22, Tue)
- download.KEGG.Path() and download.KEGG.Module() now stop with an
actionable message when the downloaded annotation is empty, or when
the gene/pathway table shares no ID with the pathway-name table,
instead of returning an empty annotation that downstream surfaced as
a misleading "No gene can be mapped"; this replaces an is.null()
guard that could never fire (2026-09-22, Tue, #146, #378, #561,
#646)
- align GSEA significance filtering with the historical behavior of
clusterProfiler <= 4.18.x: pvalueCutoff now requires both the raw
p-value and the adjusted p-value to pass the cutoff, so
significant-pathway counts from GSEA()/gseGO()/gseKEGG()/gseMKEGG()
are again comparable with the DOSE/fgsea backend (2026-08-14, Thu)
- restore the seed argument on GSEA(), gseGO(), gseMKEGG() and
gseKEGG() and forward it to enrichit::gsea_gson(), so
permutation-based GSEA results can be reproduced with a fixed seed
(or set.seed() before the call); the argument had been dropped when
the enrichit engine was introduced (2026-08-14, Thu)
- fix get_data_from_KEGG_db() to strip species suffix from pathway
names when use_internal_data=TRUE, matching the online path
behaviour (2026-08-04, Tue, #783)
- fix enrichGO() to check whether the OrgDb supports ENTREZID before
attempting the ENTREZID-remapping optimisation; custom OrgDb
packages without ENTREZID keytype (e.g., non-model organisms) now
fall back to the original get_GO_data path instead of throwing an
error (2026-08-04, Tue, #823)

                       Changes in version 4.21.1                        

- support UniProt accession -> KO conversion in bitr_kegg() via KEGG
REST and export gson_KO() for KEGG Orthology workflows (2026-06-24,
Wed)
- add nseGO(), nseKEGG(), nseMKEGG(), nseWP(), mnseGO(), mnseKEGG(),
mnseMKEGG(), and mnseWP() as high-level topology-aware enrichment
wrappers powered by enrichit, with metadata backfilling and
lightweight wrapper tests (2026-06-24, Wed)
- re-export aggregate_omics(), aggregate_enrichment(),
harmonize_ids(), and select_features_for_ora() from enrichit for
high-level multi-omics workflows (2026-06-24, Wed)
- get_ppi_network to download and cache the full STRING PPI network
for a specific species (2026-06-23, Tue)
- the getPPI is now alias to get_ppi
- fix GSEA wrappers to restore eps, forward extra arguments such as
sampleSize to enrichit::gsea_gson(), and align the GSEA method
documentation with the current enrichit interface (2026-06-22, Mon,
#822)
- re-export bayes_enrich() and bayes_summary() from enrichit
(>= 0.1.5) for Bayesian term selection and posterior-ranked
summaries of ORA enrichment results (2026-06-16, Tue)

                        Changes in version 1.1.1                        

- NEW: Added additional diagnostic plots (mostly used to generate
supplementary figures in the damidBind manuscript):
plot_catada_mean_variance() and test_weighting_vs_bias_artifact()
- NEW: load_data_peaks() and load_data_genes() now support multiple
normalisation options: quantile normalisation ("quantile"), cyclic
LOESS norm ("loess"), and RPM (reads per million) norm ("rpm". The
default is "none" (no normalisation).
- NEW: a pre_scale option has been added to both load_data_peaks()
and
load_data_genes(), which will perform zero-preserving (uncentred)
scaling (via base R scale(center=FALSE, scale=TRUE)) prior to
normalisation. The default is FALSE.
- NEW: all input metadata and genome annotation metadata are saved in
the DamIDResults S4 object. Basic metadata are displayed with the
default show() method, and all are accessible via the metadata()
accessor.
- NEW: plot_volcano() now takes a new labels option, values of "all",
"highlight", or a character vector containing one or more group
names from the highlight list. Only this group will be labelled on
the plot. The original label configuration options still remain.
- NEW: plot_volcano() supports highlight groups of either loci or
gene
names, including different categories in the same plot. The default
"auto" behaviour matches a highlight group against whichever
definition has the most matches, but use the new highlight_by option
to enforce matching by either "gene_name" or "id" (i.e. locus).
- CHANGED: deprecated the quantile_norm option for load_data_peaks()
and load_data_genes().
- Added a citation to the current bioRxiv preprint on damidBind

[dar](/packages/dar)
---

                        Changes in version 2.0.0                        

Changes since dar 1.8.0.

Breaking changes

- R 4.6 or later is required. Differential-abundance recipes
configure
their targets and taxonomic rank with add_model(). The old selectors
and recipe slots are removed. Rebuild saved recipes from their
inputs.
- Use step_aldex2() for ALDEx2 and recipe_qc() for quality control.
step_aldex(), phy_qc() and step_metagenomeseq() are removed. ALDEx2
effects now use the fitted GLM coefficient.
- Recipes use a versioned JSON exchange format. Importing bakes into
an unprepared recipe requires prepare = TRUE.
- otu_table() returns counts with taxa in rows. Sample and taxonomy
accessors return the full tables. ComplexHeatmap, gplots, heatmaply
and UpSetR are optional.

Models and results

- Shared models support covariate adjustment, longitudinal contrasts
and compatible mixed designs. Added LinDA, ALDEx3 and radEmu, with
per-stage engine_args for advanced options.
- tidy_results(), tidy_abundance(), get_execution() and effect_plt()
expose per-method results, aggregated abundances, execution details
and effect estimates.
- Abundance plots support shared or union discoveries and explicit
taxa. Automatic selection requires a contrast when ambiguous.
Consensus outputs retain the contrast and direction of each
discovery.

Fixes and maintenance

- Random-intercept models accept singleton participants alongside
participants with repeated observations. Checks use observed groups
and still reject designs with one group or no repeated observations
(#189).
- Recipes validate steps before execution, run preprocessing in
declared order, reserve result column names and assign unique
automatic IDs (#187).
- DESeq2 uses native poscounts normalization and applies the
significance threshold and result options before shrinkage (#188).
- Corrected contrast handling in MaAsLin3 and LEfSe, robust inference
in ANCOM-BC2 and corncob, and depth-dependent zero handling in
LinDA.
- Five vignettes document the current workflow. Docker Hub
publication
runs separately from GitHub package checks (#190).
