[enrichplot](/packages/enrichplot)
----------

                       Changes in version 1.99.8                        

- emapplot() / ssplot() no longer require the suggested ggforce
package, and the grouping controls are consolidated on node_label:
- when ggforce is not installed the group outline falls back to
ggplot2::stat_ellipse(). Grouping is on by default in ssplot(),
so the previous unconditional check_installed("ggforce") made
the default call abort on a machine without a merely suggested
package.
- node_label = "category_grouped" replaces group = TRUE (outline
the groups, label the categories); group = FALSE is node_label =
"none". group still works but now warns as deprecated.
- an unknown node_label is an error instead of silently drawing
nothing, and a non-default top_k / target_density that the
selected edge_filter does not use warns instead of being dropped
silently.
- group labels are now always added by emapplot() itself, so "all"
labels the groups exactly as "group" does, and the node_label
values together with their outlines and labels are tabulated in
?emapplot and ?ssplot. (2026-10-09, Fri)
- Align import_fgsea() test suite with the enrichit GSEA leading-edge
contract written for YuLab-SMU/DOSE#46:
- The rank-vector assertions in tests/testthat/test-converters.R
now check, in order: expect_type(result$rank, "integer"),
expect_false(anyNA(result$rank)), expect_true(all(rank >= 0L)).
- The final check carries an in-line comment documenting the
canonical rank == 0L no-signal sentinel — "no usable weighted
in-set signal for this pathway" (N_R == 0, empty gene-set
overlap, or a non-finite running score; matches enrichit >= 0.2.5.9008).
- Together the three assertions guard against silent type drift
(numeric 0 or NA_real_ leaking in for the documented integer
sentinel) and against accidental re-introduction of an
NA_integer_ sentinel that would collapse all(c(NA, 4) >= 0L) to
NA instead of a clean boolean. (2026-10-05, Mon, aligns with
YuLab-SMU/enrichit >= 0.2.6)

                       Changes in version 1.99.7                        

- add opt-in threshold, top_k and adaptive edge filters to emapplot()
and ssplot(); top_k keeps strongest per-term neighbors, while
adaptive targets a configurable graph density without changing the
similarity matrix or dimension-reduction input (2026-09-27, Sun)
- expose min_edge and size_edge directly in ssplot(), document
classical MDS as one available reduction choice, and add an optional
enrichplot_edge_diagnostic attribute plus emapplot_edge_density()
helper for retained-pair density diagnostics (2026-09-27, Sun)
- harden similarity-space selection for term IDs, preserve labels
through one- and two-term reductions, and validate edge/coordinate
controls before plotting (2026-09-27, Sun)

                       Changes in version 1.99.6                        

- fix hplot() visual semantics by replacing the inaccurate ribbon/rug
approximation with a pure ggplot2 horizon-band implementation: four
BluGrn score bands, minimum-origin scaling, stacked facet geometry
and right-side term labels now match the historical
ggHoriPlot::geom_horizon(origin = "min", horizonscale = 4) output
without requiring ggHoriPlot (2026-09-24, Thu)

- fix cnetplot() S3 generic/method consistency under R CMD check: the
enrichResult, gseaResult and compareClusterResult methods now match
the current ggtangle::cnetplot() signature while retaining legacy
controls such as categorySize, circular, colorEdge, pie, split and
includeAll through ... (2026-09-24, Thu)

- fix treeplot(cluster_panel = "dotplot") with current ggtreeExtra:
the fruit layer now uses the geometry name and mappings expected by
ggtreeExtra, and the method works when ggplot2 is not attached
(2026-09-24, Thu)

- fix hplot() failures when ggplot2 is not attached: expansion() is
now called through the ggplot2 namespace (2026-09-24, Thu)

- make external-result importers citation-neutral: import_enrichr(),
import_gprofiler2(), import_webgestalt() and import_fgsea() now
display imported-result summaries without claiming a clusterProfiler
citation, and use supplied adjusted p-values or deterministic
p-adjusted fallbacks for small tables (2026-09-24, Thu)

- fix package checks for test fixtures by declaring the Matrix
package
used in mnsea mock results, and add regression coverage for the
repaired plotting paths (2026-09-24, Thu)

- treeplot(), emapplot() and ssplot() now explain a missing
term-similarity matrix instead of failing with no 'dimnames'
attribute for array: when pairwise_termsim() has not been run, the
error now says so and shows the call to make. The existing
has_pairsim() guard had been left unwired, so the cryptic crash was
what users actually saw (2026-09-22, Tue)

- cnetplot() now warns when none of the names in foldChange match the
genes of the result (#177): the item nodes are drawn grey in that
case, which is easily misread as "foldChange was ignored", so the
mismatch is reported along with the expected ID style (2026-09-22,
Tue)

- fix cnetplot() categorySizeBy formulas for compareClusterResult:
the
legacy-argument shim forces the argument before it is captured,
which left the quosure's environment empty, so every formula failed
at draw time with could not find function "-"; the expression is now
evaluated in the formula's own environment, so categorySizeBy =
~-log10(p.adjust) works again (2026-09-22, Tue)

- fix cnetplot() legacy circular, edge-color, and category-size
arguments (#330): the wrapper now translates circular = TRUE to the
current circular layout, colorEdge = TRUE to category-colored edges,
and legacy categorySize strings to the current categorySizeBy
semantics, so older fold-change cnetplot calls build again without
leaking stale arguments into the layout backend (2026-09-22, Tue)

- fix dotplot() p-value color legend labels for very small values
(#277): p-value / p-adjusted / q-value breaks below 1e-3 are now
shown in readable scientific notation instead of long unreadable
decimals (2026-09-22, Tue)

- document dotplot() size behavior for gseaResult (#206): when x is
"GeneRatio" the point size defaults to "count" (number of genes);
size = "GeneRatio" scales it by the enrichment gene ratio instead
(2026-09-22, Tue)

- fix ridgeplot() for mnseaResult with small per-feature
contributions: the undersized-gene-set guard (intended for
gseaResult density estimation) no longer drops mnsea mechanism
groups that only carry a few feature scores, so layered mnsea
ridgeplots render again instead of aborting (2026-09-22, Tue)

- gseaplot2(): pvalue_table now defaults to NES and p.adjust columns
instead of two redundant p-value columns; columns remain fully
configurable via pvalue_table_columns and row names can be
suppressed with pvalue_table_rownames = NULL (2026-09-22, Tue)

- cnetplot() supports node_label_size (#41): control the font size of
the category/item node labels; defaults to the built-in size when
NULL (backed by the same parameter in ggtangle)

- guard cnetplot() compare-cluster pies across showCategory sizes
(#284): add a regression test that exercises pie = "count" while
increasing showCategory, ensuring term nodes expand consistently and
both plots still build cleanly (2026-09-22, Tue)

- guard treeplot() against tidytree helper renames (#249, #247): add
a
regression test that explicitly exercises the current tidytree
namespace shape (private .offspring.tbl_tree_item without exported
offspring.tbl_tree_item) while ensuring treeplot() still builds
cleanly (2026-09-22, Tue)

                       Changes in version 1.99.5                        

- guard dotplot() compare-cluster labels against geneRatio
regressions
(#180): add a regression test that keeps by = "geneRatio" and by =
"count" from reintroducing NA cluster labels in compare-cluster
dotplots (2026-09-22, Tue)
- fix treeplot() split-aware faceting for GSEA results (#169): split
is now carried into tree, tip, and clade metadata so treeplot(...,
split = ".sign") + facet_grid(. ~ .sign) builds instead of dropping
the faceting variable from every layer (2026-09-22, Tue)
- fix treeplot() cluster color assignment when nCluster reaches two
digits (#171): cluster palettes and clade-label groups now follow
numeric cluster ids instead of lexical ordering, so groups like
cluster_10 no longer steal cluster_2 colors when the cluster count
increases (2026-09-22, Tue)
- fix emapplot() compare-cluster pie nodes across ontologies (#228):
ontology-specific terms that share the same Description now keep
stable ID-backed labels all the way into pie-layer data alignment,
so compareCluster(..., ont = "ALL") no longer collapses those nodes
or breaks while building the pie overlay (2026-09-22, Tue)

                       Changes in version 1.99.4                        

- fix goplot() DAG construction for top-level GO terms: parent edges
that point to the synthetic all root are now dropped before the
graph is built, so plots that include terms such as GO:0008150 no
longer fail with Some vertex names in \d` are not listed in
`vertices`` (2026-09-22, Tue)
- fix heatplot() dot-mode p-value scaling: zero or non-positive gene
p-values are now clamped to the smallest positive double before the
reversed log-size transform is applied, so significance-sized dots
no longer emit infinite-value warnings for exact-zero inputs
(2026-09-22, Tue)
- fix ridgeplot() blank rows for undersized core gene sets (#288):
pathways with fewer than three ranked values are now dropped before
geom_density_ridges() is built, and the function now errors clearly
when no selected pathway has enough values to estimate a density, so
two-gene core sets no longer leave empty y-axis slots in the plot
(2026-09-21, Mon)

                       Changes in version 1.99.3                        

- fix cnetplot() for compareClusterResult terms with duplicated
descriptions (#279): category nodes now use stable ID-backed labels
internally, so distinct terms that share the same Description are no
longer merged into one network node, with regression coverage for
the duplicated-label case (2026-09-21, Mon)
- fix treeplot() heatmap panels for compareClusterResult: the
cluster_panel = "heatMap" path now calls ggtree::gheatmap() with the
active tree plot object instead of treating it like a regular layer,
so compare-cluster treeplots render again instead of failing with a
missing data argument error (2026-09-21, Mon)
- fix treeplot() dotplot panels for compareClusterResult (#232,
#224):
the cluster_panel = "dotplot" path now passes
ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit() the plain term columns it expects, so
compare-cluster treeplots render again on current ggtreeExtra builds
instead of failing while decoding the y mapping (2026-09-21, Mon)

                       Changes in version 1.99.2                        

- support importing results from external enrichment tools:
import_enrichr(), import_gprofiler2(), import_webgestalt() and
import_fgsea() map enrichr / g:Profiler / WebGestaltR / fgsea output
tables to enrichResult / gseaResult objects that plug into the
'enrichplot' visualization functions; the 'enrichit' constructors
as_enrichResult() / as_gseaResult() are re-exported for other table
formats (2026-09-21, Mon)
- fix dotplot() legend keys under plot composition (#273): size
legends now keep the hollow point shape after cowplot::plot_grid() /
similar grob composition, instead of reverting to solid circles in
combined figures (2026-09-21, Mon)
- fix dotplot() size scaling for enrichment results (#118): size =
"Percentage" now derives a percentage column from GeneRatio for
enrichResult / gseaResult data instead of failing at draw time with
a missing-column error (2026-09-21, Mon)
- fix barplot() width handling (#201): width = ... is now forwarded
to
the internal geom_col() layer for both enrichment-result and
compare-cluster barplots, so bar thickness can be adjusted directly
without stacking a second geom_col() layer on top of the original
bars (2026-09-21, Mon)
- fix dotplot() selection ordering for numeric showCategory (#345,
#219): the function now orders the fortified data by orderBy first
and only then takes the requested top rows, so the leading
categories stay stable when showCategory changes and orderBy is
honored correctly (2026-09-21, Mon)

                       Changes in version 1.99.1                        

- fix upsetplot() for readable gseaResult objects (#179): the
fold-change vector is now remapped through fc_readable(), so
setReadable() results no longer lose all ranked-score values when
pathway genes are shown as symbols (2026-09-21, Mon)
- improve gseaplot() / gseaplot2() multi-panel compatibility with
cowplot (#239): the gglist-level cowplot::as_grob() bridge is now
implemented in aplot, so plot_grid() / ggarrange() work when paired
with an aplot version that provides that helper, without making it a
hard requirement for enrichplot itself (2026-09-21, Mon)
- fix upsetplot() boxplot overlays for gseaResult and mnseaResult
(#178): the boxplot layer now suppresses its own outlier glyphs so
jittered feature points are drawn only once instead of being
duplicated on top of boxplot outliers (2026-09-21, Mon)
- fix pairwise_termsim() for enrichResult objects whose raw result
table has terms but the object cutoffs filter them all out of
as.data.frame() (#269): term selection now uses the raw result rows,
so showCategory can still pick the requested top terms and
downstream plots such as emapplot() continue to work for
non-significant result tables (2026-09-21, Mon)
- fix grouped emapplot() / ssplot() legend control (#292): the
compatibility arguments group and group_legend are accepted again,
and grouped layouts no longer force the "groups" legend on when
group_legend = FALSE is requested (2026-09-21, Mon)
- fix gseaplot2() hit-bin rectangles for single gene sets (#221,
#20):
the colored bins under the hit ticks now follow the ranked-list
direction instead of mirroring the cumulative hit counts, so highly
one-sided enrichments no longer collapse the wide interval onto the
wrong end of the plot (2026-09-21, Mon)
- fix cnetplot() / emapplot() for compareClusterResult pie nodes when
duplicated (Cluster, Description) rows are present (#314): pie
counts are now aggregated before widening, avoiding list-columns and
the tidyr cast error ("Can't convert fill to "), with regression
coverage for duplicated cluster-term inputs (2026-09-21, Mon)
- fix barplot() for compareClusterResult objects: the default by =
"geneRatio" and by = "rowPercentage" crashed in
plotting.clusterProfile(), and by = "count" failed at rendering time
under ggplot2 4.x; by is now mapped to the fortify-produced column
and bars are drawn with geom_col() (2026-09-21, Mon)
- fix emapplot() / ssplot() with similarity measures other than 'JC'
(e.g., 'Wang') (#309): label-keyed similarity matrices were
re-mapped as term IDs, producing NA edges ("edge data frame contains
NAs"); the stale re-mapping in build_emap_graph() was removed
(2026-09-21, Mon)
- add a plotting regression suite (test-plotting-regression.R)
covering the tutorial-facing visualization functions, including a
dispatch canary for the ggplot() + theme_dose() failure seen under
ggplot2 4.0.x with S7 < 0.2.2; ggplot outputs are evaluated with
ggplot_build() to catch bad aesthetics (2026-09-21, Mon)

                       Changes in version 1.33.1                        

- complete remaining mechanism-plot enhancements: pairwise_termsim()
now supports layer-aware similarity for mnseaResult, classification
thresholds are exposed through phaseplot() / consensusmap() /
mechanismflow(), and an explicit nseaResult mock plus coverage has
been added for nsea plotting paths; gsInfo.gseaResult() also
defaults exponent to 1 when params lacks it (2026-08-29, Sun)
- refactor gsInfo() into an S3 generic and add layer-aware
running-score support to gseaplot2(), gsearank() and hplot() for
nseaResult / mnseaResult; hplot() is now implemented with base
ggplot2 geoms and no longer requires ggHoriPlot (2026-08-23, Sun)
- add pairwise_termsim() support for mnseaResult so treeplot(),
emapplot() and ssplot() share one layer-aware similarity definition,
with single-pathway treeplot boundary handling
- add barplot.gseaResult() so nseaResult / mnseaResult no longer fall
through to graphics::barplot.default
- add mechanism-oriented helper layer (compute_rewiring_score(),
classify_mechanism_state(), summarize_nsea_mechanism(),
extract_rewiring_features()) with deterministic tests
- add phaseplot() for enrichment-shift versus rewiring overviews and
rewireplot() for pathway-specific feature-level rewiring evidence
- add consensusmap() for multi-context mechanism agreement and
mechanismflow() for pathway state transitions across
layers/conditions
- refine mechanism plots with real cross-object comparisons:
summarize_nsea_mechanism() now accepts a reference result to compute
delta_NES and cross-object rewiring_score; phaseplot() supports
reference / x_axis / size_var; consensusmap() uses fill for
NES/delta NES and point size for rewiring/overlap; mechanismflow()
uses flow magnitude and stable mechanism-state ordering (2026-08-23,
Sun)
- add a minimal ssplot.mnseaResult() that projects selected pathways
into a similarity-space overview using layer-aware feature overlap,
while reusing emapplot() semantics and adding stable fallbacks for
one- or two-pathway layouts (2026-06-25, Thu)
- add a minimal upsetplot.mnseaResult() that summarizes shared
feature
overlaps across selected pathways with collapsed-score or
single-layer views, including support for score magnitude display
and core_enrichment filtering (2026-06-25, Thu)
- add a minimal ridgeplot.mnseaResult() that shows pathway-level
feature score distributions from collapsed scores or a selected
single layer, with regression coverage for layer-aware ranked scores
and core_enrichment filtering (2026-06-25, Thu)
- add a minimal gseaplot.mnseaResult() that supports collapsed-score
and single-layer running-score views for one pathway at a time, with
regression coverage for stable pathway selection and layer-aware
ranked scores (2026-06-25, Thu)
- batch-refine mnsea plot semantics by aligning layer filtering and
readable legend labels across dotplot(), heatplot(), cnetplot() and
emapplot(), while fixing emapplot.mnseaResult() to retain all
selected pathways when rebuilding overlap graphs after layer
filtering, with expanded regression coverage (2026-06-25, Thu)
- add a minimal emapplot.mnseaResult() that reuses cached term
similarity when available and otherwise falls back to internal JC

(2026-06-24, Wed)
- batch-refine cnetplot.mnseaResult() readability by splitting
pathway
and feature label layers, preferring shared features when labels are

- refine default label selection in cnetplot.mnseaResult() to keep

- clarify cnetplot.mnseaResult() legend titles for edge type, node
type, layer, feature sign, and feature magnitude, with regression

- distinguish pathway and feature nodes in cnetplot.mnseaResult()
with
explicit node-type shapes and regression coverage for the updated

- refine cnetplot.mnseaResult() with edge-type legends, effective
size_edge scaling, and feature-node sign encoding backed by

- align default pathway_id resolution across mnsea helpers and
feature-level heatplot(), and add share / exclusive label support to

- add cnetplot.mnseaResult() for pathway-specific multilayer
subnetworks, including pathway anchor nodes and lightweight

- add heatplot.mnseaResult() for term-layer and pathway-specific

- refactor shared plot data preparation for cnetplot(), emapplot(),

[ensembldb](/packages/ensembldb)
---------

                       Changes in version 2.37.3                        

- Fix security issues reported by the Bioconductor Security Audit:

- `.valueForEnsDb()`: replace single quotes to avoid SQL injection.

- `ensDbQuery()` for `SeqNameFilter`: remove all single quotes from
  sequence
  names to avoid SQL injection; chromosome names are not expected to
  contain
  single quotes.

- `buildWhereForGRanges()`: remove all single quotes form sequence
  names to
  avoid SQL injection.

- `ensDbFromGtf()`: use a parameterized query for `gtfFilename` to
  avoid SQL
  injection.

- `.buildQuery()`: check parameter `order.type` for correct values to
  avoid
  potential SQL injection.

- `.getMetaDataValue()`: use a parameterized query to avoid potential
  SQL
  injection.

                       Changes in version 2.37.2                        

- Fix first security issues reported by the Bioconductor Security
  Audit:

- `fetchTablesFromEnsembl()`: fix potential command injection issue.

[epiSeeker](/packages/epiSeeker)
---------

                        Changes in version 1.1.5                        

- test-txdb.R no longer pins the tx_id -> gene mapping of
TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene. That mapping is annotation data
rebuilt for each Bioconductor release, and tx 70455 changed from
ENST00000479182.5/91653 to ENST00000798887.1/102724542 in BioC 3.24,
failing R CMD check on both Linux builders. Expected values are now
derived from the installed TxDb at test time. (2026-11-12, Thu)

                        Changes in version 1.1.4                        

- annotateSeq() keeps annotation, geneChr/geneStart/geneEnd, geneId
and transcriptId consistent with each other at transcript level
(issue #252 of ChIPseeker). The transcript id of an exon/intron/UTR
hit was taken from names(genomicRegion)[subjectIndex], indexing the
unlisted ranges with the names of the GRangesList; this mostly
returned NA and occasionally a wrong transcript, so a peak could be
reported with the metadata of an unrelated transcript (even on
another chromosome). The ids are now expanded before indexing, and
the same alignment is applied at level = "gene", where the gene of
the overlapping exon/intron/UTR is resolved with TXID2EG() and used
instead of the nearest gene. (2026-10-01, Thu)
- seq2gene() no longer fails with $ operator is invalid for atomic
vectors when none of the queried regions overlaps an exon
(getGenomicAnnotation.internal() returns NA then); host-gene
extraction is skipped and the nearest/flanking genes are still
reported (issue #248 of ChIPseeker). (2026-10-01, Thu)
- downloadGEObedFiles()/downloadGSMbedFiles() rewrite the ftp:// urls
of gsminfo$supplementary_file to https:// before downloading and
report the underlying download error when a file cannot be fetched
(issue #254 of ChIPseeker). (2026-10-01, Thu)
- Documented the distance definition of flank_gene_distances reported
by annotateSeq(..., addFlankGeneInfo = TRUE): a distance of 0 means
that the peak overlaps the feature range - at level = "transcript"
the feature is the whole transcript, which is why most entries can
be 0 - while non-overlapping peaks get the signed distance to the
feature TSS (issue #235 of ChIPseeker). (2026-10-01, Thu)
- annotateSeq() no longer fails with Error: invalid subscript when
every peak is dropped, which typically happens because none of the
seqlevels of the peaks matches TxDb (chr1 vs NC_000001.11):
.get_distance_to_gene_end() no longer hands the SortedByQueryHits
object returned by follow() for an empty query to features[], and
annotateSeq() reports the seqlevels mismatch together with how to
align the chromosome names (seqlevelsStyle()). (2026-10-01, Thu)
- enrichPeakOverlap()/enrichAnnoOverlap() accept a single GRanges as
targetPeak: it was passed on unwrapped while the overlap code works
on a list of target peak sets, so the call failed with "GRanges
objects don't support [[, as.list(), lapply()". The documentation of
enrichPeakOverlap() and enrichAnnoOverlap() now also states the
direction of the test (the observed ratio is the fraction of target
peaks covered by the query peaks and the target is the shuffled set,
so N_OL is direction free while the p-value is not) and that N_OL of
enrichAnnoOverlap() counts genes and can therefore exceed the number
of input peaks (issue #84 of ChIPseeker). (2026-10-01, Thu)
- An empty input is now handled: annotateSeq(GRanges(), ...) returns
an empty csAnno instead of failing with "Error: invalid subscript".
The root cause (follow()/precede() returning a SortedByQueryHits
object instead of indices for an empty query) is guarded in
getNearestFeatureIndicesAndDistances(), which also makes seq2gene()
return character(0) for an empty input. (2026-10-01, Thu)
- enrichPeakOverlap() gained an opt-in symmetric argument. With
symmetric = TRUE the mirrored direction (query and target exchanged)
is computed as well and the two one-sided permutation p-values are
combined as min(1, 2*min(p, p_rev)) (Hedges), so the result no
longer depends on the order of the arguments. The default stays
FALSE (one-sided) and all existing numbers are unchanged; the
mirrored test doubles the number of permutations and raises the
smallest reportable p-value to 2/(nShuffle+1). enrichAnnoOverlap()
needs no such argument, its hypergeometric p-value is already
exactly symmetric (issue #84 of ChIPseeker). (2026-10-01, Thu)
- upsetplot(vennpie = TRUE) can be drawn again with ggplot2 >= 4.0.
The vennpie sub-view is embedded as an annotation_custom() layer,
which ggplot2 only supports below coord_cartesian(). The sub-view no
longer uses coord_fixed() and the parent plot is converted with
ggplotify as well, because the ggupset coordinate system
(CoordCombMatrix) rejects such layers. No replacement for the
removed coord_fixed() is added: ggplotify rasterises the grob with
the aspect ratio of the device, and forcing a square panel distorted
the venn diagram further (measured anisotropy 1.43 without
versus 1.50 with theme(aspect.ratio = 1), against 1.41 for the
undistorted drawing). Before, the plot failed with
`annotation_custom()` only works with `coord_cartesian()`. Note that
ggupset 0.4.1 itself still maps the deprecated size aesthetic, so
drawing the plot may print "Please use linewidth instead"; the
warning comes from ggupset
(https://github.com/const-ae/ggupset/issues) and can be ignored.
(2026-10-01, Thu)

                        Changes in version 1.1.3                        

- annotateSeq() now reports geneChr and geneStrand as characters
instead of factor codes. as.data.frame() returns 'seqnames'/'strand'
as factors and assigning a factor into mcols() dropped the class, so
both columns came out as integers (e.g. geneStrand = 1/2 instead of
+/-, and a wrong geneChr whenever the seqlevels were not in numeric
order). (2026-09-15, Tue)
- annotateSeq() now warns when peaks are dropped because no feature
of
TxDb can be found for them (e.g. peaks on contigs/scaffolds without
genes, or a seqlevels style mismatch). Previously they disappeared
silently. (2026-09-15, Tue)
- annotateSeq(..., sameStrand = TRUE) no longer assigns a peak to a
feature on the opposite strand. Overlap detection in
getNearestFeatureIndicesAndDistances() was calling findOverlaps()
with unstrand(features), which bypassed sameStrand and overrode the
strand-aware nearest-feature result. Peaks with ambiguous strand (*)
are unaffected and still match features on any strand. (2026-09-15,
Tue)
- plotAnnoBar() no longer uses the deprecated ggplot2::aes_string().
It follows the tidy evaluation idiom already used by
plotDistToTSS(). (2026-09-15, Tue)
- dropped unused @importFrom directives with no call site
(aplot::xlim2, ggplot2::geom_segment, ggplot2::geom_text,
ggplot2::scale_fill_hue, utils::getFromNamespace) and a duplicate
ggplot2::scale_fill_brewer. The grid::unit() import, previously
declared in upsetplot() which never used it, now sits in
plotBmProf() where unit() is actually called, keeping grid a genuine
import. (2026-09-17, Thu)

                        Changes in version 1.1.2                        

- documentation build migrated to roxygen2 8.1.0 (re-generated Rd
pages and NAMESPACE; fixed csAnno class @aliases to be a single
line); the exported API is unchanged
- fixed bug in getNearestFeatureIndicesAndDistances() where results
for overlap=="all" were silently overridden by the overlap=="TSS"
branch, causing the two modes to behave identically (2026-09-07,
Mon)

                        Changes in version 1.1.1                        

- make csAnno subset robust to GRanges metadata columns (2027-07-07,
Tue)

[escape](/packages/escape)
------

                        Changes in version 2.9.1                        

NEW FEATURES

- plaid backend: escape.matrix() and runEscape() gain backend =
c("native", "plaid"). Setting backend = "plaid" routes ssGSEA, GSVA,
UCell, and AUCell to the replaid.* family for large speed and memory
gains. plaid is a Suggests, so the native path is unaffected if it
is not installed. These are approximations, and the gap is wider
than the plaid documentation suggests — measured pooled Pearson
agreement with the native scores was roughly 0.85 (ssGSEA), 0.83
(UCell, AUCell) and 0.73 (GSVA) on a 2000-gene simulation, and lower
on narrower matrices. See ?escape.matrix and the vignette before
substituting one backend for the other.
- Three new methods: method = "PLAID", "singscore", and "scSE". These
have no native implementation and select the plaid backend
automatically.
- backend.args: a named list carrying method-specific tuning (alpha,
tau, rowtf, aucMaxRank, rmax, nsmooth, stats, chunk, removeLog2,
scoreMean). Names are validated against the target function, so
typos error instead of being silently swallowed. Note
backend.args$normalize is plaid's median normalization of the scores
and is unrelated to escape's normalize.
- input.assay: choose which expression matrix to score. "auto"
(default) keeps raw counts for the native backend and picks
log-normalized values for plaid. "counts" and "logcounts" map to the
correct layer for both Seurat and SummarizedExperiment-derived
objects.
- SpatialExperiment support is now explicit and tested, including
spatialCoords(), imgData(), and sample_id preservation through
runEscape().
- Enrichment scores carry an escape.backend attribute recording the
engine, method, and plaid version; runEscape() stores the same
record in metadata() (SCE) or Misc() (Seurat).

BUG FIXES

- escape.matrix(normalize = TRUE) failed on every
SummarizedExperiment-derived input with unable to find an inherited
method for function 'assay' for signature 'x = "NULL"'.
.pull.Enrich() used altExp(sc)[[name]], which indexes the colData of
the first altExp rather than selecting the named one, and returned
NULL. Now uses altExp(sc, name). This also fixes
performNormalization() and performPCA() on SingleCellExperiment and
SpatialExperiment objects. Reported by Cathal King, who also
provided the Xenium test data.
- Underscored gene-set names were silently dropped during
normalization. performNormalization() rewrote every _ to - to match
Seurat's feature-name coercion, which meant HALLMARK_*, GO_*, and
REACTOME_* sets matched nothing for matrix, SingleCellExperiment, or
SpatialExperiment input. Matching is now literal first with the
Seurat-mangled form as a fallback, and per-set scale factors are
aligned to the enrichment columns explicitly so a partial match can
never divide the wrong column.
- Requesting an assay that does not exist now reports what was asked
for and what is available, instead of failing with an S4 dispatch
error.
- performNormalization() gives a supplied enrichment.data precedence
over scores stored on the object, and warns when both are present.
- %||% was used but never defined; it only exists in base R >= 4.4
while the package declares R >= 4.1.
- runEscape() now calls escape.matrix() with named rather than
positional arguments.

ENHANCEMENTS

- Removed duplicate internal definitions of .split_cols(),
.match_summary_fun(), and .filter_genes().
- escape.matrix() validates method up front rather than failing
inside
the scoring switch.
- Test suite: added a toy SpatialExperiment fixture built at run time
(no new package data), regression coverage for all three bug fixes,
and plaid dispatch tests that run whether or not plaid is installed.

links to the website and the workflow article, and shows
Bioconductor build, years, downloads and pkgdown badges next to
R-CMD-check. No change to the package

                Changes in version 1.23.49 (2026-11-09)                 

- The workflow article on the website now uses the 10x 5k PBMC
CITE-seq data set (RNA and 32 antibodies) instead of PBMC 4k, and
keeps Cell Ranger's raw matrix whole: all 6,794,880 barcodes, with
the antibodies in altExp("ADT"). Next to the RNA workflow, the same
object now holds an antibody workflow: decontPro and CLR on the
high-quality cells, stored in the subset's ADT while its counts stay
linked to the main object; the RNA cell-type labels checked against
CD3, CD4 and CD8a protein; and decontPro and CLR again on the T
cells alone, stored with unlink = c("ADT/decontPro", "ADT/clr"). RNA
decontamination now uses the decontX package rather than celda, and
the article keeps cells with up to 15% mitochondrial counts rather
than 10%, since this data set has more. No change to the package
(#93)

                Changes in version 1.23.48 (2026-11-08)                 

- The package code, tests and vignette now pass make lint with no
findings: spacing, braces, quotes, assignment, indentation and line
length follow the package's lint settings, which now also accept the
names of the exported constructors, the class generators and the
use.names and deparse.level arguments that methods take from their
generics. subsetSummary() loops with seq_along() and createSubset()
drops an internal variable that always equalled parentAssay. No
change in behavior (#37)

                Changes in version 1.23.47 (2026-11-08)                 

- New subsetRowTree(x, subsetName) and subsetColTree(x, subsetName)
return the row or column tree of a TreeSummarizedExperiment subset:
its own, if it stores one; otherwise that of the nearest subset it
was made from that stores one; otherwise the main object's.
whichTree picks one of several trees, as in rowTree(). New
subsetRowTree(x, subsetName) <- value and subsetColTree<- store a
phylo tree as the subset's own, linking each row or column to the
node labelled with its name in the subset, without changing the main
object or other subsets; NULL removes it. Every row or column name
of the subset must be a node label of the tree, or it's an error
such as "Every rowname of subset 's1' must be a node label of
'value'. Not found: t3."; TreeSummarizedExperiment's rowTree<- would
instead drop those rows. Subsets made from a subset with its own
tree use that tree, cut to their rows or columns, and
getSubsetExperiment() returns it with its links.
setSubsetExperiment() now stores a row or column tree that a tool
changed in the object from getSubsetExperiment() as the subset's
own, with the message "Subset 's1' now stores its own rowTree.";
before, a changed tree was dropped without a message. Unchanged
trees aren't stored, so the subset still follows the main object's.
A subset can store only one tree per dimension, with a node label
for each row or column, so an object with two row trees, or with a
label on more than one node of those its rows use, is an error; a
removed tree isn't stored, with the message "Subset 's1' keeps its
rowTree; a subset always uses its own tree, a parent's or the main
object's." rbind() and cbind() keep subsets' own trees. Rows and
columns are linked by node label, so each must label only one node
of the tree, or it's an error. This is a change: subsetRowLinks()
and subsetColLinks() now default to parentRowLinkData = TRUE and
parentColLinkData = TRUE, and return the links to the tree that
subsetRowTree() or subsetColTree() returns. Before, they defaulted
to FALSE and returned NULL, because subsets never had trees of their
own; code that relied on NULL needs parentRowLinkData = FALSE, which
now returns only links to a tree stored by the subset or one it was
made from. Both arguments must now be TRUE or FALSE; before, NULL,
NA or another value meant FALSE. (#35)

                Changes in version 1.23.46 (2026-11-08)                 

- New subsetImgData(x, subsetName) returns the images of a
SpatialExperiment subset: the rows of the main object's imgData()
for the samples of the subset's spots, looked up on each read.
Before, a subset's images had to be filtered from the main object's
by sample_id by hand. New subsetSpatialCoords(x, subsetName) <-
value stores a subset's own spatial coordinates, such as after a
transformation, without changing the main object's; value is a
numeric matrix with one row per spot and one or more columns, and
NULL removes them. A subset with its own coordinates returns them
from subsetSpatialCoords(), spatialCoords(x, subsetName =) and
getSubsetExperiment(), and subsets made from it see them, cut to
their spots. setSubsetExperiment() now stores coordinates that a
tool changed in the object from getSubsetExperiment() as the
subset's own, with the message "Subset 's1' now stores its own
spatialCoords."; unchanged coordinates aren't stored, so the subset
still follows the main object's. Subsets without their own
coordinates are unchanged (#72)

                Changes in version 1.23.45 (2026-11-08)                 

- assay(x, "s1", subsetAssayName = "x") <- value now prints "Storing
assay inside subset 's1'." only after the assay is stored. Before,
it printed the message first, so when value was rejected, for
example because its column names were in another order or because
subsetAssayName named an assay linked from the parent and unlink
wasn't set, the message announced a store that didn't happen,
followed by the error. Successful calls print the same message as
before, now after any message about unlinking (#107)
- setSubsetAssay() with a subsetName that isn't a subset now gives
the
error "nope subset does not exist. 'subsetName' must be the name of
a subset.", the one most other functions already give, instead of
"nope does not exist in the subsets slot of the object. You need to
create a new subset with createSubset() function." subsetParent()
with a subsetName that is neither a subset nor a "subset/assay" now
gives "nope subset does not exist. 'subsetName' must be the name of
a subset or a "subset/assay".", instead of "nope does not exist in
the subsets slot of the object." createSubset(), and
ExperimentSubset() with subset =, with a parentAssay that doesn't
exist now give "'parentAssay' must be NULL or name an assay, a
subset or a "subset/assay"; 'typo' is none of these.", instead of
"Input parentAssay does not exist." Code that matched the old text
needs the new one (#107)

                Changes in version 1.23.44 (2026-11-08)                 

- The tests use testthat edition 3, so testthat (>= 3.0.0) is now in
Suggests. Five tests that unlink an assay, whose message edition 3
no longer hides, now check it, such as "Subset 's1' now stores its
own 'counts', unlinked from the main assay 'counts'." No change in
behavior (#96)

                Changes in version 1.23.43 (2026-11-07)                 

- Errors from createSubset(), and from ExperimentSubset() with subset
=, are now one line, without the line breaks and runs of spaces they
had before, and name the argument and the problem: a subsetName that
is already a subset now gives "'subsetName' must differ from the
names of existing subsets; 's1' is already a subset name." instead
of "A subset with the specified 'subsetName' parameter already
exists in the object. Subset names must be unique."; a rows or cols
that isn't NULL, numeric or character gives "'rows' must be NULL, to
include all rows, or a numeric or character vector of the rows to
include." or "'cols' must be NULL, to include all columns, or a
numeric or character vector of the columns to include." (before, the
cols message said "all rows"); and a parentAssay that isn't NULL or
one character string gives "'parentAssay' must be NULL, to use the
default assay, or a single character string naming the assay or
subset to make the subset from." setSubsetAssay() with a subsetName
that isn't a subset keeps its message, now on one line without
trailing spaces (#96)

                Changes in version 1.23.42 (2026-11-07)                 

- altExpNames<- with a value that isn't a character vector, such as a
factor, NULL or a number, now gives the error "'value' must be a
character vector of altExp names.", with subsetName = and on the
main object. Before, both failed with "unable to find an inherited
method for function 'altExpNames<-'". Character values are unchanged
(#105)

                Changes in version 1.23.41 (2026-11-07)                 

- colData(x, subsetName =) <- with a value that isn't a DataFrame, a
data.frame or NULL, such as a vector, now gives the error "'value'
must be a DataFrame, a data.frame or NULL.", as subsetColData<- and
rowData<- with subsetName = already did. colData(x) <- on the main
object with such a value now gives "'value' must be a DataFrame or
NULL.", as it already did for a data.frame. Before, both failed with
"unable to find an inherited method for function 'colData<-'".
Values that worked before are unchanged (#99)

                Changes in version 1.23.40 (2026-11-06)                 

- subsetRowData<- and rowData(x, subsetName =) <- now stop when the
rownames of value are not NULL and not the subset's row names, in
the same order, with the error "The rownames of 'value' must be NULL
or the row names of subset 's1', in the same order.", as
subsetColData<- and colData<- already did for column names. Before,
those rownames were dropped without a message and the values were
stored against the subset's rows by position, so values meant for
other rows, or for the same rows in another order, went to the wrong
rows. This is a change: a table with other rownames, such as gene
IDs for a subset whose rows are named by symbol, is now an error;
put its rows in the subset's order and set rownames(value) <- NULL
first. A value with the wrong number of rows now gets the size error
from rowData<- or colData<- even when it has rownames; before,
subsetColData<- and colData<- with subsetName = said its rownames
were wrong instead. The main object's rowData<- is unchanged (#100)

                Changes in version 1.23.39 (2026-11-06)                 

- A subsetName that isn't a character string, such as NULL, NA or a
number, now gives the error "'subsetName' must be one subset name, a
single character string." in setSubsetAssay(), getSubsetAssay(),
getSubsetExperiment(), setSubsetExperiment(), subsetDim(),
subsetColData(), subsetRowData(), subsetColnames(), subsetRownames()
and their setters, subsetColLinks(), subsetRowLinks(),
subsetSpatialCoords() and subsetSpatialData(). A subsetAssayName in
setSubsetAssay() that isn't a character string, such as NULL, now
gives "'subsetAssayName' must be a single, non-empty character
string." Before, these failed with "unable to find an inherited
method", because the methods were chosen by the class of subsetName
and subsetAssayName; now they are chosen by the class of x only.
subsetColData<- and subsetRowData<- now take a data.frame, converted
to a DataFrame, and NULL, which removes the subset's own columns, as
colData<- and rowData<- with subsetName = already did; before, these
failed with the same error. Any other value in these and in
rowData<- with subsetName = gives "'value' must be a DataFrame, a
data.frame or NULL." This is a change for rowData(x, subsetName =)
<- with a vector, such as 1:10, which before stored it as a column
named value; wrap it in a DataFrame or data.frame with a column name
instead (#97)

                Changes in version 1.23.38 (2026-11-05)                 

- The older tests now check results instead of only running code:
subset assay values for SummarizedExperiment and
RangedSummarizedExperiment objects, what setSubsetAssay() stores,
the full subsetParent() list, the output of show() and
subsetSummary(), and the reducedDims and altExps read back with
subsetName =. They no longer read slots with @, and the
commented-out tests run again or are removed. New tests check
subsetParent() with an unknown subset name and ExperimentSubset() on
a named list of assays. No change in behavior (#31)

                Changes in version 1.23.37 (2026-11-05)                 

- A subset now sees the main object's alternative experiments
(altExps), and those stored on the subsets it was made from, cut to
its cells: altExp(), altExps() and altExpNames() with subsetName =,
subsetSummary() and getSubsetExperiment() include them. Before, a
subset saw only the altExps stored on it, so, for example, the ADT
counts of its cells weren't available. An altExp keeps all of its
features: a subset's rows pick features of the main object only.
These altExps are linked, as assays are: the subset sees their
current values, and altExp<-, altExps<- and setSubsetExperiment()
store only what differs from them. A new assay, such as decontPro
added to ADT, is stored as the subset's own while ADT's counts stays
linked; an assay with other values than the linked one needs unlink,
which names it as "altExpName/assayName", such as unlink =
"ADT/counts", with a message for each assay unlinked.
setSubsetExperiment() checks assays and altExp assays together, with
one error naming every one unlink doesn't allow. A changed linked
assay that the subset already stores, after an unlink, needs no
unlink again. A subset can't remove or rename a linked altExp:
altExpNames(x, subsetName =) <- takes a different name for each
altExp the subset sees and renames only its own, and an altExp
missing from altExps(x, subsetName =) <- stays visible. Changes to a
linked altExp carry along to the subsets below it: renaming it, with
altExpNames<- on the main object or on the subset that stores it,
renames what they store of it, and removing it, or storing it with
other rows or another class, drops what they added to it, with a
warning naming them; an altExp a subset stores whole is kept, and
keeps replacing the linked one even if that later has the same rows.
An unlink other than FALSE in altExp<- or altExps<- without
subsetName is an error. A subset that stored an altExp under the
name of one of the main object's, with the same class and features,
now also sees the main altExp's assays that it doesn't store (#58)

                Changes in version 1.23.36 (2026-11-04)                 

- unlink in setSubsetExperiment(), setSubsetAssay() and assay<- can
now name the assays to unlink, as well as being TRUE or FALSE. With
unlink = "decontXcounts", setSubsetExperiment() stores a changed
decontXcounts as the subset's own, but stops with an error, storing
nothing, if another linked assay such as counts was changed too.
Before, the only choice was unlink = TRUE, which also unlinked an
assay changed by mistake, without a message. Names of assays that
are not linked, or not changed, are ignored. Each assay that is
unlinked now gives a message such as "Subset 's1' now stores its own
'counts', unlinked from the main assay 'counts'.", whether unlink is
TRUE or a name. An unlink that is not TRUE, FALSE or a character
vector of assay names, such as NA, now gives the error "'unlink'
must be TRUE, FALSE or a character vector of assay names."; before,
it was taken as FALSE (#59)

                Changes in version 1.23.35 (2026-11-04)                 

- ExperimentSubset() on an object that is already an ExperimentSubset
now returns it as is, and subset = still creates a subset on it.
Before, it failed with "no method or default for coercing
'SubsetSingleCellExperiment' to 'SubsetSubsetSingleCellExperiment'",
so code that wraps an object without knowing whether it is already
wrapped had to check first. ExperimentSubset() on an object of a
subclass of a supported class, such as a class that contains
SingleCellExperiment, now converts it as the class it extends, with
a warning that the slots and methods the subclass adds are not kept;
before, it failed with the same kind of error. Any other x that
isn't a list, such as a matrix, now gives the error "'x' must be a
SummarizedExperiment, RangedSummarizedExperiment,
SingleCellExperiment, TreeSummarizedExperiment or SpatialExperiment
object, or a named list of assays", instead of "unable to find an
inherited method for function 'assayNames'". For an object of a
subclass of a Subset* class, createSubset(), cbind(), rbind(),
combineCols() and combineRows() now store each subset's data as the
class the object extends, such as SingleCellExperiment; before, they
stored it as the subclass itself (#89)

                Changes in version 1.23.34 (2026-11-04)                 

- New exported virtual class ExperimentSubset, which all five Subset*
classes extend, so is(x, "ExperimentSubset") tests whether x is an
ExperimentSubset object, whichever class it extends. Before, this
took a list of the five classes or a check for the subsets slot: a
SubsetSpatialExperiment, for example, is not a
SubsetSingleCellExperiment, though both extend SingleCellExperiment.
See ?"ExperimentSubset-class" (#5)

                Changes in version 1.23.33 (2026-11-03)                 

- assay() and assay<- with an i that isn't one name, such as several
names or NA_character_, now give the error "'i' must be one name of
an assay, a subset or a "subset/assay", a single character string."
Before, they failed with base R errors that didn't name the
argument, such as "the condition has length > 1" or "'length = 2' in
coercion to 'logical(1)'", or said that 'NA' is not the name of an
assay. getSubsetAssay() without subsetAssayName now gives the same
subsetName error as with it, instead of assay()'s errors. assay(x,
"subset", subsetAssayName = NA) now says that subsetAssayName must
be a single character string, as assay<- already did, instead of
that 'subset/NA' is not the name of an assay. A numeric i is
unchanged (#85)

                Changes in version 1.23.32 (2026-11-03)                 

- A subsetName that isn't one subset name, such as NULL, NA or
several
names, now gives the error "'subsetName' must be one subset name, a
single character string." in the methods that get or set a subset's
data with subsetName =: metadata(), altExp(), altExps(),
altExpNames(), reducedDim(), reducedDims(), reducedDimNames(),
rowData() and colData(), their setters, spatialCoords(),
spatialData() and subsetParent(). Several names or NA_character_
give the same error in subsetAssayNames(), subsetDim(),
subsetColnames(), subsetRownames() and their setters,
subsetColData(), subsetRowData(), subsetSpatialCoords(),
getSubsetExperiment(), setSubsetExperiment(), setSubsetAssay(), and
getSubsetAssay() with subsetAssayName =. Before, these failed with
base R errors that didn't name the argument, such as "argument is of
length zero" or "the condition has length > 1", or with "NA subset
does not exist" or "NA does not exist in the subsets slot".
subsetAssayNames(x, subsetName = NULL), the default, still lists
every subset, and reducedDimNames() on an object without subsets,
such as a plain SingleCellExperiment, still says first that it has
no subsets (#83)

                Changes in version 1.23.31 (2026-11-03)                 

- reducedDimNames() now takes only subsetName =, by name, besides x.
Before, any other argument was dropped without a message, so
reducedDimNames(x, "subset"), with the subset name by position,
returned the main object's names instead of the subset's. That call
now stops with an error saying to use subsetName =, and any other
argument, or subsetName given twice, is an error too. Calls with
subsetName =, or with no other arguments, are unchanged.
reducedDimNames<- still takes the subset name by position.
reducedDimNames() and reducedDimNames<- with subsetName = on an
object that isn't an ExperimentSubset, such as a plain
SingleCellExperiment, now say that it has no subsets and to convert
it with ExperimentSubset(). Before, they failed with "unable to find
an inherited method for function 'subsetNames'" (#82)

                Changes in version 1.23.30 (2026-11-02)                 

- reducedDims<- no longer masks SingleCellExperiment's while
ExperimentSubset is attached, so withDimnames = and the method's
other arguments work again, for plain SingleCellExperiment objects
as well as ExperimentSubset ones, with or without subsetName =.
Before, reducedDims(x, withDimnames = FALSE) <- value failed with
"unused argument". subsetName = on an object that isn't an
ExperimentSubset is now ignored, as for altExps<-, instead of giving
an error. Give the subset by name: reducedDims(x, "subset") <-
value, which the old generic allowed, now stops with an error saying
to use subsetName =, since the second argument is withDimnames.
reducedDimNames<- with a subsetName that isn't a subset now gives
the same error as the other methods (#26)

                Changes in version 1.23.29 (2026-11-01)                 

- combineCols() and combineRows() now keep the subsets of every
object, with their own assays, rowData, colData, reducedDims and
altExps. Before, they returned a plain object and dropped every
subset without a message. Each subset's rows (for combineCols()) or
columns (for combineRows()) are matched by name to the result's, or
by position with use.names = FALSE; subset names repeated across the
objects, or used as an assay name in another object, are an error.
Where the method of the class the objects extend returns another
class (combineCols() of a TreeSummarizedExperiment or
SpatialExperiment gives a SingleCellExperiment; combineRows() of a
SingleCellExperiment, TreeSummarizedExperiment or SpatialExperiment
gives a RangedSummarizedExperiment), the result is the matching
ExperimentSubset class, and each subset is converted to that class
too. A plain first object still gives a plain result: convert it
with ExperimentSubset() first (#73)

                Changes in version 1.23.28 (2026-11-01)                 

- New tests check that reducedDim(x) and reducedDim(x) <- value
without a type act on the first reducedDim of the main object, as
?"ExperimentSubset-reducedDim" says, for each class with
reducedDims. No change in behavior (#77)

                Changes in version 1.23.27 (2026-11-01)                 

- assay(x, i, subsetAssayName = ) with an i that isn't a subset name
now gives the same reason as assay<-: that i already names an assay
as "subset/assay", that i has a / but isn't "subset/assay" for an
existing subset, or that i is not a subset. Before, it said that i
was a subset that does not exist, and referred to a subsetName
argument that assay() doesn't have (#76)

                Changes in version 1.23.26 (2026-11-01)                 

- New help pages for the methods of Bioconductor generics that take
subsetName =: ?"ExperimentSubset-assay" (assay(), assay<-, which
name the subset with i), ?"ExperimentSubset-rowData-colData",
?"ExperimentSubset-reducedDim", ?"ExperimentSubset-altExp" and
?"ExperimentSubset-metadata". spatialCoords(x, subsetName = ) and
spatialData(x, subsetName = ) are now on the subsetSpatialCoords and
subsetSpatialData pages, and each show() method on its class's page.
Before, these methods had no help page (#15)
- The package now requires R 4.6.0 or later, the R version of
Bioconductor 3.24 (#52)
- The package is now listed under the SingleCell biocView (#52)

                Changes in version 1.23.25 (2026-11-01)                 

- cbind() and rbind() now keep the subsets of every object, with
their
own assays, rowData, colData, reducedDims and altExps. Before, only
the first object's subsets were kept and the others were dropped
without a message. Subsets of later objects move to where that
object's columns or rows are in the result. Subset names repeated
across the objects are an error, as is cbind() of an object with
subsets whose rows aren't the first object's, in the same order. For
SpatialExperiment objects, each subset's sample_id follows the main
object's when cbind() renames repeated sample IDs. Convert a plain
object with ExperimentSubset() before combining it with
ExperimentSubset objects (#67)

                Changes in version 1.23.24 (2026-10-31)                 

- subsetSpatialData() and spatialData(x, subsetName = ) are
deprecated, as spatialData() is in SpatialExperiment, which keeps
these columns in colData. They warn and still work; use
subsetColData(x, subsetName) instead, which returns all of the
subset's colData columns, with parentColData = TRUE to include the
main object's. They will be defunct in the next release.
spatialData(x) on the main object is unchanged (#34)
- subsetSpatialData<- is defunct and fails with an error saying to
add
each column with colData(x, subsetName = "name")$column <- values.
It skips the usual deprecation release because it already failed for
every value: SpatialExperiment's spatialData<- takes no data.frame,
and the method took no DataFrame (#34)

                Changes in version 1.23.23 (2026-10-31)                 

- createSubset() from a parent with no rows or no columns, such as a
subset none of whose rows remain after x[i, j], now says that the
parent is empty ("Parent 's1' has no rows, so a subset can't be made
from it."). Before, the error blamed the rows or cols argument, even
when it was left at its default (#68)

                Changes in version 1.23.22 (2026-10-31)                 

- x[i, j] now updates the subsets of x: each keeps the rows and
columns of the main object that remain, in its own order, with its
own assays, rowData, colData, reducedDims and altExps, and subsets
of subsets follow what remains of their parent. A subset none of
whose rows or columns remain is kept with no rows or no columns.
Before, subsets kept their old row and column positions, so reading
one failed with "subscript out of bounds" or, when the positions
were still in range, silently returned the wrong rows or columns
under the subset's names (#4)

                Changes in version 1.23.21 (2026-10-31)                 

- rowData(x, subsetName = , parentRowData = TRUE), colData(x,
subsetName = , parentColData = TRUE), subsetRowData(),
subsetColData() and getSubsetExperiment(parentData = TRUE) no longer
return two columns with the same name when a subset has its own
column with the name of a main-object column, of which $ and [[
returned the main object's. The subset's column now hides the main
object's, and comes after the main object's columns, with a message
if their values differ. A SpatialExperiment subset has one sample_id
column, the main object's current one (#57)

                Changes in version 1.23.20 (2026-10-31)                 

- stats is no longer listed in Suggests: it is a base package that R
attaches by default, including in R CMD check

                Changes in version 1.23.19 (2026-10-31)                 

- Joshua D. Campbell is now the maintainer, taking over from Irzam
Sarfraz, who remains an author

                Changes in version 1.23.18 (2026-10-25)                 

- New article on the website: an end-to-end single-cell workflow
on 4,000 PBMCs that keeps empty droplets, cells, quality-controlled
cells, variable genes and a T-cell re-analysis as subsets of one
object, using both getSubsetExperiment()/setSubsetExperiment() and
direct storage. The vignette links to the website and the article,
shows getSubsetExperiment()/setSubsetExperiment(), and sets subset
colData columns directly with colData(x, subsetName = )$column <-

                Changes in version 1.23.17 (2026-10-25)                 

- The package has a pkgdown website at
https://campbio.github.io/ExperimentSubset/, with the release
version at the root and the devel version under /dev/

                Changes in version 1.23.16 (2026-10-25)                 

- New getSubsetExperiment() returns a subset as a standalone object
of
the main object's class (for example a SingleCellExperiment), with
every assay the subset sees, its rowData and colData (after the main
object's columns, with parentData = TRUE), reducedDims, altExps and
metadata, so tools written for that class can run on the subset.
setSubsetExperiment() stores the result back: its assays, rowData,
colData, reducedDims, altExps and metadata replace the subset's own,
so an own assay or column missing from it is removed, while
unchanged linked assays and the main object's columns are not
stored. A linked assay the tool changed needs unlink = TRUE, and
removing an assay another subset was made from is an error

                Changes in version 1.23.15 (2026-10-25)                 

- A subset now sees all of its parent's assays as linked assays: the
parent's values sliced to the subset's rows and columns, under the
same names, computed when asked for rather than copied. For example
a logcounts computed on the main object is available in every
subset. Read an assay as a subset sees it with assay(x, "subset",
subsetAssayName = "a"), getSubsetAssay(x, "subset", subsetAssayName
= "a") or the name "subset/a"; subsetAssayNames(x, subsetName =
"subset") lists them (#2)
- Each subset has its own assay names: two subsets made from the same
parent can both store, say, decontXcounts. Storing an assay under a
name the subset already sees through its parent now needs unlink =
TRUE in setSubsetAssay() or assay<-; the subset and subsets made
from it then use their own version (including assay(x, "subset")
when the name is the one its parentAssay refers to), and the
parent's is unchanged
- A bare name in assay(), getSubsetAssay(), createSubset(parentAssay =
), subsetParent(), subsetRownames() and subsetColnames() now means a
main assay or a subset. An assay stored in a subset is named
"subset/assay"; a bare stored-assay name is an error that shows the
qualified form. Subsets made from such an assay record the qualified
name, and subsets in objects saved by earlier versions that recorded
a bare name are switched to the qualified name the next time a
subset is created or an assay stored. assay(x, "subset/assay") <-
value stores into that subset
- subsetAssayNames() lists the assays stored in subsets as
"subset/assay", so each listed name can be passed back to assay().
Subset names and stored assay names can't contain /

                Changes in version 1.23.14 (2026-10-22)                 

- withDimnames (for assay(), assay<-, reducedDim<-, altExp<- and
altExps<-), withColData (for altExp<- and altExps<-) and use.names
(for rowData()) now take effect, on the main object and with
subsetName (where the reducedDim(), reducedDims(), altExp() and
altExps() getters also pass them on); they were silently dropped.
reducedDims<- is unchanged (#26)
- rowData(x, subsetName = ) <- and colData(x, subsetName = ) <- with
NULL or a data.frame now change the subset; before, they changed the
main object's rowData or colData
- reducedDim(x, subsetName = ) without a type now returns, or with <-
replaces, the subset's first reducedDim instead of failing
- Writing back rowData or colData read with parentRowData = TRUE or
parentColData = TRUE no longer stores copies of the main object's
columns in the subset: those columns are left out, with a message
naming them. The getters mark them in the column metadata (mcols())
of the result
- subsetRowLinks(), subsetColLinks() and subsetSpatialData() return
the subset's row or column names instead of "1".."n", and asking for
the parent's links no longer fails when the main object has no tree
for that dimension
- subsetParent() resolves stored assay names the same way as assay()
and stops with an error if the chain of parents has a cycle
- Loading the package no longer warns about the listData and
elementType slots in the class prototypes

                Changes in version 1.23.13 (2026-10-22)                 

- Documentation fixes: the vignette lists all five supported classes,
names the createSubset() arguments rows and cols, seeds its random
data, drops the pin to Bioconductor 3.11 and installs from GitHub
with BiocManager; help pages say which input ExperimentSubset() and
createSubset() accept, fix the subsetRownames() page, and add
examples for subsetRowLinks(), subsetColLinks() and
subsetSpatialCoords(); examples no longer need scater
- DESCRIPTION gains URL and BugReports fields and drops the stale
Date
and the unused LazyData; the citation uses bibentry()

                Changes in version 1.23.12 (2026-10-22)                 

- rowData(), colData(), subsetRowData() and subsetColData() for a
subset now return the subset's row or column names as rownames (or
NULL if it has none), instead of "1".."n", so writing the result
back no longer renames the subset's cells
- Setting a subset's colData no longer changes its column names: a
value without rownames takes the subset's names, and a value whose
rownames differ from them is an error. Rename a subset's columns
with subsetColnames<-. Subsets whose cells were already renamed to
"1".."n" this way keep those names; set them back with
subsetColnames<- or re-create the subset

                Changes in version 1.23.11 (2026-10-22)                 

- The tests no longer download PBMC data from ExperimentHub: a small
simulated data set replaces it, the tests skip, rather than fail,
when a Suggests package they need is missing, and new tests cover
the TreeSummarizedExperiment and SpatialExperiment methods (except
spatialData, deprecated upstream)

                Changes in version 1.23.10 (2026-10-21)                 

- createSubset() checks its input more strictly: rows and cols must
select at least one row or column and be positive whole numbers or
names, without duplicates (duplicates were accepted in some cases
before); names given for an assay without row or column names give a
clear error; subsetName must be a single non-empty string that is
not already the name of an assay or of an assay stored in a subset;
parentAssay must be a single string
- ExperimentSubset() now stops when subset contains NA instead of
silently skipping the subset, and rejects a list of assays without
names
- Unknown subset names now give a clear error in subsetDim(),
subsetColnames(), subsetRownames() and their setters, and
reducedDims<-; assay(x, i) and getSubsetAssay(x, i) with an unknown
name are an error instead of returning NULL
- assay(x, i) <- value stores the assay inside the subset whenever i
is a subset name, and then needs subsetAssayName (giving
subsetAssayName with a name that is not a subset is an error);
before, the choice depended on the dimensions of value, so a subset
with the same dimensions as the main object got a new main assay
named after it

                 Changes in version 1.23.9 (2026-10-21)                 

- A subset with a single row or column now returns a one-row or
one-column matrix from assay(), not a vector, so subsets can be made
from it
- setSubsetAssay() (and assay(x, i) <- value for a subset) no longer
replaces the subset's row and column names with the input matrix's.
A matrix without names is stored under the subset's names; a matrix
whose names differ from the subset's, or are in another order, is
now an error instead of silently relabelling the subset; a matrix of
the wrong size gets an error that says so. assay(x, subsetName) now
returns the subset's own row and column names, including any set
with subsetRownames<- or subsetColnames<-, so setSubsetAssay(x, s,
assay(x, s), ...) always works
- A subsetName with spaces is now stored under the name with spaces
removed, which the warning already announced; before, the subset was
stored under the original name and lookups of its stored assays
failed. Refer to such a subset by the name without spaces

                 Changes in version 1.23.8 (2026-10-21)                 

- Subsets created from another subset (parentAssay set to a subset,
or
to an assay stored in one) now take their row and column names,
sample_id, and the parent rowData, colData, rowLinks, colLinks,
spatialCoords and spatialData from the right rows and columns of the
main object. Before, the indices relative to the parent subset were
applied to the main object, so these came from the wrong features
and cells while assay() returned the right values. The parent
metadata is looked up on access, so it is now right for existing
objects too; the subset's row and column names (and sample_id) are
stored when the subset is created, so objects saved with an earlier
version keep the wrong names for such subsets. Repair them with
subsetRownames(x, "s2") <- rownames(assay(x, "s2")) and the same for
subsetColnames(); a wrong SpatialExperiment sample_id needs the
subset re-created

                 Changes in version 1.23.7 (2026-10-21)                 

- Accessors and replacement methods called on the main object without
subsetName now pass on arguments that travel in the base generic's
...; for example reducedDim(x, "PCA", withDimnames = FALSE),
reducedDims(x, withDimnames = FALSE) and altExps(x, withDimnames =
FALSE) failed with "argument x is missing". Arguments that are named
formals of the base generic, such as withDimnames in assay<- or
use.names in rowData, are still dropped (#29)

                 Changes in version 1.23.6 (2026-10-21)                 

- altExp(x, e, subsetName = ) now returns the altExp named or
numbered
by e; it always returned the first one before
- altExp(x, <number>) <- value now replaces the altExp at that
position; with subsetName it replaced the first altExp, and without
it the call failed

                 Changes in version 1.23.5 (2026-10-21)                 

- The vignette's PBMC workflow now uses scrapper for QC,
normalization, highly variable genes and PCA, replacing scran and
scater functions that are deprecated
- scrapper replaces scran in Suggests; the tests also use scrapper in
place of the deprecated functions

                 Changes in version 1.23.1 (2026-10-20)                 

- Fixed a vignette example that filled a 2 x 4 matrix with 100
values,
which fails R CMD check --as-cran

[fraq](/packages/fraq)
----

                        Changes in version 1.1.3                        

- Fix fraq_concat() discarding output written to a .fifo path when
the
reader is not keeping up. Buffered bytes are now drained before the
writer is closed, matching what fraq_run() already did.
- Fix a file descriptor leak when closing a .fifo writer failed.
- Detect forked R processes with RcppParallel::isProcessForkedChild()
instead of probing parallel::isChild(), so the serial fallback
triggers regardless of which package performed the fork. This raises
the minimum RcppParallel version to 6.1.1.
- PlainWriter and FraqfFileWriter now tolerate being closed twice,
like the gzip and zstd writers already did.

                        Changes in version 1.1.2                        

- Fix .zst outputs gaining a spurious trailing empty frame:
ZstdWriter
now flushes with ZSTD_flushStream and only ends the frame in
close().
- Close .fraq/.mem writers explicitly on the success path, so write
errors at close time are reported instead of silently discarded.

                        Changes in version 1.1.1                        

- Move ShortRead from Imports to Suggests and check for it at runtime
in ShortRead bridge helpers.
- Add TBB flow graph compatibility helpers so the package builds
against both classic TBB and oneTBB (fixes a build failure caused by
an RcppParallel/TBB update that removed tbb::flow::source_node and
made limiter_node::decrement private).
- Add fraq_run_r() for block-oriented R kernels that run on the main
R
thread while file I/O and compression can continue on nthreads TBB
worker threads.
- Add serial fallback paths for C++ and R kernels when nthreads = 1,
and force the serial path inside forked R processes to avoid using
TBB after fork().
- Update bundled zstd to 1.5.7.

[gdsfmt](/packages/gdsfmt)
------

                       Changes in version 1.50.0                        

NEW FEATURES

- new storage types "rle.uint8", "rle.int32" (or "rle.int"),
  "rle.int64",
  "rle.float32" (or "rle.float"), "rle.float64" (or "rle.real" and
  "rle.double") and "rle.string": run-length encoded arrays.  The
  values
  are stored as runs of one repeated value, runs of an arithmetic
  progression (a first value and a step, so that `seq(0, 1, by=0.01)`
  takes 18 bytes) and blocks of up to 128 values kept as they are, with
  a
  table of checkpoints for random access

- add.gdsn() and append.gdsn() accept an object of class "rle" returned
  by base::rle(), for a node of any storage type.  The elements are
  written through a buffer of a fixed size, so the memory needed does
  not
  depend on the number of elements

- new argument 'allow.block' in `append.gdsn()`: if TRUE (the default),
  a GDS node given as 'val' can be appended by copying its encoded data
  as a block when it has the same storage type as the target node;
  'allow.block=FALSE' decodes every element and encodes it again, so
  that the appended data are compressed according to the target node
  (e.g., with its own compression level)

SIGNIFICANT USER-VISIBLE CHANGES

- add.gdsn(node, name, val) without `storage` stores an object of class
  "rle" in a run-length encoded array ("rle.int32", "rle.float64",
  "rle.string" or "rle.uint8"), and read.gdsn() returns an ordinary
  vector.  It used to create a folder of `lengths` and `values`, which
  `storage="list"` still does

UTILITIES

- update XZ to v5.8.4 from v5.2.9 (liblzma is now under the BSD Zero
  Clause License); GDS files stay compatible in both directions

- update zlib to v1.3.1 from v1.2.13: the bundled zlib sources are the
  unmodified upstream release, so the local changes for C23 compilers
  are no longer needed

- `append.gdsn()` copies variable-length strings ("string", "cstring"
  and
  their 16-/32-bit variants) as a raw block when the source is a GDS
  node
  of the same storage type, instead of decoding and re-encoding one
  string at a time

- `append.gdsn()` copies a sparse array ("sp.int8", "sp.real64" and the
  other sparse types) as a raw block of records when the source is a
  GDS
  node of the same storage type, instead of decoding every element and
  encoding it again.  The cost now follows the size of the encoded data
  instead of the length of the array: appending a node of a hundred
  million elements holding a hundred thousand non-zero values is about
  87 times faster

- variable-length string nodes now keep an offset index in the GDS
  file,
  so random access no longer walks the data from the first element.
  Nodes written by earlier versions carry no index and are read as
  before,
  and files written now remain readable by earlier versions

- `diagnosis.gds()` on a node reports the offset index under the name
  "index" instead of counting it as a second data stream; a node
  keeping
  more than one is reported as "index1", "index2", ...  The help page
  now
  also documents "index" and "ra_stream", the latter being the
  per-block
  raw and compressed sizes reported for a node compressed with a
  random-access coder

BUG FIXES

- add.gdsn(node, name, val, storage=<gdsn.class>) without `valdim` set
  the last dimension to zero after writing `val`, and the values were
  lost; now the last dimension is large enough to hold them

- `diagnosis.gds()` on a node failed with "attempt to set index 3/3 in
  SET_STRING_ELT" whenever the node owned more than one byte stream:
  the
  names vector was filled one position past its end.  This affected
  "vl_int" and "vl_uint", which have carried an indexing stream since
  they were introduced, and the variable-length strings once they
  gained
  one

- deleting a sparse array node ("sp.int8", "sp.real64", ...) left its
  indexing block behind, because the node did not report that block
  among
  the streams it owns; the block was unreachable but still occupied
  space
  until `cleanup.gds()` was run

- `append.gdsn(node, val)` with a GDS node 'val' that is not an array
  treated 'val' as an array without checking it: a folder gave a
  garbled
  error message ("Invalid node name ...") and a label crashed R; it now
  gives the error "'val' should be array-oriented data!"

                       Changes in version 1.49.7                        

NEW FEATURES

- new exported functions `gdsRegisterCloudHandler()`,
  `gdsUnregisterCloudHandler()` and `gdsCloudHandlers()`: the registry
  of
  cloud URL scheme handlers used by `openfn.gds()` is now part of the
  public interface, so that a companion package (e.g., gdscloud) can
  register its handlers without reaching into the gdsfmt namespace; the
  handler arguments are validated, the registering package is recorded,
  and a handler can now be unregistered, which was not previously
  possible

- the internal `.gds_register_cloud_handler()` is kept as a deprecated
  alias for one devel cycle

- `compression.gdsn()` writes the recompression progress to a text file
  (the internal temporary file name suffixed with ".progress.txt",
  located
  next to the temporary file) so users can monitor how much is left; it
  reports the GDS file name, the full node name, the percentage,
  processed/total bytes and an estimated time to completion, e.g.
  "File: /home/user/test.gds", "Node: geno/data" and
  "47%, 1234567/2600000 bytes, ETA 0:00:12".

- new argument 'sort' in `cleanup.gds()`: if TRUE (the default),
  rearrange data blocks when defragmenting -- all node header blocks
  are
  placed first in depth-first traversal order with folder headers
  prioritized before other node headers, followed by data blocks sorted
  by size (small to large) then by ID.  This layout clusters the GDS
  tree structure metadata at the front of the file, maximizing page
  cache hit rate during tree navigation;
  'sort=FALSE' for backward compatibility

UTILITIES

- `diagnosis.gds()` now appends a trailing '/' to folder node names in
  the stream info output, making it easier to distinguish folders from
  leaf nodes

- `moveto.gdsn()` supports a new `relpos="into"` option to move a node
  into a different folder within the same GDS file

BUG FIXES

- define an S4 `$` method for `gds.class` so that S4 subclasses (e.g.,
  SeqVarGDSClass in SeqArray) still support `$` element access after
  the
  `as()` coercion change in R 4.6.1 (R NEWS: "as() now correctly
  coerces
  to S4 superclasses extending old-style classes instead of returning
  only
  the S3 part").

- fixed virtual dispatch error in `unload.gdsn()`: when a node has
  unsaved attribute changes and is unloaded, the object destructor's
  call to Synchronize() now happens before Release() to ensure correct
  virtual function resolution.  This prevents writing empty class names
  to the GDS stream which would corrupt the file

- fixed `read.gdsn()` on a 1-dimensional sparse array (e.g. storage
  "sp.int32"/"sp.real64" created from a plain vector): it returned only
  the first non-zero element (and could error with "Invalid input in
  SpRead()" depending on uninitialized stack values).  Two causes: the
  single-column CSC pointer in `CdSpArray::SpRead()` was hard-coded to
  1
  instead of the non-zero count, and the R reader passed an
  uninitialized 2nd dimension to `SpRead()`.  2-D sparse arrays were
  unaffected;

- fixed `cleanup.gds(..., sort=TRUE)` to avoid loading nodes with
  unregistered class names (e.g., from external packages like
  SeqArray).
  The sort traversal now uses TNode metadata directly without
  triggering
  class deserialization for non-folder nodes
