                        Changes in version 1.9.6                        

- BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: testEnrichmentSEA reports nQ as the size of the
  query
  and nD as the size of the database. For a numeric query the two were
  the
  other way round (nQ was the set, nD the CpGs with a value).

- testEnrichment warns when no query probe is in the universe, instead
  of
  returning all-zero overlaps silently.

- Databases dropped while loading are named in a warning: a requested
  group
  with no version for the query's platform, an unknown group, an empty
  set.

- Vignettes: no sesameDataCache("HM450.address"); sesameData 1.31.2
  lists
  that record with no ExperimentHub id yet, which stopped the devel
  build.

                        Changes in version 1.9.5                        

- testEnrichment: no "Unknown or uninitialised column" warnings on
  sequencing results; the estimate's 1024 / -1022 sentinels are
  documented.

- Vignettes: an install chunk for the Suggests the examples load; the
  Manhattan and feature-aggregation chunks cache their own data; MM285
  examples use the MM285 TFBS database; the HM450 Zenodo example uses
  an
  HM450 query; the sequencing quick start runs on the shipped single
  cell;
  the bedToCg example is self-contained; permutation chunks are seeded.

- Manual: loadDBs, testEnrichmentSpearman and df_master are internal;
  no
  developer notes or local paths in examples.

                        Changes in version 1.9.4                        

- bedToCg: the bedtools/yame pipeline reached sh -c unquoted, so sh ran
  a
  bare `yame` and the output file was empty. It is now quoted.

- testEnrichment2: the odds ratio is computed in double precision.
  Integer
  counts from YAME overflowed on genome-scale tables and gave NA
  estimates.

- testEnrichment2: an unmeetable min_overlap returns the empty result
  without a second warning.

- KYCG_plotEnrichAll: geom_segment(linewidth=), not the deprecated
  size=.

                        Changes in version 1.9.3                        

- testEnrichmentSEA: the two tails now share one pooled permutation
  null, so the p-value no longer depends on the sign of the query
  (zhou-lab/knowYourCG#6)

- testEnrichmentSEA: the sign of estimate is flipped to match GSEA.
  Positive now means the set is enriched at large values, negative at
  small values. Results from earlier versions have the opposite sign.
  KYCG_plotSetEnrichment now walks from the largest value down.

[lcmsPlot](/packages/lcmsPlot)
--------

                       Changes in version 1.1.29                        

- The Compound Discoverer node's compound table has a logical
has_name
column, TRUE for compounds Compound Discoverer has named. Unnamed
compounds are labelled with their formula or ID, so a Compounds
Query of has_name (or has_name & compound_rank <= 20) plots only the
named ones. Released as node 1.1.0, which needs lcmsPlot 1.1.29 or
later.

                       Changes in version 1.1.28                        

- Compound Discoverer node released with an installer: each version
of
the Compounds Chromatograms node (its own version, starting at 1.0.0
in VERSION) is published as a GitHub release,
CompoundsChromatograms.zip, with a Windows installer (install.bat).
The installer finds R 4.4.0 or later, installs lcmsPlot at the
version the node was released with (from its GitHub tag, as
Bioconductor's release may be older) and rawrr, copies the node into
each Compound Discoverer version found and writes the R and script
paths into node.json. Package versions are tagged vX.Y.Z, and node
releases cd-node-vX.Y.Z, by the release workflow.
- The node checks, when run from a release, that the installed
lcmsPlot is at least the version it was released with, and stops
with a clear message if not. It now ships the icons its node.json
refers to, and its default ExecutablePath points to an R that
lcmsPlot supports (4.4).

                       Changes in version 1.1.27                        

- Peak integration windows in the Compound Discoverer node (#41): the
Compounds Chromatograms scripting node now requests the Features per
File and Chromatogram Peaks tables, and
CompoundDiscovererNodeSource() takes each compound's peak window in
each file from them: the left and right retention times of the
reference chromatogram peak of the compound's reference ion, the
window Compound Discoverer integrated the area over, as the
.cdResult reader does. Previously the node exported no peak bounds,
so the window was the apex ± half the FWHM (about a third of the
integrated window) or the apex alone. The reference peak is the one
flagged Is Ref Peak, else isotope 0, else the one whose apex is
closest to the ion's retention time. Exports without these tables
keep the previous behaviour, and per-file feature exports without
Left/Right RT now also fall back to the FWHM. Workflows built with
the previous node.json need the node re-registered (or its Requested
Tables and Columns updated) to benefit.

                       Changes in version 1.1.26                        

- Compound Discoverer 3.5 result files: lp_compound_discoverer()
reads
.cdResult files written by Compound Discoverer 3.5, which name the
table linking compounds to their per-file instances
UnknownCompoundInstanceItemsConsolidatedUnknownCompoundItems instead
of ConsolidatedUnknownCompoundItemsUnknownCompoundInstanceItems.
Previously such files failed with "no such table".
- Aligned MZmine feature lists: MZmineFeatureListsSource() reads
feature lists that hold several data files, such as those exported
after MZmine's join aligner, in both the MZmine 2 and the MZmine 3+
formats. Each data file contributes its own peaks (gap-filled ones
included), and rows a file has no peak for are skipped. Previously
only lists exported per sample could be read; aligned lists failed
with "Expected exactly one feature state/status column".
- Highlighted peaks stay on their own feature: with several features
in one plot (e.g. faceted by feature),
lp_chromatogram(highlight_peaks = TRUE) shaded a feature's detected
peaks on the traces of every feature of the same sample whose
retention times overlapped them. A peak is now shaded only on its
own feature's traces; peaks without a feature are still shaded on
every trace of their sample.

                       Changes in version 1.1.25                        

- Intensity axes in scientific notation: the intensity axis of
chromatograms (TIC, BPC, EICs) and of the total ion current is
labelled in scientific notation (0.0e+00, 5.0e+05, 1.0e+06, ...), so
intensities read the same in every panel of a figure. Previously
ggplot2 picked plain or scientific labels for each panel depending
on its range. Relative intensities (intensity_unit = "relative"),
transformed intensities (transform) and stacked chromatograms keep
their axes. To use other labels, replace the scale of every panel,
e.g. lp_get_plot() & ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels =
scales::label_comma()).

                       Changes in version 1.1.24                        

- FAIR metadata (#68): the package ships a codemeta.json, the
machine-readable software metadata harvested by registries, and its
biocViews add Software, Lipidomics, Visualization and ShinyApps.
- Figures with provenance (#68): lp_save(p, "figure.pdf") saves the
plot with ggsave() and writes figure.pdf.provenance.json next to it:
the versions of lcmsPlot, R, Bioconductor and every loaded package,
the layers of the pipeline with their arguments, and the input files
with their size and modification time (and MD5 checksum with
checksums = TRUE). data = TRUE also writes the plotted data to
figure_data/.
- Plotted data in an open format (#68): lp_export_data(p, dir) writes
the data a pipeline draws as CSV (or TSV with format = "tsv") files,
one per dataset in the tidy form the plot is drawn from, plus the
detected peaks, the samples, and a columns data dictionary with the
type, unit and description of every column.
- Reports with provenance (#68): lp_report() closes with a provenance
section (the last page of a PDF report) listing the versions of
lcmsPlot, R and Bioconductor, the pipeline layers, and the input
files, and writes the full record next to the report
(features.html.provenance.json). The HTML report also embeds it as
JSON and names lcmsPlot as its generator; the PDF report carries its
title in its metadata. provenance = FALSE leaves it out, and
checksums = TRUE adds the MD5 of the input files.
- Supported formats (#68): a new help page, ?lcmsPlot-formats, lists
every supported input with its versions, the way to read it, and the
packages it needs. The README and the Interoperability section of
the vignette show the same table, and the vignette has a new section
on saving figures with provenance.

                       Changes in version 1.1.23                        

- Per-feature reports (#61): lp_report(p, file, by = "feature_id")
writes one page per feature (or per name, or per any annotation
column) out of a plot pipeline built once. Each page draws the
pipeline restricted to the feature with subset_features(), with
tables of the feature's annotations and of its detected peak in
every sample (rt, into, maxo); the raw data is not read again. The
format follows the file extension:

- .html: one self-contained file with the plots embedded as PNG
images and an index of the features that can be searched and
sorted and links to each page;
- .pdf: one multi-page file with the index first, sized by
page_size and orientation.

features limits the report to some values, listed in the index as
"no data" when they match no data. sections picks the tables drawn
under the plots ("annotations", "peaks") and can add "ms2", the MS2
spectra of each feature by precursor, extracted once for the whole
report. features_per_page and ncol tile several features on a page,
and theme styles the report: "plain" (the default), "clean", or
"journal". PDF reports need gridExtra and gtable, now in Suggests.

                       Changes in version 1.1.22                        

- Refreshed Shiny app interface: a consistent type scale
(Bootstrap's 10px root font no longer shrinks the text), the bundled
Outfit font, a sidebar with views, data and samples (with All / None
selection), the active view's title in the topbar, and no icons.
Busy outputs show a spinner, the page shows a progress bar while the
server works, action buttons show a busy state, and empty plot areas
explain what to do next. Deselecting every sample now shows a
message instead of plotting all samples. Requires shiny (>= 1.8.1).

                       Changes in version 1.1.21                        

- New lp_theme() layer styles every plot type, and every panel of a
patchwork layout, from the pipeline (#60): lp_theme(preset =
"publication", palette = "okabe_ito", base_size = 8). preset is
"minimal" (the previous look, still the default), "classic",
"publication" (white background, axis lines, no minor grid, 8 pt
base size), or any ggplot2 theme. palette is "okabe_ito", "viridis",
"ggplot2" (the previous hues), or a named or unnamed vector of
colours. line_width sets the width of the plotted lines and of the
theme's lines. lp_get_plot() + theme(...) still overrides the
preset.
- The default discrete colours are now the colourblind-safe Okabe-Ito
palette, falling back to viridis beyond 8 groups. Use
lp_theme(palette = "ggplot2") for the previous hues. A series keeps
its colour across all the panels of a layout. Continuous scales
(intensity maps, peak count images, purity scores) are unchanged.
- Highlighted peaks take the colour of their trace:
highlight_peaks_factor of lp_chromatogram() now defaults to NULL,
meaning the group_by column of lp_arrange(), else sample_id. Set it
explicitly for the previous behaviour.
- The Shiny app's Options panel exposes the theme preset, palette,
and
base font size.
- The plot-data baselines in tests/testthat/fixtures/baseline are
unaffected: they record the values handed to the plotting functions,
not their colours.

                       Changes in version 1.1.20                        

- lp_spectra(mode = "precursor") plots the MS2 spectra of each
feature
from data-dependent acquisition (#54): the MS2 scans whose precursor
m/z lies within ppm of the m/z of the feature's detected peak and
whose retention time lies within the peak, or within the feature's
extraction window in samples where it has no detected peak. select
keeps the scan with the most intense precursor ("most_intense",
falling back to the total ion current), the scan closest to the apex
("closest_apex"), every scan ("all"), or one consensus spectrum per
feature and sample ("consensus", tuned by consensus_ppm and
consensus_min_prop). Spectra keep their feature_id, mirror plots
against spectral_match_db work as before, and features without a
matching MS2 scan are skipped with a single warning listing them.
- MS2 spectra mark their precursor m/z with a diamond on the m/z axis
and in the panel title. The marker's shape, position (on the m/z
axis or on top of the precursor's peak), and color are set with the
precursor_marker_shape, precursor_marker_position, and
precursor_marker_color arguments of lp_spectra().
- lp_spectra(mode = "closest_apex") and mode = "across_peak" now
select and report scans on the adjusted retention times when the
data has them, as the detected peaks and feature chromatograms
already did. They used to look up raw scan times with adjusted peak
times, so the spectra could come from a scan next to the apex and
their RT lines sat slightly off the chromatogram. The
xcms_spectra_closest_apex baseline was re-recorded.

                       Changes in version 1.1.19                        

- New MzTabMSource() reads mzTab-M 2.0 files (as exported by MS-DIAL,
MZmine, OpenMS, ...) alongside their raw files (#51). Small molecule
features (SMF) become peaks with their feature_id, adduct_ion and
charge, annotated with the name, formula, database_identifier and
reliability of the summary (SML) rows that reference them. The new
lp_mztab() layer selects the features to plot, e.g.
lp_mztab(features_query = "reliability <= 2").
- The vignette plots a real mzTab-M example: the HUPO-PSI MTBLS263
file (Progenesis QI) with the MetaboLights raw files it describes,
cut down to eight features. Both ship in inst/extdata
(MTBLS263.mztab, mtbls263-mzml.zip);
tools/mztab/make-mtbls263-example.R rebuilds them.

                       Changes in version 1.1.18                        

- Breaking: lcmsPlotDataContainer now holds RforMassSpectrometry data
structures (#52). The sample metadata is the sampleData() of an
MsExperiment, chromatograms are a Chromatograms object, and spectra
are a Spectra object. Every dataset is keyed by sample_index, and
feature annotations (feature_id, name, formula, ...) are carried by
the chromatograms, spectra, and peaks they describe. Migrating:
- create_data_container_from_obj() is replaced by
lcmsPlotDataContainer().
- The slots data_obj, metadata, feature_metadata, and the
per-dataset data frames are gone. Use the accessors
sampleMetadata(), chromatograms(), spectra(), detectedPeaks(),
and summaries() (mass traces, intensity maps, total ion current,
RT differences, peak density, peak counts, and purity scores) on
an lcmsPlot object or its container.
- The metadata_index and feature_metadata_id columns are replaced
by sample_index and the annotation columns themselves.
- XCMSnExp input is converted to an XcmsExperiment.
- aggregation_fun = "mean" on an XcmsRawList is now the mean of
each scan's centroids; the profile matrix is no longer used.
- The internal raw file readers (MsRawReader and its subclasses)
are removed; raw data is read through Spectra backends.
MsBackendRawFileReader is needed to read the spectra of
ThermoFisher .raw files, while their chromatograms are still
extracted with rawrr.
- New subset_features() keeps the data matching a condition on its
annotations without reading the raw data again, for example to draw
one plot per compound out of a single extraction.
- Plot data is computed much faster. All windows of a sample are
extracted in one pass over its raw file, and intensity maps are
binned with data.table. On three faahKO files, 100 extracted ion
chromatograms take about 2 s instead of 15.1 s, closest_apex
spectra 0.6 s instead of 12.2 s, and an intensity map 2.0 s instead
of 28.0 s.
- Spectra line up with the chromatograms' features. Each detected
peak
gives one spectrum, labelled with the feature its peak belongs to;
spectra were previously read again for every overlapping feature
window and paired with features by position.
- Compound Discoverer .cdResult chromatograms are no longer
duplicated
once per sample.
- Faceted plots draw only the panels the data has, and highlight only
the peaks of each panel's facet value.
- Raw files are only read once a layer needs them, file connections
are always closed, and corrected retention times are applied without
matching scan counts.
- lp_total_ion_current() gains initial, as in Spectra::tic(). The
default (TRUE) plots the total ion current recorded in each scan's
header for every input; FALSE sums each scan's peaks. Raw netCDF
files given as paths used to be summed, so their plot changes unless
initial = FALSE is set. netCDF headers include signal that is not
among the stored peaks, so on faahKO the header values are about
twice the sums.
- lp_total_ion_current(), lp_intensity_map(), and lp_rt_diff_plot()
are now replayed by iterate_plot_batches() and next_plot(), and
lp_total_ion_current() honours sample_ids.

                       Changes in version 1.1.17                        

- Add CONTRIBUTING.md and update README.md with latest features.

                       Changes in version 1.1.16                        

- Data extraction from mzML, mzXML and CDF files is faster. The scan
header of a file is read once and reused, and chromatograms, spectra
and intensity maps locate scans without reading every spectrum,
which on CDF files used to happen once per feature, peak or
spectrum. Extracted ion chromatograms, intensity maps and peak
highlighting are also built in a single pass instead of one row at a
time. On the faahKO data, feature chromatograms are about 10 times
faster, across_peak spectra about 15 times and intensity maps up
to 100 times. The extracted data is unchanged (#48).

                       Changes in version 1.1.15                        

- Chromatograms from ThermoFisher .raw files are extracted much
faster
for the Compound Discoverer node and LipidSearch. All compound XICs
of a sample are now read from its .raw file in a single rawrr call,
rather than one call per compound, and the mass traces these sources
never plot are no longer computed. The scan header of a .raw file is
read once and reused, which also speeds up feature chromatograms.
The extracted chromatograms are unchanged (#40).

                       Changes in version 1.1.14                        

- The Compound Discoverer Compounds Chromatograms node no longer
duplicates columns. Its node_response.json now returns only the
Compounds ID column and the new plot column, in both the data file
and the ColumnDescriptions. Compound Discoverer adds every column it
gets back, so echoing the full Compounds table used to make columns
such as Area and Gap Fill Status appear twice (#45).

                       Changes in version 1.1.13                        

- XChromatograms features can be named. Setting the row names of an
XChromatograms object now sets the feature_id used for labelling and
faceting:

chrs <- chromatogram(xdata, mz = mzr, rt = rtr)
rownames(chrs) <- c("mz344", "mz360")

Row names take precedence over xcms::featureChromatograms() feature
identifiers; rows with neither keep the M<mz>T<rt> identifier.

                       Changes in version 1.1.12                        

- Manually specified features can be named. A feature passed to
lp_chromatogram(features = ) as a matrix or data.frame now takes its
feature_id from the row names, or from a feature_id column of a
data.frame, so

lp_chromatogram(features = rbind(
mz335 = c(mzmin = 334.9, mzmax = 335.1, rtmin = 2700, rtmax = 2900)))

labels and facets the feature as mz335. Unnamed rows keep the
M<mz>T<rt> identifier derived from their ranges. Likewise, an
XChromatograms object from xcms::featureChromatograms() now uses the
feature definition row names (e.g. "FT0003") rather than M<mz>T<rt>.

                       Changes in version 1.1.11                        

- Feature identifiers now come from the feature definition row names.
Where lcmsPlot previously derived its own xcms::groupnames()-style
M<mz>T<rt> labels from mzmed/rtmed, it now uses
rownames(xcms::featureDefinitions(obj)) — whatever you have set them
to, or the "FT0001"-style defaults xcms assigns during
correspondence. This affects both the identifiers you pass to
lp_chromatogram(features = ...) and the feature_id column used for
labelling and faceting, so a call such as

lp_chromatogram(features = c('M205T2792', 'M283T3890'))

becomes

lp_chromatogram(features = c('FT002', 'FT027'))

Annotating features by renaming the rows of featureDefinitions() is
now enough to have those names appear on the plot; no separate
labelling step is needed. Objects whose feature definitions carry no
row names at all still get positional "FT..." identifiers, so a
single nomenclature applies throughout.

- Feature identifiers that match no feature are now reported.
Previously an unrecognised identifier was dropped silently and
produced an empty plot; lp_chromatogram() now warns, naming the
identifiers it skipped, and plots the ones that did match.

                       Changes in version 1.1.10                        

- lp_compound_discoverer(compounds_query = ...) can now filter on the
checked column of the Compound Discoverer Compounds table, so a
result set curated by hand in Compound Discoverer can be plotted
directly with compounds_query = "checked". This works for both
Compound Discoverer sources:

- For .cdResult files it is read from
ConsolidatedUnknownCompoundItems.Checked. Compound Discoverer
only materialises that column once compounds have been checked
and the result saved in the application, so its presence is
probed per file: referencing checked on a file that has none
raises an explanatory error instead of failing with a raw SQL
error.

- For the scripting-node source it is read from the Checked column
of the exported Compounds table, and parsed from Compound
Discoverer's True / False text (other spellings are accepted
defensively, so a differently encoded export does not silently
read as all-NA).

- The Compounds Chromatograms scripting node follows Compound
Discoverer's checked-compounds convention: if any compound is
checked in the Compounds table, only the checked ones are plotted;
if none is checked, all of them are. Checking compounds in Compound
Discoverer is therefore enough to pick exactly what gets plotted,
and the Compounds Query parameter is ignored while any box is
ticked. A query that references checked itself (for example checked
& compound_rank <= 5) is used as written and is never overridden, so
the two can still be combined. The node logs which of these applied
on every run.

- compounds_query = NULL (the default) no longer errors on the
.cdResult path, and now means "no filter", matching the
scripting-node behaviour.

                        Changes in version 1.1.9                        

- lp_spectra() gains mz_breaks_n, the approximate number of m/z axis
breaks, passed through to scales::pretty_breaks(n = ...). The break
count was previously hard-coded at 20, which crowded the axis on
narrow m/z windows. It defaults to 6.

                        Changes in version 1.1.8                        

- Closed six gaps between lcmsPlot and the plotting methods of xcms,
so the backend = "lcmsPlot" variants of those methods have an
equivalent to call.

- The Easy-to-use, intuitive, and efficient LC-MS data plotting with
lcmsPlot vignette now covers all of this. A new Quality control of
peak detection section documents the two new layers, and the four
extended arguments are documented in the sections that already
covered those layers.

- New layer lp_chrom_peak_rects() draws one rectangle per detected
chromatographic peak, spanning rtmin-rtmax by mzmin-mzmax. It covers
both xcms methods that draw that primitive. Called on its own it
owns a panel, drawing the rectangles on an otherwise empty rt / m/z
frame with one facet per sample, as xcms::plotChromPeaks() does;
rt_range and mz_range restrict it the way that method's xlim and
ylim do. Called after lp_mass_trace() or lp_intensity_map() it
decorates that panel instead, as xcms::plot(type = "XIC") does,
following the host's x_dim, window and sample_ids so the axes are
not widened and no extra facets appear. Which mode applies is
decided from the finished plot, so it does not depend on the order
the layers were added in. Every box is given a minimum height so
that peaks on m/z-binned data (where mzmin == mzmax) read as
segments instead of vanishing.

- New layer lp_peak_count_image() reproduces
xcms::plotChromPeakImage(): retention-time bins on x, samples on y,
filled by the number of chromatographic peaks per bin. Samples are
ordered by injection order, and bins with no peaks are kept at zero,
so a sample that stopped producing peaks half-way through a run
reads as an empty stretch rather than disappearing. Counts match the
xcms method's binning exactly.

- lp_peak_density() now accepts XChromatograms and XChromatogram
objects, which is what xcms::plotChromPeakDensity() takes. The type
gate is now a capability check through get_detected_peaks() rather
than a class check, the creator goes through that adapter instead of
calling xcms::chromPeaks() directly (the sample column is named
column, not sample, on chromatogram objects), and features is
redundant for these inputs because each extracted ion chromatogram
already carries its own m/z window. A new simulate argument mirrors
the xcms method: TRUE descends the density curve for candidate
features, FALSE draws the feature definitions the object already
stores.

- lp_chromatogram() gains stacked and transform, matching
xcms::plotChromatogramsOverlay(). stacked offsets each series up the
y axis in m/z order by a fraction of the intensity range so
co-eluting traces stop occluding each other, using the same offset
formula as xcms, and suppresses the y axis because a stacked axis
has no single meaning; the offsets are returned on the plot as a
stacked_offsets attribute. transform (for example log10) is applied
to the intensities and to the peak-highlight geometry alike, so
shaded peaks stay attached to their traces.

- lp_chromatogram(aggregation_fun = "mean") produces the averaged ion
chromatogram of xcms::plotChrom(base = FALSE). The ms_header()
contract has gained peaksCount and meanIntensity, letting each
backend define the mean faithfully: XcmsRawList inputs carrying a
profile matrix use the profile-matrix column mean and so reproduce
the xcms trace exactly, while file-based inputs average over the
measured peaks of each scan. Unknown aggregation functions now raise
an error rather than silently returning a TIC.

- lp_intensity_map() gains geom, point_size, bin_rt, bin_mz and
colour_scale. geom = "point" draws the individual centroids as
xcms::plotRaw() does, skipping the binning so gaps in the mass
traces stay visible instead of being implied away by a tile grid.
The retention-time and m/z bin widths, previously hard-coded at 0.1,
are now arguments.

Breaking changes

- The density argument of lp_intensity_map() has been removed. It is
replaced by geom = "density", which selects the same rendering. Two
separate switches could contradict each other, so there is now a
single one. Replace lp_intensity_map(..., density = TRUE) with
lp_intensity_map(..., geom = "density"); density = FALSE was the
default and can simply be dropped.

Bug fixes

- lp_intensity_map() no longer errors with "argument is of length
zero" on narrow m/z windows. The peak matrix was subset without drop
= FALSE, so any scan with exactly one peak in range collapsed to a
vector and the following nrow() check failed. A narrow window is
precisely what an XIC plot passes.

- plot_chromatogram() no longer joins every series in a facet into a
single zig-zagging line when the colour aesthetic is something other
than sample_id. The ggplot group was pinned to sample_id while
lp_arrange() set only the colour; it is now a composite of the
sample and the arrangement column, so colouring by feature_id splits
the lines while coarser factors such as sample_group keep one line
per sample as before.

- lp_peak_density(simulate = TRUE) no longer draws overlapping
feature
rectangles that all start at the same retention time. The internal
descent used to find each feature's boundaries compared neighbouring
density values with <=, so once the previous feature's range had
been zeroed it walked straight across that plateau and re-collected
the peaks already assigned. Each later rectangle therefore reached
back to the first feature's leftmost peak, and passed the
min_fraction test on the strength of those peaks. The comparison is
now strict, matching the DescendMin routine of xcms, and the
rectangles agree with xcms::plotChromPeakDensity().

                        Changes in version 1.1.7                        

- Every man page documenting an exported object now carries a
runnable
example. The four \dontrun{} blocks that referenced unavailable
vendor data (CompoundDiscovererNodeSource(), LipidSearchSource(),
lp_compound_discoverer(), lp_lipid_search()) have been replaced with
self-contained code, and the four precursor-purity layers
(lp_purity_overlay(), lp_purity_timeline(),
lp_purity_distribution(), lp_isolation_window()) have gained
examples where they previously had none. This satisfies the
Bioconductor requirement that at least 80% of such pages have
runnable examples; coverage is now 100% (33 of 33, up from 25
of 33).

- The purity examples use the DDA files already shipped in
inst/extdata/standards-mzml.zip, whose MS2 scans carry real
precursor selection and isolation-window metadata, so
msPurity::purityA() yields six fragmentation events with informative
inPurity scores. They are guarded with @examplesIf
requireNamespace("msPurity") because msPurity is a suggested
dependency. lp_isolation_window() uses half_width = 0.6 to match the
isolation width recorded in those files.

- The Compound Discoverer scripting-node and LipidSearch examples
build a minimal vendor export in tempdir(), following the existing
MZmineFeatureListsSource() and MsDialPeaksSource() examples, and
point sample_paths at the shipped mzML files so the documented plots
extract real chromatograms rather than only constructing a data
source.

                        Changes in version 1.1.6                        

- Added support for LipidSearch result files (both 4.2 and 5.2; the
version is auto-detected). The new LipidSearchSource() constructor
parses the lipid table, reshapes the per-sample Area / Height / RT /
observed-m/z columns into an xcms-style peak table, and builds a
plottable data source. Rejected lipids are dropped unless
keep_rejected = TRUE, and lipid ions reported at several retention
times get distinct plot labels. Plotting uses the new
lp_lipid_search(lipids_query, rt_extend) layer, whose query can
reference the lipid annotations (class, sub_class, grade, adduct,
lipid_rank, ...).

- LipidSearch 5.2 files carry no raw-file names, so their samples are
keyed s1, s2, … (from the OrgMeanArea[...] columns). For 5.2, map
raw files by naming sample_paths with those keys (c("s1" = "a.mzML",
"s2" = "b.mzML")) — order-independent and covering any subset — or
pass an unnamed vector matched positionally. 5.2 exports add a
sub_class annotation and an explicit adduct, and their per-lipid
BaseRt provides an extraction window even for lipids detected in no
sample. 4.2's basename matching is unchanged. The rej annotation is
now a logical for both versions.

- Samples plotted from a LipidSearch source are not limited to the
ones declared in the result file: sample_paths determines the sample
list and is matched to the declarations by file basename without
extension (so a result file listing .raw files works with converted
.mzML files). A supplied path that matches no declaration is still a
full sample - every queried lipid's chromatogram is extracted there
using the lipid's consensus m/z and retention-time window, it simply
has no reported peak to highlight.

- The per-compound chromatogram extraction loop is now shared between
the Compound Discoverer scripting-node and LipidSearch sources
(create_compound_chromatograms()), along with the compound ranking
and column-resolution helpers.

                        Changes in version 1.1.5                        

- lp_total_ion_current() now works when raw files are passed directly
to lcmsPlot() (a character vector of .mzML, .mzXML, .CDF, or .raw
paths), in addition to XCMSnExp / MsExperiment objects. The per-scan
TIC is read from the raw file headers via the shared raw-file reader
interface.

- Added a runnable worked example for large, multi-sample LC-MS
studies. Using a 50-sample mzML study (the published Sacurine
dataset, MetaboLights MTBLS404), it demonstrates the batching API
(batch_size + iterate_plot_batches()) together with patchwork to
build one self-contained composite figure per sample (TIC and BPC,
an EIC + mass trace for a shared compound, and a zoomed intensity
map), written to a multi-page PDF report. It is distributed as a
standalone script rather than a packaged vignette, since it
downloads and processes ~50 raw files.

                        Changes in version 1.1.4                        

- Added support for using lcmsPlot inside a Compound Discoverer
custom
Scripting Node. The new CompoundDiscovererNodeSource() constructor
reads the node_args.json file passed by Compound Discoverer together
with the tab-delimited table exports it references (Compounds,
Compounds per File, Features, and their link tables), selects a
representative ion per compound and study file (preferring [M+H]+1 /
[M-H]-1, otherwise the most abundant feature), and builds a
plottable data source. Chromatograms are extracted from the raw
(mzML) files supplied via sample_paths, which are matched to study
files by file basename (falling back to positional matching by
study-file ID). Plotting reuses the existing
lp_compound_discoverer(compounds_query, rt_extend) interface.
jsonlite was added to Imports.

                        Changes in version 1.1.3                        

- Redesigned lcmsPlotApp() as a Tailwind-based dashboard: sticky
topbar, left navigation rail with a card-style file uploader and
sample picker, and a content area with the plot in a card. The
Tailwind CSS is precompiled and shipped under inst/www/lcmsPlot.css;
no runtime network or Node dependency. Dev sources live in
tools/tailwind/ (excluded from the installed package).
- Added a per-tab Options panel that exposes lp_facets(),
lp_arrange(), lp_legend(), and lp_labels() directly from the UI.
Users can now facet, group, reposition the legend, and add titles
without writing R code.
- Dashboard CSS is now served via htmltools::htmlDependency() and the
Tailwind content scan + safelist were hardened so utility classes
referenced from R templates actually end up in the compiled
stylesheet. The UI is now wrapped in shiny::bootstrapPage() so the
hidden tabsetPanel switches correctly. Card corners reduced from
rounded-2xl to rounded-md, sidebar gap bumped to gap-6, and the
initial nav highlight is now set statically in markup.
- The Shiny uploader now accepts additional data-source types: Thermo
.raw files (multi-file), Compound Discoverer .cdResult SQLite
results (single file), serialised XCMSnExp / MsExperiment objects
via .rds (single file), and saved workspaces containing one such
object via .RData / .rda (single file). All existing mzML / CDF
workflows are unchanged.

                        Changes in version 1.1.2                        

- Added lcmsPlotApp(), an interactive Shiny app for exploring raw
LC-MS files. Users can upload one or more mzML / CDF files and view
base-peak and total-ion chromatograms, extract ion chromatograms by
m/z and ppm (with an optional retention-time window), inspect peak
density across samples, and plot spectra by scan index. The app
follows Bioconductor's Shiny code-organisation guidelines: all
UI/server code lives in R/ and lcmsPlotApp() returns a shinyApp
object rather than calling runApp() internally. shiny, shinytoastr,
and shinytest2 were added to Suggests.

                        Changes in version 1.1.1                        

- Added support for purityA objects (msPurity) as the data_obj input
to lcmsPlot(), enabling direct visualisation of precursor ion purity
results.
- Added lp_purity_overlay(): overlays per-scan inPurity scores as
coloured points on a chromatogram, with a diverging colour scale and
an optional threshold midpoint.
- Added lp_purity_timeline(): scatter plot of inPurity versus
retention time per sample, with an optional horizontal threshold
line.
- Added lp_purity_distribution(): violin or boxplot distribution of
inPurity scores grouped by sample, with an optional threshold line.
- Added lp_isolation_window(): MS1 spectrum plot annotated with the
isolation window rectangle, precursor m/z dashed line, and inPurity
score as a subtitle.
- Added purity_scores slot to lcmsPlotDataContainer for storing
per-scan purity data extracted from purityA@puritydf.
- Added msPurity to Suggests in DESCRIPTION.

[levi](/packages/levi)
----

                        Changes in version 2.0.0                        

Statistical corrections

- leviSingleCellInteractionTFCE() now tests per-donor interaction
  contrasts, (stim - ctrl) in a cell type minus (stim - ctrl) in the
  reference type, with a limma-trend one-sample moderated t and a
  within-donor sign-flip null. The previous refit of
  ~ donor + type * condition on swapped labels was valid only under the
  global null: with a shared condition effect and no interaction it
  rejected in 85% of null data sets (now 3%, attainable level 3.1%).
  Cell types are aligned on their shared genes before the contrasts are
  formed; stacking matrices filtered per type had mixed genes across
  rows or aborted.

- leviBulkGraphInference() refits the whole DESeq2 pipeline in every
  permutation by default (refit_dispersions = TRUE). Keeping the
  label-dependent size factors and dispersions fixed gave a
  family-wise error rate about three times the attainable level; that
  mode now warns that it has no level guarantee. Cook-outlier
  replacement is switched off so that observed and permuted fits use
  the
  same pipeline.

- leviGraphMoran() computes local P-values by conditional permutation
  (each node keeps its own score; its neighbours are drawn from the
  other scores), as in spdep and GeoDa, and centres the two-sided
  P-values on the null expectations. Total permutation called an
  isolated outlier with iid neighbours significant in about half of
  null
  data sets.

- Documentation of the node-label and rewiring tests (levi(),
  leviGraphGetisOrd(), leviGraphSpectrum(),
  leviGraphWeightedTopology(),
  leviGraphRewiringInference(), leviGraphTFCERewiring()) states that
  their nulls treat scores as exchangeable over nodes and reject under
  co-expression or degree association without any condition effect.

Behaviour changes (these alter landscapes and regional P-values

- Nodes without a measurement have weight zero in the landscape, and so
  do the edge midpoints that touch them. They used to enter the average
  at the neutral value with full weight, which pulled the surface to
  "no
  change" around every unmeasured gene. Unmeasured parts of the network
  now drop out of the average and out of the silhouette; the weights
  are
  the same in every permutation, and the result stores them in
  $metadata$support_weights. The effect grows with the share of missing
  nodes; a complete expression table gives the same result as before.

- Reciprocal edges (A-B and B-A) and self-loops count once in the
  landscape, as they already did in the graph tests. A network file
  that
  lists both directions no longer puts two support points on each edge
  midpoint.

- leviFromEdges() scales both axes of the layout with one factor, so
  the
  aspect ratio of the layout is kept. Each axis used to be stretched to
  [1, 100] on its own, which made every layout square. Landscapes of
  networks laid out by leviFromEdges() change; shipped files are
  unaffected.

- The peak of a region (PeakRow, PeakCol) is the first cell within 1e-9
  of the extreme score. It was the first cell with the exact extreme,
  which on a plateau depended on the last bit of the surface and
  differed between x86_64 and arm64. The peak score, mass and P-values
  are unchanged; the peak cell of a region on a plateau can move.

- The thresholds of the C++ TFCE are computed without fused
  multiply-add, so that it agrees with the R reference on arm64.

- permutation_method = "auto" no longer exceeds n_perm. It enumerates
  every label assignment only when that takes at most n_perm
  permutations (and at most max_exact); otherwise it draws n_perm Monte
  Carlo permutations. It used to enumerate up to max_exact assignments
  whatever n_perm said, so an 8 vs 8 design with n_perm = 99 ran 12,869
  permutations. With the default n_perm = 999, designs with more than
  1,000 assignments (7 vs 7 and larger) are now sampled; use
  permutation_method = "exact" for the full enumeration.

New options (default behaviour and P-values unchanged

- levi(region_statistic = "standardised") measures a region on the
  landscape standardised by its standard deviation under node-label
  permutation, computed analytically from the layout and the weights
  (landscape_null_scale(); it matches the permutation value to within a
  few per cent). A fixed excess over 0.5 favours sparse parts of the
  network, where the null surface varies most. The threshold is then in
  standard deviations (default 2), mass and PeakScore are on the 0.5 +
  Z
  scale, and the same field is used by the node-label and sample-label
  tests. The default, "excess", is unchanged; the displayed landscape
  is
  the same either way.

- leviGraphSpectrum() and leviGraphWeightedTopology() take 'strata'
  (NULL, "degree" or one value per node) to permute scores within
  groups
  of nodes, for example degree bins, as an approximation to removing
  the
  dependence of the score on degree. leviGraphMoran(),
  leviGraphGetisOrd(), leviGraphSpectrum() and
  leviGraphWeightedTopology()
  warn (class "levi_degree_warning") when the scores correlate with log
  degree.

- leviGraphSpectrum() adds DegreeNormalisedEnergy and its P-value, the
  Rayleigh quotient of the normalised Laplacian. The plain EnergyP is
  the
  same test as Geary's C (the sum of squared scores does not change
  under permutation); the degree-normalised version is not.

- levi(bandwidth_edges = ) sets the kernel width as a multiple of the
  median edge length, independent of the network and of the zoom;
  smoothValueInput is ignored when it is given. The default keeps the
  slider.

- The graph and pseudobulk tests take 'sig_level' (default 0.05) for
  their Significant and GlobalSignificant flags; it also feeds the
  warning about the smallest attainable P-value. It does not change any
  P-value.

- leviGraphMoran() and leviGraphGetisOrd() warn, with the condition
  class
  "levi_resolution_warning", when n_perm is too small for BH across the
  nodes to declare a single node significant.

- leviGraphGetisOrd() adds PConditional and PConditionalAdjusted, a
  conditional-permutation P-value that keeps the node's own score fixed
  like the local Moran (the unconditional P rejected 11% of extreme
  nodes under an iid null, the conditional one 4%). The node-wise tests
  carry a 'Null' column naming the permutation null.

- leviGraphTFCEInference(), leviGraphTFCEFreedmanLane(),
  leviGraphClusterInference(), leviBulkGraphInference() and
  leviReplicateInference() warn (class "levi_group_order_warning") when
  'test' and 'control' are taken from the order in which the group
  labels appear, and the first four store them in the result as $test
  and $control.

- leviFromDESeq2(value = "stat") and leviFromLimma(value = "t") carry
  the
  Wald or moderated t-statistic instead of the fold change.

- levi() stores $metadata$diagnostics: number of components, share of
  nodes in the largest one, diameter, median edge length, the kernel
  width in edge lengths and the share of the grid inside the
  silhouette.

Performance (results unchanged

- The graph TFCE statistic runs in C++ with union-find components
  (src/tfce.cpp), 25 to 40 times faster on a 1,000-node graph and equal
  to the plain-R version (kept as .tfceR() for the tests) to a relative
  4e-16.

- The permutation loops of levi(), leviReplicateInference() and
  leviSingleCellRegionalInference() compute the combined-signal
  landscape
  with the smoothed occupancy cached (landscape_occupancy() and
  landscape_m1()): one blur per draw instead of four, bit-identical to
  landscape_gauss(). levi() with n_perm = 200 on the 30-node medusa
  network at resolution 100 went from 46 s to 8 s with identical
  p-values and the same random-number stream.

- The maximum regional mass of every null draw is found in C++
  (src/region_mass.cpp; the R version stays as .maximumRegionMassR()).

- leviBulkGraphInference() estimates the size factors once, reads the
  Wald statistic from the fitted coefficients and silences DESeq2's
  per-permutation messages: about 20% faster with identical statistics
  and p-values.

- leviGraphMoran() and leviGraphGetisOrd() fold the null into running
  counts in blocks of 250 draws instead of keeping a draws x nodes
  matrix, so memory no longer grows with n_perm (identical P-values).

- The C++ entry points skip the random-number scope, and the shared
  library registers its routines (useDynLib(levi, .registration =
  TRUE)).

- tests/testthat/test_characterization.R compares the landscape and
  regional results of levi() on the hub and medusa networks with stored
  values (tolerance 1e-8).

Bug fixes

- leviFromLimma() no longer defaults to the first coefficient, which in
  a ~ group design is the intercept. 'coef' is required when the fit
  has
  several coefficients, and an intercept is refused.

- leviFromSE() accepts sparse (dgCMatrix) and DelayedArray assays
  (MatrixGenerics is now imported). An 'assay_name' that does not exist
  and duplicated gene names are errors instead of a silent fallback to
  the first assay. Averaging the raw "counts" assay warns that the
  Test/Control ratio then depends on sequencing depth.

- leviFromSeurat() now warns, rather than prints a message, that
  FindMarkers() statistics are cell-level.

- The graph and pseudobulk inference functions
  (leviGraphTFCEInference(),
  leviGraphTFCEFreedmanLane(), leviBulkGraphInference() and the
  leviSingleCell*() functions) stop with a clear message when the
  expression has no gene in common with the network, has duplicated
  gene
  names, or 'test'/'control' are not levels of 'groups'. They used to
  return zeros with one warning per permutation or fail inside limma.

- The package license is GPL (>= 2), as stated in DESCRIPTION; the
  stray LICENSE.txt (Apache-2.0) was removed. limma and edgeR, which
  the adapters call, are now in Imports.

- The ALL examples in the vignettes collapse the B/T subtypes, map
  probe
  sets to gene symbols and select a coefficient by name.

- Graph tests stop with an informative error for unnamed scores, fewer
  than three matched nodes, an invalid n_perm or an unknown
  fileTypeInput (case is now ignored). In the graph tests (TFCE, Moran,
  Getis-Ord, rewiring) reciprocal edges (A-B and B-A) are counted once,
  and so they are in the landscape (see Behaviour changes).

- leviEnrich(), leviRegionGenes() and leviDiff() explain how to pick
  one
  result when given the list that levi() returns for several
  comparisons. print() of a result no longer fails when both regional
  and cell-wise P-values are present.

- Permutation P-values are counted by binary search on the sorted null
  (same values; memory O(n) instead of O(n x nodes)).

- Vignette HTML files and tests/testthat/Rplots.pdf are excluded from
  the build.

                       Changes in version 1.99.4                        

Bug fixes

- Pseudobulk preserves grouping labels containing delimiters and gives
  count columns unique names. Missing grouping labels are rejected.

- Calibration includes datasets without regions as non-rejections in
  error rates and power; saved summaries use the corrected
  denominators.

- Degree-weighting documentation no longer claims unit incident sums.

- The Shiny camera observer waits for an actual relayout event before
  reading Plotly event data, avoiding warnings before 3D is rendered.

                       Changes in version 1.99.0                        

Overview

- This is the Bioconductor devel version of the rewritten package; it
  will be released as levi 2.0.0. The landscape core was rebuilt, an
  inference layer with permutation tests was added, the Shiny interface
  now shares every computation with script mode, and adapters bring
  data in from the main Bioconductor and single-cell workflows.

Landscape core

- The landscape is computed as a Gaussian-kernel weighted average
  (normalised convolution) instead of an unweighted mean over the k
  nearest points. Every landscape value is a convex combination of the
  input signals and lies within their range; data with no variation
  gives the neutral value 0.5 at any smoothing and any network density.

- The previous implementation injected a zero-signal point at every
  background grid cell, which divided the landscape amplitude by k
  (about 11% of the colour scale at the default smoothing), put
  result$scores off the documented [0, 1] scale and made peaks
  unreachable on sparse networks. All ten Expected results assertions
  of the bundled toy datasets now pass (three passed before).

- The network silhouette is carried by the sum of kernel weights.
  Cells outside the network return NA and are drawn in a background
  colour, so "no network here" and "network present, minimal
  expression" are no longer the same value.

- The kernel is separable, so the convolution runs as two 1-D passes.
  medusa.dat at resolution 135 went from 28.5 s to about 12 ms and the
  cost no longer grows with network size.

- New argument edge_weighting in levi(): "midpoint" (default) keeps
  the historical deposit of one support point per edge midpoint,
  "degree" weights the midpoint of edge (i, j) by (1/d_i + 1/d_j)/2,
  reducing their influence relative to unit weights, and "none" smooths
  the
  node values alone. The choice and the weights are recorded in the
  result metadata and reused by the sample-label null.

- The grid always leaves room for the smoothed silhouette. The margin
  used to be the zoom alone, while the kernel carries occupancy about
  20% beyond the outermost node, so landscapes were clipped wherever a
  node sat near the border. zoomValueInput now adds up to 20% on top
  of a frame that fits the silhouette (0 = widest, 100 = tightest).

- contrastValueInput and smoothValueInput keep their 0-100 range but
  now set the occupancy threshold of the silhouette and the Gaussian
  width in grid cells. The width is scaled to resolutionValueInput, so
  changing the resolution no longer changes the apparent smoothing,
  and smoothing no longer changes the value scale.

- The same transformed signal feeds the surface, the scores, the peaks
  and the tests. Ratio scores keep the absolute Test/(Test+Control)
  scale; the old max() normalisation of the per-condition matrices was
  dropped.

- SigCoordPiso(), matrix_entrada() and matrix_saida() were replaced by
  landscape_gauss(); nearest_node_grid() labels each grid cell with its
  closest node.

Signal modes and input guards

- New argument signal_mode: "ratio" (default) for counts, TPM, FPKM
  and linear proteomics; "logfc" (sigmoid of the log fold change, with
  steepness logfc_k) for RMA microarray, VST/rlog and single-cell
  avg_log2FC; "zscore" for multi-condition or heterogeneous-scale
  data. Single-column logFC input uses readExpColumn("logFC-logFC")
  with signal_mode = "logfc".

- expressionLog back-transforms from log2 only in ratio mode; in the
  other modes it is ignored with a message, because log-scale data
  must stay in log2 for the fold change.

- Ratio mode warns when the expression data contain negative values,
  which invert the landscape; Test + Control == 0 is reported and set
  to the neutral score instead of escaping as Inf.

- The [0, 1] range of LandscapeScore is enforced for every signal mode
  in one place and fixed by a test.

- Duplicated identifiers are still averaged, but the number collapsed
  is reported; a warning is raised when no identifier of the network
  matches the expression data, and a message states how many nodes
  have no expression value.

- expressionInput accepts a data.frame or matrix as well as a file
  path, and the stg branch accepts in-memory node and edge tables.

- The error for a missing expression column now reads "Column not
  found in the expression data".

Result object, scores, peaks and regions

- levi() returns an object of class "levi_result" with a print()
  method summarising the comparison, the scored nodes, the score
  range, the strongest and weakest genes, the peaks and valleys and
  whether a permutation test ran. The fields are unchanged, so
  result$scores and the rest keep working.

- result$scores ranks every gene by LandscapeScore in [0, 1];
  result$peaks lists local maxima and minima with the nearest gene,
  matrix position and score.

- Explicit eight-connected landscape regions with direction, area,
  mass, peak, centroid and member cells. Without permutations they
  remain descriptive; with them they carry regional p-values.

- Result provenance is recorded and leviDiff() rejects incompatible
  comparisons.

Inference layer

- Permutation test in levi() with n_perm, sig_level and perm_side
  ("both", "over", "under"). result$pvalues holds $over and $under
  matrices; 2D figures overlay the sig_level contours, dashed for
  over-expression and dotted for under-expression, and the 3D surface
  traces the same boundary.

- inference_unit = "region" (now the default) runs a maximum
  excess-mass permutation test over eight-connected regions in both
  directions, keeps the null maxima, reports a spatial p-value per
  region and draws regional boundaries. inference_unit = "cell" keeps
  the legacy per-cell test, which the Shiny contours still use. Both
  directional families are adjusted jointly (BY by default) and the
  raw p-values remain available.

- Node-label permutations shuffle only the signals, never the
  coordinates, so the silhouette and the denominator are computed
  once. p-values use (k+1)/(n+1), so none is reported as exactly 0.
  Optional perm_strata shuffles within bins of expression, detection
  rate or degree.

- New leviReplicateInference(): regional maximum-mass inference by
  permuting biological sample labels, optionally within blocks.
  Regional figures label only the regions that pass sig_level.

- New leviAdjustPathways() to correct regional results across a
  family of pathway networks, and leviRegionGenes() to rank the genes
  that contribute to a region.

- New graph statistics on the network itself: leviGraphMoran()
  (global and local autocorrelation from the same permutations, with
  BH-adjusted local p-values), leviGraphGetisOrd() (hotspots and
  coldspots with PTwoSided and PAdjusted; Significant uses the
  adjusted value), leviGraphSpectrum() (Laplacian smoothness and
  low-frequency energy; the eigenvector order was corrected and the
  decomposition is computed once) and leviGraphWeightedTopology().

- New sample-label graph tests: leviGraphClusterInference() for
  connected cluster mass, leviGraphTFCEInference() for threshold-free
  cluster enhancement, leviGraphTFCEFreedmanLane() for residual
  permutation under covariates, leviGraphRewiringInference() and
  leviGraphTFCERewiring() for degree-preserving rewiring nulls, and
  leviBulkGraphInference() on DESeq2 counts.

- leviBulkGraphInference() keeps the observed size factors and
  dispersions fixed across permutations by default
  (refit_dispersions = FALSE) and uses one dispersion estimator for
  the observed statistic and every draw, falling back to gene-wise
  dispersions when the trend fit fails; the choice is returned as
  dispersion_estimator.

- Single-cell pseudobulk tests: leviPseudobulk() aggregates counts per
  sample and cell type; leviSingleCellRegionalInference(),
  leviSingleCellGraphInference(), leviSingleCellTFCEInference(),
  leviSingleCellInteractionTFCE() and
  leviSingleCellTopologyInference() permute within donor. They use
  TMM-normalised log2 CPM and the limma-trend moderated t
  (normalize = "none" restores plain CPM) and drop genes with fewer
  than 10 counts in two pseudobulks before the fit, always keeping the
  network genes; the interaction coefficient is located by its exact
  design column name.

- Graph TFCE builds the igraph object once per call and recomputes the
  components only when the set of nodes above the threshold changes,
  instead of rebuilding the graph at each of the 100 integration steps
  of every permutation. The single-cell TFCE example runs in under a
  second instead of about 6 s; results are identical.

- All permutation tests share one engine with a BPPARAM argument.
  SerialParam is the default; MulticoreParam() and SnowParam() give
  identical results because all randomness stays in the calling
  process. Sparse adjacency matrices are used throughout (Matrix in
  Imports).

- A warning states when a design cannot reach the significance level.
  Under exact enumeration of a design balanced within every block,
  swapping every label negates each statistic and the tests take
  their maximum over both directions, so arrangements come in tied
  pairs and the attainable floor is 2/n_possible, not 1/n_possible:
  3 vs 3 unblocked (20 arrangements) has a floor of 0.10 and four
  paired donors (16) a floor of 0.125, and both now warn at alpha =
  0.05. Monte Carlo draws keep the floor 1/(n_perm + 1). The floor
  is returned as p_floor beside exact and possible_permutations by
  leviReplicateInference() (in metadata), the graph cluster, TFCE,
  DESeq2 and single-cell tests; it applies to the joint p-values
  (PGlobal, PSpatial), while the per-direction POver and PUnder keep
  1/n_possible. Arrangements are counted with
  choose() before enumeration, so unblocked designs with more than
  about 30 samples no longer abort. Blocks holding a single condition
  contribute one fixed arrangement instead of an error.

- Global and per-direction p-values of the TFCE and graph-cluster
  tests count a null maximum within a relative 1e-12 of the observed
  value as a tie, as the regional test already did. Under exact
  enumeration the complement arrangement reproduces the observed
  statistic up to rounding, so these p-values no longer come out as
  1/n or 2/n depending on BLAS rounding; the joint p-values are now
  at least 2/n_possible.

- leviFromSeurat() states in a message and in its documentation that
  FindMarkers() output is cell-level and pseudoreplicated for
  donor-level inference: use it for visualisation and node-label
  tests, and run donor-level inference through leviPseudobulk() and
  the single-cell functions.

- leviSingleCellRegionalInference() builds the null landscapes with the
  logfc_k passed through '...', as leviReplicateInference() does. The
  null used to be computed at logfc_k = 1 whatever the observed
  landscape used, so with logfc_k < 1 the null was steeper than the
  observed surface and the landscape PSpatial was conservative (and
  anti-conservative with logfc_k > 1); results at the default
  logfc_k = 1 are unchanged.

Data adapters and network construction

- leviFromDESeq2(), leviFromEdgeR(), leviFromLimma() and
  leviFromSeurat() convert differential expression tables to levi
  input; leviFromSE(), leviFromExpressionSet() and leviFromBioc()
  read SummarizedExperiment and ExpressionSet objects, selecting
  samples by name, index or colData condition.

- leviFromSTRING() builds a network from the STRING database from a
  vector of gene symbols, and leviFromEdges() builds one from a plain
  edge list (data.frame, matrix or igraph graph), computing a layout
  with igraph (fr, kk, lgl, dh or circle) scaled to the range levi
  expects. Both share the same layout routine and report interactions
  dropped for a missing endpoint.

- leviFromSTRING() returns one edge per interacting pair. STRING lists
  every interaction in both directions and the graph from STRINGdb
  carries two parallel edges per pair, so $edges, the "N edges"
  message and the layout saw every interaction twice. The landscape
  core and the graph tests already kept one support point per
  distinct edge row, and Kamada-Kawai layouts do not depend on edge
  multiplicity, so results built with layout = "kk" are unchanged;
  Fruchterman-Reingold layouts of STRING networks move, and edge
  counts reported from $edges halve.

- Network parsers live in one place, one per format (dat, dyn, net,
  stg), and are shared by script mode and the interface.

Comparison, enrichment and export helpers

- leviGrid() arranges several results side by side (patchwork,
  cowplot or gridExtra); leviDiff() subtracts two landscapes cell by
  cell into a diverging map.

- leviEnrich() runs GO and KEGG enrichment on the top and bottom genes
  of result$scores through clusterProfiler; the KEGG background
  identifier mapping was fixed.

- plot3d draws an interactive plotly surface next to the 2D map, with
  the significance boundary when a test ran. New leviSave3D() writes
  it to html, png, jpeg, webp, svg, pdf or tiff from a chosen camera
  position.

- Contour layers drop out-of-silhouette cells before stat_contour()
  and say when there is no curve to draw instead of warning.

Shiny interface

- The interface no longer compiles its own copy of the C++ core at
  startup and no longer keeps private copies of network parsing, the
  permutation test, the palettes or the figure. It calls the same
  routines as script mode, so no compiler is needed and the two paths
  cannot drift (they had: the same palette name gave different
  colours and the scale arrows sat at different heights).

- The 2D landscape and the 3D surface are shown in two tabs; the
  gene, node score, peak and region tables are tabs of their own
  below the figure, each with a CSV download. "Genes" lists what was
  brushed on the map. The 3D tab has a "Download 3D (HTML)" button
  that keeps the rotated view, and the toolbar PNG export was raised
  to 1600 x 1200 at scale 2.

- Settings tab exposes signal_mode, logfc_k, n_perm, perm_side,
  sig_level and a "Test unit" selector. The regional test runs by
  default and the significant regions are outlined and labelled as in
  script mode; a permutation progress bar reports each iteration.

- Gene highlight accepts several genes, draws one circle per gene at
  its own grid cell and offers a colour selector; "Label peaks on map"
  overlays gene names at the detected peaks.

- The interface could not compute anything under igraph >= 2.0
  because a deprecation warning was caught as fatal and reported as
  "Incorrect file format". graph_from_edgelist() is used and warnings
  are shown as notifications while the computation continues; a file
  without a trailing newline is read instead of rejected.

- tests/testthat/test_gui_parity.R drives the server with
  shiny::testServer and requires the same scores, surface and, under
  a fixed seed, the same p-values as script mode.

Documentation, datasets and validation

- Four vignettes: "levi" (introduction, workflow and every control of
  the interface, with new screenshots), "levi_guide" (Bioconductor
  data, adapters and STRING), "levi_inference" (which null answers
  which question, the p-value floor of small designs, BPPARAM and a
  reporting checklist) and "levi_validation" (type I error, power and
  layout sensitivity from offline simulations, plus the airway
  dexamethasone experiment). All vignettes cite their methods and data
  sources from a shared bibliography.

- Twelve self-contained scripts in inst/scripts/ with a README, from
  first steps to degree weighting, calibration and the airway
  preprocessing; they run on the bundled data alone.

- Toy datasets in inst/extdata/, each documented with expected
  results: hub, gradient, bimodal, flat, sparse, logfc and
  multi-comparison, beside the original medusa data, the airway
  summaries and the validation tables.

- Real-data integration tests replay the analyses of the supplement
  (airway, GSE10072 and Kang 2018 on STRING and KEGG networks) and are
  skipped unless LEVI_INTEGRATION is set.

- Every argument of the inference functions is documented and the
  examples run on the hub dataset. Examples that need objects the
  user must supply (a DESeq2, edgeR, limma or Seurat fit, a
  SummarizedExperiment, real gene symbols for STRING or
  org.Hs.eg.db) are marked \dontrun so R CMD check --as-cran passes.

- Title, Description and biocViews describe the inference layer
  (RNASeq, GraphAndNetwork and StatisticalMethod added). NAMESPACE
  uses specific importFrom() directives; knitr, rmarkdown and
  BiocStyle moved to Suggests. Comments, test names and messages are
  all in English.

Breaking changes

- The argument geneSymbolnput of levi() was renamed geneSymbolInput.
  No alias is kept; positional calls are unaffected.

- Every landscape changes with the new core, so figures produced with
  levi 1.x are not comparable to figures produced with this version.

- inference_unit defaults to "region"; use inference_unit = "cell"
  for the former per-cell test.

Bug fixes

- Operator precedence in the DAT parser (3:(delimiter-1)).

- C++ buffer overflow in the former matrix_saida() and matrixOutFun()
  when smoothValue >= h.

- colorSet() returned inside an else block; duplicate coord_fixed()
  call; deprecated size aesthetic in annotate() segments.

- Internal networkNodesInput renamed networkCoordinatesInput to match
  the public API.

- edgeR test-object conversion, medusa validation on the linear ratio
  scale with a matched smoking category, and the ".logFC" title on
  replicate landscapes.

[limma](/packages/limma)
-----

                 Changes in version 4.0.0 (2026-10-30)                  

- voomLmFit() transferred to limma from the edgeR package.
  Previously, voomLmFit() needed to call edgeR::glmFit() in order
  to identify exact zero fitted values, but voomLmFit() now calls
  a new limma C routine 'poisfit' for the same purpose, removing
  the dependence on edgeR.

- For the purpose of estimating sample weights, voomLmFit() calls
  arrayWeights() with 'method="reml"' if there is no loss of df
  due to exact zero fitted values and 'method="genebygene"'
  otherwise.

- The voomLmFit help page has been expanded, while the voom and
  voomWithQualityWeights help pages now have preambles that point
  users to voomLmFit.

- voomLmFit() now gives priority to 'offset' over 'offset.prior'
  or 'lib.size' and no longer forces the rows of 'offset.prior'
  to add to zero.

- New argument 'contrasts' for voomLmFit(), lmFit(), lm.series()
  and gls.series(), which converts coefficient estimates and
  standard deviations into contrast estimates and standard
  deviations. This argument provides the same functionality as
  calling 'contrasts.fit' on the output object, but with exact
  rather than approximate standard deviations.

- New argument 'nthreads' for voomLmFit(), lmFit(), lm.series(),
  gls.series(), duplicateCorrelation(), and arrayWeights() to
  enable OpenMP parallelization of genewise fits.

- C code backends for lm.series() and gls.series().

- C code backend for duplicateCorrelation().
  duplicateCorrelation() previously called statmod::mixedModel2()
  to estimate genewise correlations, but this functionality is
  now absorbed into the C code. The new code is able to evaluate
  the genewise SVDs needed by mixedModel2() more efficiently than
  was possible for the univariate R function, resulting in
  substantial speed and memory improvements.

- C code backend for .arrayWeightsPrWtsREML(), which is called by
  arrayWeights() when 'method="reml"' and prior weights are set.

- Minor changes to weightedLowess() C code to fit in with the new
  C code elsewhere.

- New function normalizeBetweenSamples(). Similar to
  normalizeBetweenArrays() but works on ELists.

- camera() and cameraPR() now support gene sets as expression
  signatures, whereby a logFC or similar expected directional
  change is provided for each gene in the gene set.

- avearrays() methods for EList and MAList objects now sum the
  weights instead of averaging them. Other matrices are still
  averaged.

- Fix filtering error in Agilent rat case study in User's Guide.

- All the Rd pages have been checked for typos and inconsistent
  formating, especially regarding the reference lists. Reference
  URLs converted to DOIs where possible and some new DOIs added.
  Old statsci.org/smyth/pubs preprint URLs updated to
  gksmyth.github.io/pubs URLs.  Author lists converted to compact
  PubMed style without unnecessary punctuation. A few instances
  of British spellings converted to American spellings.

- Expand changelog.txt entries for limma 1.0 and earlier.

- Minor code update to strsplit2().

- Add test files dupcor.R, gls-series-c.R, lmfit-contrasts.R,
  lm-series-c.R, and voomlmfit-contrasts.R.

[lisaClust](/packages/lisaClust)
---------

                       Changes in version 1.21.13                       

- lisaClust() put regions on the right cells only when cell IDs were
  unique across images; with cell IDs
  that repeat in each image (1, 2, ... per image), most cells were left
  without a region. Regions now go
  back to the cells by position, and results with unique cell IDs are
  unchanged.

- lisa() returns its rows in the order of `cells` rather than grouped
  by image, so its curves can be
  clustered and put back on a SingleCellExperiment or SpatialExperiment
  directly. Input that is already
  ordered by image gives the same matrix as before. Without a cellID
  column, the rows are named cell_1,
  cell_2, ... in the order of `cells`.

- lisa() and lisaClust() stop with a message naming the column when
  image IDs, cell types or coordinates
  are missing (a missing cell type crashed R; a missing image ID
  dropped the cell). Image IDs that are
  factors with unused levels work. lisaClust() checks the length of
  `cellWeights`.

- hatchingPlot() treats a numeric region column as categories instead
  of failing with "Continuous value
  supplied to a discrete scale".

- Deprecated arguments of lisa() are reported as lisa()'s rather than
  lisaClust()'s.

                       Changes in version 1.21.12                       

- Matrix is listed in Suggests (it is used only when `cellWeights` is a
  sparse Matrix), and inhomLocalK()
  documents its internal `membership` argument, clearing the two R CMD
  check warnings.

                       Changes in version 1.21.11                       

- regionBoxPlot() takes `subject`: the shares are then those of each
  patient's cells, all images pooled, one
  point per patient.

- regionMap() turns the region labels upright when there are more than
  six regions, so they do not overlap.

- The vignette is simpler: the example tumours are named rather than
  computed, the group medians come from
  spicyR's colTest() (which now reports them), patients are given as
  `subject`, and the region labels need no
  theme() adjustment. Needs spicyR 1.99.38.

                       Changes in version 1.21.10                       

- Tests pass with a single-threaded BLAS (R's reference BLAS, as on the
  Bioconductor build machines).

                       Changes in version 1.21.9                        

- Cell weights: lisa() and lisaClust() take cellWeights, either a
  vector with one weight in [0, 1] per cell for
  its own cell type (for example a quality score) or a cells x labels
  matrix (base or sparse) of soft cell type
  membership, for example a classifier's confidence. The curves are
  then
  one per label: each neighbour counts towards a label in proportion to
  its weight, and a label's density is its
  summed weight per unit area. Labels may overlap (a group and its
  subtypes). A matrix of 0s and 1s with one 1
  per row gives the curves of the cell types exactly. The weighted
  curves are computed in the shared core
  (localCurvesWeighted()), as in lisaclust.

                       Changes in version 1.21.8                        

- lisa() and lisaClust() with cores > 1 start their workers once per
  call and send them only the number
  of each image, in about eight chunks per worker, instead of forking a
  new process for every chunk.
  BLAS and OpenMP run one thread in each worker during the call
  (RhpcBLASctl, now imported), so OpenBLAS
  no longer starts one thread per core in every worker. Results are
  unchanged.

                       Changes in version 1.21.7                        

- Concave windows are computed by a C++ port of concaveman in the core,
  which gives the same polygon as
  concaveman::concaveman(); concaveman is no longer needed.
  hatchingPlot(), whose default window is
  "concave", works without it again.

                       Changes in version 1.21.6                        

- concaveman moves to Suggests: it is needed only for window =
  "concave".

                       Changes in version 1.21.5                        

- nameRegions() names each region by the marker cell type it is most
  enriched for; regions most enriched
  for the same marker get the same name.

- regionBoxPlot() draws the share of each region in each image, or each
  patient, by group.

- regionMap(type = "table") returns the relative frequency of each cell
  type in each region as a matrix.

- The vignette uses spicyR's colTest() to compare regions between
  groups and tidySpatialExperiment to
  summarise the cells of each image.

                       Changes in version 1.21.4                        

- hatchingPlot(), geom_hatching() and scale_region_manual() have 12
  hatchings instead of 7: none, /, \, -,
  |, x, +, dots, circles, / with dots, \ with dots and - with dots (in
  that order). Regions beyond the
  twelfth are drawn as the first. Legend keys are drawn from the same
  definitions as the hatching.

                       Changes in version 1.21.3                        

- hatchingPlot() and geom_hatching() outline each region by the union
  of the Voronoi tiles of its cells,
  clipped to the window, instead of a grid of nbp x nbp points: the
  outlines follow the cells exactly and
  `nbp` is no longer used. The hatching lines are clipped to each
  outline by polyclip, so they cannot cross
  into another region. Drawing an image of about 6,000 cells takes
  about 3 s, and printing it again 0.8 s.

- The concave window is built without a loop over cells (about 3 times
  faster, same window).

                       Changes in version 1.21.2                        

- A cell now counts itself among the cells of its type (at distance 0),
  as the local indicators are defined in
  Patrick et al. (2023). Before, it was left out of its own count. This
  changes the LISA of every cell for its
  own type, and so the regions; cells with no neighbour within the
  largest radius now have LISA values
  rather than zeros.

- hatchingPlot() and geom_hatching(): a hatching line that passed
  exactly through or touched a corner of a
  region's outline could be counted as crossing it an odd number of
  times, which put later segments of the
  line out of step and drew them across neighbouring regions (with the
  warning "data length is not a
  multiple of split variable"). Crossings now follow a half-open rule,
  so each outline is crossed an even
  number of times.

- geom_hatching() keeps the hatching of the most recently drawn panels,
  so printing a plot again (for
  example when resizing its window) does not recompute it.

                       Changes in version 1.21.1                        

- The neighbour counts and edge corrections of lisa(), lisaClust() and
  inhomLocalK() are computed in C++
  (src/core, shared with the Python package lisaclust): about 8 to 18
  times faster. The edge correction
  intersects each disc with the window exactly instead of through
  spatstat's integer-rounded polygon
  clipping, which changes the LISA by less than 1e-6; regions are
  otherwise unchanged.

- hatchingPlot() and geom_hatching() are about 10 times faster: the
  hatching lines are intersected with the
  region outlines all at once, and the region of each grid point is
  that of the nearest cell, found in
  C++. Equidistant cells vote and a tied vote goes to the first region,
  so the plot no longer depends on the
  random seed.

- Bug fix: lisaClust() assigned the regions to the wrong cells when the
  cells of different images were
  interleaved rather than ordered by image. Regions are now matched to
  cells by their position in the input.
  hatchingPlot() had the same problem with the region column, and now
  also accepts a data.frame.

- Bug fix: regionMap() failed when a cell type had no cells (an unused
  factor level).

- Bug fix: lisaClust() failed on a SpatialExperiment whose coordinates
  are only in spatialCoords().

- lisaClust no longer depends on spicyR, simpleSeg, class, data.table
  or tidyr. The examples use simulated
  data, and the vignette finds tissue domains in triple-negative breast
  cancer and cellular niches in
  colorectal cancer, compared between groups of patients.

[mariner](/packages/mariner)

                       Changes in version 1.13.1                        

New features:

Support for reading .cool and .mcool (cooler) files, contributed by
Sarah Parker.

- pullHicPixels() and pullHicMatrices() now accept .cool and .mcool
files in addition to .hic. File type is detected automatically, so
no change to existing code is required. Functions built on top of
these, such as pileupPixels(), pileupDomains(), pileupBoundaries(),
and calcLoopEnrichment(), therefore accept cooler files as well.

- coolStraw() extracts a sparse contact matrix from a cooler file,
mirroring the interface of strawr::straw().

- readCoolChroms(), readCoolBpResolutions(), and readCoolNormTypes()
report the chromosomes, resolutions, and normalizations available in
a cooler file.

Limitations:

- Only matrix = "observed" is supported for cooler files. Expected
and
observed/expected matrices remain .hic only.

- A single call cannot mix .hic and cooler files.
