[MassSpecWavelet](/packages/MassSpecWavelet)
---------------

                 Changes in version 1.79.2 (2026-07-05)                 

- tuneInPeakInfo(): Fix several crashes:

- A peak whose local refinement window contains no usable ridges
(e.g. a quiet/flat neighborhood, or a window near the edge of
the spectrum with too few scales to search) no longer crashes
with Error in strsplit(ridgeName, "_") : non-character argument;
the peak is now reported as unprocessed instead.
- Calling tuneInPeakInfo() with peakIndex/peakScale directly
(instead of majorPeakInfo) no longer crashes with Error in
names<-.

- Deprecated the internal, unexported functions getRidgeValue(),
i2u(), u2i(), mzInd2vRange(), mzV2indRange() and smoothDWT(). These
functions appear to be unused, both internally in MassSpecWavelet
and by known downstream packages, and are scheduled for removal in a
future release. If you rely on any of them (e.g. via :::), please
open an issue at https://github.com/zeehio/MassSpecWavelet/issues.

- Migrated the unit test suite from RUnit to testthat (3rd edition).
Tests now live in tests/testthat/ instead of inst/tests/, following
the standard testthat package layout. Significant increased in test
coverage.

                 Changes in version 1.79.1 (2026-07-05)                 

- identifyMajorPeaks(): Fix Error in strsplit(ridgeName, "_") :
non-character argument crash when no ridges are found (e.g. for a
flat/constant input signal). An empty (but well-formed) result is
now returned instead.

- getRidge(): Fix ridge name/lookup mismatches on high resolution
spectra (m/z indices at or above 1e5). Ridge indices were internally
promoted from integer to double partway through the tracing loop,
and R's default number-to-string coercion uses scientific notation
for large "round" doubles (e.g. 200000 -> "2e+05") but never for
integers. The same peak could therefore end up keyed under two
different strings, causing the internal ridge lookup to silently
miss and ridges to be dropped or duplicated. Ridge names are now
always built with a representation- independent formatting helper.
Thanks to drobertsicl for reporting the issue and suggesting the
fix. Closes #8

[MeLSI](/packages/MeLSI)
-----

                        Changes in version 1.1.7                        

- Performance: the weak-learner metric optimizer
(optimize_weak_learner_robust, the hot path of ensemble metric
learning) is now a C++ kernel (melsi_opt_weak_learner in
src/melsi_fstat.cpp, via Rcpp). Profiling showed this
gradient-descent loop accounted for ~83% of total runtime; the C++
port runs it ~4.6x faster, for roughly ~2x end-to-end speedup,
composing with the 1.1.6 F-statistic kernel and BPPARAM parallelism.
- Reproducibility: results are bit-faithful to the R implementation.
The C++ loop draws its within/between-class pairs with R's own index
sampler (R_unif_index), so it consumes the global RNG stream
identically to the previous sample()-based loop. End-to-end
F-statistics reproduce 1.1.6 to floating-point precision (~1e-15
relative) with no p-value changes.

                        Changes in version 1.1.6                        

- Performance: the PERMANOVA pseudo-F statistic is now computed by a
fused C++ kernel (src/melsi_fstat.cpp, via Rcpp) that accumulates
squared distances in a single pass over sample pairs, instead of
materialising and squaring the full n x n distance matrix in R. This
speeds up the F-statistic by ~4x and the overall analysis by
roughly 1.3-2.2x (most for two-group / pairwise analyses), and
composes multiplicatively with BPPARAM parallelism.
- Numerical note: results are statistically equivalent but not
bit-identical to 1.1.5. Computing squared distances directly (no
sqrt round-trip) and summing in a different order changes
F-statistics at the ~1e-12 relative level. Across extensive testing
no permutation p-value changed; in rare boundary cases a p-value
could differ by a single permutation step (1/(n_perms+1)). Set a
larger n_perms if exact reproducibility of borderline p-values
matters.

                        Changes in version 1.1.5                        

- Dependencies: vegan moved from Imports to Suggests. The package
computes the PERMANOVA F-statistic directly and no longer calls
vegan::adonis2() at runtime, so vegan (and its transitive
dependencies) is no longer installed for users; it is needed only to
build the comparison section of the vignette.
- Cleanup: removed unused stats::aov, stats::as.dist, and
stats::t.test imports and an unreachable t-test pre-filtering branch
in the metric learner. Pre-filtering is handled by
apply_conservative_prefiltering() as before.
- UX: permutation progress is now shown with a single progress bar
instead of one message per permutation.
- UX: melsi() gains an optional seed argument for reproducible runs
and now returns an object of class "melsi" with a print() method
summarising the F-statistic, p-value, and top features. The returned
object is still a list, so existing $ access is unchanged.
- All statistical results (F-statistics, p-values, feature weights)
are numerically identical to 1.1.4; these changes do not alter the
method.

                        Changes in version 1.1.4                        

- Documentation: document the BPPARAM argument to melsi() for
parallel
permutation testing. The argument has been available since the move
to a BiocParallel backend; this release adds a worked example to the
README and vignette and surfaces it in NEWS. Pass any
BiocParallelParam object (for example MulticoreParam(workers = 8))
to distribute the permutation loop across cores; the default (NULL)
runs permutations sequentially.

                        Changes in version 1.1.3                        

- Performance: additional ~22% speedup via diagonal vector storage in
ensemble aggregation (eliminates B x p^2 matrix allocation per
permutation) and rejection sampling in gradient optimizer
(eliminates setdiff() allocation per iteration). Combined
with 1.1.2, total speedup is ~2.9x over 1.1.1.

                        Changes in version 1.1.2                        

- Performance: 2.3x faster permutation testing via vectorized
prefiltering, direct PERMANOVA F-statistic (replacing adonis2
overhead), and diagonal metric matrix optimization (replacing O(p^3)
eigen decomposition with O(p) column scaling). Results are
numerically identical; p-values unchanged.
- Suppress spurious NaN warnings from log2 fold-change on
CLR-transformed data.

[methylclock](/packages/methylclock)
-----------

                        Changes in version 2.0.0                        

(In Bioconductor devel as the 1.99.x series, following the convention
for a major rewrite; it becomes 2.0.0 at the next release.)

A ground-up rewrite. The package now computes 44 epigenetic clocks
behind a declarative registry, runs out-of-core on HDF5 through
BigDataStatMeth, and ships a toolbox to compare, interpret and
quality-control the results.

Architecture

- Declarative clock registry (clock_register(), clock_list(),
clock_info(), and the shipped clock_catalog table): one entry per
clock — target, engine, what it estimates, native platforms,
training tissue, licence and citation. Adding a clock is adding a
row, not editing the engine.
- Manifest-backed resource resolver (mcd_resource(), mcd_backends()):
coefficients are resolved through a configurable backend chain — a
local mirror, ExperimentHub, or a direct Zenodo download — and
normalized to one canonical shape on entry (normalize_coef()).
- Three predictor engines in this release: linear (including models
with squared-beta terms), counter (mitotic clocks, including the
parametric epiTOC2), and neural networks (AltumAge with weights from
HDF5; a compiled Bayesian network).
- A unified methylclock() entry point; DNAmAge() and DNAmGA() remain
as compatible wrappers.

Clocks

- 44 clocks: chronological (including the cross-platform Garma 2024
model, the only one here native to EPICv2), biological (PhenoAge),
pace of ageing (DunedinPACE), telomere length, gestational (cord
blood and placenta), neonatal (the four NEOage clocks), mitotic
counters, causal clocks, and nine trait/exposure EpiScores (opt-in
via target = "trait").
- Every clock declares the tissue it was trained on, the quantity it
estimates with its units (the four NEOage clocks report
post-menstrual and postnatal age in weeks; Levine, phenotypic age;
TL, telomere length in kilobases), and its native arrays. The arrays
are where a clock was built and validated, not where it can be
computed — CpG coverage decides that. Restrictively licensed clocks
are implemented and clearly marked.

Scale

- Input can be an in-memory matrix or an HDF5-backed matrix;
whole-array clocks (BLUP, EN) stream from disk without materializing
the array, and the heavy algebra runs through BigDataStatMeth.
mc_to_hdf5() converts a matrix or a text file once, to work on disk
from then on.
- Results follow the same policy: HDF5 as the durable store with an
in-memory cache, and persist() to keep a session result.

Missing data

- Configurable imputation: impute = "mean", "reference", "none", or
"knn" — a C++ k-nearest-neighbours imputation that runs out-of-core
on HDF5, exposed also as imputeKNN(); plus a per-sample coverage
floor (min.perc.sample) so heavily imputed samples are not passed
off as measured ones.

Interpretation toolbox

- Cell composition and acceleration: cellCounts(), ageAcceleration()
(ageAcc, residual, and the cell-adjusted residualCells), plus the
canonical named measures: IEAA() (Horvath residual adjusted for the
seven immune covariates of Chen et al. 2016, the three rare subsets
computed from published CpG estimators) and EEAA() (the fixed-weight
Hannum blend of Chen et al. 2016, with the parameters published in
European patent EP 3 494 210 B1). ageAccelerationChen() computes a
related Chen-style blend whose Klemera-Doubal weights are
re-estimated from the data at hand; its output column is chenAcc, to
keep the EEAA name for the canonical measure.
- Plots: predicted-vs-age (per group), clock agreement,
distributions,
densities by group (overlay, mirror and ridge layouts), acceleration
by group, forest/dumbbell group differences, per-sample discordance,
sample PCA, Bland–Altman — one consistent theme, colour-blind-safe
palettes.
- Reference ranges (plotReferenceRange()): percentile bands of a
named
reference cohort with the user's samples on top; nine shipped
reference cohorts spanning four continents, each described by what
it is.
- Longitudinal tools: clockTrajectories(), trajectoryRates() (each
subject's pace, with its uncertainty caveats) and
plotTrajectories(), plus a real repeated-measures example dataset.
- Quality control: clockAccuracy(), sampleQC() (outlier score and
clock discordance) and qcReport() — an HTML report where every
section carries a written reading of its own numbers.

Data

- Only estimates and phenotypes ship with the package; coefficient
tables live in methylclockData/Zenodo, and validation used frozen
public cohorts. Bundled datasets: clock_catalog, methylclock_demo,
methylclock_validation, methylclock_references,
methylclock_longitudinal, methylclock_smoking, methylclock_cells,
methylclock_betas.

Compatibility notes

- Estimates were verified against the previous implementations; the
one deliberate change: Wu uses adult.age = 48, the value of the
clock's publication.
- EPICv2 arrays: the pre-2023 clocks do not apply to EPICv2 probe
names and say so rather than guessing; the Garma model runs on
EPICv2 natively. A proper probe mapping for the older clocks is
planned.

[methylSig](/packages/methylSig)
---------

                       Changes in version 1.26.0                        

NEW FEATURES

- diff_methylsig() has local_disp and local_meth parameters, which
  choose
  whether local information (local_window_size > 0) is used for the
  dispersion estimate and degrees of freedom, the group methylation
  estimates and likelihood ratio, or both (issue #47). Both are TRUE by
  default, which gives the same results as before. These were the
  local.disp and local.meth options of methylSigCalc() before 0.5.0.

- diff_dss_test() has a covariate_percentiles parameter, which sets the
  percentiles used to group samples by a numerical
  methylation_group_column
  (issue #44). The default, c(25, 75), is the same grouping as before.

- diff_dss_test() checks the contrast before testing. A contrast of the
  wrong size gives an error with the number of values it needs and the
  columns of diff_fit$X they correspond to, in order, e.g.
  "1: (Intercept)" and "2: Typenormal". A message says what the
  contrast
  tests, e.g. "Testing Typenormal = 0", so a contrast that is the right
  size but tests the wrong coefficient is easier to catch.

- The contrast can be a vector as well as a matrix, and named values
  (or
  row names) are matched to the columns of diff_fit$X by name.
  Contrasts
  with NA values, a column of zeros, or linearly dependent columns give
  an error.

SIGNIFICANT USER-VISIBLE CHANGES

- diff_dss_test() with a numeric methylation_group_column reports
  methylation rates the other way around, so they agree with the
  covariate. The case group (meth_case) is now the samples at or above
  the
  upper covariate percentile, and the control group (meth_control) the
  samples at or below the lower one. meth_diff is high minus low, and
  direction is Hyper when methylation increases with the covariate,
  which
  is the sign of stat for a contrast on the covariate. Before, the low
  group was the case group, so a locus gaining methylation with the
  covariate was labeled Hypo with a negative meth_diff. Results with
  character or factor columns, and the test statistics and p-values,
  are
  unchanged.

- The example data sets (bsseq_stranded, bsseq_destranded,
  bsseq_multichrom, promoters_gr) are no longer lazy-loaded, as
  Bioconductor recommends. Load them with data(), e.g.
  data(promoters_gr, package = 'methylSig'), as the examples and
  vignettes
  already do.

BUG FIXES

- diff_methylsig() used the wrong log likelihood for the unmethylated
  reads
  when local information was used for the methylation estimates
  (local_window_size > 0 and local_meth = TRUE): the term for the
  unmethylated reads was missing the dispersion, lgamma((1 - mu) +
  1e-100)
  instead of lgamma((1 - mu) * phi + 1e-100). This inflated the
  likelihood
  ratio statistic and gave many false positives. For example, on 2,374
  CpGs of bsseqData's BS.cancer.ex with a 200 bp window and group
  labels
  that mix cancer and normal samples, 22.3% of loci had FDR < 0.05
  before
  the fix and none after. Results without local information, or with
  local_meth = FALSE, are unchanged. Also in 1.24.2.

- diff_methylsig() drops every locus it can't test because of too few
  degrees of freedom. Before, only loci with df = 1 were dropped, and
  loci
  with df = 0, e.g. tiles with no coverage, were returned with NA
  results
  (issues #47 and #56). Also in 1.24.1.

- diff_methylsig() and diff_binomial() work with one sample in a group,
  instead of failing with "'x' must be an array of at least two
  dimensions" (issue #51). diff_methylsig() still needs enough samples
  in
  disp_groups to estimate dispersion, and now says so with a clear
  error.

- diff_methylsig() with local information (local_window_size > 0) takes
  time proportional to the number of loci. Before, each locus was
  compared
  with every other locus, which made large data sets take hours or days
  (issues #42 and #43). Results are the same, except that local
  information
  no longer comes from loci on a different chromosome.

- diff_methylsig() warns when local information is used
  (local_window_size > 0) and bs isn't sorted by position. Neighbors
  are
  found among the 5 loci on either side, so unsorted loci miss some.

- diff_methylsig() with n_cores > 1 stops with the error from a
  parallel
  worker. Before, mclapply() returned the error as a value, and the
  results failed later with an unrelated error.

- diff_binomial() used every sample in the pooled model under the null
  hypothesis, not only the samples in case and control. With other
  groups
  in group_column, the likelihood ratio statistic was wrong: on 2,374
  CpGs
  of bsseqData's BS.cancer.ex, with one cancer and one normal sample
  relabeled as a third group, 2,301 loci had FDR < 0.05 instead of 156.
  Results with only the case and control samples are unchanged. Also in
  1.24.3.

- diff_binomial() drops loci where case or control has no coverage,
  with
  a message, as diff_methylsig() does for loci it can't test. Before,
  they
  were returned with NaN results. The FDR is computed over the tested
  loci.

- diff_binomial() computes meth_diff before rounding meth_case and
  meth_control, instead of from the rounded values.

- diff_dss_test() takes the methylation rates from the loci of bs that
  match diff_fit$gr, in that order. Before, it used every locus of bs,
  so a
  bs with more loci than the fit gave an error, and a bs with the same
  number of loci in another order gave rates for the wrong loci. It
  errors
  if bs is missing fit loci or has a different number of samples than
  diff_fit$design. Also in 1.24.4.

- diff_dss_test() errors when methylation_group_column is a character
  or
  factor column and methylation_groups is missing. Before, meth_case,
  meth_control, and meth_diff were all NaN, and direction was NA. A
  column
  that isn't character, factor, or numeric (e.g. logical) gives a clear
  error, instead of "object 'case_idx' not found", and
  methylation_groups
  with a numeric column gives a warning that it is ignored.

- These diff_dss_test() checks happen before the test, instead of after
  it.

- filter_loci_by_group_coverage() names only the groups whose
  thresholds
  no locus satisfies, instead of every group. When each group alone has
  loci that pass but no locus passes for all groups at once, it says
  so.

DOCUMENTATION

- The vignette refers to diff_dss_test(), not diff_fit_test(), and
  notes
  that the sign of stat follows the contrast (normal minus cancer for
  Typenormal), while meth_diff is case minus control.

- The diff_binomial() docs no longer mention t_approx, which it doesn't
  have, or methylSigReadData(), which was replaced by
  bsseq::read.bismark().

INTERNAL CHANGES

- Check the package with R CMD check and BiocCheck in the Bioconductor
  devel container, locally (docker/check.sh) and in GitHub Actions on
  every
  push and pull request, and weekly. This replaces Travis CI.
  docker/check.sh exits with an error when BiocCheck finds an error.

- Depend on R (>= 4.6.0), and drop the Date field from DESCRIPTION.

- Add the URL field and the Sequencing and Coverage biocViews to
  DESCRIPTION, and label the vignettes' setup chunks.

- Move NEWS to inst/NEWS.

- Move the tests to testthat 3rd edition. expect_equivalent() is
  replaced
  with expect_equal(ignore_attr = TRUE), and the tiling tests compare
  the
  Cov and M values as matrices, instead of the DelayedMatrix objects.


[methylumi](/packages/methylumi)
---------

                       Changes in version 2.59.3                        

Bug fixes

- methylumIDAT() reads IDAT files from per-slide subdirectories,
which
is the layout Illumina's own software produces
(<idatPath>/<Slide>/<Slide>_<Array>_Grn.idat). Both the
file-presence check and the code that actually opened the files
assumed a flat directory, so a nested run reported every sample as
missing. Flat layouts are unaffected. If the same basename appears
under more than one subdirectory the read now errors and lists the
candidates rather than picking one. getBarcodes() had the same blind
spot and is fixed too. (#19)

- diagnostics() works on objects with no color-channel annotation,
such as the bundled GoldenGate mldat. Three if (annotation(x) ==
"...") tests errored outright on a zero-length annotation, and past
those, the plotting loop split probes on a COLOR_CHANNEL column that
such objects do not have, so every panel would have been drawn from
zero probes. The long-reported call to the non-existent
plot.density() was real, on the same path, and is also fixed. (#23)

- methylumi.bgcorr() explains itself when asked for noob correction
on
an object that has no out-of-band intensities. Objects built from
GEO series matrices or GenomeStudio output via methylumiR() carry
only methylated/unmethylated/p-value data; OOB probes come only from
reading raw IDATs. This used to fail deep inside method dispatch
with "unable to find an inherited method for 'intensities.OOB'".
(#24)

Deprecated and defunct

- The gamma-family background corrections — method = "goob", "gamma"
and "mode" — have been removed. They called gamma.mle(),
gamma.mode() and gamma.integral() from rGammaGamma, a GitHub-only
package that is not available from CRAN or Bioconductor and was
never declared as a dependency, so these methods have errored for
years. Requesting one now produces an error saying so. method =
"noob" (the default) is unaffected. (#18)

Internal changes

- qc.probe.plot(), plotNAs() and plotProbeNAs() no longer use
ggplot2's deprecated qplot(). Plot output is unchanged except in
plotNAs(), where the segment layer now maps linewidth rather than
the also-deprecated size; scale_linewidth uses a linear palette
where scale_size used an area one, so line widths differ slightly.
(#40)

- A pkgdown site is published to
https://seandavi.github.io/methylumi/
from a GitHub Actions workflow. (#43)

                       Changes in version 2.59.2                        

Bug fixes

- The package installs again. lattice removed parallel() from its
exports (it was renamed parallelplot() years ago, then deprecated,
then made defunct). Because the import resolved at lazy-load time,
this broke R CMD INSTALL for the whole package rather than just
parplot(), and took several downstream packages with it.

- QCdata() is no longer silently lost when a MethyLumiSet is subset.
eSet's [ method drops the QC slot, and the previous guard tried to
subset it after that had already happened — NULL[, j, drop = FALSE]
returns NULL without erroring, so the guard was a no-op. QC data is
now captured before dispatch and reattached. Feature indices no
longer apply to QC probes, which live in their own feature space;
only sample selection does. As a consequence combine() no longer
reports "Dropped control probes" when combining subsets.

- The example dataset mldat no longer shares its assayData between
copies. It had been saved with storageMode = "environment" instead
of "lockedEnvironment", so x <- mldat; methylated(x) <- ... silently
mutated the original. The assay values themselves are unchanged.

- plotNegOob() works again. It had two independent ggplot2 breakages:
scale_y_continuous(breaks = NA) (now NULL) and opts() (removed from
ggplot2 years ago, now labs()).

Internal changes

- .mclapply() is now a thin wrapper around BiocParallel::bplapply()
instead of parallel::mclapply() behind a require(). mclapply()
forks, so it degraded to serial on Windows regardless. The signature
is unchanged, and parallel results are verified identical to serial
results. Configure it the standard Bioconductor way, with
BiocParallel::register().

- require() calls inside package code have been replaced with
declared
imports, or with requireNamespace() guards that produce an
actionable error for genuinely optional packages (MASS, Biostrings,
lumi). require() returns FALSE rather than erroring, so a missing
package used to change behaviour silently.

- Bare T/F are now TRUE/FALSE throughout (105 occurrences). These are
ordinary variables, not reserved words, so a user with a variable
named T in scope could change the meaning of a default argument.

- 1:length(x), 1:nrow(x) and 1:ncol(x) are now seq_along()/seq_len(),
which behave correctly when the length is zero.

- Base-package functions used by the package are now properly
imported, rather than resolving by accident because the packages
happened to be attached.

Documentation

- Most man pages are generated from roxygen blocks now. The S4 class
and generic documentation remains hand-written on purpose; see the
note in R/data.R.

- extractBarcodeAndPosition() was documented as returning three
columns with numeric row and column. It returns five, and row/column
are strings such as "R006"; the numeric ones are
rowNumber/columnNumber.

Testing and infrastructure

- The package has a test suite for the first time: 36 tests covering
import from IDAT and text, normalization, background correction,
coercions, filtering, subsetting and every plotting entry point.

- CI runs R CMD check against Bioconductor devel on GitHub Actions,
replacing a .travis.yml that had not run in years.

Known issues

- methylumi.bgcorr() with method = "gamma" or method = "mode" does
not
work. It calls gamma.mle(), gamma.mode() and gamma.integral() from
rGammaGamma, which is not declared as a dependency and is not
available from CRAN or Bioconductor. The default noob method is
unaffected.

- qc.probe.plot(), plotNAs() and plotProbeNAs() still use ggplot2's
deprecated qplot().

                        Changes in version 1.21                         

- Fixed explained percentages on PCA axes for jointRPCA and hardened

- Implement Striped Unifrac algorithm (1.21.4, 2026-07-29)

- Added conversion functions between MAE and TreeSE (1.21.8,
  2026-09-22)

- Added applyByModule (1.21.11, 2026-10-02)

- Fixed getAlpha/addAlpha returning the first rarefaction round instead
  of
  the mean over niter rounds (1.21.12, 2026-10-19)

- getAlpha/addAlpha rarefy once per iteration and calculate all indices
  from
  the same rarefied data (1.21.13, 2026-10-13)

- Add Allen and Rao alpha diversity indices (1.21.14, 2026-10-22)

- Added getQCMetrics and addQCMetrics (1.21.15, 2026-10-26)

- Added getDysbiosis and addDysbiosis (1.21.16, 2026-10-26)

- Fixed Camargo evenness, which was computed on the wrong entries when
  samples contained zeroes and depended on feature order (1.21.17,

- Fixed UniFrac truncating sample totals to integers, which gave NaN or
  wrong
  distances on relative abundances and percentages (1.21.18,
  2026-10-27)

- Added method = "sd" and "cv" to getTop (1.21.19, 2026-10-27)

- Formula handling in RDA, CCA and PERMANOVA no longer uses
  as.character() (1.21.20, 2026-10-27)

- transformAssay and rarefyAssay warn instead of failing when
  overwriting an assay (1.21.21, 2026-10-27)

- getMDS and addMDS use all features by default (1.21.22, 2026-10-27)

- Added getPCA and addPCA (1.21.23, 2026-10-27)

- Renamed getQCMetrics and addQCMetrics to getQC and addQC (1.21.24,
  2026-10-28)

- Added exporters (1.21.25, 2026-10-28)

- Fixed applyByModule failing on parallel workers in separate sessions,
  e.g. on Windows (1.21.26, 2026-10-29)

- transformAssay: method = "log" now computes natural log consistently
  with "log2" and "log10"; the previous vegan::decostand log
  transformation is available as method = "log_zero_replace" (1.21.27,
  2026-10-30)

- Renamed agglomerateByModule to agglomerateBySet (1.21.28, 2026-11-05)

- Renamed applyByModule to applyBySet (1.21.28, 2026-11-05)

- getPERMANOVA: binary=TRUE when Jaccard calculated (1.21.28,
  2026-11-05)

- Tree agglomeration simplified. When data is agglomerated, tree is
  dropped by default as it is not matching with the agglomerated data.
  If specified, the tree is aggregated based on MRCA. (1.21.29,
  2026-11-11)

- Fixed weighted UniFrac when multiple rows are linked to the same node
  (1.21.29, 2026-11-11)

- mergeSEs: improve efficency (1.21.30, 2026-11-12)

- Added subsetBy for subsetting features and samples by conditions
  evaluated on the current data; collapse = TRUE merges the removed
  features into one (1.21.31, 2026-11-17)

- Deprecated subsetByPrevalent, subsetByRare and
  agglomerateByPrevalence in favor of subsetBy (1.21.32, 2026-11-18)

- Removed filterRPCAInput; use subsetBy instead (1.21.32, 2026-11-18)

- subsetBy: fixed collapse = TRUE when only one feature is collapsed
  (1.21.33, 2026-11-19)

- getPrevalentAbundance/addPrevalentAbundance: thresholds and rank are
  now passed on for SummarizedExperiment (1.21.33, 2026-11-19)

- getNMDS/addNMDS: FUN = getDissimilarity by default, for consistency
  with getMDS and getDivergence; getDivergence/addDivergence gain the
  FUN argument; getDissimilarity generic defaults to method = "bray",
  so getMDS and getNMDS work without method (1.21.34, 2026-11-20)

- getMediation/addMediation: with dimred, mediators are named by the
  component names of the reducedDim (e.g. "PC1") instead of the
  reducedDim name and an index ("PCA1"), which is still used when the
  components have no names (#901) (2026-11-21)

- Added normalized option for weighted and unweighted Unifrac (1.21.35,
  2026-11-21)

- Tengeler2020: sample names and colData are matched to the counts by
  sample name; they were misaligned, so patient_status was correct for
  only 11 of 27 samples (#904) (2026-11-21)

- convertToPhyloseq: tree.name = NULL leaves out the tree, which keeps

- References in the documentation use Rdpack and inst/REFERENCES.bib
  (#707) (2026-11-21)

- transformAssay: verbose = FALSE silences its messages and warnings,
  e.g. in pipelines (#788) (2026-11-21)

- parseTaxonomy: new exported function that splits taxonomy strings
  such as "k__Bacteria; p__Firmicutes" into one column per rank; it
  uses the parser of the importers (#769) (2026-11-21)

- getTaxonomyLabels: with make.unique = TRUE, the message lists the
  labels that were changed, e.g. "Family:o -> Family:o_1" (#729)

- getPERMANOVA/addPERMANOVA: method = "unifrac" uses the rowTree of a
  TreeSE; earlier it failed with "argument tree is missing"; unused
  factor levels are dropped from the covariates, as vegan::adonis2()
  can crash R with them, e.g. when samples are subsetted for pairwise
  tests, and a grouping variable with only one group gives an error
  instead of a warning (1.21.36, 2026-11-21)

- Vignette: overview of the functions grouped by use case, with
  examples (2026-11-21)

- exportMothur: the OTU column of taxonomy.tsv is taken from the row
  names; with stringr < 1.6.0 the export failed (2026-11-22)

- getDissimilarity: method = "overlap" returns the dissimilarity 1 -
  overlap; it returned the overlap similarity, so identical samples had
  the largest dissimilarity (#787) (2026-11-22)

- getAlpha/addAlpha: allen and rao placed the tip abundances by table
  row instead of node, which gave wrong values on most trees
  (2026-11-22)

- transformAssay: pseudocount = TRUE (and method = "pseudocount"
  without a value) is deprecated; the warning gives the value used. A
  numeric pseudocount on an assay with only positive values is an error
  instead of a warning, and the error for zeroes suggests a pseudocount
  (#813) (2026-11-22)

[miaViz](/packages/miaViz)
------

                        Changes in version 1.21                         

NEW FEATURES

- plotHeatmap: heatmap of features by samples straight from a TreeSE,
  as a
  ggplot2 object, with row and column facets from rowData/colData and
  an
  optional row tree

- plotDissimilarity: heatmap of a dissimilarity matrix between samples

- getHeatmapOrder and sort.method (in plotHeatmap and
  plotDissimilarity):
  sort the rows and columns of heatmaps

- plotOrdination for ordinations stored in reducedDims

- Joint-RPCA visualisations: plotJointRPCA, plotJointRPCACovariance,
  plotJointRPCAExplainedVariance and plotJointRPCANetwork

- plotRowTree, plotColTree: heatmap.by shows per-taxon values as a
  heatmap
  or as rings next to the tree tips

- plotSeries: each feature is drawn as its own line, as in matplot(),
  also
  without colour.by

- plotBoxplot: outlier.size, outlier.colour, outlier.alpha and
  outlier.shape
  style the boxplot outliers (shown with add.points = FALSE). The help
  page
  now lists all customisation arguments, grouped by plot layer

- New example datasets in multimedia_data_demo: se_relative,
  tse_relative and
  tse_pathway

SIGNIFICANT USER-VISIBLE CHANGES

- plotRDA, plotCCA: the vectors are scaled by a common factor so that
  the
  longest one reaches 75% of the extent of the samples (as in vegan
  biplots), instead of crowding at the origin. Their relative lengths
  and
  directions are unchanged; vec.scale = FALSE draws them at the
  original
  length, and a number sets the multiplier

- Colour-blind-friendly colours by default: discrete variables are
  coloured
  with the Okabe-Ito palette for up to 9 groups (black is used only for
  the
  9th), with the Paired palette for 10 to 12 groups and with viridis
  for
  more, instead of the Tableau palette

- plotOrdination and the functions built on it (e.g. plotJointRPCA)
  draw
  points with point.alpha = 0.7 instead of 0.4, so that light colours
  stay
  visible

- A palette set with options(ggplot2.discrete.colour = ...) or
  options(ggplot2.discrete.fill = ...) is used in all plots, so one
  palette
  can be chosen for every figure, e.g. the earlier Tableau palette
  (see ?"mia-plot-args")

- More readable default labels:
  - plotHeatmap and plotJointRPCACovariance draw column labels
    vertically
  - plotOrdination titles the axes by the method and component, e.g.
    "MDS1 (23.4%)" instead of "MDS_bray1"
  - plotLoadings shows the components in their order (PC2 before PC10),
    names unnamed components "Component 1", ..., titles the value axis
    "Loading" and leaves out the sign legend when all loadings have the
    same sign
  - Prevalence plots title their axes "Detection threshold (<assay>)",
    "Number of features" and "Mean relative abundance"
  - plotBoxplot facets (facet.by = "rownames") follow the order of
    'features', and plotMediation forest panels the order of the
    components
  - plotJointRPCANetwork keeps labels off the nodes

- plotMediation heatmap: each tile shows the effect estimate with its
  significance, the colours use the colour-blind-safe red-blue palette
  and
  the panel is grey, so that small ACME effects stay visible on the
  shared
  colour scale. add.estimate = FALSE shows only the significance, and
  add.significance = "numeric" shows "p=0.012" or "p<0.001"

- plotForest: confidence intervals from 'err.var' use the degrees of
  freedom
  given with the new 'df.var' or 'df' arguments; without them, the
  normal
  distribution is used with a warning. Earlier, the number of columns
  of the
  results table was used as the degrees of freedom

DEPRECATED AND DEFUNCT

- plotPrevalence, plotRowPrevalence, plotPrevalentAbundance:
  as.relative and
  as_relative are deprecated. Calculate relative abundances with
  transformAssay(x, method = "relabundance") and use
  assay.type = "relabundance" instead

- getNeatOrder is deprecated; use getHeatmapOrder

- plotTaxaPrevalence and plotFeaturePrevalence are removed (deprecated
  since
  2025); use plotRowPrevalence

- plotBoxplot: the misspelled argument add.chance is renamed to
  add.change

BUG FIXES

- Legend titles of coloured or filled variables (colour.by, fill.by,
  ...)
  can be changed with labs(), e.g. + labs(colour = "Sample type"); the
  title was set as the scale name, which labs() cannot override

- plotOrdination: the explained variance shown in the axis titles is
  the
  percentage of the total variance for ordinations that store
  eigenvalues
  (e.g. MDS); earlier the eigenvalues were multiplied by 100

- plotOrdination: aspect.ratio = "eigen" now scales the panel by the
  explained
  variance (it had no effect); the documentation named a non-existent
  panel.by.eigen argument

- plotBoxplot: significance brackets no longer run through boxes or
  each
  other, and hide.ns = TRUE stacks the shown brackets without gaps

- plotBoxplot: paired lines follow the time order with more than two
  time
  points

- plotBoxplot: variables named "x", "y" or "df" work

- plotRowPrevalence: count thresholds are no longer multiplied by 100

- plotHeatmap, plotDissimilarity: labs(fill = ...) sets the legend
  title

- plotHeatmap: facetting rows and columns by variables with the same
  name
  works

- plotRDA, plotCCA: samples left out of the ordination (e.g. with
  na.action = na.exclude) no longer add an empty "NA" legend entry

- plotAbundance: rows named in the new other.name argument (default
  "Other", e.g. the group from subsetBy(collapse = TRUE)) are shown
  last in
  the bars and legend instead of among the features; other.name = NULL
  turns this off

- plotAbundance: a row named "Other" (e.g. from subsetBy(collapse =
  TRUE))
  is shown last in the bars and legend instead of among the features

- plotForest: labels use two decimals for the CI ("-0.45 (-1.59,
  0.70)")
  and show p-values below 0.001 as "<0.001" instead of "0"

- plotRowGraph, plotPrevalentAbundance: points are coloured correctly
  when
  both colour.by and shape.by are given

MINOR NOTES

- plotBoxplot: the error message for a wrong p.adjust.method asks for a
  method name (it said 'must be TRUE or FALSE')

- Vignette: overview of all functions grouped by use case, and new
  examples
  of heatmaps, ordination, group comparisons and forest plots

- Requires mia (>= 1.21.31), whose subsetBy() is used in examples and
  tests

- plotBoxplot: variable names that clash with internal columns
  (e.g. "x_point") give an error instead of being silently overwritten

- plotBoxplot: step.increase is applied once (it was applied twice) and
  is
  measured from the highest group a bracket spans; other arguments are
  passed to ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual

- plotSeries: legends keyed by rownames follow the order of
  rownames(x), and
  colour.lab also titles the line type and size legends when they use
  the
  same variable

- plotOrdination, plotBoxplot: size.by titles the size legend

- plotPrevalence, plotRowPrevalence: until removed, as.relative works
  as
  documented (earlier only as_relative did)

- The pkgdown reference page groups the functions into categories

[microbiome](/packages/microbiome)
----------

                 Changes in version 1.35.2 (2026-10-25)                 

- Fixed Camargo evenness (#231). Zeroes were not removed, so the index
  was computed on the wrong entries and depended on the order of taxa.
  All Camargo values change; samples with no observed taxa now return
  NA instead of an error

- Documented that the zeroes argument of evenness() has no effect

                 Changes in version 1.35.1 (2026-08-10)                 

- Added support for TreeSummarizedExperiment and other
  SummarizedExperiment-derived objects
  - abundances(), meta() and taxa() now accept these objects alongside
    phyloseq objects, which extends support to most of the package
  - abundances() gains an assay.type argument, defaulting to the counts
    assay when present and otherwise the first assay
  - transform() stores its result as a new named assay and leaves the
    original assays untouched, following the mia transformAssay
    convention. It gains a name argument to control that assay name, and
    the result is read back with abundances(x, assay.type = name) rather
    than abundances(x)
  - Functions that manipulate the taxonomy table (aggregate_taxa,
    plot_composition, map_levels, psmelt2, the tibble utilities and the
    read_* family) remain phyloseq only

- We recommend switching from phyloseq to the TreeSummarizedExperiment
  based methods described in the Orchestrating Microbiome Analysis
  (OMA)
  online book, https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OMA/, which is
  where method development now takes place

- Passing a phyloseq object now emits a one-time deprecation notice per
  session, recommending the (Tree)SummarizedExperiment framework and
  the
  mia package. Silence it with
  options(microbiome.phyloseq_deprecation = FALSE)

- Fixed low_abundance returning an unnamed vector for phyloseq input

- Fixed collapse_replicates failing when given a single replicate field

[MicrobiomeProfiler](/packages/MicrobiomeProfiler)
------------------

                       Changes in version 1.19.2                        

- move the external-data builders for Disbiome and eggNOG from
data-raw/ into R/ so that they ship with the package and their tests
run under R CMD check instead of being skipped (2026-09-17, Thu)
- data-raw/build_disbiome.R and data-raw/build_eggnog.R are now
thin loaders, so the scheduled external-data update workflow is
unaffected
- stop advertising placeholder OG0001-style identifiers for eggNOG
(2026-09-15, Tue)
- the Example button now builds its input from the published
eggNOG artifact instead of hard-coded fixture IDs, and uses a
complete KEGG pathway that fits the analysis window, so the
generated example really produces a non-empty enrichment result
- the GSEA example also carries background identifiers from
outside the pathway, without which the permutation p-values
cannot be computed
- when the eggNOG artifact cannot be loaded the app reports the
problem instead of filling the input with identifiers that
cannot be analysed
- guard against an NA condition while the universe selector has
not rendered yet
- expose an explicit seed argument on all GSEA entry points —
gseKO(),
gseModule(), gseCOG(), gseMDA(), gseMBKEGG(), gseSMPDB(), gseHMDB()
and gseEggNOG() — forwarded to enrichit::gsea_gson() (2026-08-15,
Fri)
- set it to a number (or TRUE for a fixed default seed) to get
identical GSEA results across runs, FALSE (default) draws a
fresh seed on each run; set.seed() before the call still works
- pvalueCutoff is applied to both pvalue and p.adjust inside
enrichit::gsea_gson() (requires enrichit >= 0.2.2), matching the
historical clusterProfiler/DOSE double-filtering behavior

                       Changes in version 1.19.1                        

- setup GitHub Actions workflow for automated internal data updates
(KEGG, COG, SMPDB, HMDB, Disbiome) (2026-05-21, Thu)
- support shinyserver (2026-05-21, Thu, #3)
- import clusterProfiler to prevent R check error (2026-05-21, Thu)

[mixOmics](/packages/mixOmics)
--------

                       Changes in version 6.38.0                        

Bioconductor 3.24, November 2026.

new features / enhancements / changes

- mixOmics is now licensed under AGPL-3 instead of GPL (>= 2) (#421)
- circosPlot is drawn by new code (#419)
- predict on multi-block models is 3 to 67 times faster, and perf and
tune.block.plsda about 2 times faster, with identical results (#369,
#383)
- perf and perf.assess on DIABLO models accept folds as a list (#400)
- mint.block.pls, mint.block.spls, mint.block.plsda and
mint.block.splsda return model objects with the same structure as
the block.* models, so predict works on them (#386)
- ?plot.perf.pls now has examples (#414)
- citation("mixOmics") gives the full author names and the DOI (#416)
- the GitHub repository moved from mixOmicsTeam/mixOmics to
mixOmics-org/mixOmics
- expanded test coverage for model utilities and internal helpers
(#381)
- the official Bioconductor package maintainer is now correctly set
as
Professor Kim-Anh Lê Cao, founding author and project lead of
mixOmics
- new title and description, reflecting the package as it is today
- mixOmics logo updated in the vignette
- ORCID iDs added for authors and contributors where known

bug fixes

- circosPlot no longer fails when a block, including the Y block, has
a single selected variable (#402, #324)
- circosPlot showed block names containing "chr" truncated and failed
with line = TRUE (#419)
- circosPlot with several blocks in blocks.link kept only about half
of the links (#419)
- plotVar no longer places points outside the correlation circle when
the plotted components are not orthogonal (#405)
- keepX and keepY of block.spls and mint.block.* models now give the
values used (#386)
- plotLoadings handles a vector xlim for contribution plots in the
graphics style (#377)
- the vignette link in the startup message returned 404; it now
points
to https://guides.mixomics.org/mixomics-guide-vignette/, and the
website and contact links use https
- ?tune.rcc gave the wrong default for BPPARAM; it is SerialParam()
- error messages now link to the mixOmics-org issue page instead of
the old mixOmicsTeam address
- help pages now link to https://mixomics.org, and references and
data
sources whose pages have moved or gone link to the paper's DOI
- citations of González et al. (2012) corrected to match the
published
paper

                       Changes in version 1.24.0                        

New features

- create_mofa_from_SingleCellExperiment() can now load altExps as
additional views (alt_experiments).
- create_mofa_from_MultiAssayExperiment() can now select experiments,
assays and altExps (experiments, assays, alt_experiments).
- New mofa2() wrapper runs create_mofa() and prepare_mofa() in one
call, taking only the options that differ from the defaults.
- New plot_factor_mean_cor() heatmap to identify factors related to
intercept or library-size effects.

Significant user-visible changes

- create_mofa() and the SingleCellExperiment and MultiAssayExperiment
constructors have new arguments before groups; pass groups by name.
- create_mofa_from_SingleCellExperiment() argument assay is renamed
to
assays.
- Documentation and vignettes now recommend reticulate::py_require()
to set up mofapy2.

Bug fixes and minor improvements

- Updated to mofapy2 0.7.5, which fixes MEFISTO for some covariate
grids and adds pandas 3 compatibility.
- The warning about intercept factors now names the affected views
and
points to plot_factor_mean_cor().
- run_mofa() no longer warns when mofapy2 is a newer patch release
than the pinned version.

[msPurity](/packages/msPurity)
--------

                       Changes in version 1.99.8                        

- Thomas N. Lawson, the original author of msPurity, is listed first
in the package authors.

                       Changes in version 1.99.7                        

- Daily package checks use compact SQLite examples and a bundled
spectral library, reducing check time and source package size.
Bioconductor's weekly long tests cover full-library matching and
compare results against the historical fixtures in
msPurityData 1.41.2.

                       Changes in version 1.99.6                        

- The new msPurity-msn-standards vignette follows L-tryptophan and
L-kynurenine from MS1 feature detection through MS2–MS4 purity
assessment, spectral trees and matching. It uses the suggested
package lcmsPlot to display chromatograms, detected peaks and
precursor purity.
- The general and LC-MS/MS matching vignettes now use Parquet studies
and xcms 4. The matching workflow compares the default score and
BLINK against a bundled MoNA library and reads the saved match
evidence from Parquet. Vignette HTML is generated from the R
Markdown sources during package builds.
- writeGraphML() returns the normalized output path on Windows after
the file has been written.
- The README and package description document the LC-MSn workflows
and
cite the BLINK method. citation("msPurity") includes both the
original package paper and the deep metabolome annotation workflow
paper.

                       Changes in version 1.99.5                        

- Build scan and precursor–fragment trees from measured spectra and
follow a branch with subsetTree(). Peak trees reuse the parent peaks
recorded by purityA() for MS3/MS4. For raw spectra, peak matching
uses 5 ppm by default. fragmentLinks() exposes measured masses and
their signed difference for fragment and candidate neutral-loss
searches. Plot or export a selected branch with plot(), as_igraph()
or writeGraphML() (#155).

                       Changes in version 1.99.4                        

- BlinkMatchingParam() selects BLINK fragment scoring for MS2–MS4
searches. Hits report approximate cosine and estimated matching-ion
count. Parquet evidence records both scores and the settings used
(#161).

- For Spectra queries, spectralMatching() reports an outcome for
every
input query. Retained hits identify shared scans and source files,
with the original measurements contributing to each stored consensus
(#160).

- spectralMatching() accepts experimental Spectra queries for
in-memory MS2–MS4 searches against experimental spectra or a
reference library. Hits carry the input positions, compatibility
reason, scores and rank (#159).

- scoreSpectrumPair() checks MS2–MS4 precursor masses, acquisition
conditions and available ancestry before reading peaks. It reports
the decision alongside the six existing scores.
SpectralMatchingParam() sets separate ppm and Da windows for each
side of the comparison (#158).

- Parquet spectral matching accepts a Spectra library directly,
including disk-backed libraries. Searches read candidate peaks in
batches and can record the library release and checksum with the
evidence (#154).

- DIMS retirement: purityD, its associated processing functions and
standalone DIMS functions, including dimsPredictPuritySingle(), are
deprecated. Calls remain functional during deprecation, but DIMS
functionality will receive no further bug fixes or feature
development. There is no direct replacement in msPurity. The
interfaces will become defunct and be removed in subsequent release
cycles.

                       Changes in version 1.99.3                        

- processedSpectrumInfo(), readProcessedSpectra() and
readProcessedProvenance() reopen Parquet results by feature, MS
level, averaging method or run. They expose stored peak statistics,
raw study references and the measurements behind an average (#129).

- purityX() now accepts XcmsExperiment and XCMSnExp alongside
xcmsSet.
It predicts feature purity from the selected MS1 spectra within each
sample's chromatographic peak boundaries. Spectrum subsetting and
peak processing on modern xcms inputs carry through to the
prediction (#144).

- PurityXParam() collects reusable settings for isolation-window
offsets, isolation-efficiency weighting, intensity thresholds and
isotope handling. For a saved result, processingParameters() returns
the settings used and processingHistory() identifies the
chromatographic peaks and MS1 scans behind each prediction.
updateObject() preserves older predictions and imports the settings
available in the saved object (#144).

- purityX(singleFile = ...) now uses the requested sample in
multi-file experiments and applies the default isolation-efficiency
weighting when requested. purityFWmean and purityFWHMmean now
average the MS1 purity estimates across the full or half-height peak
width, respectively. If a half-height flank is missing, the
full-width estimate can still be used (#144).

                       Changes in version 1.99.2                        

- Parquet export writes spectra and results tables in batches. Scalar
averages with zero retained peaks keep their spectrum and
membership. Attempted averages that produced no spectrum are
recorded in the loss ledger (#128).
- validateParquet() uses DuckDB to query the columns it needs and can
use temporary disk space for large joins. SQLite-to-Parquet
conversion now assigns the same run IDs across platforms when source
files are unavailable, and relative study links work on Windows
(#128).
- When exporting raw fragmentation peaks, the database writer reads
only MS2 and higher scans. This avoids failures while decoding
unrelated MS1 peaks. The LC-MS/MS vignette now reuses bundled
grouped xcms peaks, and package checks reuse shared workflow results
(#128).
- createMSP() now works after frag4feature(useGroup = TRUE). It
writes
the grouped feature's median m/z and retention time into MSP headers
for both measured scans and averaged spectra (#145).
- Fragment clustering (#141): matching peaks stay together across
processing blocks, preventing incorrect support counts and lost
averaged fragments. Blocks whose peaks all fit within one m/z
tolerance window are grouped directly, reducing computation and
memory use. Groups above blockSize that cannot be grouped directly
or split without separating matching peaks now raise an error.
- Execution controls: blockSize (default 5,000 peaks) sets the
clustering block limit in intra/inter/all fragmentation averaging
and DIMS averaging/grouping. Explicit cores values apply to the
current call; omitting cores uses the object's stored setting.
- MSn ancestry uses lineageScanId to link scans and their parents and
sourceSpectrumId for parent references expressed as source keys.
- Fragmentation averaging supports named AverageFragSpectraParam sets
to select or combine acquisition conditions for MSn (e.g. MS2-MS4)
spectra. Incompatible precursor paths stay separate. Inter-file
averaging uses each file’s averaged spectrum once per group,
regardless of how many scans went into it.
- Averaging provenance (#31) adds averageMembers(),
averagePeakMembers() and averageProvenance() to trace selected
inputs and retained peaks through intra-file and inter-file
averaging. Repeated feature links remain distinct.
- Mean averaging no longer warns when optional normalized intensities
are absent.
- Raw MS1-MS4 data in Parquet studies (#127): a Spectra on a dataset
written by MsBackendParquet's mzMLToParquet() (0.99.12 or later)
runs through purityA(), frag4feature(), filterFragSpectra() and
averaging with the same results as the mzML files, for MS2 to MS4.
Peaks are read from the dataset, never from the mzML files, so these
need not exist; a dataset that has moved or changed since purityA()
read it is reported as such. A selected or processed input numbers
its raw peak rows as the matching mzML input does. An activation
method the dataset records as a PSI-MS accession is read as its
method name, so selectors match it as they match a filter string,
and activationTypeBasis records which applied.
- With automatic parentReference, a Parquet dataset's own spectrum
ids
are no longer offered as sourceSpectrumId readings of parent scan
numbers once acquisition numbers resolve, which made parent
references ambiguous in studies of several runs.
- Parquet results written directly, for MS2 to MS4 (#127, #128):
createDatabase(format = "parquet") no longer stages an SQLite
database; the MS2 output is unchanged. Results version 1.1.0 adds,
without changing what 1.0.0 datasets hold:
- MS3 and MS4 scans in x_mspurity_scan, with ms_level, MSn stage
purity and status, the activation method used and its basis, and
each scan's parent and MS2 root, as references and as rows of
the table;
- MS3/MS4 feature links in the new x_mspurity_msn_feature, and the
retention-time mapping of MS2 links in spectrum_feature;
- filter flags of every filtered spectrum in x_mspurity_scan_peak,
including those of feature-linked scans when allfrag = FALSE,
which were lost before;
- each step's processing history in tool_provenance.
- Study links without the mzML files (#127): with study, scans and
the
MS1 scans their MS2 precursors name are matched from the study's own
metadata by native id, then scan number at the same position and
level; files are no longer read or checksummed for this. When
purityA() read a Parquet dataset it is the default study; study = NA
opts out. Conditions the study does not record are reported as
unavailable in the loss ledger.
- Averages in Parquet results (#127, #128, #31): averages computed
with AverageFragSpectraParam, at MS2 to MS4, are exported with their
MS level, parameter set and group, acquisition conditions and
precursor path. Where averaging recorded its provenance,
merge_member lists the inputs each average selected, with whether
each contributed a peak, and the new x_mspurity_merge_peak gives the
input peak each averaged peak came from; averages without a record
keep reconstructed members. Empty averages are exported as spectra
without peaks. Spectral matching stays on MS2 averages.
- The SQLite writer refuses MS3/MS4 feature links as it refuses
MS3/MS4 spectra and averages computed with AverageFragSpectraParam.

                       Changes in version 1.99.1                        

- Retention-time correction in frag4feature() (#137): precursor times
of each file are mapped to the adjusted XCMS scale by interpolation
and compared with peak and feature windows on that scale, in both
modes. Before, individual mode converted peak bounds back to raw
time by exact match, which silently dropped every filled peak, and
grouped mode compared raw precursor times with adjusted feature
windows, so convert2RawRT had no effect there.
- purityA files are matched to XCMS samples by file name instead of
by
position. Each file gets a mapping status (aligned, unaligned,
external, estimated or missing) in the new rtMapStatus column, and
files without a mapping are named in a warning.
- Filled peaks are excluded explicitly; includeFilled = TRUE links
them, flagged by is_filled. intense applies in both modes, falling
back from iMz to aMz to precursorMZ, and precurMzSource records the
value used.
- New frag4feature() arguments: ms2RtMap maps DDA files outside the
XCMS object (an XCMS object, named functions or named offsets),
estimateRtMap = TRUE estimates the shift for them in grouped mode,
rtTol widens the windows, rtSource = "ms2" uses the MS/MS scan time
and groupWindow = "median" uses median feature bounds.
Frag4FeatureParam holds the same settings, apart from ms2RtMap.
- New grped_df columns matchRank and rtApexDist order the matches of
each scan; per-file diagnostics are stored in
pa@params$frag4feature. Legacy columns keep their order and types.
MS3 and MS4 rows keep their own precursor m/z and time.
- Faster linking: the nested plyr::ddply matching and the SNOW
cluster
are replaced by one dplyr interval join, so dplyr (>= 1.1.0) is
required. On 32 files linking takes about 5 s instead of 870 s.
Processing history records one effective worker, and grouped mode
now records the RT conversion as used for association.
- Data frames passed to the deprecated grp_peaklist/grpPeaklist
arguments no longer error, the plim filter handles missing purity,
and the SQLite and Parquet writers and createMSP() prefer fileid
over sample when mapping links to files.

                       Changes in version 1.99.0                        

- MS3 and MS4 spectra (#138): purityA(), frag4feature() and
filterFragSpectra() take msLevel to process MS2 to MS4. purityA()
calculates MS3/MS4 precursor purity from the linked parent spectrum;
frag4feature(msLevel = 2:4) associates MS3/MS4 spectra with features
through their validated MS2 ancestors, with parentReference choosing
how parent spectra are identified. filterFragSpectra() applies
purity thresholds to each spectrum's own assessment, so a failed
parent does not exclude its descendants. MS3/MS4 averaging and
processed export are not supported yet.
- Parameter objects: PurityAParam, Frag4FeatureParam and
FilterFragSpectraParam extend ProtGenerics::Param and are passed
through param. Purity and filtering settings can be assigned by MS
level, activation method, collision energy or mass analyzer.
Explicit arguments that conflict with param are an error.
- Processing history records the resolved settings and their
assignments, the MS1 measurements used for each purity estimate, the
inputs used for feature association, the RT conversion and the
number of workers, and which filtering call produced each purity
flag on extracted Spectra.
- Bug fixes (#133, #103, #107): each MS2 event uses its recorded
isolation window, with explicit offsets taking precedence; an
Agilent isolation width is no longer assumed. Isolation-efficiency
weighting is corrected for asymmetric windows. Purity is NA with a
distinct reason outside valid isolation bounds or when no
neighbouring MS1 measurement can be used, and a later spectrum no
longer replaces a missing preceding one.
- purityTable() returns MS2 rows only. Filtering reads unchanged peak
arrays once, and equivalent parameter settings are resolved once.
- MSn parent-reference checks now run in batches, and frag4feature()
builds descendant feature associations in one pass, preserving
repeated links and their order (#138).

                       Changes in version 1.39.4                        

- Faster on Windows (#136): raw spectra are read serially through
Spectra. The default bpparam() on Windows is a SnowParam that
started a new cluster for every read, which made purityA(),
frag4feature() and the fragment filters many times slower there.
msPurity still runs files in parallel through its cores argument.
BiocParallel moves from Suggests to Imports.
- Examples load stored objects instead of rerunning the xcms and
purityA pipelines, spectralMatching() examples use the bundled mini
library instead of downloading the full one, and createDatabase(),
create_database() and createMSP() examples write to tempdir().

                       Changes in version 1.39.3                        

- Parquet built on MsBackendParquet (#126): manifests, mzStack
conditions, and writing and reading spectra now use the
MsBackendParquet dataset API, so msPurity and MsBackendParquet apply
one set of mzStack rules. MsBackendParquet (>= 0.99.10), arrow and
jsonlite move from Suggests to Imports.
- Parquet errors carry both mzstack_<class> and
msPurity_parquet_<class> classes; parquetCapabilities() reports the
mzstack_* names. A manifest commit refused by another writer keeps
msPurity_parquet_conflict.
- Parquet datasets store run paths relative to the dataset, so a
dataset can be moved or renamed. spectrum_index is int64 in every
run, part files are named by MsBackendParquet, core variables with
no values in a run are not written, and library sources without
spectra are not written as empty runs. The Parquet format is
unreleased, so no migration is needed.

                       Changes in version 1.39.2                        

- Bug fix: identifiers for processing records and Parquet datasets
could repeat when created in quick succession, most often on macOS,
where the clock that seeded them has microsecond resolution. A
repeated processing identifier replaced an earlier record and made
the processing history invalid. Identifiers now come from a random
stream seeded once per R process, and the caller's random number
stream is still left unchanged.

                       Changes in version 1.39.1                        

- flag_remove() now handles sample classes containing a single file
and combines validity flags across non-reference classes when
deciding which features to retain (#102).
- Package checks now run R CMD check and BiocCheck on Linux, macOS
and
Windows with matching R and Bioconductor versions (#130).
- Parquet output: new Parquet output, alongside SQLite.
createDatabase(), spectralMatching() and combineAnnotations() take
format = "parquet"; SQLite remains the default. Needs the suggested
packages arrow and jsonlite.
- Parquet conversion and validation: new functions
convertSqliteToParquet() converts an msPurity SQLite database to a
Parquet dataset, convertLibraryToParquet() converts an msp2db or MSP
spectral library or a Spectra object (such as an MSP file read with
MsBackendMsp), validateParquet() checks a Parquet dataset against
the specification, and parquetCapabilities() reports what the
Parquet output supports.
- Faster spectral matching on Parquet: spectralMatching() on Parquet
datasets gives the same scores as on SQLite and runs much faster
against large libraries. New argument topn keeps the best-ranked
matches per query. Their peaks are read through MsBackendParquet
when it is installed.
- SQLite output deprecated: every function that writes SQLite raises
one deprecation warning per call. Its output is unchanged.
- Spectra containers: msPurity reads raw data through Spectra and
stores spectra in Spectra objects. All results are unchanged.
Spectra and MsExperiment move from Suggests to Imports.
- New slots: purityA objects gain spectra, fragSpectra and avSpectra
slots: the MS/MS scans with their purity as spectra variables, the
scans linked to features (each once) with filter flags as peak
variables, and the averaged spectra. They also gain a params slot
recording the arguments of purityA() and frag4feature(). purityD
objects gain avSpectra (the averaged peak lists) and experiment (the
files as an MsExperiment) slots.
- New accessors: purityTable(), groupedSpectra(), allFragSpectra(),
averagedSpectra() and averagedPeaks() return either the legacy data
frames and lists or Spectra objects. Use them instead of reading
slots directly.
- Legacy slots: the legacy slots (puritydf, grped_ms2,
all_frag_scans,
av_spectra and avPeaks) are still filled by default.
options(msPurity.legacySlots = FALSE) leaves them empty; outputs are
the same either way. The default is planned to change in the next
release.
- Saved objects: updateObject() converts purityA and purityD objects
saved by earlier versions; every method does this on its input.
- More input types: purityA() accepts Spectra, MsExperiment and
XcmsExperiment objects as well as file paths, and reads each file
once. purityD() accepts an MsExperiment. frag4feature() and
createDatabase() accept XcmsExperiment objects.
- The mzRback argument is deprecated and ignored.
- Processing history: new functions processingHistory() and
processingParameters() for purityA objects and extracted Spectra.
purityA(), frag4feature(), filterFragSpectra() and the averaging
functions each record their effective settings (defaults included),
the software version, execution times and references to the spectra
they read and wrote, not copies of peaks. Repeated calls keep
earlier records. A subset of extracted Spectra returns only the
history of its own spectra. Objects saved by earlier versions get
their known settings imported, marked incomplete, with unknown dates
left unknown.
- Resolved purity settings: purityA() records, for each file, the
isolation offsets it used and where they came from (the caller, the
recorded metadata, or the Agilent approximation), and the iwNormFun
it applied when iwNorm = TRUE.
- Filtering by acquisition condition: new FilterFragSpectraParam(), a
ProtGenerics::Param holding complete filter settings, and a param
argument to filterFragSpectra() taking one such object or a named
list of them. Its select field assigns settings to spectra by MS
level, mass analyzer, activation type, collision energy and its
unit, and polarity, without discarding spectra. Spectra matched by
no set use the call's own arguments, and overlapping sets with
different settings stop with an error. CID, HCD and ETD are
recognised by abbreviation, CV name or accession. Where structured
metadata are missing, ordinary scan filter strings supply CID/HCD
and FTMS/ITMS. plim = NA skips purity filtering for the spectra a
set matches. Filtering with parameter sets needs cores = 1.
ProtGenerics is added to Imports.
- Peak provenance: filtered fragmentation spectra keep each peak's
position in its source spectrum (original_peak_index), and source
peak ids (sid) count the rows of the source data, including those of
intervening MSn spectra. Averaged spectra record the feature links
they were built from (msPurityContributors,
msPurityClusterContributors) and whether their inputs share one
acquisition configuration (msPurityAcquisitionConfiguration:
uniform, incomplete, mixed or unknown). Averaging itself is
unchanged, so MS2 averages can still combine acquisition conditions.
- Stale results cleared: running frag4feature() or
filterFragSpectra()
again clears the filter flags and averages that depended on the
previous run, and recomputing intra-file averages clears the
inter-file averages. Their history records are kept.
- allFragSpectra() names the scan of every peak correctly. The legacy
all_frag_scans table, and the scan peaks in SQLite output, number
scans with a count that skips scans without peaks, so after such a
scan they name the wrong scan; they are kept as they were because
the SQLite output is frozen.
- Bug fix: raw peaks and their filter flags could be assigned to the
wrong spectrum when a file had empty MS2 spectra or MS3/MS4 spectra
between them. Peaks are now matched by file and spectrum position.
When converting SQLite to Parquet, raw peaks sharing a pid with an
averaged spectrum were added to that average; an average now
contains only its own peaks. Ambiguous assignments are refused and
inconsistent identities in older databases raise a warning (#124).
- Bug fix: duplicate seqNum columns stopped new and RDS-reopened
objects from being exported to SQLite or Parquet (#124).
- Bug fix: spectral matching could pair a fragment peak outside the
m/z tolerance when it tied with an eligible peak on relative
intensity difference or mass error. Only eligible, unused library
peaks are now considered, in both the current and the deprecated
aligners, for SQLite and Parquet (#125).
- Bug fix: averaging after filterFragSpectra(rmp = TRUE) failed when
every spectrum of a feature lost all its peaks. Such features now
get no averaged spectrum, and the other averages equal those of rmp
= FALSE.
- Bug fix: createMSP(method = "max") failed when one peak of the
chosen spectrum passed the filters, and could write the wrong scan
when a scan was linked to a feature more than once. It now writes
the scan with the highest precursor intensity and skips spectra with
no passing peaks.
- Bug fix: createDatabase() called featureValues() without the xcms::
prefix and failed unless xcms was attached.
- Test data: four reduced mzML files with MS1-only and MS1 to MS4
acquisitions of L-tryptophan and L-kynurenine (#123). BiocParallel
is added to Suggests.

[msqrob2](/packages/msqrob2)
-------

                        Changes in version 1.21                         

Changes since Bioconductor 3.23 (msqrob2 1.20).

New features

- Empirical Bayes variance trend: argument trend in msqrob(),
msqrobLm(), msqrobLmer(), msqrobAggregate() and msqrobHurdle()
(intensity component). trend = FALSE (default) or "none" keeps a
global prior variance. "mean" conditions the prior on mean
log-intensity (as limma::eBayes(trend = TRUE)). "count" conditions
it on log2 of the number of features (e.g. peptides) summarised into
each protein: the .n column of QFeatures::aggregateFeatures() for
protein-level data, the number of features per group for
msqrobAggregate() and msqrobLmer(featureGroups = ), or counts in
msqrobLm()/msqrobLmer(). This is similar in spirit to DEqMS. The
binomial models (msqrobGlm(), msqrobQB(), the count component of
msqrobHurdle()) have no trend.
- Designs that are rank deficient for a feature, e.g. when a
condition
or the reference level is not observed for a protein, are now fitted
(msqrobLm(), msqrobLmer(), also with robust = TRUE) instead of
returning fitError. Contrasts that are not estimable for that
feature are NA (using the estimability package).
- msqrobLmer() stores the estimated variance component ratios of each
fit in getModel(model)$theta (lme4's parameterisation and names).
- msqrobLmer() also accepts a data.frame as data.

Changes in results

- Robust fits without random effects or ridge (msqrob() and the
intensity component of msqrobHurdle() with such a formula, and
msqrobLm()) use the variance of the Huber M-estimator (as
MASS::summary.rlm(method = "XtX")) instead of the weighted least
squares variance. The latter treats the Huber weights as known and
underestimates the variance, which made robust tests liberal. Log2
fold changes are unchanged; standard errors are typically a few
percent larger. Robust mixed and ridge models (msqrobLmer(), and
thus msqrobAggregate()) keep the previous variance.
- Empirical Bayes variance moderation always estimates the prior with
limma's fitFDistUnequalDF1() (squeezeVar(legacy = FALSE)), on the
fitted features only. Previously limma switched to its moment
estimator fitFDist() as soon as one feature failed to fit, so the
method depended on fit failures and filtering. Posterior variances,
and hence p-values, change slightly. Requires limma >= 3.62.0.
- msqrobLm(): maxitRob now defaults to 1, as in msqrob() and the
other
functions (was 5). Results of msqrob() are not affected.

Bug fixes

- msqrobAggregate() (and msqrobLmer() with rowdata): when the formula
uses exactly one sample variable and one feature variable (e.g. ~
condition + (1 | Sequence)), the sample variable keeps its type (in
the previous release a factor became integer codes and a numeric
covariate was treated as a factor).
- msqrobHurdle(ridge = TRUE) stores the intensity models on the
correct rows when the rows are not sorted by name (in the previous
release it could fail or attach the model of another protein).
- msqrobLmer(): a failure after the lmer fit gives a fitError instead
of an incomplete lmer model without coefficients.
- No error, but a warning, when no feature can be fitted.
- msqrobLm() no longer warns that rlm "failed to converge in maxitRob
steps": stopping after maxitRob iterations is intended (a one-step
M-estimator by default). Other warnings are kept.

Internal

- Modular implementation of the fitting functions and unit tests for
all functions in msqrob.R.

[MungeSumstats](/packages/MungeSumstats)
-------------

                       Changes in version 1.21.4                        

Bug fix

- P-values below ~4.9e-324, the smallest number R can store, are set
to 0. This now gives a message rather than happening silently
(#218):
- read_log_pval() counts the -log10 p-values above ~323.3 that
become P=0 and notes that the exact values are kept in the
-log10 column.
- check_small_p_val() counts text p-values (e.g. "1e-400", which
fread keeps as character) that become 0 whatever convert_small_p
is. It previously reported "0 p-values are <=5e-324" for these
and only converted P to numeric in the next check.
- read_log_pval() no longer errors when the -log10 p-value column
contains an NA ("missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed").
- The convert_small_p documentation now explains this limit.

                       Changes in version 1.21.3                        

Bug fix

- get_chain_file() (used by liftover()) now falls back to the bundled
Ensembl chain file whenever the download fails. Previously it only
did so if the failed download left an empty file behind, so a
failure that left no file stopped liftover() with a "No such file"
error (seen building the vignette on the Bioconductor nebbiolo2
builder). A failed UCSC download now gives a clear error.
- Chain files are now downloaded over https rather than ftp.

                       Changes in version 1.21.2                        

Bug fix

- pkgdown GitHub Action: skip the unused
SNPlocs.Hsapiens.dbSNP155.GRCh38 Suggests, free runner disk space
and disable the package cache, as installing every reference genome
Suggests ran the runner out of disk (#170).

                       Changes in version 1.21.1                        

Bug fix

- format_sumstats() with the default ref_genome=NULL (genome build
inference) errored in validate_parameters() since dbSNP tarball
support was added (#49, #114).
- check_chr() converted MT/chrMT to MTT, removing mitochondrial SNPs
when they were kept with rmv_chr (#116, #130, #158).
- check_on_ref_genome(): SNPs not on the reference genome were not
corrected or removed when indels were present, SNPs sharing an ID
with an indel were silently dropped and the indel removal could
exceed data.table's 2^31 join limit (#164).
- check_bp_range() now checks BP for chr-prefixed, 23/24 and lower
case CHR names (#144) and no longer silently drops rows with an
unknown CHR (#150).
- check_zscore() no longer errors when some p-values are NA (#212).
- infer_effect_column() no longer errors when swapping mixed case
allele column headers (#208).
- liftover() no longer deletes a gzipped local_chain file (#183) and
now applies rmv_chr (#211). Its documented rmv_chr default is
corrected.
- load_snp_loc_data() no longer reuses a dbSNP tarball extraction
made
from a different tarball (#204).
- write_sumstats(): .vcf.gz output is written to the given path with
no leftover .vcf, tabix-indexed VCFs return the indexed file path
(#216), and only the end of save_path is treated as a suffix, here
and in check_save_path() (#34).
- Logging (log_mungesumstats_msgs=TRUE) no longer warns "no sink to
remove", closes its log connection and leaves a caller's own sink in
place (#207, #80).
- parse_logs() default pattern now matches the current
&lt;save_path>_log_msg.txt log names (#68).
- read_sumstats() matches file suffixes literally so e.g.
gwas_vcf.tsv
is read as a tabular file (#155).
- read_vcf() with nThread>1 works for VCFs without a ##SAMPLE line or
with header contigs that have no records (#21).
- compute_nsize() sets IMPUTATION_n again (#43). check_n_int()
handles
a character N column with imputation_ind=TRUE (#26).
- A data.table mapping_file is accepted by format_sumstats() (#174).
- check_ldsc_format() prints its allele_flip_check message and
accepts
a vector compute_n (#3).
- get_chain_file() finds cached chain files in any save_dir (#84).
- The number of SNPs reported by check_multi_rs_snp() with
remove_multi_rs_snp=TRUE now matches the number removed (#48).
- Messages report the number of indels found (#139).
- Reusing a previously formatted file with return_data=TRUE no longer
picks up a global sumstats_return object (#24).
- N_dropNA now works as documented (TRUE drops rows with a missing N)
and a missing N no longer turns off the N_std filter (#29).
- *.vcf.tsv(.gz) files that are tab-delimited text rather than VCFs
(e.g. PGC sumstats) are now read as tabular files (#91, #154).
- The bi-allelic and allele flip checks no longer drop SNPs that are
not on the reference genome (e.g. indels) when other SNPs are
removed (#139, #140).
- Minor allele frequency columns (MAF, MINOR_AF) are only used as FRQ
when no allele frequency column (e.g. REGENIE's A1FREQ) is present
(#142).
- standardise_header() accepts a data.table or lower case
mapping_file
(#174).
- Rerunning with log_mungesumstats_msgs=TRUE overwrites the previous
log files instead of appending to them (#80) and a caller's message
sink is restored afterwards (#207).
- infer_effect_column() identifies which allele an effect/frequency
column refers to from its allele naming in any case (e.g. METAL's
Freq1, FREQ.ALLELE1.HAPMAPCEU) (#208).
- check_no_chr_bp() works when passed pre-loaded reference data
(#150).

New features

- Regression tests for past GitHub issues added (test-issues_*.R in
tests/ and longtests/), each named after the issue it covers.
- Long tests: test-write_sumstats.R and test-missing_data.R synced
with the unit test versions (fixes the failing long tests build).
- testthat (>= 3.1.7) is now required to run the tests (for mocking).
