[musicatk](/packages/musicatk)
--------

                 Changes in version 2.7.19 (2026-11-15)                 

- R/benchmarking.R now passes lintr. This changes only formatting,
not
results, messages or the exported functions and their arguments
(#257).

                 Changes in version 2.7.18 (2026-11-13)                 

- benchmark() splits a composite signature (one matching several true
signatures) into pieces that keep its noise. The composite is fitted
to its true signatures with non-negative least squares, and each
mutation type's probability is divided among them in proportion to
the fit, so the "<true signature>_like" pieces add up to the
composite (a true signature with no weight in the fit gets no
piece). Each piece gets the composite's exposure times its share of
the composite, so Final RE equals the reconstruction error before
the split, also for composites that don't sum to 1. Before, a
composite was replaced by copies of the true signatures, with cosine
similarity 1, so a prediction with a composite scored better than
the correct one (#191). Composites of three or more signatures
(#189) and DBS78 composites (#190) work; before, they stopped with
an error. Summaries of predictions with composites change.
- The benchmark() summary's Num Found, Num Missing, Mean/Min/Max CS
and Sigs Found all describe the Final stage, with each true
signature counted once at its best cosine similarity, so Found +
Missing is the number of true signatures. Before, Found counted rows
of the Final comparison (a signature matched twice counted twice)
and Missing came from the Initial one (#198). sig_view_summary()
also uses each run's best cosine similarity, and lists the true
signatures in their own order.
- benchmark() merges each predicted signature into at most one group
of duplicates, that of the true signature it matches best. Before, a
signature matching two duplicated true signatures was merged into
both, counting its exposure twice (#188). After composites are
split, a piece and another predicted signature that match the same
true signature best are merged too, so the Final stage has one
signature per true signature. The summary counts each predicted
signature once: a duplicate matches a true signature that another
prediction also matches, a composite matches several, and Dup/Comp
is both; before, a signature in two duplicate groups was counted in
both. Predicted signatures whose names contain "like" are no longer
left out of duplicate merging.
- method_view_summary(), sig_view_summary() and single_summary()
return data.frames, with one row per benchmark run (or per signature
for sig_view_summary()), integer counts, and numeric reconstruction
errors and cosine similarities. Before, they were character matrices
with runs or signatures as columns (#201, ADR 0004). A
full_benchmark made with an earlier version must be recreated with
create_benchmark() before benchmark() adds to it.
full_benchmark_example is rebuilt by
data-raw/make_full_benchmark_example.R; its results are unchanged. A
global variable named duplicated_signature_components no longer
changes the summary counts.
- benchmark(plot = FALSE) no longer draws plots (#196). A prediction
with no match above threshold is recorded as a total miss instead of
stopping with "No matches found" (#200).
- create_benchmark() stores the ground truth under the count-table
name, "SBS96" or "DBS78", when given an alias such as "SBS" or
"DBS", and create_musica_from_counts() accepts "DBS78". Before,
"SBS" made benchmark(..., "SBS96") fail, and DBS benchmarks could
not be run (#195). benchmark() stops with a clear error when
prediction_modality isn't the ground truth's.
- benchmark_get_comparison() accepts the stage aliases the other
benchmark functions accept, such as "final"; before, they stopped
with "object 'comparison' not found" (#193). The aliases ("Init",
"Inter", "Fin", in any case) are now documented.
- predict_and_benchmark() benchmarks the model it has just discovered
when <algorithm><k> already exists in the musica object, and names
the run after it (for example lda2.1); before, it benchmarked the
older model (#197). It checks full_benchmark and modality before
running any discovery.
- benchmark() names a repeated method_id <id>.10, <id>.11, and so on;
before, the eleventh repeat became <id>..11 (as #148 for model_id).
- The benchmark functions accept subclasses of full_benchmark and
musica (#94). An internal duplicate of .get_reconstruction_error()
was removed (#199).

                 Changes in version 2.7.17 (2026-11-12)                 

- Code in R/ (except R/benchmarking.R) now passes lintr. This changes
only formatting and internal names, not results or the exported
functions and their arguments (#257).

                 Changes in version 2.7.16 (2026-11-12)                 

- Added the COSMIC v3.6 (May 2026) signatures as new data objects,
following ADR 0003: cosmic_v3_6_sbs_sigs_grch37,
cosmic_v3_6_sbs_sigs_grch38, cosmic_v3_6_sbs_sigs_grch37_exome,
cosmic_v3_6_sbs_sigs_grch38_exome, cosmic_v3_6_dbs_sigs_grch37,
cosmic_v3_6_dbs_sigs_grch38 and cosmic_v3_6_indel_sigs. v3.6 has 101
SBS, 22 DBS and 25 Indel signatures, and revises the probabilities
of signatures that were in v3.0. COSMIC publishes one Indel
catalogue per version, so the Indel object has no build.
data-raw/make_cosmic_v3_6.R rebuilds them from the COSMIC files; the
exome SBS files come from SigProfilerAssignment, whose genome files
match COSMIC's.
- cosmic_v3_sbs_sigs, cosmic_v3_dbs_sigs, cosmic_v3_indel_sigs and
cosmic_v3_sbs_sigs_exome are unchanged and stay COSMIC v3.0
(GRCh37), so code that uses them, for example in predict_exposure(),
gives the same results. Their documentation now states the version
and build.
- compare_cosmic_v3() gains genome_build ("hg19"/"GRCh37" or
"hg38"/"GRCh38", default "hg19") and cosmic_version ("latest", "3.0"
or "3.6", default "latest"). "latest" uses the newest version with a
catalogue for the sample type, modality and build, which is v3.6 for
every catalogue musicatk ships, exome included. With the defaults,
genome and exome comparisons now use v3.6 instead of v3.0, so their
matches and similarities change; cosmic_version = "3.0" gives the
earlier results. Each call prints a message naming the version,
modality, sample type and build used. A combination musicatk doesn't
ship, such as cosmic_version = "3.0" with genome_build = "hg38", is
an error that lists the catalogues available. The two new arguments
come last, so existing calls are unaffected. The result's
"cosmic_catalogue" attribute names the data object compared against.
- In the Shiny app, the prediction tab offers the COSMIC v3.6 sets
for
each build (including SBS exome) and the v3.0 sets, labelled with
version and build, and defaults to v3.6 SBS for the build the
variants were imported with. The comparison tab has one COSMIC V3
choice with a genome build choice, set from the import genome, and a
COSMIC version choice; the comparison table names the COSMIC object
used, and the plot title names its version. A failed comparison
shows its error without ending the session. Signatures new in v3.6
without an aetiology label show their name, and SBS22a/b/c and
SBS40a/b/c have labels.

                 Changes in version 2.7.15 (2026-11-11)                 

- plot_heatmap(scale = TRUE), the default, z-scores each signature
across samples. Before, it z-scored each sample across signatures,
so default heatmaps look different; a signature with the same value
in every sample is shown as 0 (#176).
- plot_heatmap(subset_tumor =) works. It keeps samples whose value in
any sample annotation column exactly matches one of the given values
(several are allowed), stops naming values found in no column or
matching no sample in the model, and shows the annotation columns,
or the columns the values were found in. Before, it always stopped
with an error about the number of observations in the top annotation
(#175).
- plot_signatures() colours the motif header boxes by name from
color_mapping, matching the bars, and uses white text on dark boxes.
Before, header colours were taken in the order of color_mapping, so
a reordered mapping coloured headers and bars differently. An
unnamed color_mapping now works, used in the order the values first
appear along the motifs (before, it stopped with "arguments imply
differing number of rows"); one missing a value stops with an error
naming it (#177).
- plot_signatures(color_variable =) uses the named column of the
count
table annotation, and a vector with one value per motif is matched
to the motifs. Before, a column name was ignored and a vector was
recycled across signatures. Without color_mapping, colours are
generated when the table's default mapping doesn't cover the values
(#178).
- plot_signatures() header boxes follow runs of equal values along
the
motifs, so a color_variable whose values recur in several places
gets one box per run instead of overlapping boxes (#177, #178).
- plot_signatures() no longer adds a global variable named
annotation_text to the plot (#186).
- plot_exposures(plot_type = "box") and "violin" with the default
group_by = "none" give one box or violin per signature. Before, they
silently gave a bar plot (#179).
- plot_exposures(threshold =) sets exposures below the threshold to
0,
as documented. Before, it dropped them, which removed points from
box and violin plots (#184).
- plot_umap() colour scales include the largest exposure; before,
rounding could leave the top samples grey (#180). Annotation labels
no longer stretch the y-axis (#181). color_by = "cluster" needs
clust, not annotation (#182). Before create_umap(), it says to run
create_umap() first (#183).
- create_umap(), and with proportional = TRUE cluster_exposure(),
k_select(), plot_cluster(group = "signature"), plot_umap(),
plot_heatmap() and plot_exposures(), stop with an error naming
samples whose exposures are all 0. Before, they failed with unclear
errors or plotted missing values (#183).
- plot_cluster() no longer uses aes_string(), deprecated in ggplot2
(#95).

                 Changes in version 2.7.14 (2026-11-11)                 

- build_standard_table(..., "DBS78") works when no DBS has a
reference
that needs reverse-complementing (for example, only CC>TT); before,
it stopped with "Must be character or character vector" (#132, #52).
rc() returns an empty vector for an empty input, and is vectorised,
so it is much faster on long vectors.
- build_standard_table(..., "SBS192") without strand_type stops with
an error saying it is needed; before, it failed with "argument is of
length zero" (#136). The check for an existing table uses the
table's name, SBS192_Trans or SBS192_Rep, as for the other tables:
building it again stops with "already exists" instead of "Table
names must be unique", and with overwrite = TRUE it warns that the
table is overwritten, which it didn't before.
- build_standard_table() messages name the table they create, for
example "Building count table 'SBS96' ..." for modality = "SNV96",
so the name to use afterwards is clear (#17).
- combine_count_tables() names the tables in to_comb that don't
exist;
before, that error failed with 'argument "y" is missing' (#137).

                 Changes in version 2.7.13 (2026-11-10)                 

- exposure_differential_analysis(method = "glm.nb") adjusted the
wrong
p-values: each <group>(fdr) column held the next group's adjusted
p-values, and the last held the ANOVA's. Each non-reference group's
p-values are now BH-adjusted across signatures. The reference group
(the first level of the annotation) has no group effect: its
columns, which hold the intercept, are named Intercept(coef),
Intercept(Std. Error), Intercept(z) and Intercept(Pr(>|z|)), and it
has no (fdr) column. The other groups' (coef) is their log fold
change against the reference. Coefficients are read by name, so an
aliased group gives NA instead of shifting the columns (#169).
- exposure_differential_analysis(method = "wilcox") works with any
number of comparisons in group1 and group2; three or more failed
with "only 0's may be mixed with negative subscripts" (#170). The
p-values and FDRs are numbers instead of character strings, in
columns renamed p-value and fdr (from Pr(>|z|) and (fdr)), as for
method = "kruskal". The FDR is adjusted within each comparison,
across signatures. For two groups (one comparison) this gives the
same values as before; with two comparisons, the FDR was adjusted
across both together (#171).
- cluster_exposure(method = "kmeans") runs k-means with
stats::kmeans(), which k_select() already used, and needs dis.method
= "euclidean". It uses 10 random starts (new nstart argument) seeded
by a new seed argument, default 1, applied with withr::with_seed(),
so the clusters are the same each time and the caller's random
number state is left unchanged; seed = NULL uses it. Before, it ran
fuzzy clustering (cluster::fanny()) with at most 10 iterations,
which often warned that it hadn't converged; that is now method =
"fanny", with up to 500 iterations by default (iter.max now defaults
to NULL: 10 for "kmeans" and "hkmeans", 500 for "fanny"). The Shiny
app offers only Euclidean distance for k-means (#34).
- k_select() takes a seed argument, default 1, so its plot is the
same
each time, and runs k-means with 10 random starts.
- cluster_exposure(method = "hclust") clusters the dissimilarity
matrix that dis.method chooses. Before, it clustered the Euclidean
distances between rows of that matrix, so dis.method acted only
indirectly and the clusters differ from those of the chosen distance
(#173).
- cluster_exposure(dis.method = "cosine") uses 1 - cosine similarity
as the distance. Before, "pam" and "kmeans" used the cosine
similarity itself, treating the most similar samples as the farthest
apart.
- plot_differential_analysis() plots -log10(FDR) for each signature,
for all three methods, with a dashed line at its new threshold
argument (default 0.05). The method is read from the table's
columns. Before, it plotted only the first columns of the table as
given, so for "wilcox" it plotted text and for "glm.nb" the
intercept, and for other values of analysis_type it returned NULL.
analysis_type and samp_num are ignored with a warning. For "glm.nb",
bars are labelled "<group> vs <reference>", from a "reference"
attribute that exposure_differential_analysis() now sets; NA FDRs
are left out with a message (#174).
- k_select() lowers n to the number of samples minus one, with a
message; with the default n = 10 it failed on ten or fewer samples.
It stops with an error for fewer than three samples, or when n isn't
a number of at least 2 (#185).

                 Changes in version 2.7.12 (2026-11-09)                 

- predict_exposure() and auto_predict_grid() take a seed argument,
default 1, so algorithm = "lda" gives the same exposures each time,
as discover_signatures() does; the caller's random number state is
left unchanged, and seed = NULL uses it as before. LDA predictions
change from earlier, unseeded runs. withr moves from Suggests to
Imports for this (ADR 0002) (#152).
- generate_result_grid() uses its annotation argument. Before, it
always read a Tumor_Type column: with any other column it stored no
models, and with Tumor_Type every group's model overwrote the
previous group's. Models are now named <algorithm><k>_<group> (for
example lda3_Lung), samples with a missing annotation are left out
with a message, and an error in one group names the group (#140).
- generate_result_grid() keeps the new fit when a model of the same
name already exists, storing it as lda2.1 and so on. Before, it
silently kept the old model and discarded the new fit.
auto_predict_grid() had the same problem with its per-group models
(#141).
- predict_exposure() matches signatures to the count table by motif
name, and stores the signatures in the table's motif order, as does
combine_predict_grid() for the models it combines. Before,
signatures whose rows were in a different order from the table gave
wrong exposures without an error, and signatures of another type
(for example DBS78 on an SBS96 table) ran with only a recycling
warning; these now stop with an error. algorithm = "decompTumor2Sig"
stops for tables other than SBS96 (#142).
- Samples with no mutations in the count table are left out of the
exposures with a message naming them, by discover_signatures(),
predict_exposure(), generate_result_grid() and auto_predict_grid();
before, they were left out silently. generate_result_grid() and
compare_k_vals() no longer fail on them ("subscript out of bounds",
"NA in probability vector"). discover_signatures() needs at least
two samples with mutations (#143).
- auto_predict_grid() works with a result_name other than "result"
(#145) and with a factor annotation column (#146), and says which
thresholds to lower when no signature passes them (#147).
- Repeated model ids are numbered .1, .2, … .10, .11; the 12th copy
was ..11 (#148).
- compare_k_vals() stops with an error for an invalid error_type
before running any fit; before, it ran every fit and returned NA
(#149).
- predict_exposure(algorithm = "lda") no longer gives 100 warnings
for
a single sample. generate_result_grid() documents its reconstruction
error metric (#152).
- compare_cosmic_v2() and the other comparison functions work for a
model with one signature (#162).

                 Changes in version 2.7.11 (2026-11-09)                 

- The example files in inst/extdata are replaced by 12 TCGA samples
chosen for strong mutational signatures, so the examples and
vignette show clean signatures (#217, #238):
- four lung tumors with a strong smoking signature (COSMIC SBS4)
and four with a strong APOBEC signature (SBS2 and SBS13), and
four melanomas with a strong UV signature (SBS7a and SBS7b),
each with 150 to 500 SBS, from GDC open-access aliquot ensemble
masked MAFs (hg38). data-raw/choose_example_samples.R chose them
and data-raw/example_files.R writes the files.
- The files are public_LUSC_TCGA-22-5472-01A-01D-1632-08.vcf,
public_TCGA_lung.maf (the other seven lung tumors) and four
public_SKCM_*.vcf files, 4,233 variants in all. They replace
public_LUAD_TCGA-97-7938.vcf, public_TCGA.LUSC.maf and three
public_SKCM_*.vcf files (911 variants from 7 samples), whose two
lung signatures were weak and in which six insertions had a REF
base that wasn't the hg38 base at POS. Code that reads the old
file names must use the new ones.
- VCF REF and ALT match hg38, and indels start with the base
before the event, so building a musica object from the example
files no longer warns "Reference bases for 6 out of 911 variants
did not match".
- inst/extdata is 659 KB instead of 912 KB.
- inst/extdata/sample_annotations.txt labels the lung tumors "Lung"
and the melanomas "Skin"; the earlier file labelled its three
melanomas "Breast".
- The vignette names each discovered signature after the etiology of
its most similar COSMIC V3 signature (Smoking, APOBEC or UV),
instead of by position, and its comparison to COSMIC reports the
matches it found. The vignette had named the signatures in the wrong
order.
- The example datasets are rebuilt with the current import and table
code, all from TCGA on hg38, and each has a data-raw/ script and a
@source (#217):
- musica, musica_annot, musica_sbs96 and musica_sbs96_tiny are
built from the new example files by
data-raw/example_musica.R: 12 samples, 4,014 SBS, 64 DBS, 73
deletions and 15 insertions (three complex deletion-insertions
in the MAF are removed on import, as usual). musica_sbs96_tiny
holds 40 SBS each of a smoking and an APOBEC lung tumor.
- res and res_annot are a three-signature NMF fit on that SBS96
table: Signature1 is an APOBEC signature (0.99 cosine to a mix
of SBS2 and SBS13), Signature2 a smoking signature (SBS4, 0.86)
and Signature3 a UV signature (SBS7a, 0.95), each carrying at
least 93% of the exposure of its group's samples.
- These six objects take 137 KB instead of 45 KB.
- dbs_musica holds all variants of the five TCGA-LUAD tumors with
the most DBS in GDC open-access MAFs, leaving out
whole-genome-amplified DNA (176 DBS), with SBS96 and DBS78
tables. Before, it mixed 400 SBS on hg38 with 400 DBS from other
samples on hg19.
- indel_musica holds the 211 insertions and deletions of the same
five TCGA-UCEC tumors as before, from their current GDC MAFs.
Its earlier 300 indels could not be traced to a source.

                 Changes in version 2.7.10 (2026-11-08)                 

- extract_variants() and the VCF readers keep records whose FILTER is
. (no filters applied) when filter = TRUE, as well as PASS. Before,
VCFs that mark passing calls with ., such as the PCAWG consensus
VCFs, returned no variants. When no record passes, the warning lists
the FILTER values found (#214).
- extract_variants() and extract_variants_from_maf_file() read MAFs
whose records are all silent or non-coding; before,
maftools::read.maf() stopped with "No non-synonymous mutations
found". A MAF with no records gives a warning and no variants, as a
VCF does, so one such file no longer stops extract_variants() from
reading the others (#241).
- VCF alleles are trimmed to their minimal form. Splitting a
multiallelic site can leave alleles that share more than one base:
REF ATG with ALT A,AT gave ATG>AT, which was removed as a compound
deletion, and REF AT with ALT A,GT gave the DBS AT>GT. They are now
the deletion TG>T and the SBS A>G. Counts change only for VCFs with
multiallelic sites or other alleles that share more than one base;
the bundled example files have none (#213).
- ALT * (an allele missing because of an overlapping deletion) and
symbolic alleles such as <DEL> are left out of VCF input with a
message. Before, * was counted as an SBS (#215).
- IND83 tables count indels near the start or end of a chromosome,
using the flank that is there; before, the whole table failed
(#233).
- build_standard_table(..., "IND83") stops with an error when indels
are not standardized (built with standardize_indels = FALSE);
before, the VCF anchor base was counted as part of the indel and
gave wrong bins (#234).
- IND83 tables warn when indels are left out because their motif
isn't
in the table, for example an insertion of N (#236).

                 Changes in version 2.7.9 (2026-11-08)                  

- IND83 tables put some indels in the wrong bin. On indel_musica, 16
of 300 indels move to another bin (12 of the 56 1 bp insertions, 3
longer insertions and 1 microhomology deletion); totals are
unchanged. Rebuild IND83 tables made with an earlier version (#9):
- Insertion flanks start next to the insertion. Before, the left
flank skipped the base before the insertion, and for MAF
insertions the right flank skipped the base after it, so for
example chr1:153056355 +T in indel_musica was INS_T_1_4 instead
of INS_T_1_5+ (#129).
- Repeats of multi-base units are counted on the left of the indel
too. Before, a unit like AC never matched on the left, so indels
with copies of their unit on the left (for example, deleting any
copy but the first in a repeat) counted too few copies (#128).
- Microhomology on the left of a deletion is compared with the
bases next to it, not the far end of the flank (#127).
- Insertions of 2 bp or more look five unit lengths to each side,
as deletions do. Before, they looked 10 bp, so INS_repeats_4_5+
and INS_repeats_5+_5+ were almost never counted (#130).
- build_standard_table() builds IND83 tables when some indel classes
are missing, for example with only deletions or only insertions;
before, it stopped with an error. With no indels at all, it stops
with "No insertions or deletions found." The help page says how
indels are binned (#126).

                 Changes in version 2.7.8 (2026-11-07)                  

- annotate_transcript_strand() leaves SBS in overlapping genes on
opposite strands as NA, like SBS outside genes, so they are left out
of SBS192_Trans tables. Before, they took the strand of whichever
gene came last in the overlap list, so their "T" or "U" label was
arbitrary. SBS192_Trans counts drop: on data(musica), from 807
to 719 with hg38 and from 584 to 556 with hg19. Re-run
annotate_transcript_strand() on objects annotated with an earlier
version before building SBS192_Trans (#221).

                 Changes in version 2.7.7 (2026-11-06)                  

- annotate_replication_strand() gives A>* and G>* SBS the replication
strand of their pyrimidine, the strand SBS192 counts them on.
rep_range labels the plus strand, so these SBS now take the opposite
label: a G>T in a lagging range is a C>A on the leading-strand
template. Before, they kept the plus-strand label, so they were
counted on the wrong strand in SBS192_Rep tables. SBS192_Rep counts
and the Replication_Strand table change for every SBS with an A or G
reference base; SBS with a C or T reference base are unchanged.
Re-run annotate_replication_strand() on objects annotated with an
earlier version before building SBS192_Rep. A GRanges passed as
rep_range must label the plus strand, as rep_range does (#222).

                 Changes in version 2.7.6 (2026-11-06)                  

- New rep_range_hg38: rep_range lifted over to hg38, for annotating
replication strand on hg38 variants. Labels are swapped in regions
inverted between the builds. The examples and the Shiny app use the
object that matches the genome build; for mm9 or mm10 the app now
shows an error instead of annotating with human data (#220).
- annotate_replication_strand() accepts the genome build for
rep_range: "hg19" (or "GRCh37") uses rep_range and "hg38" (or
"GRCh38") uses rep_range_hg38. A GRanges still works as before
(#220).
- rep_range is tagged with genome "hg19" and its chromosome lengths,
and is documented with its source (GEO GSM4305465) and what
"leading" and "lagging" mean. data-raw/rep_range.R rebuilds both
objects (#220).
- rep_range bins are 1-based. Before, neighbouring bins shared an
edge
position, so a variant on an edge could match two bins and take
whichever label came last. Replication strand changes only for
variants on a bin edge (#220).

                 Changes in version 2.7.5 (2026-11-06)                  

- annotate_transcript_strand() leaves SBS outside genes as NA;
before,
they got the string "NA" and were labelled "T". SBS192_Trans tables
now count only SBS in genes, so their counts drop (on data(musica),
from 884 to 807) (#105).
- add_flank_to_variants() takes the flank of A>* and G>* SBS from the
pyrimidine strand; before, a left flank returned the bases 3' of the
mutated base and a right flank those 5' of it (#104).
- annotate_transcript_strand() accepts a TxDb object for genome_build
(#117).
- annotate_replication_strand() no longer fails, or copies one strand
to every row, when the variant table doesn't end in SBS. Variants
without a replication strand are NA rather than the string "NA"
(#118).
- annotate_variant_length() gives indels a length: the number of
inserted bases, or minus the number of deleted bases. Before, every
indel length was NA (#119).
- SBS96 and SBS192 tables warn when variants are left out because
their motif isn't in the table. For SBS96 this happens when a
reference base doesn't match g, for example when g is not the genome
build the variants were called on; for both tables, when the context
has N bases (#135).
- Examples and the vignette use the hg38 genome for the hg38 example
data. The rep_range docs say it is on hg19 (#120).

                 Changes in version 2.7.4 (2026-11-05)                  

- extract_variants_from_vcf() with multiallele = "expand" gives each
sample only the alternate alleles in its GT; before, a sample
carrying any alternate allele at a multiallelic site got all of them
(#106).
- multiallele = "exclude" returns alt as a character column and no
longer drops every indel from an ExpandedVCF (#110).
- VCFs without a GT field (for example from Strelka) keep all
variants
passing the filter, with a message; before, they returned NULL. Such
a VCF with several sample columns needs id or rename, and one
without sample columns needs rename (#111).
- extra_fields keeps the column name of a single INFO field, gives
per-allele (Number=A) fields the value for each allele, and joins
other multi-value fields with commas (#121).
- extract_variants_from_vcf_file() with fix_vcf_errors = TRUE removes
malformed lines and reads the rest, with a warning; before, it
returned the function stats::dt (#112).
- extract_variants() reads .vcf.gz and .maf.gz files (#113).
- create_musica_from_variants() accepts a matrix and factor columns
(#114), and reads lowercase bases as uppercase instead of removing
them (#123).
- create_musica_from_variants() moves VCF-style deletions to start at
the first deleted base, as in MAF files, so a deletion gets the same
ID83 bin from either format. ID83 counts from VCF input can change
(#108).
- Indels whose first base differs between ref and alt (for example A >
GGT) are removed as complex variants with a message; before, they
were rewritten as indels (#109).
- convert_dbs = TRUE merges adjacent SBS only within a sample;
before,
SBS from different samples could become one DBS, and unsorted
neighbours were missed. A run of three or more adjacent SBS becomes
one variant of type "MNV", which no standard count table includes.
DBS78 and SBS96 counts can change (#107).
- Variants on chromosomes missing from the genome are removed with a
warning; before, they crashed the reference check (#115).
- create_musica_from_counts() matches rows to motifs by row name;
before, it overwrote the row names, so tables in another order were
mislabelled. COSMIC/SigProfiler row names (A[C>A]A, AC>CA) are
converted to musicatk motif names; other row names give an error
(#116).

                 Changes in version 2.7.3 (2026-11-05)                  

- name_signatures() returns the renamed musica object (invisibly), so
res <- name_signatures(res, ...) works; before, it returned the
vector of names. The object passed in is still renamed in place as
before (#154).
- The setters num_signatures<-, other_parameters<-,
credible_intervals<-, model_id<- and modality<- now work; they could
never be called before. model_id<- and modality<- on a musica or
result_collection object also rename or move the stored model, so
get_model() finds it by the new id or modality (#156).
- hyperparameter<- on a musica object now assigns the value; before,
it always failed (#157).
- subset_musica_by_annotation() gives its intended error when the
requested values are missing (#163).
- samp_annot<- accepts Date and date-time (POSIXct, POSIXlt) vectors,
and variants<- accepts a data.frame (#164).
- subset_variants_by_samples() returns all variants of every
requested
sample; with several names it returned only some of them (#48).

                 Changes in version 2.7.2 (2026-11-04)                  

- Samples are now matched by name everywhere. sample_names() (the
Samples column of the sample annotations) sets the sample order;
count tables and stored exposures follow it, and new validity
methods for musica, result_model and result_collection check this
(#153, #160). Objects saved with older versions whose tables are out
of order give an error asking to rebuild the table with overwrite =
TRUE; a full_benchmark saved with an older version must be recreated
with create_benchmark().
- exposure_differential_analysis(), plot_heatmap() and plot_cluster()
pair annotations with exposures by sample name; before, results were
wrong when the orders differed, as in the shipped res_annot (#153).
plot_cluster(group = "annotation") now uses the annotation argument
(#172).
- The shipped musica datasets and full_benchmark_example were
repaired
so their annotations, count tables and exposures share one sample
order; no count or exposure values changed. The vignette now matches
sample_annotations.txt to the samples by name; before, 6 of 7
samples got the wrong Tumor_Subtypes label.
- sample_names() returns a character vector and no longer partially
matches a Sample column (#158).
- create_musica_from_counts() stores the column names as sample
names,
so its objects can be annotated; it stops on missing or duplicated
column names (#159).
- subset_musica_by_counts() and subset_musica_by_annotation() also
subset stored exposures (#155).
- Count tables no longer get all-zero columns for samples removed by
subsetting (#134), IND83 columns are named correctly (#131), and
combine_count_tables() aligns samples by name (#133).
- add_result() matches exposure columns to the samples by name and
puts them in sample order; unknown or missing sample names give an
error.
- combine_predict_grid() returns exposures in sample order and sets
num_signatures and model_id; it stops when the models share samples
(#144).
- create_benchmark() stores true exposures as signatures x samples
and
matches them to the count table by sample name; either orientation
is accepted (#194).

[MutSeqR](/packages/MutSeqR)
-------

                        Changes in version 1.1.2                        

- spectra_comparison() selects the existing G2 test with method =
"g2"
(the default) or the replicate-aware test with method = "rpdmm". The
summary report now uses the latter with sample-level counts and a
ridge penalty chosen by select_optimal_lambda() using leave-one-out
cross-validation. The replicate-aware, ridge-penalized
Dirichlet-multinomial model accounts for replicate heterogeneity and
overdispersion in high-count ECS data. The L2 penalty stabilizes
category probability estimates, and hybrid and penalized
likelihood-ratio tests are calibrated by parametric bootstrap. Both
methods share input validation, contrast handling, and count-matrix
preparation while retaining pooled G2 counts and per-sample RPDMM
counts.

- filter_mut() matches custom_filter_val as a literal substring (not
as a regular expression) in rows of custom_filter_col, including a
FILTER label among semicolon-separated labels, and warns when a
value matches no rows. Empty or missing custom_filter_val values now
produce an error. A custom_filter_col given without
custom_filter_val now stops, where it silently filtered on the
column's first value.

- spectra_comparison_rpdmm() is now internal. Use
spectra_comparison(method = "rpdmm") instead of calling it directly.

                        Changes in version 1.1.1                        

- import_vcf_data() reads FORMAT SITE_DP, the read depth at the
record's position that vartovcf writes, as the total_depth. Records
whose total_depth is missing take it from AD or DP.

- import_vcf_data() takes alt_depth from the alternate allele depths
of AD when a VCF has no VD, instead of setting every record's
alt_depth to 1. Records without an alternate allele get 0.

- import_vcf_data() no longer counts a missing AD value as 0 reads. A
record whose AD lacks the reference depth, as VarDict writes for MNV
and complex calls, takes its total_depth from DP, so its vaf is no
longer inflated toward 1.

- import_vcf_data() reads an INFO CONTEXT_3mer, as vartovcf writes
with --context-3mer, as the context, so no BS genome is needed.

- import_vcf_data() keeps the VCF FILTER value in a new filter
column,
which filter_mut() can act on with custom_filter_col = "filter".

- import_vcf_data() imports large VCFs several times faster: each
file's records are bound as data frames rather than VCF objects,
FORMAT fields with several values are spread without a per-record
loop, and each distinct REF/ALT pair and context is classified once.
Three 48,000-record gVCFs import in 4 seconds instead of 23, with
identical results.

- calculate_mf() gains an optional depth_group_cols argument to
declare sample-level precalculated depths explicitly, including
context-resolved inputs with dose metadata. Declared sample depths
are validated and pooled to requested groups; missing sample depths
warn with affected groups. Default interpretation is preserved, with
guidance for invalid grouped inputs.

- calculate_mf() infers the grouping resolution of precalculated
depths and aggregates finer inputs to cols_to_group, preserving
context resolution.

- Import functions check for installed BSgenome packages before
checking online for available genomes, avoiding an unnecessary
internet connection.

- calculate_mf() now warns when joining pre-calculated depth data
renames mutation-data columns, listing each original name and its
suffixed name.

- Fixed directory VCF imports losing header-derived sample
identifiers
during VCF combination. Distinct samples now retain their identities
without sample metadata and can join matching metadata correctly.

                 Changes in version 1.1.0 (2025-12-09)                  

Development version following the Bioconductor 3.23 release (version
numbering bumped by the Bioconductor team). No functional changes
since
1.0.0.

[NanoMethViz](/packages/NanoMethViz)
-----------

                        Changes in version 3.9.4                        

- Fixed get_cgi_t2t() returning exon annotation instead of CpG
islands.
- Fixed CpG island annotations from get_cgi_hg19(), get_cgi_hg38(),
get_cgi_t2t(), get_cgi_mm10() and get_cgi_grcm39() using 0-based
starts. Starts are now 1-based like the rest of the package, so
every island starts 1 bp later than before.
- Fixed query_methy(simplify = FALSE) collapsing duplicated regions
into a single entry, and double counting their data for modBAM
input. Each input region now gets its own output entry.
- Fixed query_methy() on modBAM input returning data in the wrong
order when regions on the same chromosome were interleaved with
regions on other chromosomes.
- Fixed query_methy() on modBAM input failing when a sequence is
missing from the headers of only some BAM files. It now warns and
returns no data for the affected samples.
- Fixed query_methy() on modBAM input dropping regions with no reads.
They now return an empty table with the standard columns.
- Changed query_methy() on modBAM input to warn about sequences
missing from all BAM files and error if no queried sequence is
present, unless force = TRUE. This matches the behaviour for tabix
input.
- Changed query_methy() to require site_filter to be a single number
of at least 1.
- Fixed create_tabix_file() merging all modification types from
modkit
input into one indistinguishable set of calls. Modkit input is now
filtered to a single modification code, set with the new mod_code
argument (default 5mC, "m"). It errors if no calls match, or if
mod_code is given for non-modkit input.
- Fixed ModBamFiles() rejecting BAM files indexed with .csi instead
of
.bai.
- Fixed create_tabix_file() continuing with an unsorted file when the
system sort command failed. It now errors instead.
- Fixed create_tabix_file() default sample names keeping .tsv from
compressed inputs (e.g. sample1.tsv.gz became sample1.tsv).

                        Changes in version 3.9.3                        

- Fixed methy_to_bsseq() silently attributing methylation data to the
wrong samples when the sample annotation order differs from the
order samples appear in the methylation file.
- Fixed modBAM MM tags declaring multiple modification codes (e.g.
C+mh from dorado's 5mCG_5hmCG model) being silently dropped during
parsing.

                        Changes in version 3.9.2                        

- Fixed ModKit positions being off by 1.
- Fixed modbam_to_tabix() leaving the tabix index (.tbi) in the
temporary directory, making the converted file unqueryable.
- Fixed methy_to_bsseq() failing or corrupting output when called
multiple times in the same R session due to internal state
persisting between calls.
- Fixed plot_mds() plotting unscaled MDS eigenvectors, distorting the
geometry of the plot relative to the variance explained shown on the
axes.

[netboost](/packages/netboost)
--------

                 Changes in version 2.21.5 (2026-06-29)                 

- nb_consensus()/nb_consensus_transfer() reworked. The module_retention
  criterion ("all"/"any"/"median"), the new min_pc1_cor threshold and
  robust_PCs are now
  included.

- Added network_type="signed" (keep only positively co-directional
  pairs) and
  consensus_method="median" for both adjacency and TOM aggregation.

- Filter-mask cache keys now include a data fingerprint, so caches are
  no
  longer reused across different datasets that share the same
  dimensions.

                 Changes in version 2.21.2 (2026-06-17)                 

- The bundled MC-UPGMA clustering suite (external C++/Perl/GNU-make
  tool) has
  been replaced by a portable in-package C++ reimplementation. netboost
  no
  longer requires GNU make, Bash, Perl or Gzip and now builds on
  Windows in
  addition to unix/macOS. Sparse-clustering output is byte-identical to
  previous versions for the supported single-round regime (edge count
  up to the
  former 1e7 heap size); very large inputs that previously triggered
  the
  external tool's multi-round mode may yield identically-structured
  trees with
  differently-numbered cluster IDs.

- SIMD (AVX) acceleration of the boosting step is now selected at
  runtime via
  the executing CPU's capabilities instead of being baked in at build
  time. The
  same binary runs correctly across heterogeneous CPU clusters (AVX and
  non-AVX nodes) and on non-x86 architectures; CPU-feature
  autodetection
  (autoconf) was removed.

- Removed the exported helper mcupgma_exec(), which only operated on
  the
  now-removed external clustering binaries.

[OmaDB](/packages/OmaDB)
-----

                 Changes in version 2.29.2 (2026-11-18)                 

- BUG FIXES
  - CITATION file uses bibentry() and includes the DOI of the
    publication

                 Changes in version 2.29.1 (2026-11-13)                 

- NEW FEATURES
  - caching of all API responses in memory, and optionally on disk with
    setOmaCache(persistent = TRUE). The persistent cache is cleared
    automatically when a new OMA release is available. clearOmaCache()
    empties the caches.
  - new functions getHOGs() (all HOGs / ancestral genes at a taxonomic
    level), getSynteny() (ancestral synteny), getSharedAncestry() and
    getOrthoXML(), providing similar functionality as the pyomadb package
  - getProtein() gains the attributes 'hog_derived_orthologs', 'xref'
    and
    'isoforms', and the argument rel_type to filter orthologs
  - getHOG() gains the argument attribute to retrieve the members, the
    Gene Ontology annotations and HOGs with similar phylogenetic profiles
  - getGenome() gains the attribute 'genes'
  - getTaxonomy() gains the argument collapse
  - as.data.frame() and print() methods for omadb_obj objects

- BUG FIXES
  - resolveURL() always returns a data.frame for endpoints that return
    a
    list of entries, also if the list contains a single entry (GitHub
    issue #4)
  - getProtein(attribute = 'homeologs') queried a non-existing endpoint
  - getTopGO() with format 'GO2geneID' and formatTopGO() for lists of
    proteins failed
  - getTree() keeps the full names of species containing special
    characters

- CHANGES IN RETURN TYPES AND BEHAVIOUR
  - all functions return results of consistent types: a single entity
    is
    an omadb_obj, a list of entities a data.frame - independent of the
    number of entries
  - getHOG() always returns a data.frame (one row per matching HOG)
  - loci are GRanges objects with the chromosome as seqnames and the
    OMA
    id as names (previously the OMA id was used as seqnames)
  - errors of the OMA Browser API (e.g. unknown ids) raise R errors
    with
    the explanation of the server instead of returning NULL
  - accessing an attribute of an omadb_obj that is loaded from the OMA
    Browser no longer modifies the object in the global environment;
    the data is cached instead
  - getObjectAttributes() returns a named character vector
  - getTopGO() requires topGO to be attached with library(topGO)
  - the deprecated functions getXref(), getAnnotation(),
    getGenomeAlignment() and getData() are now defunct

- INTERNAL
  - the package uses httr2 instead of httr and no longer depends on
    plyr
  - example datasets were regenerated from the current OMA release (see
    inst/scripts/make-data.R); LazyData is no longer used, load them with
    data()
  - extensive unit tests using recorded API responses

[OmnipathR](/packages/OmnipathR)
---------

                        Changes in version 4.1.7                        

Bug fixes

- consensuspathdb_download and consensuspathdb_raw_table read the
current ConsensusPathDB file (version 35), which has 9 columns.
Before, they read it with 4 columns: the columns were shifted, and
the filters of min_score and complex_max_size did not work. The
UniProt ACs and Gene Symbols come from the ConsensusPathDB file,
there is no UniProt ID mapping query any more. The uniprot_a and
uniprot_b columns contain UniProt ACs instead of entry names
- consensuspathdb_download: in_complex is TRUE for records with more
than two participants, and self pairs come only from records of one
participant. Before, in_complex was TRUE for all records
- Cache: a cache file that can not be read, or that contains NULL, is
removed when loaded, and the data is downloaded or built again.
Before, loading such a file failed, e.g. "attempt to set an
attribute on NULL"
- Databases (get_db) are not saved to the cache if they are empty. On
build servers, the slow loaders return NULL while R checks
OmnipathR, and this NULL was saved and used by the later R processes
of the check
- Databases are not saved to the cache if UniProt or Ensembl failed
on
a build server, and the loader got an empty table
- uniprot_id_mapping_table: if UniProt rejects the job, the error
gives the message of UniProt. The default of
omnipathr.uniprot_idmapping_timeout is 120 seconds instead of 30

Technical

- R-universe builds (the environment variable MY_UNIVERSE is set)
count as build servers, and skip the tests of the live web service,
like the Bioconductor build machines
- The debug information at errors shows the R-universe URL

                        Changes in version 4.1.6                        

Bug fixes

- consensuspathdb_download: the UniProt ID mapping query used the ID
type labels of the retired UniProt API ("ACC", "GENENAME"), and
UniProt rejected it with HTTP 400
- uniprot_id_mapping_table: if the UniProt ID mapping job does not
finish within omnipathr.uniprot_idmapping_timeout, it stops with an
error that names the job and its status. Before, it went on, and
failed with "object 'result' not found"

                        Changes in version 4.1.5                        

Bug fixes

- Cache lock: the cache database is locked by an operating system
lock
on the file cache.flock, instead of the existence of the file
cache.lock. The lock is released even if the R process crashes or is
killed, so a stale lock can not block other processes any more.
Before, a killed process left the lock behind, and every later
process failed with "The cache directory is locked for longer than 5
seconds". Locking is also atomic now, and the lock is released if an
error occurs while it is held
- The cache database is written to a temporary file and then renamed,
so it is never read half written
- The default of the omnipathr.cache_timeout option is 60 seconds
instead of 5: the wait applies only while another live process holds
the lock
- omnipath_unlock_cache_db releases the lock of the current session,
and removes the legacy cache.lock file of older versions
- On build servers, the cache is not wiped any more when the package
is loaded. Each R process of the build or check of OmnipathR wiped
the cache and removed its lock: all data was downloaded again
several times, which exceeded the time limit of the checks, and
packages built at the same time by the same user failed with a
locked or wiped cache

New features

- Errors raised by OmnipathR print debugging information to the
console: the OmnipathR version and the library it is loaded from, R
and the platform, the versions of the main dependencies, libcurl,
and the cache directory. The full information is printed at the
first error of the session, later errors print only the version
line. The errors have the class omnipathr_error

Technical

- New dependency: filelock
- database_summary is not run in the examples on build servers

                        Changes in version 4.1.4                        

Bug fixes

- Organism names: the Ensembl species page is not available any more,
and the functions that translate organism names (e.g. ncbi_taxid,
latin_name) failed (#130). The Ensembl organisms now come from the
species.json file at https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/ensemblorganisms/. It
has more than 11,000 organisms, before there were about 340
- ensembl_organisms_raw returns a different table: one row for each
organism in species.json, with the NCBI Taxonomy IDs of the organism
and of its species, the scientific and the common name
- The Ensembl organism IDs (e.g. "hsapiens") are the names of the
BioMart datasets, from a table in the package. Before, they were
derived from the scientific names, and for some organisms (e.g.
gorilla) they were wrong
- If one of the resources of organism names (Ensembl, OMA or UniProt)
is not available, the names from the other resources are still
available. The incomplete table is not saved to the cache
- The database cache keys contain the package version: after an
upgrade, the databases are built again from their sources

Technical

- rvest is not a dependency any more
- On build servers, the verbose console log and the cache wipe at
package load happen only when R builds or checks OmnipathR itself.
Before, the log output gave a NOTE in the checks of the packages
that depend on OmnipathR

                        Changes in version 4.1.3                        

Technical

- Downloads from rest.uniprot.org use HTTP/1.1. Over HTTP/2, UniProt
sometimes resets slow transfers, and the download fails with "HTTP/2
stream 1 was not closed cleanly". The new option
omnipathr.http1_hosts lists the hosts that use HTTP/1.1
- UniProt queries (all_uniprots and the functions built on it): on
build servers, if UniProt fails, they give a warning and an empty
table, and skip UniProt for the rest of the session
- Faster examples on build servers: kinasephos and the deprecated
NicheNet network functions do not download in the checks of
OmnipathR

                        Changes in version 4.1.2                        

Deprecated

- The NicheNet functions (nichenet_*) are deprecated, and the
NicheNet
vignette is removed. A new version will retrieve the NicheNet prior
knowledge built by the OmniPath server. The resource clients written
for NicheNet (e.g. EVEX, Harmonizome, ReMap) stay
- static_table and static_tables are deprecated. The regular query
functions try the plain HTTP server if the HTTPS server fails
- The packages mlrMBO, parallelMap, ParamHelpers and smoof are not in
Suggests any more. nichenet_optimization asks for them if they are
not installed

Bug fixes

- static_table: works again for interaction tables. Before, it
stopped
with "argument is of length zero" in unnest_evidences
- Slow functions return their full result when another package calls
them on a build server. Before, they returned NULL in the checks of
dependent packages, such as wppi

Technical

- The downloader accepts fallback URLs (mirrors). Each round of
attempts tries all URLs once, then the next round starts after a
short wait
- HTTP errors: the log shows the status, the final URL and the
response headers. After HTTP 429 or 503, the wait follows the
Retry-After header, but it is never longer than the new option
omnipathr.retry_downloads_max_wait (30 s)
- biomart_query: tries the US East and Asia mirrors of Ensembl if the
main site fails. On build servers, if all mirrors fail, it gives a
warning and an empty table, and skips Ensembl for the rest of the
session

                        Changes in version 4.1.1                        

Bug fixes

- KEGG: the organism list comes from the list/genome endpoint,
because
list/organism returns 400
- oma_organisms: reads the new OMA header, and downloads the table
again when the cached copy is malformed
- subnetwork: selects the vertices with igraph::V()
- omnipath_cache_remove: with max_age or min_age, it removes only the
matching versions. Before, it removed all versions when status was
not given
- resources: the category filter works again

Technical

- resources: downloads with retries, and keeps the list in the cache
for one hour at most
- The environment variable OMNIPATHR_BUILDSERVER marks a build server
- Vignettes build when a third-party server does not answer; the
chunk
shows the error
- Tests of the live web service do not run on Bioconductor build
machines
- Runnable examples for 32 more manual pages
- CITATION file in ASCII

[onlineFDR](/packages/onlineFDR)
---------

                       Changes in version 2.21.3                        

MODIFICATIONS

- the help pages and vignettes now state the dependence conditions
  under
  which each procedure controls the FDR or FWER. In particular, LORD,
  SAFFRON, Alpha_investing and ADDIS do not in general control the FDR
  for
  positively dependent p-values (examples are given in
  vignette("theory")), and the original LOND (original = TRUE) also
  controls the FDR under positive dependence (PRDS)

- the help pages of ADDIS_spending and ADDIS_exhaustive state that FWER
  control is not guaranteed for positively dependent p-values, and
  those
  of Alpha_spending and bonfInfinite that they allow arbitrary
  dependence

- LONDstar and LORDstar with version = 'async' are documented to
  control
  the FDR when the null p-values are independent (Zrnic et al., 2021,
  Theorem 3); the 'dep' and 'batch' versions of the star functions are
  documented as guaranteed to control only the mFDR

- the help page of SAFFRONstar now states that version = 'async'
  follows
  Algorithm 3 of Zrnic et al. (2021) with asynchronous conflict sets,
  counting candidates among tests that started after each rejection
  became known (their Appendix Algorithm 7 counts candidates by
  decision
  time instead, which can give an undefined index); a test checks this
  against a reference implementation

                       Changes in version 2.21.2                        

MODIFICATIONS

- ADDIS_exhaustive now checks that lambda >= alpha * tau, as required
  by
  Fischer et al. (2024); this also ensures no p-value above lambda is
  rejected

- ADDIS_exhaustive now rejects alpha = 1, lambda = tau and gamma
  summing
  to more than 1, which previously gave invalid results without an
  error

- ADDIS now rejects lambda = tau, as required by Tian and Ramdas (2019)

- ADDIS with async = TRUE now follows Algorithm 3 of Tian and Ramdas
  (2019)
  exactly. Rejection times and candidate counts were previously based
  on the
  order in which tests started rather than on their decision times,
  which
  gave different (sometimes higher) test levels when tests overlapped

- LOND now checks that a user-supplied betai is at least as long as the
  number of p-values

- the default gamma (or beta) sequences based on Javanmard and
  Montanari
  (2018), equation 31, now use the normalising constant 0.07908197, so
  that
  they sum to 1; the constant given in the paper (0.07720838) gives a
  sum of
  about 0.976. This affects the defaults of LOND, LORD, LONDstar,
  LORDstar,
  Alpha_spending, bonfInfinite, online_fallback and supLORD

- LORD with version = 'discard' now requires w0 <= tau.discard * alpha,
  as
  in Tian and Ramdas (2019), and its default w0 is min(alpha/10,
  tau.discard * alpha/2). Previously FDR control could be lost when
  tau.discard < 0.1

- LORD with version = 'dep' and LORDdep now check the condition of
  Javanmard and Montanari (2018), example 3.7, sum(xi_i * (1 + log(i)))
  <=
  alpha/b0, instead of sum(xi_i) <= alpha/b0. setBound("LORDdep") now
  returns a sequence satisfying this condition

- LORD with version = 3 now adds the reward b0 to the wealth at the
  time of
  each rejection, as in Javanmard and Montanari (2018), equation 9; the
  reward was previously credited two steps late

- LORD with versions 3 and 'dep' now give an error if w0 >= alpha and
  b0 is
  not supplied (b0 = alpha - w0 was previously negative)

- BatchStBH and StoreyBH no longer cap the adjusted p-values at 1,
  which
  made every hypothesis in a batch rejected when the test level was 1
  or
  more

- SAFFRONstar with version = 'batch' now caps the test levels of the
  first
  batch at lambda, as for later batches

- ADDIS_spending with dep = TRUE now sums over j < t - L_t, as in Tian
  and
  Ramdas (2021), equation 23; the sum previously included one more
  test,
  and could read past the end of gammai

- ADDIS, ADDIS_spending, Alpha_investing, LONDstar, LORD, LORDstar,
  online_fallback, SAFFRON and SAFFRONstar now check that a
  user-supplied
  gammai (or betai) is at least as long as the number of p-values

- fixed a memory error in LORDstar with version = 'async' for a single
  p-value

- the checks that gammai (or betai) sums to at most 1 (or alpha) now
  allow
  for rounding error, so the output of setBound() is always accepted

- LORD, LORDstar, SAFFRON, SAFFRONstar, ADDIS and Alpha_investing now
  check
  that a user-supplied gammai is non-increasing, as the source papers
  require

- the batch versions of LONDstar, LORDstar and SAFFRONstar no longer
  fail
  when some test levels are exactly zero

- SAFFRON, SAFFRONstar, BatchStBH, StoreyBH and ADDIS_spending now
  require
  lambda < 1

- ADDIS_spending test levels are now capped at lambda, as Tian and
  Ramdas
  (2021) require

- StoreyBH now accepts a data frame, as documented, and its help page
  gives
  the Storey-BH rejection threshold

- bonfInfinite and LORDdep now use the date-sorted data frame

- supLORD is much faster: the normalising constant of each rejection's
  spending sequence is computed once rather than at every later step
  (e.g. 6 s to 0.03 s for 1000 p-values with rho = 1000)

- supLORD now follows Xu and Ramdas (2021) exactly: the boost from the
  first
  rejection is spent from the next test onwards (previously only after
  a
  second rejection); the r-th rejection earns b rather than beta0
  (equation 21); the offset a is the root of equation 20 (previously
  searched for only on (0, r/10)); and the spending sequence is
  computed on
  the log scale, avoiding NaN levels for large eta. These changes
  increase
  power, in some settings substantially

- supLORD now accepts rho greater than the number of p-values with the
  default gammai, and checks the length of a user-supplied gammai

- LORDstar and SAFFRONstar (all versions) are much faster, with
  identical
  results: the times of known rejections and the counts of candidates
  are
  updated as tests are made rather than recomputed at every step (e.g.
  LORDstar with version = 'async' takes under 0.01 s rather than 150 s,
  and SAFFRONstar 0.01 s rather than 350 s, for 8000 p-values)

- all functions now give an error if no p-values remain after missing
  values are removed; several functions previously crashed R for empty
  or
  all-missing input

- missing p-values in a data frame now remove only those rows (rows
  with
  missing values in other columns were also removed), and are an error
  when
  the data frame has decision times or lags

- LOND, Alpha_investing and online_fallback now return the id column,
  as
  LORD, SAFFRON and ADDIS do, so results can be matched to the input
  after
  the p-values are sorted by date

- decision times must be finite, and ADDIS with async = TRUE now checks
  them as LONDstar, LORDstar and SAFFRONstar do; decision times larger
  than
  the integer range were previously treated as already known

- ADDIS_spending with dep = TRUE gives a clear error if there is no
  column
  of lags

- Alpha_spending, BatchBH, BatchPRDS and BatchStBH (and the deprecated
  LORDdep and bonfInfinite) now check that a user-supplied gammai (or
  xi or
  alphai) is long enough, instead of returning NA levels

- the default sequence of LORD with version = 'dep' and w0 > b0 no
  longer
  depends on the number of p-values, and the default for w0 <= b0 uses
  the
  constant 0.1393066, so that the condition of Javanmard and Montanari
  (2018), example 3.7, holds exactly

- the progress bars of ADDIS, Alpha_investing, LONDstar, LORD and
  SAFFRON
  count tests, and no longer overflow for more than 46,340 p-values

- corrected several error messages

- added tests of ADDIS_exhaustive testing levels and of the async ADDIS
  candidate threshold

- corrected errors in the documentation, vignettes and references

                       Changes in version 2.21.1                        

MODIFICATIONS

- added the ADDIS_exhaustive procedure and documentation

- fixed bugs in ADDIS

- fixed a floating-point precision issue in the LOND check on betai

- refreshed documentation and pkgdown site for the new release

- tidied build ignores for development-only files

[orthogene](/packages/orthogene)

                       Changes in version 1.19.3                        

Test coverage

- Lifted overall test coverage from ~84% to ~92% by adding ~370 new
assertions across 7 new test files and 4 expanded ones. New tests
cover:
- check_species_babelgene, check_agg_args, check_keep_popular,
check_sparseMatrix, check_gene_map, check_gene_df_type,
check_gene_output, check_bool_args, check_agg_opts (helper
validation functions);
- map_orthologs_gprofiler non-chunked, chunked-serial, and
chunked-parallel paths plus null/empty-input and
same-source/target early returns and chunk_size validation;
- prepare_tree local-newick else-branch and age_max calibration
paths;
- aggregate_mapped_genes transpose=TRUE, within-species,
sort_rows, as_integers, and the early-exit "rename only" branch;
- infer_species test_species=NULL defaults and
method-as-test_species expansion plus make_plot=FALSE;
- create_background use_intersect=FALSE (union), user-supplied bg,
and within-species fast path;
- run_benchmark_once cache-hit, run_convert_orthologs=FALSE, and
within-species (is_human) branches;
- aggregate_rows_monocle3 mean and count aggregation;
- rotate_clades, is_gha, load_rda, cache_dir,
gconvert_target_opts, non121_strategy_opts, is_human,
is_matrix/is_sparse_matrix, is_converted, add_rowcol_names,
messager, format_species, methods_opts,
gene_input_opts/gene_output_opts, invert_dictionary, and
get_orgdb_gprofiler (use-local + use-remote) paths;
- Error/skip paths in filter_gene_df, aggregate_rows,
map_orthologs, all_genes, and many2many_rows
(aggregate_orthologs=FALSE).

                       Changes in version 1.19.2                        

Bug fixes

- test-map_genes: replace message(e) with
message(conditionMessage(e))
in the planarian (Schmidtea mediterranea) tryCatch error handler.
Same pattern as the 1.17.4 fix to run_benchmark_once(): passing a
condition object to message() re-signals it, and under testthat's
calling handlers an error condition signaled this way escapes the
tryCatch and is reported as a test failure. This caused
test-map_genes to fail on the GitHub Actions Windows runner whenever
the planosphere mapping file failed to download. Same fix has been
backported to RELEASE_3_23 as 1.18.1.

                       Changes in version 1.19.1                        

Bug fixes

- Revert the g:Profiler workarounds shipped in 1.17.3. Upstream
(g:Profiler) confirmed and fixed the API regression that was
returning literal NaN in JSON responses; unmatched genes are once
again returned as "N/A". Examples and tests that test the default
ortholog-mapping path now exercise g:Profiler honestly again — no
method = "homologene" workarounds, no skip-on-error wrappers around
explicit g:Profiler tests. The point of these tests is to catch an
API regression, not to mask it.
- Kept from 1.17.4: run_benchmark_once()'s
message(conditionMessage(e)) fix — message(e) re-signals condition
objects, which under testthat's calling handlers escapes tryCatch as
a test failure. Unrelated to the g:Profiler API issue and remains a
real bug.
- Kept from 1.17.3: test-infer_species tolerates ties in top_match.
When two species (e.g. human and monkey via babelgene) tie at the
top percent_match, infer_species() returns both; the test now passes
as long as the expected species is among them.

[pairedGSEA](/packages/pairedGSEA)
----------

                       Changes in version 1.13.1                        

Bug fixes

- paired_ora(): the combined (paired) analysis now uses genes tested
for both expression and splicing as its universe; previously genes
without a splicing result were included. Missing paired results are
now filled in the paired columns instead of overwriting the splicing
relative risk and enrichment score. Affects paired ORA results
since 1.1.0 (Bioconductor 3.18); expression-only and splicing-only
ORA are unchanged.
- paired_diff(): test = "Wald" no longer fails; the reduced model is
only used for the likelihood ratio test.
- The reduced model for the likelihood ratio test now removes the
group term by name instead of the first term of the design.
- paired_diff(): surrogate variable estimation is now seeded
(sva_seed), so results are reproducible between runs.

Changes

- paired_diff(): the number of automatically estimated surrogate
variables is capped so that the model keeps enough residual degrees
of freedom (sva_min_residual_df). An optional upper limit can be set
with sva_max_n; when set, the number is also capped at the square
root of the number of samples. An exact request (sva_n) stops with
an informative error when it is unsafe instead of being reduced
silently.
- paired_diff(): SVA diagnostics (requested, estimated and retained
surrogate variables, residual degrees of freedom) are stored in
metadata(result)$pairedGSEA_sva.

[planttfhunter](/packages/planttfhunter)
-------------

                       Changes in version 1.13.1                        

This release adds two new classification schemes (TAPscan and
Plant-TFClass) and redesigns the API around a simpler workflow:
annotate_domains() -> classify_tfs() -> get_tf_counts().

NEW FEATURES

- TFs can now be classified using the classification scheme of
TAPscan
v4 (Petroll et al., 2025), in addition to PlantTFDB's scheme. The
TAPscan classification algorithm (tapscan_classify.pl v4.76, with
rules v82 and coverage values v11) was ported to R and reproduces
the results of the original Perl implementation. TAPscan
classifications include a variable TAP_class indicating whether each
family contains transcription factors (TF), transcriptional
regulators (TR), or putative TAPs (PT).

- TFs are also classified into superclasses, classes, and families
from the structure-based classification of Plant-TFClass
(Blanc-Mathieu et al., 2024). Plant-TFClass classifications are
inferred from TAPscan classifications using a correspondence table
between the two systems. When a TAPscan subfamily corresponds to
more than one Plant-TFClass family (TAPscan's AP2, ABI3/VP1, and
MADS), PlantTFDB subfamilies are used to resolve the ambiguity; when
that is not possible, all possible classifications are reported,
separated by ';'.

- PlantTFDB classifications now include both families (e.g., AP2/ERF)
and subfamilies (e.g., ERF), as in PlantTFDB's classification
scheme.

- New function annotate_domains() to annotate sequences with the
domains used by PlantTFDB and TAPscan. It has a threads argument to
run HMMER with multiple threads.

- New data sets tapscan_scheme (TAPscan's classification rules),
planttfclass_scheme (correspondence between TAPscan and
Plant-TFClass), and tap_class (classes, descriptions, and references
for TAPscan families).

BREAKING CHANGES

- annotate_pfam() was replaced by annotate_domains(), which returns a
list of two data frames (PlantTFDB and TAPscan) with variables Gene,
Domain, qlen, c_evalue, hmm_from, and hmm_to.

- classify_tfs() now takes the output of annotate_domains() as input
(data frames returned by annotate_pfam() are no longer accepted),
and returns a data frame with one row per gene and variables Gene,
PlantTFDB_family, PlantTFDB_subfamily, TAPscan_family,
TAPscan_subfamily, TAP_class, PlantTFClass_superclass,
PlantTFClass_class, and PlantTFClass_family. Note that the
classifications previously reported in the variable Family (e.g.,
ERF) are now in PlantTFDB_subfamily, and PlantTFDB_family contains
PlantTFDB families (e.g., AP2/ERF). Genes assigned to more than one
PlantTFDB family have families (and subfamilies) separated by ';'.

- get_tf_counts() now takes a named list of data frames with TF
classifications (as returned by classify_tfs()) as input, instead of
a list of AAStringSet objects. This way, domains are annotated only
once, and TFs can be counted in different ways (and filtered, if
needed) without running HMMER again. By default, TFs are counted per
PlantTFDB family (previously, PlantTFDB subfamily).

- Data set classification_scheme was renamed to planttfdb_scheme, and
names 'M_type', 'MYB_related', and 'LBD (AS2/LOB)' were changed to
'M-type', 'MYB-related', and 'LBD', respectively, to match the
output of classify_tfs().

- Data sets gsu_families and tf_counts were removed, as they can be
obtained in a few milliseconds with classify_tfs(gsu_annotation) and
get_tf_counts(), respectively. Data sets gsu and gsu_annotation were
updated.

BUG FIXES

- HD-ZIP (via HD-ZIP_I/II), TALE (via BELL), and WOX TFs were never
identified, because the names of these domains did not match the
names of their profile HMMs. Such TFs were classified as HB-other.

- Trihelix and STAT TFs were never identified for the same reason.

- Genes with two B-box domains and a CCT domain were classified as
both CO-like and DBB. They are now classified as CO-like only.

- get_tf_counts() returned an error when species names were not in
alphabetical order, and did not reorder species metadata to match
the order of species in the count matrix.

[RAMEN](/packages/RAMEN)
-----

                        Changes in version 3.0.0                        

This version reflects RAMEN's incorporation to Bioconductor. Apart
from
the removal of the seed argument described below, the analysis
functionsreturn the same results as in 2.1.2, and the error and
warning
messages are unchanged.

- The seed argument was removed from selectVariables() and
nullDistGE(). Call set.seed() before either function instead. As a
consequence, nullDistGE() no longer hands the same seed to
selectVariables() in every permutation, so the cross-validation
folds now differ from one permutation to the next instead of being
held fixed. Null distributions computed with this version therefore
differ numerically from those computed with earlier ones.
- big fix: selectVariables() no longer fails when
environmental_matrix
holds a single variable and no covariates are given.
- findVML(), selectVariables() and lmGE() were split into internal
helper functions, so that each step of their work can be read on its
own. The three are now roughly half their former length. This is a
refactoring only: all three return exactly what they returned
before.
- Every package listed in Imports now has a matching importFrom()
entry in NAMESPACE. These are collected in R/RAMEN-package.R rather
than spread across the individual function files.
- The vignette calls functions by name instead of prefixing them with
package::, and every one of its chunks now has a label.
- The vignette Introduction describes how RAMEN fits into the
Bioconductor ecosystem and how it relates to other Bioconductor
packages.
- Package metadata was updated: biocViews terms were added, the R
dependency was raised to 4.6.0, and the Title and Description fields
were revised.

Claude Opus 5 was used to assist the function refactoring, using
specific prompts for the blocks that were to be moved to internal
helpers. All modifications were manually reviewed, corrected where
necessary, and fully validated by the package developer.
