[Rarr](/packages/Rarr)
----

                         Changes in version 2.1                         

Breaking changes

- (Minor:) s3_client = argument default value in read_zarr_array(),
zarr_overview(), etc. is now set to NULL instead of missing. In
practice, we expect this grant to be invisible to most users but it
makes it easier to pass down missing values in Rarr reverse
dependencies.
- The name and configuration options for the fixed-length-ascii (|S
in
Zarr v2) and fixed-length-ucs4 (&#60;U or &#62;U in Zarr v2) data types have
been updated to null_terminated_bytes and fixed_length_utf32
respectively to match their newly specified format in Zarr v3.
- Structured data types (record arrays) now always return lists as
the
internal elements, instead of vectors as previously. This allows
structured data types to contain different data types in a single
element.
- Unless data_type is specified explicitly, integers are now written
using the smallest possible bitsize based on the array x range in
write_zarr_array().
- Attributes can no longer be written before an array or group has
been initialized at the target location. This is visible in two
situations:
- write_zarr_attributes(zarr_version = 3L) fails if ran before
write_zarr_array()/ create_empty_zarr_array() or
write_zarr_group().
- create_empty_zarr_array() (and thus write_zarr_array()) fail if
attributes already exist at the target location.
- ZSTD compression and decompression now relies on base R
memCompress() and memDecompress() functions. The bundled ZSTD
library and the custom ZSTD compression/decompression of R objects
code will be removed in a future version of this package. Please get
in touch if your R installation does not come with ZSTD support and
you rely on our custom implementation.
- User-specified compression levels are now ignored when writing.
This
change is necessary to eventually enable writing on S3, and writing
sharded arrays. It allows results in better speed performance when
writing. A patch will be provided to base R to enable custom
user-specified compression levels again in the future.
- Functions related to the DelayedArray backend have been dropped
entirely after being deprecated in the previous release. To use the
DelayedArray backend, or lazy reading or Zarr datasets, look at the
ZarrArray package.
- Empty or missing attributes are now returned as NULL instead of an
empty list by read_zarr_attributes().
- Character arrays are now written as VLen-UTF8 by default if
write_zarr_array(data_type = ) argument is left empty or "character"
and no NAs are present.
- null_terminated_bytes (|S in Zarr v2) and fixed_length_utf32 (<U in
Zarr v2) no longer support preserving NA in roundtrip as this
resulted in data unreadable by other Zarr implementations.

New features

- Zarr v3 struct datatype (equivalent to Zarr v2 structured datatype)
is now supported. Deprecated Zarr v3 structured datatype is
implemented as well, but only for reading, as per specification for
a deprecated type.
- The new zarr_consolidate_metadata() function consolidates metadata
of all elements under a given group in its associated .zmetadata
(for Zarr v2 trees) or zarr.json (for Zarr v3 trees). Creating this
consolidated metadata has two benefits:
- better performance: the metadata of all elements under a group
can be accessed more efficiently since a single file needs to be
read instead of multiple smaller files.
- easier direct access of all the elements in a remote S3 store,
even though Rarr doesn't have yet store-agnostic verbs to list,
read, etc. elements.
- The sharding_indexed codec is now supported to read sharded Zarr
arrays. Thanks to William Colgan for early testing, reporting issues
and providing bug fixes (#254).
- zarr_overview() now returns a new logical field attributes
indicating whether each array or group has associated attributes.
- A new write_zarr_group() function is available, based on a request
and initial draft from Artür Manukyan in #18.
- The read_zarr_consolidated_metadata() function is now exported,
fulfilling the request from Sharla Gelfand in #116.
- The new bfloat16 data type is now supported for reading.
- read_zarr_array(), write_zarr_array() and update_zarr_array() now
integrate the {progressr} package for optional and customizable
progress report feedback when reading or writing large / complex
arrays. Progress can be enabled via the progressr::handlers()
function.
- zarr_overview() now returns the zarr_version of the array or group,
based on a request from Artür Manukyan.
- zarr_overview() now works on groups with non-consolidated metadata,
based a request from Artür Manukyan.
- update_zarr_array() no longer writes chunks filled with the fill
value, and no longer overwrites chunks that wouldn't be modified.
- This package now compiles on WASM, making it available in webR
(shinylive, etc.)
- create_empty_zarr_array() and write_zarr_array() now accept Zarr v3
data types as their data_type argument.
- VLen-UTF8 data types can now be written directly via
write_zarr_array(data_type = "string"), following requests from the
spicyR and anndataR maintainers.

Minor improvements

- normalize_array_path() has been slightly optimized for speed. It is
not likely to have a significant impact if you reading a single
large array but can be noticed if you reading many attributes and
small arrays (as in some anndata objects).
- Empty chunks, i.e., chunks were all elements are equal to the fill
value, are no longer written by write_zarr_array(), saving disk
space, and improving performance when reading it back.
- More blosc options (clevel, shuffle, etc.) are exposed via
use_blosc().
- Writing & reading VLen-UTF8 arrays (used by default for string in
v3) is now much faster after rewriting the vlen-utf8 codec in C.
- When writing VLen-UTF8 arrays, string lengths are now always
written
in little-endian byte order, as the format requires, also on
big-endian platforms.
- Unsupported data types are now caught explicitly and early early in
the reading pipeline rather than potentially failing or returning
incorrect output later.
- Chunks larger than the whole array in one or multiple dimensions
are
now permitted, based on a request by Artür Manukyan.
- 0 is now a valid, and the default, compression level for Zstd. In
practice, it doesn't have any effect because level 0 currently
corresponds to level 3.
- Performance has been improved for writing and in the case where the
index argument in read_zarr_array() is a continuous sequence. One
such example is when the entire array is read (index argument
missing). Improvements to the first draft contributed by Patrick
Ellis in #260.
- Performance has been improved when reading
- S3 access with credentials is now more robust and compatible with
more providers.
- write_zarr_array() and create_empty_zarr_array() now warn when
using
the unstandardized / unregistered lz4, lzma, bz2 and zlib codecs
with Zarr v3.
- write_zarr_array() now errors if x has a different storage mode
than
expected from data_type (if specified). The previous situation could
lead to doubles being marked as, e.g., int in the Zarr metadata, and
encode incorrect values.
- Zarr arrays with v2 chunk key encoding are now explicitly
supported.
Zarr arrays with unsupported chunk key encodings now return an
explicit error message.
- Endian configuration in metadata for the bytes codec is now omitted
for single byte types (bool, uint8, int8).
- create_empty_zarr_array() now errors when the specified length for
fixed-width string types is too short to fit the fill value.
Similarly, write_zarr_array() now takes into account the length of
the fill value (if specified) when computing the default value for
the nchar argument (if unspecified).
- write_zarr_array() no longer warns on oversized chunks for empty
dimensions. Based on a request from Robrecht Cannoodt, and motivated
by the use of empty arrays in anndataR.
- In line of recent changes in Zarr v3 spec, 0-length chunk
dimensions
are explicitly disallowed when writing. Reading arrays with 0-length
chunk dimensions is still supported.
- A clear error is now returned for unsupported transpose
configurations.

Bug fixes

- Using blosc compression via variable-length types such as when
using
the vlen-utf8 filter / codec, is no longer causing R to crash.
- zarr_overview() and read_zarr_array() on Zarr v3 files hosted on
S3.
Thanks to a report and a patch by Artür Manukyan.
- create_empty_zarr_array() and by extension write_zarr_array() now
use the correct data type (bool) in metadata for boolean arrays.
Thanks to a report by Artür Manukyan.
- Rarr is now stricter regarding allowed names for arrays and groups,
as requested by the Zarr specification.
- create_empty_zarr_array() (and consequently write_zarr_array()) now
refuses to write in a non-empty location, because this could lead to
inconsistent or broken zarr arrays, based on a request from Hervé
Pagès (#136).
- Rarr now compiles properly on Window ARM64, thanks a to report and
patch from Jeroen Ooms (#224).
- use_gzip() now uses GZIP (RFC 1952) instead of ZLIB (RFC 1950).
Thanks to a report from Patrick Ellis.
- Zarr v3 arrays compressed with Python's numcodecs.zlib,
numcodecs.lz4, numcodecs.bz2 and numcodecs.lzma can now be read by
Rarr. Thanks to a report from Patrick Ellis.
- Large arrays (at least one shape element larger
Machine$integer.max)
and arrays with large chunks can now be written and read correctly.
Thanks to a report and reproducible example from Robrecht Cannoodt.
- create_empty_zarr_array() no longer coerces scalars to dim 1 arrays
in the Zarr metadata. Thanks to a report from Robrecht Cannoodt.
- write_zarr_array() and update_zarr_array() no longer clamp float32
values beyond the int32 range (including Inf and -Inf) to
±2147483648 (#304).

Internal changes

- A refactor reinforced shared the use of internal functions handling
indices across read_zarr_array(), write_zarr_array(), and
update_zarr_array(). Some redundant internal functions have been
merged. This reduced the cyclomatic complexity in every function
back to <15 and it opens the door to further optimizations which now
only need to take place in a single function.
- Some code duplication has been removed by moving metadata file
existence in the lower-level shared utilities .read_array_metadata()
and read_zarr_consolidated_metadata(). While this is still
discouraged, this also facilitates re-use of the internal functions
in other packages (e.g., ZarrArray).
- Parsing Zarr v2 datatypes and the bytes codec decoding operation
are
now handled internally by the new grumpy CRAN package.
- When reading a Zarr array composed of a single chunk,
read_zarr_array() now takes a shortcut which saves a data copy.

[rawrr](/packages/rawrr)
-----

                       Changes in version 1.21.1                        

- Provide native rawrr executables for linux-arm64, osx-arm64,
  and win-arm64 in addition to the x64 runtimes; the runtime is
  derived from the architecture of the running R session, so
  Apple Silicon no longer requires Rosetta #96 #97.

- Use Thermo Fisher RawFileReader 8.0.42 (.NET 8) #97.

- buildRawrrExe() gains the arguments runtime, allowing
  cross-builds for all six runtimes, and sourceUrl; it mirrors
  inst/rawrrassembly/build.sh: the RawFileReader NuGet packages
  are downloaded once into a local feed and passed via dotnet
  publish --source, leaving the user's global NuGet configuration
  untouched #97.

- Remove the internal helpers .addPackages() and
  .addNupkgSource().

- .isAssemblyWorking() reports the exit status and hints (e.g.,
  macOS quarantine attribute) instead of failing with 'argument

                       Changes in version 1.99.2                        

- bayes_reactome() default false_negative follows the enrichit change
(0.9, was 0.1): the old rate assumed hits carry 90% of every active
program's genes, which pushed every posterior to ~0 on realistic
Reactome data -- hierarchical pathway sets with 20-30 hits among
hundreds of genes. With the realistic rate the wrapper returns a
useful selection layer (see enrichit 0.2.7 NEWS for the measured
size of the difference). Requires enrichit >= 0.2.7 (2026-10-26,
Mon)

- gsePathway() now exposes eps and forwards extra arguments (...) to
enrichit::gsea_gson(), matching the other GSEA wrappers in the
family (2026-09-22, Tue, #47)

- gsePathway() and nsePathway() now expose an explicit seed parameter
for reproducible GSEA results, aligned with enrichit::gsea_gson():
set it to a number (or TRUE for a fixed default seed) to get
identical results across runs; FALSE (default) draws a fresh seed on
each run (2026-08-15, Fri)

- prepareReactomeNetwork() is ~40x faster: the per-pathway conversion
no longer round-trips through
graphite::convertIdentifiers()/pathwayGraph() (whose per-call
mapIds() overhead was hash/SQLite-bound and capped parallel scaling
at ~4-5 effective cores). It now builds a single UNIPROT->Entrez map
up front and converts the protein edges with vectorized lookups,
keeping mclapply() parallelization over pathways. The resulting
network is identical to the previous output (same nodes and edge
values; only node ordering may differ). The default cores is now 1
(serial, ~40 s for human; options(mc.cores=...) or an explicit
cores= still enables parallel) instead of detectCores() (2026-08-16,
Sat)

                       Changes in version 1.99.1                        

- nsePathway(): network-based set enrichment analysis (NSEA) on the
Reactome reaction graph using Random Walk with Restart (2026-07-08,
Wed)
- bayes_reactome(): Bayesian term selection for compressing redundant
Reactome pathway output via enrichit::bayes_enrich() (2026-07-08,
Wed)
- prepareReactomeNetwork(): utility to build and cache the Reactome
reaction graph for reuse in nsePathway() (2026-07-08, Wed)
- enrichPathway() and gsePathway() now accept a weight parameter for
weighted ORA/GSEA (2026-07-08, Wed)
- migrate caching from custom environment (reactome_env) to
yulab.utils::with_cache(); delete get_Reactome_DATA(), getALLEG()
(2026-07-08, Wed)
- gson_Reactome() now caches the final GSON object directly, with
data
cleaning inlined (2026-07-08, Wed)

[rhdf5](/packages/rhdf5)
-----

                       Changes in version 2.58.0                        

New features

- `H5Fopen()` now supports opening remote files on S3. Thanks to
  a PR contribution from Michael Sumner
  (https://github.com/mdsumner).

- New h5getAllChunkInfo() function iterates over all stored
  chunks of a chunked HDF5 dataset, returning a list with
  elements offset (chunk origins as an integer matrix),
  filter_mask, addr (file byte offsets), and size (compressed
  chunk sizes). Requires chunked storage; contiguous datasets
  raise an error Thanks to PR #217 from Michael Sumner
  (https://github.com/mdsumner).

- Variable length string datasets now support writing and reading
  NA_character_ values. These values will be read as the empty
  string "" in Python.

- It is no longer necessary to pass a file name to h5set_extent()
  when providing a dataset handle.

Deprecations & breaking changes

- The `H5Pget_version()` function was removed entirely after
  being deprecated in version 2.56.0.

- It is no longer possible to pass a missing value or "default"
  to the `bit64conversion` argument in `H5Aread()` and
  `H5Dread()`.

- The `native` argument to `H5Pcreate()` has been removed
  entirely after being deprecated in version 2.56.0.

- The `h5tid` argument to `H5Pset_lzf()` is now deprecated and
  will be removed in the next release.

- Writing `NA_character_` values to fixed-length string datasets
  is now deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

- Variable length strings is now the default behavior for
  `h5write()`, `h5writeDataset()` and `h5writeAttribute()`. This
  makes them consistent with the behaviour of `h5create()`,
  `h5createDataset()` and `h5createAttribute()`.

- Logical attributes are now always written as a TRUE/FALSE/NA
  enum even if no NA are present in the dataset, rather than
  TRUE/FALSE in some cases and TRUE/FALSE/NA in others. As a
  consequence, the checkForNA argument to h5writeAttribute() is
  now deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

- The callGeneric argument to h5read() is now deprecated and will
  be removed in the next version. Please get in touch if you rely
  on this feature. As far as we know, this feature has never been
  used.

Bug fixes

- H5T_enum datatypes (factors in R) are now read correctly when
  the drop argument in H5Dread() is set to TRUE.

- native = TRUE now works correctly on large arrays with more
  than 2^31-1 elements.

- BLOSC and LZF compression no longer fail when applied to
  variable length types. Thanks to Luke Zappia for the report and
  reproducible example.

- h5write(variableLengthString = TRUE) now properly ignores the
  size argument, as already documented, instead of incorrectly
  writing a fixed-length string dataset.

- h5read() no longer crashes when reading variable-length string
  datasets with non-continuous indices in index. Thanks to
  Johannes Rainer for the report and reproducible example.

- Passing a H5IdComponent object to h5set_extent() now works
  without error and warning. This issue was present since
  Bioconductor 3.17.

- Values of length greater than 1 for the argument storage.mode
  to h5create() and h5createDataset() of length greater than 1
  now errors instead of silently ignoring the extra values.

Other user-facing changes

- More exported functions now include examples.

- `H5Ocopy()` no longer errors when passed the `obj_cpy_pl`
  argument.

- h5write() and h5writeDataset() will now warn about ignored
  arguments when the dataset was already existing, instead of
  silently ignoring them.

Internal changes

- Compiler warnings and C linting issues have been resolved.

- C code formatting has been standardized with clang-format.

- The output buffer size is no longer guessed for BLOSC and LZF
  compression. This was virtually not used in rhdf5filters
  already and led to unnecessary complexity in both packages.
  This was also the source of the bug related to compression of
  variable length types whose fix is documented above.

- Unused internal functions and arguments have been removed.

- Cyclomatic complexity of some functions has been reduced.

- A number of try() calls have been removed to surface errors
  instead of silently ignoring them. If you see any new errors as
  a result of this, please report them.

- Dead / unreachable / unused code has been removed.

- on.exit() is used more consistently to close open handles.
  This reduces the risk of leaving open handles in case of
  unexpected errors.

- The h5writeDataset() and h5writeAttribute() methods for matrix
  has been removed since they only forwarded the object to the
  array method and matrices are a subclass of arrays since R
  4.0.0.

[SAIGEgds](/packages/SAIGEgds)
--------

                       Changes in version 2.14.0                        

- SPA root-finding hardening in `SPATest.cpp`: the saddlepoint equation
  solvers `Saddle_Prob()` and `Saddle_Prob_Fast()` now use a bracketed
  safeguarded Newton (rtsafe) fallback for `getroot_K1()` /
  `getroot_K1_fast()`. Since K1_adj is strictly increasing (dK1/dt = K2 > 0)
  the root is unique and bracketable, so the bisection safeguard
  guarantees
  convergence. The fallback is hybrid: the existing fast Newton runs
  first
  and rtsafe is invoked only when it reports non-convergence, so there
  is no
  added cost on the common path. This removes the rare non-convergence
  that
  silently reverts the variant to the anticonservative normal
  approximation

- `seqFitNullGLMM_SPA()` and `seqAssocGLMM_SPA()` support time-to-event
  (survival) outcomes via `trait.type="survival"` and a new
  `event.time`
  argument, fitting a Cox proportional-hazards frailty model through
  the
  Breslow Cox-Poisson equivalence and applying a Poisson saddlepoint
  approximation in the single-variant score test (the GATE method, Dey
  et
  al. 2022); the Cox risk-set information correction (W - U) is used in
  the
  variance-ratio estimation via a Woodbury identity

- a new vignette "Set-based Rare-Variant Association Analysis in
  SAIGEgds", covering Burden, SKAT, ACAT-V and ACAT-O tests with full
  and
  sparse GRMs

- a new vignette "Time-to-event (survival) analysis in SAIGEgds"

[sangeranalyseR](/packages/sangeranalyseR)
--------------

                       Changes in version 1.23.0                        

Performance

- BiocParallel-backed per-SangerRead construction loop. Replaces all
parallel::mclapply call sites with BiocParallel::bplapply. The
constructor now accepts a BPPARAM = bpparam() argument and a
.resolveBPPARAM(processorsNum, BPPARAM) helper maps the legacy
integer processorsNum argument onto the right backend (SerialParam
for 1 worker, MulticoreParam on Unix and SnowParam on Windows for
≥ 2 workers). Cross-platform parallel is now first-class.

- Lazy 3-frame amino-acid translation (new lazyAA = TRUE default).
When no refAminoAcidSeq is supplied, Biostrings::translate is no
longer called eagerly during SangerRead construction. The slots
primaryAASeqS{1,2,3} start as empty AAStrings; the new exported
accessors primaryAASeqS1(), primaryAASeqS2(), primaryAASeqS3()
compute on demand. Eliminates ~35 % of construction wall time on
protein-coding ABIF reads.

- Rcpp port of the peak-detection inner loop. New src/peakvalues.cpp
exports peakvalues_cpp and peakvalues_batch_cpp. The latter
processes all peak windows for one channel in a single .Call,
eliminating ~22,400 per-window R-to-C++ marshalling round-trips per
SangerAlignment build. Saves ~320 ms per build on the bundled
fixture (≈ 1.28× end-to-end).

Cumulative end-to-end timings on the bundled
Allolobophora_chlorotica/ACHLO fixture (8 reads, 4 contigs, mean
of 5 repetitions, single thread)

Full methodology and raw artifacts under
plans/05_e2e_validation_report.md, plans/06_scaling_summary.md, and
plans/07_rcpp_optimization_log.md.

- Removed redundant mclapply parallelism around nPairwiseDiffs and
oneAmbiguousColumn — the per-element work was sub-millisecond and
fork-setup overhead dominated. They are now serial lapply calls and
~5 % faster on small alignments.

New features

- chromatogram_plotly(obj, max_points = 8000, showtrim = FALSE,
colors
= "default") — interactive Plotly htmlwidget rendering of Sanger
chromatograms via scattergl (WebGL). Uniform-stride downsampling
caps points-per-channel; the returned widget carries a
downsample_info attribute reporting the original / rendered counts.
- globalTrimApp(SA) — Shiny gadget that exposes M1 / M2 trim sliders
across an entire SangerAlignment. Each "Apply" click calls
updateQualityParam(SA, ...) which cascades to every child read; live
previews of consensus length, contig count, and per-contig stats
update reactively. Returns the re-trimmed SangerAlignment on "Done".
- primaryAASeqS1(sr), primaryAASeqS2(sr), primaryAASeqS3(sr) — lazy
AA
accessors that return the cached slot when populated, otherwise
compute on demand via the existing calculateAASeq helper.
- BPPARAM argument added to SangerRead(), SangerContig(),
SangerAlignment(). Defaults to NULL (derived from processorsNum);
pass any BiocParallelParam to override.
- lazyAA argument (default TRUE) on the same three constructors. Pass
lazyAA = FALSE for the legacy direct-slot eager-translation
behaviour.

Robustness

- File-extension regex bug fixes. The pre-Phase-4 patterns ".fa$" /
".fasta$" / ".ab1$" (in checkFASTA_File and checkReadFileName) used
unescaped ., so files like Sanger_all_reads.Xfa and Achl_006_F.Xab1
slipped through as valid. Now \\.fa(sta)?$ and \\.ab1$. Centralised
as .FASTA_EXT_REGEX and .AB1_EXT_REGEX constants.
- Validator framework refactor. All 31 check* functions in
R/UtilitiesFuncInputChecker.R now route through 5 internal helpers
(.errAppend, .requireType, .requireEnum, .requireRange,
.requireExt). Public signatures and error-type tags
(PARAMETER_RANGE_ERROR, FILE_TYPE_ERROR, etc.) are preserved exactly
— no consumer change required. File shrunk 603 → 523 lines (-13 %).
- S4 setValidity invariants added on QualityReport,
ChromatogramParam,
and ObjectResults. Catch any code path (including slot<- mutations
after construction) that would land an out-of-range value in the
slots. Sanger* user-facing classes intentionally have no validity
(preserves the "construction never throws" contract).
- Lazy-AA report compatibility. All 30 direct @primaryAASeqS{1,2,3}
slot reads in the Shiny servers and RMarkdown report templates were
converted to the accessor functions, so reports rendered against
lazyAA = TRUE objects no longer produce empty AA tables. (The 12 <<-
write sites are intentionally preserved — they're reactive caches.)
- Removed stray cat() / print() / message() debug statements from
R/UtilitiesFunc.R, R/UtilitiesFuncInputChecker.R,
R/ShinyServerModule.R, and R/ShinySangerContigServer.R. User-facing
reporting now uses log_info consistently.

Build / compliance

- R CMD check is fully clean: 0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 notes (was 0
/ 5 / 7 before Phase 9).
- 1360 testthat tests, all passing. New test files added across
phases:
- test-Validator-EdgeCases.R, test-Validator-Helpers.R,
test-Regex-Boundary.R (validator + regex regression).
- test-OrthogonalAxes.R (input-source × process-method ×
trim-method matrix).
- test-SangerRead-SlotInvariants.R, test-S4Validity.R (S4
invariants).
- test-Rcpp-peakvalues.R (R / C++ equivalence + 200-trial fuzz).
- test-LazyAA-BiocParallel.R, test-LazyAA-Reports.R (Phase 6 / 8).
- test-Phase8-PlotlyChromatogram.R, test-Phase8-GlobalTrim.R,
test-Phase9-GlobalTrim-testServer.R (UI).
- test-Phase10-Coverage.R (coverage maximisation).
- Coverage measured by covr::package_coverage(): 35.7 % overall, > 87
% on every non-Shiny R file (the three Shiny server files at 0 %
require a real browser harness; deferred).
- DESCRIPTION modernised: Authors@R (replacing the deprecated Author: + Maintainer: pair), URL, BugReports, License: GPL-2 | file LICENSE,
LinkingTo: Rcpp, R version dependency >= 4.0.0 (intentionally
permissive).
- Depends: slimmed from 27 entries to the 4 packages whose types are
publicly returned (Biostrings, DECIPHER, sangerseqR); the rest moved
to Imports: (or Suggests: for vignette-only deps).
- ASCII-only source: replaced curly apostrophes, em-dashes, arrows,
and multiplication signs across R/UtilitiesFunc.R, R/Class*.R (was a
R CMD check warning).
- Re-saved data/*.RData with xz compression (largest file 1.5 MB →
698
KB).

Bug fixes

GitHub-issue cleanup across three resolution sprints (Phases 15–17):

- #100 (CSV substring contig-name match): processCSV.R now matches
contig names exactly instead of via grepl(name, …), so a contig
named good is no longer accidentally absorbed into a contig named
good_extra.
- #92 (forward-only NULL handling): SangerContig() accepts
REGEX_SuffixReverse = NULL (or NA_character_) and minReadsNum = 1
for forward-only / reverse-only datasets. Previously the constructor
errored with argument is of length zero.
- #76 (missing PCON.2 block): ABIF reads with empty PCON.2 quality
data now get a synthetic Phred-30 score per base with a
MISSING_QUALITY_SCORES_WARN, instead of silently constructing an
unusable read.
- #89 (single-read writeFasta): writeFastaSC no longer errors on
SangerContigs built from a single read.
- #94 (low-overlap detection): new minOverlapBases (default 20) and
minOverlapFraction (default 0.4) post-alignment guards in
calculateContigSeq. Spurious low-overlap merges emit
LOW_OVERLAP_WARN and the contig is rejected before it propagates to
the alignment.
- #66 (degenerate consensus): IUPAC ambiguity-code handling in
ConsensusSequence(ambiguity = TRUE) is correctly preserved;
consumers that called as.character() on the consensus once again see
ambiguity codes rather than N collapse.
- #65 (multi-contig duplicate reads): when a read is matched into
more
than one contig (CSV or REGEX), SangerAlignment now logs
READ_ASSIGNED_MULTIPLE_CONTIGS_WARN and assigns the read to the
first matching contig only.
- #42 (length-1 reads): reads of width < 2 bp are dropped at
alignment
time with MIN_READ_LENGTH_DEFENSIVE_DROP, allowing the contig to
build from the surviving reads instead of failing the whole
alignment.
- #91 (M2 trimming on degraded reads): the QualityReport validator
now
accepts the degenerate "no usable trim window" state
(trimmedFinishPos == 0 while trimmedStartPos > 0) on extremely
low-quality reads.

New features (Phase 17 — consensus algorithms)

- consensusMethod argument on SangerContig() and SangerAlignment()
with three options:
- "strict" (default; pre-Phase-17 behaviour) — IUPAC ambiguity
codes preserved at disagreeing columns.
- "majority" — most-frequent base wins per column; ties break
alphabetically. No IUPAC codes in the output.
- "quality_weighted" — votes weighted by per-base Phred from the
source reads; falls back to flat Phred 30 (with a warning) when
scores are missing or for FASTA inputs.
- qualityAware = TRUE is a shorthand for consensusMethod =
"quality_weighted".
- Per-position consensus quality scores. attr(@contigSeq,
"qualityScores") is now an integer vector of length
length(contigSeq) under "majority" and "quality_weighted" modes
(empty integer(0) under "strict" for backwards compatibility).
Closes the long-standing #87 / #48 / #33 cluster.

Documentation (Phase 18)

- Vignette overhaul. vignettes/sangeranalyseR.Rmd rewritten
end-to-end
with a "How to..." recipe gallery (10 recipes covering single-contig
assembly, CSV mapping, forward-only data, low-quality trimming,
low-overlap detection, consensus methods, secondary peaks, Shiny
launch, FASTA / HTML export), a constructor parameter reference (4
tables), a troubleshooting matrix mapping common errors to the
Phases 15–17 fixes, and a sessionInfo() block. Closes #13, #49, #71,
#99.
- R CMD check --run-donttest hardening. Multiple pre-existing latent
example bugs were fixed:
- inst/rmd/SangerContig_Report.Rmd now loads library(knitr) so
kable() resolves during report rendering.
- readTable.SangerRead and readTable.SangerContig examples no
longer call readTable(sangerAlignmentData) (no method exists for
SangerAlignment).
- globalTrimApp, launchApp, launchAppSC, launchAppSA examples
switched from \donttest{} to \dontrun{} so runGadget() /
auto-printed shiny.appobj no longer hang the example runner.
- Maintainer tooling. plans/close_issues.py (Phase 16.5) now parses
an
Action: close|comment metadata flag from each issue's reply Markdown
— comment-only entries (used for "please retest on devel" responses)
skip the state=closed PATCH. Backwards-compatible with the existing
Phase-16 / Phase-17 reply files.

[SCArray](/packages/SCArray)
-------

                       Changes in version 1.21.3                        

- bug fix: `rowProds()` and `colProds()` returned NaN instead of 0 when
  the
  running product overflowed before a zero (Inf * 0); the product is
  now
  accumulated as mantissa and exponent, so it can not overflow, and the
  result no longer depends on the precision of 'long double'

- the unit tests compare products with matrixStats'
  `method="expSumLog"`,
  since the "direct" reference (base::prod) is platform-dependent on
  overflow; this fixes the test failure on x86_64 and aarch64 Linux

                       Changes in version 1.21.2                        

- register the native routines (src/init.c) and stop searching symbols
  dynamically; .Call() now checks the number of arguments

- bug fix: `colWeightedMeans()` ignored the weights on a non-transposed
  SC_GDSMatrix (it called the unweighted C kernel instead of
  c_colWMeans)

- bug fix: `rowProds()` and `colProds()` failed on a GDS-backed matrix
  because the parent method was called with the unsupported `method=`
  argument; both now use the native kernels in either orientation

- bug fix: `rowWeightedVars()`, `colWeightedVars()`, `rowWeightedSds()`
  and `colWeightedSds()` returned an incorrect weighted variance (the
  sum-of-squares term used the weight squared and a non-standard
  normalization); now matches matrixStats: sum_w(x-mu)^2 / (sum_w - 1)

- bug fix: `colWeightedMeans(., na.rm=TRUE)` on a sparse matrix used a
  wrong denominator (the full weight sum was not initialized)

- bug fix: memory protection leak in the C kernel `c_colProds`

- `rowLogSumExps()` and `colLogSumExps()` are now numerically stable
  (max-subtraction) and no longer overflow for large values

- `useNames=TRUE` is now the default for the row*/col* statistics,
  matching
  DelayedMatrixStats; names are kept unless `useNames=FALSE`.
  `rowRanges()`
  and `colRanges()` gain a `useNames` argument and set the row names

- `rowCollapse()` and `colCollapse()` no longer keep state in C
  file-scope
  globals (which were not reentrant and shared a column cursor between
  the
  two); the row map is held in an external pointer and the column
  offset is
  passed per block. This also removes a dangling-pointer hazard in the
  old
  colCollapse code

- new unit tests checking every overridden row*/col* statistic against
  matrixStats for both matrix orientations, with and without NAs, plus
  tests for log-sum-exp overflow, name handling, and
  rowCollapse/colCollapse

                        Changes in version 1.8.0                        

- Added calculateReconstructionError() to detect out-of-distribution
anomalies using cell-type-specific PCA reconstruction errors.
- Replaced the 4 general-purpose vignettes with 4 vignettes built
around the package's manuscript: an introduction with a simulated
ground-truth example, a benchmark of

PBMC scRNA-seq and MERFISH spatial colitis data) walking through the
project/detect/characterize diagnostic workflow.

allowing Isolation Forests to run on the union of query and
reference Highly Variable Genes (via n_hvgs) when pc_subset = NULL.
- Improved anomaly detection by switching default thresholding to a
dynamic, data-driven Median Absolute Deviation method
(threshold_method = "MAD", mad_multiplier = 2) across relevant
functions.

[scrapper](/packages/scrapper)
--------

                        Changes in version 1.8.0                        

- Respect default options from the underlying C++ libraries in
  most functions. Specifically, almost all R defaults are now set
  to NULL, and we only replace the defaults in the C++ library if
  a non-NULL argument is passed in R. This eliminates the need
  for manual synchronization between R and C++ when updating
  libraries with new defaults. We also add *Defaults() utility
  functions to report the C++ defaults for user inspection. This
  has some additional specific consequences for individual
  functions:
  
  - Updated default max.bias= in choosePseudoCount() to reduce
    log-transformation bias.
  
  - Updated default extra.work= in runPca() and scoreGeneSet()
    for better performance.
  
  - Updated default compute.median= in aggregateAcrossCells()
    to avoid unnecessary work.
  
  - Updated default use.min.width= in fitVarianceTrend() and
    modelGeneVariances() to improve trend fits for typical
    scRNA-seq datasets.

- Deprecated the num.neighbors= argument in runTsne(). Now, the
  number of neighbors is fully determined by perplexity=. For
  precomputed KNN results, an error is thrown if there are any
  mismatches between the number of supplied neighbors and
  tsnePerplexityToNeighbors(perplexity).

- Optionally add column names to the dimensions for runTsne.se(),
  runPca.se() and runUmap.se(). This is occasionally helpful for
  downstream plotting frameworks.

- Added fit.trend= option to skip trend fitting in
  modelGeneVariances().

- Check for IRLBA convergence in scoreGeneSet() and raise a
  warning if the algorithm did not converge.

- Bugfix to preserve assay names so that they match up to
  character subsets= in various compute*QcMetrics() functions.

- Added subsampleByPartition() to subsample cells within each
  partition.

- Improved support for experiments with spike-in transcripts:
  
  - Added centerSpikeInFactors() for convenient centering of
    size factors for endogenous genes and spike-in transcripts.
  
  - Added normalizeRnaCountsWithSpikeIns.se() for convenient
    normalization in the presence of spike-in transcripts.
  
  - Added chooseRnaHvgsWithSpikeIns.se() for convenient
    variance modelling against a spike-in trend.

- Renamed components.from.residuals= to center.scores.by.block=
  in runPca(), for consistency with the C++ code.

- Prevent an R session crash when an NA is supplied to block= and
  group= in functions like suggestRnaQcThresholds() and
  scoreMarkers(). Now, an error is thrown if a NA value is
  detected.

- Consistently overwrite existing columns when saving results in
  the colData or rowData of a SummarizedExperiment. This affects
  chooseRnaHvgs.se(), quickAdtQc.se(), quickCrisprQc.se() and
  quickRnaQc.se(), where the results would be appended onto the
  existing DataFrame and introduce columns with duplicate names.

- Removed the defunct analyze() and convertAnalyzeResults()
  functions.

- Various improvments to aggregateAcrossCells.se():
  
  - Added an include.factors= option to omit storage of the
    factor combinations in
  
  - Propagate the rowRanges() of the input SummarizedExperiment
    to the output object.

- Updated the work-sharing scheme for certain parallelized
  operations on matrices to improve efficiency. This introduces
  some very small changes in floating-point results when a
  different number of threads is used, due to differences in
  round-off error. Affected functions include
  modelGeneVariances(), runPca(), scoreMarkers(), scoreGeneSet(),
  aggregateAcrossCells(), aggregateAcrossGenes(), and all of the
  compute*QcMetrics() variants.

- Respect the number and ordering of pre-existing factors that
  are passed to functions accepting categorical variables in
  group=, block=, etc. This will not change any calculations but
  may result in some reordering of the output for functions that
  return a result per factor level.

- Added a filter.cells= option to quickRnaQc.se(),
  quickAdtQc.se() and quickCrisprQc.se(). If set to TRUE, these
  functions will subset the output SummarizedExperiment to only
  retain high-quality cells.

- More convenient specification of custom thresholds= in
  quickRnaQc.se(), quickAdtQc.se() and quickCrisprQc.se(). Users
  can now supply partial thresholds for some metrics and the
  thresholds for the remaining metrics will be filled in by the
  appropriate suggestions. Users can also supply a single
  threshold value for each metrics in a blocked analysis, which
  will then be used for all blocks.

- suggestRnaQcThresholds() and suggestAdtQcThreshods() now return
  a list of thresholds in subsets when block=NULL. This is more
  consistent with the data structure that is returned when block=
  is supplied.

- Include an unfiltered object in the output of analyze.se(), to
  report the full distribution of QC metrics prior to any
  filtering. This is not reported if filter.cells=FALSE, in which
  case it would be redundant with the information in x.

[scRepertoire](/packages/scRepertoire)
------------

                        Changes in version 2.9.5                        

BUG FIXES

- clonalSizeDistribution() no longer aborts on a sample whose clones
are nearly all the same size. The discrete GPD likelihood raised an
error when the optimizer drove the scale out of range, which
discarded that threshold entirely; once every threshold in threshold
had failed, which.min() returned integer(0) and the next line
reported attempt to select less than one element in get1index. The
likelihood now returns an infinite penalty the optimizer can step
away from, so these samples fit normally. Affected combineTCR()
output on the bundled contig_list at four and five samples.
- The fallback that re-initializes the GPD after a failed fit ran
inside an error handler, so anything it raised escaped the
surrounding tryCatch() rather than marking that threshold
unfittable. A threshold with a single clone above it leaves var()
undefined and tripped this, which is why threshold = 1:5 failed
across the full eight-sample example.
- If no threshold in threshold can be fit, clonalSizeDistribution()
now says so and names the sample instead of surfacing a subscript
error.

UNDERLYING CHANGES

- Internal function conversion for clonalSizeDistribution() - removed
evmix from dependencies ahead of its CRAN deprecation. The
generalized Pareto density, distribution, quantile and random
generation functions, along with the threshold fit used to
initialize the spliced gamma-GPD model, are now internal. The
replacements reproduce the previous parameter estimates and distance
matrices exactly.

                        Changes in version 2.9.4                        

BUG FIXES

- clonalCluster(chain = "both") now resolves the two chains from the
data (Heavy/Light for BCR, TRA/TRB for TCR) instead of always asking
for TRA/TRB. The chain name drives how the V(D)J block is parsed, so
BCR data was read with the wrong layout: the heavy slot took the D
gene as its J call and the light slot took the C gene. With use.J =
TRUE (the combineBCR() default) the J filter was therefore matching
on the wrong gene. Affects combineBCR(chain = "both") as well.
- clonalCluster(group.by = ...) writes cluster IDs into the .Cluster
column. The column was renamed by position, and the grouping
variable occupies that position once group.by is set, so the output
held group labels and the real IDs were left in a trailing cluster
column.
- combineBCR() reads the cluster column from clonalCluster() by name.
It previously took the last column, which picked up an unrelated
column in the case where no sequence pair passes the threshold and
clonalCluster() returns the input untouched.
- Deprecated argument warnings now actually reach the caller.
lifecycle decides whether to signal from user_env, whose default
sits two frames above the signaller; because the deprecation is
raised from an internal helper rather than from the exported
function itself, that default landed inside the package namespace
and every deprecation was classified as indirect. deprecate_soft()
is silent for indirect callers, so renamed arguments such as
clonalBin(cloneCall =) or combineBCR(removeNA =) were accepted with
no notice at all. The existing tests passed because TESTTHAT_PKG
also counts as direct, which masked this everywhere except real use.

UNDERLYING CHANGES

- clonalCluster() collapses repeated notices from the distance engine
to one per distinct message. dist.type = "hamming" emits an
equal-length notice on every call, which meant one copy per chain
per group.by level.
- Documented that dist.type = "hamming" only compares sequences of
equal length, that unequal-length pairs are assigned the maximum
distance and never cluster, and that sequence = "nt" reads CTnt. The
internal CDR3 column is named cdr3_aa regardless of alphabet, which
read as though clustering were always on amino acids (resolves
#587).
- The test suite forces lifecycle_verbosity = "warning", so a
deprecation assertion no longer depends on which test file reached
that argument first.

                        Changes in version 2.9.3                        

BUG FIXES

- StartracDiversity(pairwise = ...) labels each pair consistently
across groups (resolves #585). Pairs were built from unique(), which
returns categories in order of first appearance, so the same
unordered pair was written "1 vs 3" in one group.by level and "3
vs 1" in the next. Categories are now sorted alphanumerically before
pairing, and the label carries no direction.
- The group column of the StartracDiversity() export table now holds
the group.by level rather than the list position ("1", "2", ...).
This affects both the standard and pairwise output.
- StartracDiversity() reports expa as NA for a group with clusters
but
no recovered clonotypes. 1 - (0 / -Inf) was evaluating to 1, which
read as a fully expanded cluster. migr and tran were already NA in
this case.

UNDERLYING CHANGES

- StartracDiversity(index = "tran", pairwise = "cluster") gains a
partner column naming the other member of the pair, so the anchor
and its comparator can be read without parsing the label. The
accompanying plot now facets by anchor cluster with one box per
partner. Previously it faceted on the first token of the pair label,
which mixed several pairs into a single box. The pairwise export
table is also column-ordered group, cluster, partner, comparison,
variable, value.
- The documentation for StartracDiversity() and the STARTRAC vignette
section now spell out what each column of the pairwise table means
and note that pairs are unordered, so the index cannot be read as a
directional or time-ordered transition.

                        Changes in version 2.9.2                        

BUG FIXES

- getCirclize() self-links (the diagonal, include.self = TRUE) no
longer always return 0. The private-clone subtraction counted
zero-count clone-by-group rows from the underlying cross-tabulation
as shared, cancelling the full count. It now restricts to clones
actually observed (n > 0) in other groups, so the diagonal correctly
reports each group's private clones. The same n > 0 guard was
applied to the n.shared statistic in the include.metadata = TRUE
output.
- clonalHomeostasis() now orders the clonal groups by their
proportion
bins (Hyperexpanded -> Large -> Medium -> Small -> Rare) instead of
alphabetically. The fill categories were being sorted as a character
vector, which placed Rare before Small.

                        Changes in version 2.9.1                        

NEW FEATURES

- Full-length sequence retention (resolves #535). loadContigs() now
keeps a standardized sequence/sequence_aa column for every format
(reconstructed from framework/CDR regions for 10x and MiXCR, copied
natively for AIRR-family inputs, NA where unavailable), plus
sequence_alignment/germline_alignment when present. This is additive
and does not change existing columns.
- combineTCR() and combineBCR() gain retain.sequences (default
FALSE).
When set, full-length sequences are carried into the combined object
as per-chain columns (sequence_nt1/sequence_nt2,
sequence_aa1/sequence_aa2, and optionally
sequence_alignment*/germline*) without altering
CTaa/CTnt/CTgene/CTstrict. The retained columns flow through
combineExpression() into single-cell metadata.
- exportClones(format = "airr") now populates sequence/sequence_aa
(and alignment/germline) fields when those sequences were retained.
- New exportDowser() function (and exportClones(format = "dowser"))
reshapes BCR/TCR data into an AIRR data frame ready for
dowser::formatClones(), enabling B cell lineage / phylogenetic
analysis in the Immcantation framework (resolves #578).
exportDowser() errors with guidance when the required IMGT-gapped
alignments are absent.

UNDERLYING CHANGES

- clonalCluster() now passes the tight similarity threshold to
immApex::buildNetwork() instead of the loose value that was
refiltered afterward. The engine prunes early rather than returning
a large edge list that is mostly discarded. Raw thresholds are
unchanged, and cluster assignments match the previous behavior.
- clonalCluster() selects the edge expansion from cluster.method.
Connected-components clustering uses the memory-efficient star
expansion, which is exact for components. Community-detection
methods use the full clique expansion for exact edge multiplicity.

BUG FIXES

- combineBCR(retain.sequences = ...) now resolves the retained
columns
against the intersection of columns shared by all samples, rather
than the first sample only. This prevents an "undefined columns
selected" error (or silent dropping of a column) when samples carry
heterogeneous fields, matching combineTCR().
- Retained per-chain sequences from multi-contig chains no longer
carry literal "NA" placeholder tokens (e.g. "seq1;NA") when a contig
lacks a full-length sequence; such tokens are dropped from the join
and an all-placeholder value becomes a real NA.

DEPENDENCIES

- Added dowser to Suggests for the new lineage export path.
- clonalCluster() requires immApex (>= 1.7.1) for the new expand
argument and the faster network engine.

DOCUMENTATION

- Documented full-length sequence retention and the dowser export
path
in the main vignette and the "Combining Contigs into Clones"
article.
- Added a "Exporting scRepertoire Clones to dowser" section to the
Immcantation article covering the retain.sequences to exportDowser()
to dowser::formatClones() workflow.

[scTensor](/packages/scTensor)
--------

                       Changes in version 2.23.3                        

- Fixed empty \item label in newCCSParams.Rd (R CMD check WARNING).

- Added manual page for BuildSignedCCI (R CMD check WARNING).

- Removed unused symTensor from Imports (R CMD check NOTE).

- Fixed 'no visible binding' NOTE for m and v in
  .simulateDropoutCounts.

                       Changes in version 2.23.2                        

- DGN enrichment (enrichDGN) is no longer available because enrichDGN()
  was removed from DOSE (>= 4.7.1) due to a DisGeNET licensing change.
  The dgnenrich parameter default is changed from TRUE to FALSE.
  Setting dgnenrich=TRUE now issues a warning and returns empty
  results.

[SeqArray](/packages/SeqArray)
--------

                       Changes in version 1.54.0                        

NEW FEATURES

- new argument '.package' in `seqParallel()`, `seqApply()`,
  `seqBlockApply()` and `seqUnitApply()` for the packages loaded before
  calling the user-defined function, so that the functions in these
  packages can be used directly: they are loaded in each child process
  of a cluster or a `BiocParallelParam` object, or in the current R
  process before forking or when only one process is used

- `seqParallel()`, `seqUnitApply()` and `seqParallelSetup()` accept a
  `BiocParallelParam` object

- AARCH64 NEON SIMD optimization for vectorized internal functions,
  providing hardware-accelerated performance on Apple Silicon and other
  ARM64 platforms

UTILITIES

- `seqParallel()` with a `BiocParallelParam` object sends the jobs to
  the
  workers one by one and combines each result once it is received, as
  with a cluster object; the workers not started yet are started once
  for the whole call, and `.initialize` and `.finalize` are called once
  in each worker

- `seqGetData(, "position")`, "$chrom_pos", "$chrom_pos2" and
  "$chrom_pos_allele", and `seqApply()` with these variables no longer
  load the positions of all variants into memory: the positions are
  read
  from the GDS file via a cache of up to 131072 consecutive variants
  per file, which is efficient when the variants are accessed in order
  (e.g., `seqBlockApply()` and `seqUnitApply()`)

- `seqSetFilterChrom(, from.bp=, to.bp=)`, and so `seqSetFilter()` with
  GRanges or IRanges and `seqSetFilterPos()`, no longer load the
  positions of all variants into memory: only the minimum and maximum
  positions of every 131072 variants on a chromosome are kept, the
  chunks of variants out of the requested ranges are skipped without
  reading, and binary search is used in a chunk if its positions are
  sorted

- `seqFilterPush()` and `seqSetFilter(, action="push")`, also used
  internally by `seqBlockApply()`, `seqUnitApply()`, etc., store the
  pushed sample and variant filters as bit vectors instead of byte
  vectors, so each pushed filter uses 1/8 of the memory (1 bit per
  sample or variant) until it is popped back

- to reduce memory usage, `seqOpen()` no longer allocates the sample
  and variant filters (1 byte per sample or variant), since all samples
  and variants are selected; a filter is allocated only when it is
  needed (e.g., to set a filter or read data), and resetting the filter
  (e.g., `seqResetFilter()`) does not release the allocated memory,
  which is released when the file is closed

- the internal function `.buffer_position()` is removed, since the
  positions of all variants are no longer loaded into memory

- `seqVCF2GDS()` is faster on VCF files with many INFO fields

- `seqVCF2GDS()` parses diploid genotypes with single-digit alleles
  (e.g., "0|1" and "0/1") faster

- `seqVCF2GDS(, parallel=n)`: each parallel job seeks to its starting
  position directly instead of reading the file from the beginning (for
  a plain text or BGZF file, but not a gzip file), no tabix index is
  needed, and the temporary files are merged while the other jobs are
  still running

- new `split` in `seqVCF2GDS()`: "block" (default) splits BGZF files at
  the block boundaries without counting the variants; "variant" counts
  the variants (in parallel for BGZF files) and splits by the variant
  index, which is used if not all files are BGZF or 'start', 'count' or
  'variant_count' is given

- SeqArray no longer needs the Rsamtools package: reading and writing
  the BGZF format (i.e., bgzip) and building the .csi index are
  implemented in the package using zlib, so they work on all platforms
  including Windows; `use_Rsamtools` in `seqVCF_Header()`,
  `seqVCF2GDS()` and `seqGDS2VCF()` is deprecated and ignored

- `seqGDS2VCF()` always outputs a BGZF file (i.e., bgzip) when the file
  name ends with .gz or .bgz, together with a .csi index instead of a
  .tbi index, since the position in a .tbi index is limited to 2^29
  (~512Mb)

- `seqUnitMerge()` now properly supports merging more than two
  'SeqUnitListClass' objects via '...'

- new `seqUnitSetDiff()` to remove variant indices of one unit list
  from another, returning the set-difference version of units

- 'val' in `seqAddValue()` can be a function returning the data block
  by
  block, when adding a variable to "annotation/info": the blocks are
  written to the GDS file one by one, so the memory usage does not
  depend
  on the total number of variants ('packed' and 'packed.idx' are
  ignored
  in this case, since the data are unknown before writing). New 'param'
  in `seqAddValue()`, passed to the second argument of the user-defined
  function 'val(k, param)'

BUG FIXES

- `seqGetData(, "position")` and `seqSetFilterChrom(, from.bp=,
  to.bp=)`
  used the old positions after `seqAddValue(, varnm="position")`
  replaced them in the opened file

- `seqSetFilterAnnotID()` ignores "" and "." in `id`, instead of
  selecting all variants without an ID

- `seqVCF2GDS()` failed with "more columns than what expected" on a VCF
  file with a FORMAT column but no sample

- `seqVCF2GDS(, parallel=)` failed with "'arg' should be one of ..." if
  `storage.option` was an object from `seqStorageOption()`

- `seqDigest()` and `seqGet2bGeno()` in parallel failed if another GDS
  file had been opened before the input file, and `seqDigest()`
  returned
  an incorrect digest with a BiocParallel `MulticoreParam` object

- `seqParallel()` and `seqUnitApply()` with a cluster object returned
  incorrect results after a previous call on the same cluster failed

- `seqApply()` and `seqBlockApply()` failed with a `BiocParallelParam`
  object, and `seqGet2bGeno()` crashed R with it

- `seqParallel()` with a `BiocParallelParam` object: the variables set
  by
  `.initialize` were not visible in `FUN` unless the workers had been
  started, `process_index` was 0 for a numeric `gdsfile`, and
  `process_block_index` was 0 for `.balancing=TRUE`

- `seqParallel()` with a `BiocParallelParam` object called `FUN` with
  an
  empty selection if fewer variants (or samples) were selected than the
  workers

- `seqParallelSetup(FALSE)` did not remove the setting of
  `seqParallelSetup(TRUE)` or `seqParallelSetup(<number>)` on Linux and
  macOS, so the following calls still ran in parallel

- `seqParallel(, gdsfile, split="none")` failed with a cluster or a
  `BiocParallelParam` object, if `gdsfile` was a GDS file

- `seqUnitApply()` with a cluster object did not load the package in
  `attr(gdsfile$filename, "pkgname")` in the child processes, as
  `seqParallel()` does

- `seqParallel()` with a cluster object, if fewer variants (or samples)
  were selected than the nodes: `.initialize` and `.finalize` were
  called more than once in a node with incorrect `process_index` and
  `process_count`, and `FUN` was also called with an empty selection
  if `.balancing=FALSE`

- `seqParallel(, .balancing=TRUE, .status_file=TRUE)` with a cluster
  object did not remove the status files "_parallel_*.txt" in the
  working directory, e.g., `seqApply(, parallel=, .progress=TRUE)`

- `seqParApply(, .balancing=TRUE)` with a `BiocParallelParam` object
  did
  not balance the workload, since `x` was split into one chunk per
  worker in advance

- `seqParallel()` and `seqUnitApply()` with a `BatchtoolsParam` object
  failed with "Registry must be empty" after all jobs were done, if
  `.finalize` was given or the workers had been started by the user

- `seqVCF2GDS(, start=, count=, parallel=n)` returned more variants
  than
  requested, and split the variants wrongly when 'start' was not 1;
  'variant_count' should be exact now, since the variants beyond it are
  not converted

- `seqSetFilterPos()` errored for an empty 'pos' vector (e.g.,
  `integer(0)`), or when 'chr' contained `NA` values (e.g.,
  `c("1", NA, "2")`); an empty 'pos' now clears the variant filter,
  and `NA` chromosomes simply do not match, with `ret.idx` staying
  aligned with the query

- `seqGetData()` and `seqBlockApply()` failed with "LENGTH or similar
  applied to S4 object" when reading a FORMAT variable stored in a
  sparse array (e.g., "sp.real32" or "sp.real8u"); a sparse matrix is
  returned with the dimnames 'sample' and 'variant', or a list of
  sparse
  matrices if '.tolist=TRUE'

- `seqGetData(, .tolist=TRUE or NA)` and `seqBlockApply(, .tolist=TRUE
  or
  NA)` on a FORMAT variable: each matrix in the returned list should
  have the number of selected samples, instead of the total number of
  samples, when there is a sample filter

                       Changes in version 1.52.1                        

NEW FEATURES

- `seqParallel()` can load cloud-related packages on worker processes
  before calling the user-defined function, with backward compatibility
  for older gdsfmt versions

UTILITIES

- faster `seqSetFilterPos()` than v1.52.0

- `seqApply()` supports "$ref", "$alt", "$chrom_pos",
  "$chrom_pos_allele"
  and "$variant_index" as variable names, consistent with
  `seqGetData()`

- `seqAddValue()` supports `LogicalList`, `IntegerList`, `NumericList`
  and `CharacterList` from the IRanges package as variable-length
  annotation data input

- `seqMulticoreSetup()` invisibly returns the newly created cluster
  object when a multicore cluster is set up

                       Changes in version 1.31.12                       

- The Basic Usage vignette's note on the C implementation names it

  for enrichment of CpG sets instead.

                       Changes in version 1.31.10                       

- The startup message points at the knowYourCG package for enrichment
  of CpG sets.

                       Changes in version 1.31.9                        

- Documentation fixes from a review of the vignettes. The inference
  vignette shows its library(sesame) and caching setup, gives raw
  download URLs for the two clock files, states the mouse age the code
  returns (1.18 months) and re-identifies from ~/Downloads in both
  calls.
  The Basic Usage and QC vignettes define idat_dir as the built-in HM27
  IDATs. The non-human vignette drops an undefined tmp and uses prep
  code
  SHCDPB, as the Basic Usage table recommends for Mammal40. Ethnicity
  is
  no longer listed as an inference in DESCRIPTION or the vignette.

- sesameQCtoDF() works on HM27: the median beta statistics are unnamed,
  so an array without ch or rs probes no longer gives "row names
  contain
  missing values".

- matchDesign() (prep code M) stops with an install line when the
  suggested package RPMM is missing.

- inferSpecies() warns when fewer than 30% of the probes are detected,
  since the species call is then unreliable.

                       Changes in version 1.31.8                        

- inst/CITATION writes the one non-ASCII author name (Szab\u00f3) as an
  escape, so utils::readCitationFile() reads the file without a
  declared
  encoding. BiocCheck warned "Unable to read CITATION file".

                       Changes in version 1.31.7                        

- visualizeRegion() (and visualizeGene/visualizeProbes through it) can
  draw annotation tracks under the heatmap: show.cgi adds CpG context
  (island, shore, shelf, open sea, from UCSC cpgIslandExt) and
  show.regulatory adds Ensembl Regulatory Build features (needs
  biomaRt,
  in Suggests). Each track is built on first use and cached in
  BiocFileCache. show.beta.legend and show.annotation.legend add
  legends;
  show.loci with show.probeNames = FALSE labels probes by coordinate.
  All
  default to off, so existing calls draw as before. New
  sesameAnno_buildHeatmapAnnotations() builds the tracks. Contributed
  by
  Pancreas-Pratik (zwdzwd/sesame#220).

                       Changes in version 1.31.6                        

- qualityMask()'s recommended set for HM450 and EPIC is now the five
  M_*
  tracks EPICv2 and MSA already use (M_1baseSwitchSNPcommon_5pt,
  M_2extBase_SNPcommon_5pt, M_mapping, M_nonuniq, M_SNPcommon_5pt),
  read
  from KYCG.HM450.Mask.20261008 / KYCG.EPIC.Mask.20261008 in
  sesameData,
  which are built from the InfiniumAnnotation v8.2 masks. The older
  KYCG
  tracks (mapping, channel_switch, snp5_GMAF1p, extension, sub30_copy)
  masked about twice as many probes and are still available through
  mask_names. This brings R and SeSAMe2 to the same quality mask on all
  four human arrays (zhou-lab/sesame#1). KYCG.EPICv2.Mask.20261008 and
  KYCG.MSA.Mask.20261008 are rebuilt from the same v8.2 masks.

- getMask(), listAvailableMasks() and backgroundMask() read the newest
  KYCG.<platform>.Mask.<date> sesameData lists. They used to search
  every
  listed version, whose tracks share names, so which build a track came
  from depended on listing order. A track name only an older build has
  is still found there. backgroundMask() for HM450/EPIC therefore now
  uses M_nonuniq and the M_1baseSwitchSNPcommon tracks, as SeSAMe2
  does.

                       Changes in version 1.31.5                        

- Fixed readControls() building the control data.frame by positional
  assumption. It named the columns with colnames(ctl) <-
  c('G','R','col',
  'type') over a frame whose signal matrix has four columns, so
  Color_Channel and Type were cbind-ed past the end of that name vector
  and
  arrived unnamed, while `type` silently took a signal column.
  Downstream,
  controls(sdf)$Type was a vector of integers, so negControls()'s
  grep("negative", ...) matched nothing and detectionPnegEcdf() failed
  in
  ecdf() with "'x' must have 1 or more non-missing values" on EPIC and
  HM450 -- the platforms whose controls arrive through readControls()
  rather
  than as SigDF rows. The columns are now named explicitly.

- qualityMask() gained `platform` and `mask` arguments, so a custom or
  combined-array mask can be supplied directly instead of being applied
  as a
  separate addMask() step after the fact.

                       Changes in version 1.31.4                        

- Removed the Google Analytics tag from the vignette header. Vignette
  rendering no longer contacts an external host at build time, and
  installed
  vignettes no longer load a remote tracking script.

- Documented sesame-cli, a standalone C implementation of the SeSAMe
  preprocessing workflow (IDAT to betas, QC, differential methylation,
  copy
  number) for large cohorts and pipeline deployment. Its betas agree
  with
  this package to within ~1e-3 worst case; the intentional divergences
  are
  documented in the sesame-cli NUMERICS.md. This package remains the
  reference implementation. See the README and
  https://zwdzwd.github.io/sesame-cli.

[simpleSeg](/packages/simpleSeg)
---------

                 Changes in version 1.15.2 (2026-10-14)                 

- Tiled segmentation of large images supports pca, cellBody =
  "discModel" or
  cell body markers, and transform "tissueMask". The PCA and the cell
  body
  models are fitted on pixels sampled across the whole image (up to
  100,000
  and about 1,000,000), chosen by their position so that the sample
  does not
  depend on the tiles or the number of cores.

- Image files are opened once per process, which makes reading tiles
  much
  faster.

- Channel names are read from the band names of multi-band TIFF files.

- Pixels equal to a file's "no data" value (such as 255 in 8-bit TIFFs
  written by terra) keep that value instead of becoming missing.

- Cell body models no longer fail when the cell body signal is
  constant.

                 Changes in version 1.15.1 (2026-10-14)                 

- cellBody = "discModel" and cell body markers work again for several
  images
  of the same size, and cell body markers work for a single image.

- An image where no nuclei pass the threshold gives a warning and an
  empty
  mask instead of an lm.fit error (#20).

- simpleSeg() checks that nucleus and tissue markers exist, and checks
  watershed, cellBody and cores; nucleus can be given as channel
  positions.

- normalizeCells() stops when imageID is missing and a per-image method
  is
  requested (#16, #22), and works with a single marker.

- Faster segmentation with lower memory use: each image is processed
  once in
  one task, on plain arrays, with fitted values from one QR fit.

- Parallel processing starts the BiocParallel workers once per call,
  runs
  BLAS with one thread per worker, and gives every image its own random
  number stream, so masks do not depend on the number of cores.

- simpleSeg() reads images from files: multi-channel files (OME-TIFF,
  QPTIFF, multi-page TIFF), folders of single-channel files (one image
  split
  by marker) and folders of such folders.

- New argument output: "masks", "cells" (a SpatialExperiment with the
  mean
  intensity of every channel, area and centroid of each cell, as from
  cytomapper::measureObjects()) or "none"; maskDir saves the masks as
  TIFF
  files. Paths return cells by default, images in R return masks.

- Images larger than tileSize are segmented tile by tile without
  reading them
  into memory; the cells and masks are those of the whole image.

- Gaussian smoothing is done in C++ (faster, and much less memory than
  the
  FFT used before; values agree to about 1e-13).

- Pixels of equal height are separated by a tiny amount (1e-6 of the
  tolerance) depending on their position before the watershed, so masks
  no
  longer depend on how ties are ordered. Masks from watershed =
  "distance",
  where most pixels are tied, and from transform "norm99" change
  slightly.

- PCA uses the markers that vary over the pixels it is fitted on.

- spatstat.geom and grDevices are no longer imported; terra is
  suggested
  (for reading files) rather than imported.

[singleCellTK](/packages/singleCellTK)
------------

                 Changes in version 2.23.6 (2026-10-08)                 

- Help pages link to other packages' topics with package anchors (for
example \link[SummarizedExperiment]{colData}), as R CMD check and
Bioconductor now require. No change to functionality.

                 Changes in version 2.23.5 (2026-10-08)                 

- runFastMNN() hides deprecation warnings raised inside batchelor's
fastMNN() and reducedMNN(), as runMNNCorrect() already did for
mnnCorrect(). batchelor still calls deprecated scuttle functions.
Other warnings are unchanged.

                 Changes in version 2.23.4 (2026-10-07)                 

- Fixed feature selection on the Celda tab of the Shiny app. Both the
Scran_modelGeneVar and SeuratFindHVG options failed: the first
called a function that does not exist, the second was never run
because its option value did not match, and both requested the top
genes with an argument that getTopHVG() does not accept. With
SeuratFindHVG, only the vst method works with Seurat 5. The selected
genes are now stored in the featureSubset alternative experiment
used by Celda; the main dataset keeps all genes, as with the None
option, instead of being reduced to them.
- Fixed starting the Shiny app with data, singleCellTK(inSCE = sce),
which failed for any object without alternative experiments.
- The SoupX help page in the app describes the new clustering method.

                 Changes in version 2.23.3 (2026-10-07)                 

- runModelGeneVar() now models gene variances with
scrapper::modelGeneVariances() instead of the deprecated
scran::modelGeneVar(). Means and total variances are unchanged, but
the biological component comes from a different trend fit, so the
ranking of highly variable genes changes (about 90-97% of the
top 500 genes are the same on the test datasets). Results that
depend on modelGeneVar HVGs, such as PCA, UMAP, and clusters, can
change.
- runSoupX() clusters cells (when no clusters are supplied) with the
steps of scran::quickCluster(), computed with scrapper and bluster.
The automatic clusters, and therefore SoupX's contamination
estimates, can change slightly.

                 Changes in version 2.23.2 (2026-10-07)                 

- Replaced functions deprecated in scuttle 1.22 and scran 1.40.
Results are unchanged (identical, or within floating-point error):
- runClusterSummaryMetrics(), plotSCEHeatmap(), and the TSCAN
functions aggregate with scrapper or base R instead of
scuttle::aggregateAcrossCells().
- scaterlogNormCounts() normalizes with
scrapper::normalizeRnaCounts.se().
- runPerCellQC() and sampleSummaryStats() compute the per-cell QC
metrics with scrapper::computeRnaQcMetrics() and singleCellTK
code (for the top-N, gene-set, and altExp columns) instead of
scater::addPerCellQC(). This is about 4 times faster on large
data. runPerCellQC() uses BPPARAM to set the number of threads.
The metadata packageVersion recorded by runPerCellQC() is now
singleCellTK's.
- runScranSNN() builds graphs with bluster::makeSNNGraph().
- runWilcox() uses an internal Wilcoxon rank-sum test, the same
test scran::pairwiseWilcox() performed.
- New dependencies: scrapper, bluster, and BiocSingular. scuttle is
no
longer imported directly.
- runMNNCorrect() hides deprecation warnings raised inside
batchelor::mnnCorrect(), which still calls deprecated scuttle
functions. Other warnings are unchanged.
- Fixed plotSCEHeatmap() with aggregateRow, which always failed.
- Fixed runScranSNN() with useAltExp and altExpRedDim, which always
failed.

                 Changes in version 2.23.1 (2026-10-06)                 

- runDecontX() now calls the decontX package directly instead of
going
through celda. Since celda 1.23.0, celda::decontX() requires decontX
to be installed, which made runDecontX() and runCellQC() fail where
it was not. decontX is now imported, and the run metadata records
the decontX version. Results are unchanged. Note that decontX 1.11
initializes its cell clusters with scrapper, so contamination
estimates can differ slightly from earlier Bioconductor releases.
- Moved scMerge from Imports to Suggests. It is only used by
runSCMerge(), and it cannot currently be installed on all platforms
(an unrelated toolchain problem in one of its dependencies), which
blocked installing singleCellTK there entirely. runSCMerge() now
stops with an informative message if scMerge is not installed.
- Fixed runHarmony() with harmony >= 1.0.0, where HarmonyMatrix() was
removed. The function now detects the installed harmony version and
calls RunHarmony() on 1.0.0 and above, while keeping the original
HarmonyMatrix() code path for older installations. With harmony >= 1.0.0 the PCA for a full-size assay is computed by singleCellTK,
since harmony no longer performs it, using all features of the
selected assay with scaling so that it matches the PCA the legacy
interface performed internally. Corrected embeddings are not
expected to match between harmony versions. After upgrading harmony,
the legacy tuning arguments (tau, block.size, max.iter.cluster,
epsilon.cluster, epsilon.harmony) are no longer accepted through
'...'; harmony raises an error for them, and they must be passed
through .options = harmony::harmony_options(...) instead.
- Changed runScDblFinder() defaults for nNeighbors and simDoublets to
NULL, so scDblFinder chooses these values itself

[SingleR](/packages/SingleR)
-------

                       Changes in version 2.16.0                        

- Added top= option to combineRecomputedResults() to restrict the
  number of per-label markers used for integrated classification.
  This defaults to 10 to reduce the feature space for faster
  compute, but can be set to Inf to recover the previous results.

- Bugfix to SingleR() to respect non-default assay.type.ref=.

[smartid](/packages/smartid)
-------

                        Changes in version 1.9.2                        

- All the main wrapper functions keep the same usage.

Performance

- top_markers() no longer scales the full feature-by-cell matrix. Row
centring densifies a dgCMatrix by construction, and that dense
intermediate was the single largest allocation in the pipeline. The
scaling is now deferred to the reduced G x K / K x G statistic:
scale_mgm() applies a per-row affine map with a strictly positive
scale, and every statistic downstream of it is affine-equivariant,
so scaling the reduced result is the same operation on a matrix
thousands of times smaller. On a 5000 x 3000 input at 3% non-zero
this is 9-18x faster and uses 10-17x less memory for sparse input,
and roughly 1.2x faster with 1.4x less memory for dense input.
- mad and the 1-vs-max beta contrast are location-invariant, so they
take the scale factor only; mean, median and the raw label
coefficients take both terms.
- scale_mgm() itself is unchanged, including its return class. The
new
row_scaling_params() holds the centre and inverse SD both it and the
deferred path use, so the two cannot drift apart.
- Scores are unchanged. median and mad are bitwise identical; the
mean
and glm paths agree to within 1e-15, the round-off expected from
reassociating the arithmetic, and the selected marker sets were
identical across every scaling, aggregation, batch and softmax
combination tested.
- The deferral applies only where fit_label_betas() takes the
closed-form solve. A non-identity link is not affine in the
response, and a rank-deficient design (a batch or donor covariate
nested inside the label) is rejected by the closed form, so both
cases fall back to the previous materialised route with no change in
behaviour.

                        Changes in version 1.9.1                        

Bug fixes

- Completed the sparse-matrix support started in 1.7.1. The IAE
branch
had been converted but the IDF branch had not, so cal_score() still
aborted on a dgCMatrix for four of the eight idf_iae_methods() with
'x' must be an array of at least two dimensions. idf(), idf_m() and
idf_sd() now use sparseMatrixStats::rowSums2(), and idf_m() masks
with (expr > thres) * n_sub instead of ifelse(), which silently
drops dim on a sparse logical matrix. Affected methods: standard, m,
sd and hdb.
- gs_score_init() used base::colMeans() and therefore rejected all
sparse input, which also broke gs_score() and ova_score_boxplot().
It now uses sparseMatrixStats::colMeans2().
- iae_sd() took row SDs over the whole matrix instead of the
requested
features, so with a features subset it returned nrow(expr) values
instead of length(features) and the closing log1p() silently
recycled a mismatched vector. Values were wrong for any subset other
than the leading contiguous rows. idf_sd() was already correct; the
two now match.
- top_markers(use.glm = FALSE, method = "median" | "mad") failed on
sparse input. Row centring turns a dgCMatrix into a dense dgeMatrix,
for which sparseMatrixStats carries no rowMedians() or rowMads()
method. The scaling step now returns an ordinary matrix once
sparsity is gone, which costs nothing because the data is already
dense at that point.
- AnyMatrix named only matrix and dgCMatrix, so dgRMatrix, dgTMatrix
and dgeMatrix inputs failed with "unable to find an inherited
method". The class union now uses the Matrix virtual class, covering
every representation that package defines.

Testing

- New tests/testthat/test-sparse-parity.R: parameterised dense vs
dgCMatrix parity across all eight IDF/IAE methods, every internal
helper, the features subset paths, gs_score(), scale_mgm() and seven
top_markers() configurations.
- New tests/testthat/test-idf-iae-oracles.R: the IDF/IAE formulas
re-implemented independently in base R, guarding dense values across
the sparse conversion without shipping a snapshot file.

Known issues

- top_markers(family = poisson()) fails with length of 'dimnames' [1]
not equal to array extent. This is unrelated to sparsity and affects
dense input equally: the default scale = TRUE produces negative
values, glm.fit() then errors for every gene, and the unnamed
fallback coefficients leave fit_label_betas_glm_loop() returning a
zero-row matrix. Deciding the correct behaviour is deferred (to fit
poisson distribution, should not use scale=TRUE).
- SVT_SparseMatrix from the SparseArray package, which current
SingleCellExperiment readers emit, is still rejected; it is not a
Matrix subclass and supporting it would add a dependency.
