[UCell](/packages/UCell)
-----

                       Changes in version 2.17.1                        

- Accept any matrix-like inputs, includes DelayedArrays (credit
  to B. Demaille, see PR #55:
  <https://github.com/carmonalab/UCell/pull/55>)

- Add tests for main functions

- Default BPparam to SerialParam() for single-threaded runs

[UCSC.utils](/packages/UCSC.utils)
----------

                       Changes in version 1.10.0                        

- No significant changes in this version.

[universalmotif](/packages/universalmotif)
--------------

                       Changes in version 1.32.0                        

NEW FEATURES

- Added CWM (Contribution Weight Matrix) motifs for signed,
  unnormalised scores from TF-MoDISco / DeepLIFT-style attribution
  methods. Create with type = "CWM" and plot with use.type = "CWM".
  convert_type(cwm, "PPM") normalises absolute contributions per
  column, enabling downstream analyses; conversion from probabilistic
  types to CWM is not supported. MEME readers/writers accept
  CWM = TRUE, and generic matrix readers/writers accept type = "CWM".
  CWM input is opt-in, not auto-detected. See ?create_motif and
  ?convert_type.

- Added trim_cwm(), a CWM-aware trimmer that drops edge
  columns by absolute column sum. Defaults to the
  TF-MoDISco-lite fraction-of-peak rule (`trim.threshold =
  0.3`); an optional `abs.threshold` argument switches to an
  absolute-value cutoff. Walks inward from the chosen edges
  only (`trim.from = c("both", "left", "right")`),
  mirroring `trim_motifs()`'s edge-only semantics. Returns a
  trimmed CWM with the type tag preserved.

- Added compare_motifs_lite(), a DNA/RNA motif comparison function
  aligned with yamtk cmp (https://github.com/bjmt/yamtk). Uses
  per-column Pearson correlation and a TOMTOM-style empirical or
  parametric null, with Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment.
  Returns a score/p-value/q-value matrix or a table of significant
  pairs. Score-only comparisons were ~40x faster than compare_motifs()
  on a 200x200 motif set at 4 threads. See ?compare_motifs_lite.

- Added scan_sequences_lite(), a minimalist DNA/RNA scanner using
  the same C++ core as scan_sequences(). It omits multifreq scoring,
  gapped motifs, q-values, exhaustive p-values, non-pvalue thresholds,
  respect.strand, and allow.nonfinite. On a 50-motif HOCOMOCOv11
  benchmark it was ~2-3x faster than scan_sequences(calc.pvals = TRUE)
  at 4 threads on equivalent work. See the Sequence Searches vignette
  for benchmarks, including comparisons with yamtk scan.

- Added view_motifs_lite() and motif_tree_lite(), DNA/RNA plotting
  alternatives using compare_motifs_lite(). Logos align to the
  highest-IC motif; trees use Pearson distances, (1 - score) / 2.
  Both reuse the existing plotting machinery. For amino-acid or
  custom-alphabet motifs, use view_motifs() and motif_tree().

- Added geom_motif(), annotate_motif(), geom_logo(), and
  annotate_logo(): ggplot2 layers that embed sequence logos into
  arbitrary plots. The annotate_*() helpers use fixed coordinates;
  geom_*() layers support mapped positions and different motifs per
  group. The *_motif variants accept universalmotif objects, while
  *_logo accepts row-named numeric matrices. Letter colours do not
  affect the plot's fill scale. See ?geom_motif.

- motif_tree_lite() now draws a sequence logo at each tip by default
  (tiplogo = TRUE), with aligned motif positions. The default layout
  changes from "circular" to "rectangular". Tip logos support only
  "rectangular" and "slanted" layouts and are unavailable for dist
  input. See ?motif_tree_lite for alignment and sizing options.

- New vignette "MotifDatabaseCuration.Rmd": end-to-end recipe for
  consolidating motif sets from several public sources into a
  single deduplicated, trimmed, and annotated MEME file. Uses human
  JASPAR2022, HOCOMOCOv11-core, and CIS-BP motifs to demonstrate
  threshold selection, clustering, provenance tracking, and export
  verification.

- New vignette "ChIPseqWorkflow.Rmd": an end-to-end ChIP-seq motif
  analysis on real data, starting from a peak BED file bundled in
  inst/extdata (VAL1-GFP peaks in Arabidopsis from Yuan et al.
  2021, NAR 49:98-113). Covers discovery, deduplication, database
  comparison, enrichment, scanning, positional bias, and co-occurrence.
  New Suggests dependencies: rtracklayer,
  BSgenome.Athaliana.TAIR.TAIR9.

- view_motifs() gains a `sort.by` argument controlling the display
  order: "none" (default; input order), "ic" (descending information
  content), or "similarity" (Pearson-based hierarchical clustering).
  Alignment always uses the highest-IC anchor, regardless of display
  order.

- Added motif_coocc(), testing pairwise per-sequence co-occurrence
  with one-sided Fisher's exact tests and BH correction. Scans DNA/RNA
  internally or accepts precomputed hits plus n.sequences for any
  alphabet. max.distance adds descriptive spatial summaries without
  changing the test. Optional no.overlaps removes within-motif
  overlaps during scanning, affecting only spatial summaries and
  preserving between-motif overlaps. See ?motif_coocc.

- Added implant_motifs(), planting sampled motif instances at known
  positions for testing analysis pipelines. Supports fixed counts
  per sequence, a per-bp Poisson rate, or explicit positions, with
  controls for central bias, spacing, and strand. return.indices = TRUE
  includes placement metadata alongside the modified sequences.
  See ?implant_motifs.

- Added match_bkg() and plot_match_bkg(): composition-matched
  background sampling for DNA/RNA motif enrichment and de novo
  discovery analyses. Samples from an XStringSet universe or BSgenome
  to match target GC fraction and length, with plots for match-quality
  assessment. Optional per-sequence covariates allow matching on
  additional properties such as conservation or mappability; these
  require an explicit universe and cannot be combined with genome.
  return.indices = TRUE includes matched covariates for plotting via
  plot_match_bkg(indices = ...). See ?match_bkg.

- Rewrote motif_peaks() as an analytical CentriMo-style positional
  enrichment function (Bailey & Machanick 2012), accepting scan hit
  tables as data.frame or GRanges. Tests central (default) or local
  windows with one-sided binomial tests, Bonferroni correction across
  windows, and BH correction across motifs. Added plot_motif_peaks()
  to show hit distributions and the best window per motif.
  See ?motif_peaks.

- Added merge_motifs_lite() and merge_similar_lite(), minimalist
  DNA/RNA
  counterparts to merge_motifs() and merge_similar() built on
  compare_motifs_lite(). Merging aligns to the highest-IC motif and
  averages columns, optionally weighted by nsites. Clustering uses
  connected components of pairs passing a q-value cutoff, then merges
  each cluster. return.clusters = TRUE returns the original motifs
  and cluster assignments instead. See ?merge_motifs_lite and
  ?merge_similar_lite.

- Added motif_finder(), a DNA/RNA _de novo_ motif discovery function
  aligned with the command-line tool yamtk me
  (https://github.com/bjmt/yamtk), whose design is based on STREME
  (Bailey 2021). Combines enriched k-mer seeds, iterative refinement,
  Fisher tests against shuffled or supplied backgrounds, deduplication,
  BH filtering, and IC trimming. Runs motif widths in parallel and
  returns a universalmotif_df with discovery statistics. Replaces the
  previous unexported stub. See ?motif_finder.

- Added enrich_motifs_lite(), a minimalist DNA/RNA motif-enrichment
  function aligned with the command-line tool yamtk enr
  (https://github.com/bjmt/yamtk). Uses scan_sequences_lite(), Fisher
  tests on sequence presence or per-position hit rates, and BH
  adjustment. Returns a data.frame of counts, enrichment, and
  p/q-values,
  controlled by a hit p-value and result q-value cutoff.
  See ?enrich_motifs_lite.

- Added dedup_hits(), a fast C++ implementation of yamtk's greedy
  overlap-dedup algorithm. Accepts data.frame or GRanges input;
  auto-detects pvalue-vs-score priority direction. Used internally
  by scan_sequences_lite(no.overlaps = TRUE) and available for
  post-processing of any hit set. Distinct from scan_sequences()'s
  existing no.overlaps argument, which uses connected-components
  clustering and is left unchanged.

- Added plot_comparison(), a clustered heatmap of compare_motifs_lite()
  results with dendrograms, logos and an optional tree cut.

- Added plot_hits(), plot_enrichment(), plot_coocc() and
  plot_score_distribution() for scan, enrichment, co-occurrence and
  score distribution results.

- Added mask_complexity(), which masks low-complexity regions with
  symmetric DUST (as in dustmasker), and soft-masked letters if asked.

MINOR CHANGES

- ggplot2 >= 4.0.0 is now required.

- merge_motifs() and merge_similar() now emit one-line hints
  pointing at merge_motifs_lite() / merge_similar_lite() when the
  user's
  argument set maps cleanly onto the leaner functions. Silence with
  options(universalmotif.suggest.merge_motifs_lite = FALSE) and
  options(universalmotif.suggest.merge_similar_lite = FALSE).

- enrich_motifs() now emits a one-line hint pointing at
  enrich_motifs_lite() when the user's argument set maps cleanly onto
  the leaner function. Silence with
  options(universalmotif.suggest.enrich_motifs_lite = FALSE).

- compare_motifs() now emits a one-line hint pointing at
  compare_motifs_lite() when the user's argument set maps cleanly onto
  the leaner function. Silence with
  options(universalmotif.suggest.compare_motifs_lite = FALSE).

- motif_pvalue(method = "dynamic") now batches across motifs in a
  single C++ call parallelised with RcppThread, instead of
  dispatching one C++ call per motif via mapply. Identical numerical
  output; 2.3x faster at nthreads = 1 and 7.4x faster at nthreads =
  4 on a 50-motif HOCOMOCO benchmark. scan_sequences(calc.pvals =
  TRUE) and scan_sequences_lite() both benefit automatically.

- scan_sequences() now emits a one-line hint pointing at
  scan_sequences_lite() when the user's argument set maps cleanly onto
  the leaner function. Silence with
  options(universalmotif.suggest.scan_sequences_lite = FALSE).

- motif_tree() now emits a one-line hint pointing at motif_tree_lite()
  when the user's argument set maps cleanly onto the leaner
  function. Silence with
  options(universalmotif.suggest.motif_tree_lite = FALSE).

- Reduced repeated power calculations in the C++ backends for
  shuffle_sequences(), get_bkg(), create_sequences(), and
  compare_motifs(). Results are numerically identical, with roughly
  10-20% speed-ups in informal benchmarks.

- motif_pvalue(method = "exhaustive") now stops with a clear error
  when a motif is too wide for exhaustive score enumeration (the
  nrow^width path would overflow a 32-bit integer).

- Various textual improvements to the vignettes.

BUG FIXES

- scan_sequences() gives every motif its own P-values when gapped
  motifs are scanned with others.

- mask_ranges() stops with an error for ranges on sequences not in
  `seqs` instead of ignoring them.

- get_matches() no longer returns words scoring just below the score,
  and works for single-column motifs.

- score_match() gives the same scores as scanning.

- normalize() gives PCMs without a pseudocount a pseudocount of 1, so
  scanning them no longer gives hits almost everywhere.

- An ICM column of zeros converts to a uniform column rather than NaN.

- create_motif(bkg = NULL) uses the default background.

- read_transfac() keeps counts from a single site.

- Negative letters in sorted logos mirror the positive ones.

- motif_rc() keeps gaps and no longer fails for motifs with
  higher-order matrices, which are now reverse complemented correctly.

- trim_motifs() and trim_cwm() move gaps with the trimmed columns, and
  trim_motifs() no longer fills in an empty nsites slot.

- create_motif() accepts one-column matrices with row names, rejects
  letters outside a custom alphabet, and only reads 20-row matrices as
  amino acids when the row names are amino acids.

- Validation now checks single gaps, gap sizes, NaN values and
  negative pseudocounts.

- PPM to PCM conversion no longer gives uneven or negative counts when
  rounding overshoots.

- round_motif(), normalize() and convert_type() with a new pseudocount
  update the total IC and consensus.

- Relative entropy is 0 rather than NaN for letters with probability 0.

- motif_range(allow.nonfinite = TRUE) no longer returns NA, and
  log_string_pval() works for values below 1e-308 on all platforms.

- read_transfac() skips header blocks, keeps whole HC and OS fields,
  names motifs by accession whatever the field order, and follows the
  letter order of the P0 line.

- read_cisbp() keeps whole TF Name, Family and Species fields.

- read_jaspar() follows row labels, reads custom alphabets from them
  and reads unlabelled 20-row matrices as amino acids.

- read_homer() keeps spaces in names from tab-separated headers.

- read_meme() matches custom alphabet backgrounds by letter, reads
  sites at positions of 10,000 or more and joins block diagrams over
  any number of lines.

- write_meme() no longer writes E= 0 for motifs without an E-value or
  leaves trailing spaces, and meme_alph() declares each complementary
  pair once.

- Matrices of probabilities rounded to two decimals are read as PPMs
  rather than ICMs.

- Logos draw negative letters smaller than 0.03, with the same gaps
  between them as positive letters, keep their top y-axis break, and
  give CWMs round breaks without excess space below zero.

- motif_tree_lite() tip logos no longer fail for motifs sharing a name.

- shuffle_sequences(method = "markov") and create_sequences() with
  k-mer frequencies now condition each letter on the letters just
  generated.

- get_bkg() skips k-mers with letters outside the alphabet, which
  could be miscounted or crash R for long k-mers, and writes MEME
  background files without trailing spaces.

- Wootton-Federhen complexity no longer gives NaN for windows of 171
  letters or more.

- calc_windows(return.incomp = FALSE) keeps a complete last window, and
  mask_ranges() works with one range per sequence or none.

- motif_finder() ranks seeds with tied P-values by k-mer, so results no
  longer depend on the standard library.

- compare_motifs_lite() breaks tied alignments by overlap length and
  then order instead of rounding, writes RNA consensus strings with U
  using the motif consensus rule, and no longer gives P-values of
  exactly 0 under the parametric null.

- compare_motifs() and compare_columns() normalize WPCC weights, and
  KL and ALLR no longer give NaN for letters with probability 0.

- scan_sequences() scans gapped motifs on both strands, with gaps that
  can have size zero and after ungapped motifs, and sequences shorter
  than a motif give no hits for it in both scanners instead of an
  error.

- write_homer() writes thresholds on HOMER's own score scale instead
  of log2 odds, which made them about 44% too high.

- motif_coocc() odds ratios no longer overflow to NA for large tables.

- match_bkg(genome = ...) keeps the width of a single target sequence
  instead of drawing random widths.

- motif_peaks() numbers motifs by code point rather than locale, and
  motif_proximity() keeps the motif.i from scan_sequences().

- motif_finder() corrects each motif's P-value for the words tried in
  its search and counts every word tried in the q-values, so random
  sequences no longer give significant motifs. The default `qvalue`
  cutoff is now 0.05.

- motif_proximity() places hits at their middle positions, which
  stops wide hits being reported as enriched near random anchors, and
  clips anchor zones at chromosome ends.

- motif_coocc(self.pairs = TRUE) no longer tests a motif against
  itself; self-pairs count sequences with hits at two or more distinct
  positions.

- create_motif() warns when a matrix with negative values is converted
  to a PPM because no type was given.

- CWMs have no total IC, which is computed when they are converted to
  another type.

- calc_complexity() scores DNA and RNA against ACGT or ACGU by default,
  as sequence_complexity() does, rather than each string's own letters.

- get_matches() now returns no matches for an Inf threshold from an
  unattainable motif_pvalue() cutoff, fixing an error in the examples.

- Native motif files now retain gap definitions, including in minimal
  output. Fixed the constructor confusing gap positions with minimum
  gap widths and gap expansion passing probabilities to the scanner
  instead of PWM scores. External exports warn when gaps or
  higher-order
  matrices cannot be preserved.

- create_motif() now accepts NA site counts as unknown and rejects
  non-finite or fractional counts clearly.

- Fixed dynamic P-value thresholds admitting hits above the requested
  cutoff in scan_sequences() and scan_sequences_lite(). Thresholds
  now respect inclusive comparisons, and unattainable cutoffs return
  no hits instead of admitting the highest-scoring matches. Some
  scans and downstream analyses will therefore report fewer hits.

- Fixed decimal score thresholds rounding down during conversion to
  the integer score grid. Dynamic P-value queries now use the same
  inclusive boundary convention. Documented the distinction between
  integerised and original real-valued score distributions.

- Dynamic motif_pvalue() now preserves supplied finite PWMs when the
  background is unchanged, avoiding conversion round-trips that could
  shift entries across integer-score boundaries.

- Fixed scan_sequences() reporting truncated stop coordinates and
  matched sequences for higher-order motifs (use.freq > 1). Hits and
  the short-sequence check now use the full nucleotide span.

- Fixed scan_sequences(), view_motifs(), and view_motifs_lite()
  accepting motif lists in which only some motifs contained the
  requested multifreq matrix. Every motif is now checked before
  scanning or plotting.

- Fixed motif_pvalue() rejecting use.freq > 3 when method was omitted.
  The default dynamic method is now resolved before validation.

- Fixed shuffle_sequences() accepting the unsupported method =
  "random". It now reports the supported methods in a clear error.

- Fixed get_consensus() and get_consensusAA() crashing R on invalid
  input. Both now require a single numeric motif column of the
  expected length (4 for DNA/RNA, 20 for amino acids) and raise a
  clear error otherwise.

- Fixed overlapping letters in view_motifs() when three or more
  letters at a position had negative heights. Stacking now uses
  cumulative offsets; one- and two-letter stacks are unaffected.

- Fixed view_motifs() / view_logo() inverting small letters when
  y.spacer exceeded their height. Spacing is now capped at half the
  letter height. Also affects geom_motif() / geom_logo(), which
  share the renderer.

- Fixed create_motif() ignoring an explicit DNA/RNA/AA alphabet when
  the input matrix had rownames. This left the consensus and motif
  column names unset and broke to_list() / update_motifs() round-trips.

- Fixed nthreads = 0 silently running serially instead of using all
  available threads as documented (RcppThread::parallelFor treats 0
  as "no workers" rather than "all hardware threads"). Affected
  scan_sequences(), shuffle_sequences(), compare_motifs(),
  motif_pvalue(), motif_tree(), create_sequences(), get_bkg(),
  enrich_motifs(), make_DBscores(), sequence_complexity(), and
  window_string().

- Fixed convert_motifs(motifs, class = "TFBSTools-PFMatrixList") (and
  the PWMatrixList / ICMatrixList variants) erroring with "unknown
  'class'". These documented output classes now return the
  corresponding TFBSTools list objects.

- Fixed compare_motifs() using the first motif's background for both
  motifs when nthreads > 1. Each motif's own background is now used.

- Fixed unsafe parallel calls to R's probability functions in
  compare_motifs(), which could corrupt state under load. P-value
  evaluation now runs serially; the lookup search remains parallel.

- Fixed compare_motifs() row-not-found path in the db.scores lookup
  infinite-looping when n1 / n2 ran past the table without finding a
  matching row.

- Fixed shuffle_sequences() crashing R when k was larger than the
  shortest input sequence. The C++ backends now refuse the call with
  a clear "'k' must be <= the shortest sequence length" error.

- Fixed read_homer() storing NA in the nsites and bkgsites slots when
  those header fields were missing. ifelse(is.na(...), numeric(0), x)
  cannot return numeric(0); replaced with explicit if/else so missing
  fields parse to an empty vector as documented.

- Fixed read_jaspar(), read_cisbp(), read_meme(), and read_transfac()
  silently returning an empty list when the input file had no
  motif headers / separators. All four now error with
  "no motifs found in '<file>'".

- Fixed read_jaspar() producing an nsites slot of -Inf when a header
  was followed by an empty matrix. The reader now errors with a
  clear "empty motif matrix" message before the downstream
  max(colSums(motif)) on numeric(0).

- Fixed convert_motifs() for motifStack 'pcm' inputs silently
  picking unique(colSums(...))[1] as nsites when the column sums
  disagreed. Now checks the column sums within tolerance and errors
  with the observed range if they don't agree.

- The S4 validity method for PCM motifs now also checks that the
  motif matrix's column sums are all equal (within the same 1%
  tolerance the PPM validity check uses).

                       Changes in version 1.30.1                        

MINOR CHANGES

- Improved memory usage of scan_sequences() for larger motif
  collections &
  genomes.

BUG FIXES

- Fixed filter_motifs() erroring when filtering by nsites (malformed
  apply()
  call instead of vapply()).

- Fixed motif["name"] <- NA_character_ (and other atomic slots) being
  silently
  accepted instead of raising an error.

- Fixed to_list() writing literal "0" into the name slot when altname
  was NA
  and a dplyr::rename() swap was performed on the data frame.

- Fixed new("universalmotif", altname = ...) silently dropping the
  altname
  argument due to a missing assignment operator.

- Fixed motif_score() erroring with allow.nonfinite = TRUE and the
  default
  threshold.type = "total".

- Fixed motif_pvalue() rejecting non-finite scores even when
  allow.nonfinite =
  TRUE was specified (sanitize_input() was not checking the flag).

- Fixed shuffle_motifs() silently resetting the pseudocount to 1 and
  the type
  to PPM regardless of the input motif's values.

- Fixed shuffle_sequences() and get_bkg() not guarding against
  window.size <
  k, or fractional window.size values that resolve to 0 after
  expansion.

- Fixed enrich_motifs() crashing inside fisher.test() when input
  sequences are
  shorter than the widest motif. Now gives a clear error message.

- Fixed read_jaspar() leaving the nsites slot empty for PCM motifs; it
  is now
  derived from the column sums of the count matrix.

- Fixed an unsigned-integer underflow in src/scan_sequences.cpp that
  could
  cause out-of-bounds reads when scanning sequences shorter than motif
  width + k.

- Fixed a signed-integer overflow in scan_sequences_cpp() when the
  threshold
  supplied via threshold.type = "logodds.abs" exceeded ~2e6; on x86_64
  the
  overflow wrapped to INT_MIN, causing all positions to be returned
  regardless
  of the threshold.

- Fixed the shuffle.method error message in enrich_motifs() which
  listed
  "random" instead of "euler" as a valid option.

- Fixed a wrong variable name (seq.names instead of bkg.names) in the
  fallback
  for unnamed background sequences in enrich_motifs().

- Fixed a wrong assignment operator (= instead of ==) in the
  motif_pvalue.method compatibility check in scan_sequences() which was
  silently clobbering the calc.pvals variable.

- Fixed scan_sequences() BH q-value calculation; previously used an
  inverted
  ratio with an erroneous 100x factor instead of the standard BH
  formula.

- Fixed a wrong inner-loop index in motif_pvalue(method="exhaustive")
  that
  produced incorrect p-values for motifs wider than 2*k.

- Fixed get_matches() failing when passed a length-1 list of motifs due
  to an
  undefined variable and the list-unwrapping occurring after the @
  access.

- Fixed get_bkg() validation incorrectly rejecting multi-element
  window.overlap
  when merge.res = FALSE, due to missing parentheses around an ||
  sub-expression.

- Fixed merge_motifs() silently dropping the bkgsites slot when only
  one of the
  merged motifs had it populated (threshold was > 1 instead of >= 1).

- Fixed get_matches() error message incorrectly referencing the max
  possible
  score when reporting a min-score violation.

- Removed a dead NULL check in enrich_motifs() that would have errored
  (nrow(NULL) < 1 yields logical(0)) had it ever been reached.

- Removed a leftover debug print() call in enrich_motifs() input
  validation that
  caused error messages to be printed twice.

- Fixed scan_sequences(return.granges = TRUE) failing when sequences is
  empty,
  due to 1:length(sequences) producing c(1, 0) for length-0 input.

- Fixed shuffle_sequences() producing identical shuffles across
  parallel threads
  when rng.seed = 0.

- Fixed score_match(allow.nonfinite = TRUE) returning NA instead of
  -Inf for
  match positions that correspond to non-finite motif cells.

- Fixed read_motifs() failing with 'object motif not found' when
  reading a
  saved motif file containing a multifreq block, because the motif
  object was
  used before it was constructed.

- Fixed convert_motifs() Motif-method (motifRG) passing the PCM matrix
  as a
  positional argument due to a stray <- instead of = in the argument
  list.

- Fixed possible undefined behaviour in scan_sequences() when scanning
  sequences shorter than k with a multifreq motif (size_t underflow in
  deal_with_higher_k / deal_with_higher_k_NA).

- Fixed merge_motifs() populating pval, qval, eval, nsites, and
  pseudocount
  slots with NA when all input motifs had those slots empty; they are
  now
  correctly left empty.

- Fixed trim_motifs() discarding all successfully-trimmed motifs when
  any
  single input motif was fully trimmed away (partial-trim case now
  correctly
  returns only the surviving motifs).

- Fixed read_motifs() using lexicographic string comparison for version
  dispatch; 1.1.7 was incorrectly treated as older than 1.1.67. Now
  uses
  numeric_version().

- Fixed read_cisbp() off-by-one error when CIS-BP files contain
  consecutive
  TF metadata lines, caused by mutating meta_starts during seq_along
  iteration.

- Fixed a temp-file leak in the compare_motifs() HTML report path where
  the
  second on.exit() call overwrote the first (now uses add = TRUE).

- Fixed add_multifreq() retry loop erroring with 'missing value where
  TRUE/FALSE needed' or keeping the failing k value, due to a stale
  seq_along
  and an off-by-one in seq_len(counter) vs seq_len(counter - 1).

- Fixed runtime error ('argument FUN.VALUE is missing') in
  read_motifs() when
  reading pre-1.2.x files containing multifreq blocks.

- Fixed filter_motifs() erroring when filtering by pval, qval, eval,
  altname,
  family, or organism and any motif had an empty slot for that field
  (sapply
  returned a list of mixed lengths; now uses vapply).

- Fixed shuffle_motifs() dropping the matrix dimension when shuffling a
  length-1 motif (missing drop = FALSE in column slice), causing
  downstream
  errors.

- Fixed read_motifs() silently accepting non-logical values for the
  progress
  and BP arguments (logi_check was computed but not appended to
  all_checks).

- File connections in all read_*() and write_*() functions are now
  closed via
  on.exit() so they are released cleanly even when an error occurs
  mid-read.

[VISTA](/packages/VISTA)
-----

                        Changes in version 1.1.7                        

Internal

- The test that PCA and MDS plots do not depend on the order genes
are
supplied in no longer fails when an axis comes back negated.
Shuffling the input genes can make prcomp() return the mirror image
of the same embedding on some LAPACK/BLAS builds (it did on Linux
CI), which the test read as an order dependence. Axes are now
oriented with the same canonicalisation the 1.1.4 snapshots use, and
a new test checks that a sign flip passes while a moved point still
fails. No user-visible behaviour changes; only the test suite is
affected.

                        Changes in version 1.1.6                        

New features

- edgeR's quasi-likelihood F-test. create_vista(),
run_edger_analysis(), benchmark_vista_equivalence() and
validate_vista_deep() gain edger_test = c("LRT", "QL"). "QL" runs
glmQLFit()/glmQLFTest() (edgeR v4 pipeline), which the edgeR authors
recommend for bulk RNA-seq; the likelihood-ratio test treats the
dispersion as known and is liberal with few replicates. The test
used is recorded in cutoffs(v)$edger_test, and the report config
accepts edger_test:; for an edgeR object made before 1.1.6, which
does not record the test, the report states the likelihood-ratio
test and marks it as inferred. The equivalence check runs its own QL
reference. The vignettes now set edger_test.

Default changing in VISTA 1.4.0

- edger_test will default to "QL". It stays "LRT" in this release so
that no results change without warning. A call that runs edgeR
(method = "edger" or "both") without setting edger_test, or with
edger_test = NULL, prints a message, classed vista_default_change
and throttled like the deprecation warnings, saying so. Set
edger_test = "LRT" to keep current results after the change, or
edger_test = "QL" to use the new default now; either silences the
message. DESeq2 and limma-voom analyses are not affected. See
?VISTA-deprecated.

Bug fixes

- tximport abundance or lengths could be analysed as counts.
read_vista_counts(format = "tximport", counts_from = "abundance")
imported TPM, and counts_from = "length" transcript lengths, as if
they were counts, and edgeR and limma tested them without complaint.
Both now raise an error.

- tximport counts were analysed without transcript-length correction.
tximport's default countsFromAbundance = "no" leaves estimated
counts unscaled and expects the DE method to use length offsets,
which VISTA does not. Such input that carries abundance and length
(also when it does not say how it was scaled) is now converted to
length-scaled TPM counts (tximport's countsFromAbundance =
"lengthScaledTPM", recommended when the method does not use
offsets), with a message. With tx2gene, transcript-level input is
summarised to genes as tximport's summarizeToGene() does, which
rebuilds gene counts from abundance and length even when the
transcript counts were already scaled; summing them, as VISTA did,
undid the gene-level length correction. The results agree with
tximport's own to within numerical precision (relative differences
below 1e-14). abundance and length are matched to counts by name,
and missing or negative values, a sample with zero total abundance,
or a tx2gene that matches no transcript are clear errors, as is an
unrecognised countsFromAbundance value. Without abundance/length,
VISTA warns and uses the counts as given. Were you affected? If you
imported tximport output made with the default countsFromAbundance =
"no", a hand-built list without that field, or transcript-level
"lengthScaledTPM"/"dtuScaledTPM" output with tx2gene (scaledTPM sums
to the same gene counts); re-run those analyses.

- DESeq2 stopped on estimated counts. Non-integer counts from
tximport
or RSEM made create_vista(method = "deseq2") fail with "some values
in assay are not integers". DESeq2 now receives them rounded, with a
message, as DESeqDataSetFromTximport() does. Filtering is applied to
the counts as given, as for edgeR and limma, so method = "both"
keeps one set of genes, and its counts(v) holds DESeq2's rounded
counts whichever source is active.

- Values that are not counts could be analysed without comment. All
three engines now refuse negative values, and warn (class
vista_not_counts_warning) about non-integer values with an
unmistakable sign of not being counts: every sample summing to
exactly one million (TPM, CPM) or small, almost all fractional
values (log scale). These are warnings because no rule on the values
alone separates counts from normalised data: estimated counts from
libraries of about a million reads must not be refused, and TMM-CPM,
FPKM or filtered TPM cannot be recognised. Supply raw or estimated
counts. Integer counts are unaffected.

- RSEM TPM or FPKM could be imported as counts. Where count_column
selects the values read from RSEM output, only RSEM's count columns,
expected_count (the default) and posterior_mean_count, are now
accepted. A merged table whose sample columns are named in
sample_names is read as given.

- Untested genes were stored with pvalue = 1. DESeq2 reports NA for
genes it does not test (Cook's-distance count outliers); VISTA
replaced that with 1 when it stored the comparison, beside a padj
that stayed NA, so an untested gene read as tested and the row
disagreed with itself. On airway this affected 51 genes. Tables from
comparisons() and those written by export_vista_assets() now show
NA, as the engine reported, and so do the per-backend
pvalue_deseq2/pvalue_edger columns of a consensus table. Plots and
rankings already substituted their own value for a missing p-value,
so figures are unchanged.

- Filtering a consensus table on padj returned the union, not the
intersection. With consensus_mode = "intersection", a gene called by
only one backend is not called, but its padj was that backend's
significant value, contrary to the documented "less-significant of
the two". Selecting padj <= 0.05 on the table, as
get_foldchange_scatter() and the volcano thresholds do, therefore
picked up every single-backend gene. Such genes now carry the
less-significant pvalue and padj of the two backends, and their
log2fc follows consensus_log2fc (the mean of the two by default)
instead of the calling backend's estimate, as for every other
uncalled gene. On airway this changes log2fc for all 119
single-backend genes (by up to 0.36) and the p-values of most of
them. In union mode, where they are called, they keep the calling
backend's values, as before. regulation was always correct and is
unchanged.

- DEG-count plots dropped comparisons with no DEGs.
get_deg_count_barplot(), get_deg_count_pieplot() and
get_deg_count_donutplot() left out a comparison whose summary was
all "Other", asking for it by name aborted with "not found in DEG
summary", and when no requested comparison had any DEG they returned
NULL with a warning. Such comparisons are now drawn at zero.
Comparison order is unchanged. A summary that uses none of the
labels Up, Down or Other (possible with as_vista()) is left out with
a warning naming the labels found, rather than drawn as zero.

- limma MA plots put the wrong quantity on the x axis. For limma the
table's baseMean is AveExpr, already log2-CPM, and get_ma_plot()
preferred it to the object's mean expression, so the axis showed
log10(log2-CPM + 1). It now uses the object's mean expression for
every engine, as its own comment intended.

- An explicit intercept was not removed for edgeR and limma. For
design_formula = "~ 1 + cell + group", VISTA prefixed 0 +, which + 1
then undid, so the model kept its intercept. VISTA now reads the
intercept from the formula's terms. The fitted model spans the same
space, so results differ only within numerical precision.

Verification

- benchmark_vista_equivalence() no longer shares code with what it
checks. Its reference pipelines used VISTA's own helpers for sample
matching, design construction, contrasts, DEG calls and row
alignment, so a defect in any of them was reproduced on both sides
and passed -- which is how the first and third defects above went
unnoticed. The reference now calls only base R, stats and the
engines, re-implements the documented contract from scratch (see
?benchmark_vista_equivalence), derives contrasts from the design
itself, reads VISTA's tables through its exported accessors and
matches rows by identifier. It compares every numeric column the
engine reports, the retained gene set and the set of comparisons;
the summary gains gene_sets_identical, comparison_sets_identical,
all_columns_within_tolerance and columns_compared.
baseMean_within_tolerance is NA for edgeR, which reports no baseMean
(it was a vacuous TRUE); a numeric column VISTA stores but the
reference does not report (columns_not_in_reference) counts as a
mismatch; and a mismatch between a value and NA is reported as an
infinite difference instead of 0. The MA, PCA and DEG-count checks
now read the data get_ma_plot(), get_pca_plot() and the DEG-count
plots draw, and the PCA check compares every sample-sheet column;
the volcano check still rebuilds its inputs from the stored table.
- Each method's reference element has a new shape. Its comparisons
are
data frames in VISTA's column names (gene_id, log2fc, stat, pvalue,
padj, plus baseMean and lfcSE for DESeq2, logCPM for edgeR, and
baseMean (limma's AveExpr), B, P.Value and adj.P.Val for limma), not
the engines' own tables. row_data is removed (use
rowMeans(reference$norm_counts)), group_column is added, and each
deg_summary table has exactly two rows, Up and Down.
- New tests check that no reference function uses VISTA code -- as a
call, as a function value, through VISTA::/VISTA:::, or by name in a
string. They inject defects into VISTA's own helpers that the
benchmark must report: a flipped contrast sign, swapped Up/Down
calls, values under the wrong gene labels, samples matched to the
wrong metadata rows, a dropped covariate, untested genes stored as p
= 1, and a comparison dropped from DEG-count plot data. The 1.1.5
check caught two of the first five; those five were chosen to target
the helpers it shared, so this shows the new check can fail where
the old one could not, not a detection rate.

Other changes

- Objects record the VISTA and R versions and the installed DESeq2,
edgeR and limma versions in metadata(x)$provenance, as ?VISTA-class
already described. The stored object behind example_vista() was
regenerated to carry them.
- ?create_vista documents how a sample sheet without sample_names is
matched to count columns, and what the consensus padj is: a
conservative ranking score, not an FDR-adjusted p-value of the
consensus. In simulations the intersection lowered, but did not
control, the single backends' false discovery rate, and the union
raised it.
- The DESCRIPTION now names limma-voom among the engines.
- The code-economy vignette now computes every tally from its own
chunks at build time, states its counting rule, attaches what each
workflow needs, and checks that both workflows give the same DESeq2
results.
- min_counts and min_replicates in benchmark_vista_equivalence() and
validate_vista_deep() are now described as they behave:
min_replicates counts samples across the whole experiment, not per
group.

                        Changes in version 1.1.5                        

New features

- get_foldchange_matrix() gains display_id, display_from and
display_orgdb, matching [get_foldchange_heatmap()]. genes may now be
given as display labels, and the returned matrix is labelled with
them. Because symbols are not unique, duplicated labels are made
unique with a warning rather than left to collide -- duplicated
rownames would make m["SYM", ] return whichever row came first and
silently hide the other. Rows keep the object's identifiers unless
display_id is supplied, so existing calls are unaffected.

Bug fixes

- get_foldchange_heatmap(annotate_columns = TRUE) annotated nothing.
The columns of a fold-change heatmap are comparisons, but the
annotation was built by filtering colData for samples named in those
columns -- an intersection that is always empty -- so the track
carried no levels and no colours. It now annotates by comparison,
coloured from the object's comparison palette, and accepts
column_anno_colors like the expression heatmap.
- A display_id supplied without a display_orgdb failed with missing
value where TRUE/FALSE needed. The internal comparison to_type ==
from_type is NA when from_type is NA and logical(0) when it is NULL,
and || can evaluate neither. It now names the missing argument.
- get_expression_lineplot() accepted display_from/display_orgdb and
ignored them -- its private copy of the identifier mapping handled
only the rowData() path. All gene-taking plots now share one
resolver.

                        Changes in version 1.1.4                        

Internal

- Plot-stability snapshots for PCA and MDS no longer depend on
eigenvector sign. prcomp() and cmdscale() may return an axis or its
negation for identical input, decided by the LAPACK/BLAS build, so
the snapshots could fail on one machine and pass on another with
nothing in the package changed. Each axis is now canonicalised
before comparison. No user-visible behaviour changes; only the test
suite is affected.

                        Changes in version 1.1.3                        

Bug fixes

- Statistical annotations failed under ggpubr 1.0.0. Passing
stats_group = TRUE produced a plot that constructed normally and
then died when drawn, with could not find function "create_p_label".
ggpubr 1.0.0 builds p.label = "p.format" into an expression calling
that package-internal helper, which is not visible from the
environment of the mapping VISTA supplies, so the annotation layer
could not be evaluated. VISTA now names the statistic's own computed
columns via ggplot2::after_stat(). The rendered label text is
unchanged on every ggpubr version, and an unrecognised p.label still
falls through to ggpubr rather than silently dropping the
annotation.

Affects get_expression_boxplot(), get_expression_violinplot(),
get_expression_barplot(), get_expression_raincloud(),
get_foldchange_boxplot() and get_foldchange_raincloud() — anywhere
stats_group = TRUE was combined with the default p.label =
"p.format". Users on ggpubr < 1.0.0 were unaffected.

Documentation

- Figure cropping is disabled (crop = NULL). BiocStyle's crop hook
shells out to magick; without it every figure emitted a warning.

                        Changes in version 1.1.2                        

Targeted at Bioconductor 3.24 (VISTA 1.2.0). This release fixes
several
defects that produced silently wrong results, makes VISTA behave like
a
proper Bioconductor object, and begins a deprecation cycle for a
number
of inconsistent argument names. No existing script stops working:
every
renamed argument still functions and warns.

Data-integrity fixes

Check whether you were affected:

- get_expression_matrix(genes = ..., summarise = TRUE) mislabelled
rows. Rows were subset in assay order but labelled in the order
genes was supplied, so whenever those differed every row carried
another gene's identifier and values.

Scope: no other VISTA function called get_expression_matrix(), so no
plot, heatmap, DEG table, export or generated report was affected.
Internal group averaging goes through norm_counts(summarise = TRUE),
which labels rows from the matrix itself and was never affected by
this. Only code that called get_expression_matrix() directly could
be wrong.

Were you affected? Only if you passed genes and summarise = TRUE and
your gene vector was in some order other than the object's own row
order. Passing genes already in rownames(x) order (or omitting
genes) always produced correct output. Note that ranked inputs — for
example get_genes_by_regulation(top_n = ...), which sorts by
absolute fold change — are normally not in row order, so those calls
were affected. Re-run them.

The bug dates back to the first release, so it is present in 1.0.0
and every 0.99.x.

- GSEA ranked vectors slid scores onto the wrong genes. get_gsea()
reassigned names(rank_vec) from a mapping helper that drops unmapped
and duplicate identifiers, so the shorter vector was padded with NA
and every score after the first gap moved to a different gene. The
resulting NES values and leading-edge gene lists were meaningless.

Scope: only set_type = "kegg" was affected in practice. That path
always converts to ENTREZID, and any real dataset contains
identifiers with no ENTREZ mapping, so the vector always shortened.
set_type = "msigdb" converted an identifier type to itself, which
short-circuits before querying the annotation database and cannot
shorten. set_type = "go" never reassigned the names at all. Verified
on a 22-gene input containing two identifiers absent from the OrgDb:
"kegg" returned 20 names for 22 scores, "msigdb" returned 22.

No other VISTA function called get_gsea(), so nothing else in the
package consumed a corrupted ranking. Re-run any get_gsea(set_type =
"kegg") results; MSigDB and GO results are unaffected.

- get_corr_heatmap() drew a staircase, not a triangle. The triangle
mask was computed against input order while the axes were
re-levelled to clustered order, under the default cluster_by =
"correlation".

- Multi-file count importers bound columns positionally. The STAR,
HTSeq and RSEM importers took gene identifiers from the first file
only and never checked that row i described the same gene in the
others, so files with equal row counts but different ordering were
silently misaligned and every count for those samples was attributed
to the wrong gene.

Scope: only read_vista_counts() given a vector of two or more file
paths with format of "star", "htseq" or "rsem", and only when those
files did not already list the same genes in the same order. A
single file, a data frame, a matrix, "featurecounts" and "tximport"
all take a name-keyed path and were never affected. Files written by
one pipeline run normally do share an order, so a uniform set of
inputs was fine; the risk is mixing files produced at different
times or by different pipeline versions, where HTSeq's trailing
__no_feature/__ambiguous rows or STAR's four leading N_* rows may
differ.

Imports now match by gene identifier and error, naming the file and
up to five missing identifiers, when a file does not cover the
reference gene set. This can surface an error where a script
previously appeared to work; it was producing wrong numbers.
Anything built from a multi-file STAR, HTSeq or RSEM import should
be re-imported and re-analysed.

- run_vista_report() reported its own defaults as your parameters.
When a prebuilt object was supplied via vista_rds, the report
printed deseq2 / 1 / 0.05 / padj regardless of how the object was
built.

- run_cell_deconvolution()'s SYMBOL retry told xCell2 the wrong
identifier type. When the first scoring attempt failed, VISTA
retried with a SYMBOL-keyed matrix built from rowData, but carried
the original gene_id_type (for example "ensembl") into the retry --
handing xCell2 symbols while declaring them Ensembl IDs. The retry
therefore either failed with the real error masked behind a generic
message, or scored against a near-empty gene overlap.

- Deconvolution was broken for ENSG...:SYMBOL rownames — the common
case reached automatically by gene_id_type = "auto".

- Fixed get_ma_plot() reading a non-existent metadata key for its
threshold fallback, get_expression_lollipop() failing to resolve
symbols through an OrgDb, comparison colours collapsing to
character(0) and crashing get_foldchange_lineplot(), NaN columns
when summarising over a factor with unused levels, and YAML/filename
escaping in report and asset output.

- Hardened the DE-table alignment helper, which reindexes every
comparison onto the counts matrix and so underpins the whole
package. It now rejects a duplicated reference gene list instead of
emitting rows whose names R had silently de-duplicated (g2 -> g2.1)
away from the gene_id column they came from, coerces tibble input to
a plain data frame — a tibble ignores rownames<-, so every gene read
as absent and was replaced by an NA row with a perfectly correct
label — and asserts as a post-condition that the returned rownames
and gene_id column both match the reference exactly. No shipped code
path reached the tibble case; both are closed against future
callers, because a wrong answer here is invisible in the output's
shape.

Reproducibility

- Pathway gene capping is now deterministic.
get_pathway_heatmap(max_genes) and get_enrichment_chord(max_genes)
truncated the pathway gene set positionally. Pathway membership is a
set, and clusterProfiler's ordering of it is arbitrary and, verified
here, differs between R sessions -- so the same call could plot a
different subset of genes on different runs. The heatmap now ranks
candidates by expression variance (most informative rows first) and
the chord by pathway participation, both breaking ties on the gene
identifier.
- Deconvolution scores are no longer aligned to samples by position
when their own labels disagree. run_cell_deconvolution() accepted
scores whose row count matched the sample count and stamped the
object's sample names onto them, even when the scores carried
different labels of their own -- which would attach every sample's
cell fractions to the wrong sample. Alignment is now by name
whenever names are available in either orientation; contradictory
labels are an error; and position is used only when the scores carry
no labels at all, with a message saying so.
- The airway vignette sets a seed. GSEA estimates p-values by
permutation and ComplexHeatmap's row k-means is unseeded, so the
rendered document previously changed on every build for reasons
unrelated to the code.

Analysis changes

- The edgeR and limma backends now filter with the same predicate as
DESeq2 (a gene is kept when at least min_replicates samples reach
min_counts); they previously ignored min_counts and used a hardcoded
cpm > 1. They also filter before calcNormFactors(), per the edgeR
user's guide. edgeR and limma results shift slightly relative
to 1.1.1.
- min_replicates is documented accurately: it counts samples across
the whole experiment, never within each group.

New features

- Raw counts are retained as a counts assay, reachable with
counts(v).
as_deseq_dataset() converts a VISTA object back into a DESeqDataSet.
Roughly doubles the assay footprint; opt out with
create_vista(keep_raw_counts = FALSE).
- [ method. Subsetting now keeps metadata consistent: row subsetting
reindexes every DE table and recounts DEG summaries, column
subsetting prunes orphaned colour maps and warns when a comparison
loses its samples. Previously v[1:10, ] left the DE tables
describing all original genes and validObject() still returned TRUE.
- show() method. Objects now display as class: VISTA with their
grouping, comparisons, active DE source, cutoffs and schema version.
- updateObject() migrates objects from older metadata schemas.
- ?VISTA resolves, and there is a package overview page.
- Unknown arguments passed through ... are now rejected with a
did-you-mean suggestion. A typo such as get_expression_heatmap(v,
gene = my_genes) previously plotted the default gene set instead of
erroring.
- get_foldchange_lineplot() gains return_type. Its default stays
"both" (the list it has always returned); pass "plot" for a bare
ggplot.
- get_enrichment_chord() gains return_type. Its default stays "data"
because it draws to the active device and has always returned its
table invisibly; "plot" returns a recorded plot that
save_vista_plot() can now write to a file. VISTA enables the device
display list before drawing, since png() and pdf() leave it off and
would otherwise yield an empty recording that silently saved
nothing.

Deprecations

All still work and warn once per session. See ?VISTA-deprecated for
the
full table and timelines; each becomes defunct in 1.4.0.

| Function | Deprecated | Use instead | |---|---|---| |
get_deg_count_pieplot(), get_deg_count_donutplot() | label |
label_type
| | get_corr_heatmap() | cluster_by | order_by | | get_corr_heatmap()
|
show_corr_values, col_corr_values | label, label_color | |
get_celltype_group_dotplot() | error | errorbar | | four
get_expression_*() plots | comparisons | stat_comparisons | |
get_pca_plot(), get_mds_plot(), get_umap_plot() | top_n_genes | top_n
|
| get_expression_lollipop(), get_foldchange_lollipop() | line_size |
linewidth | | get_volcano_plot() | col_up, col_down, col_other(s),
lab_size | colors, label_size | | get_pca_plot() | sample.seed |
removed; it never had any effect | | get_expression_barplot(),
get_expression_lollipop() | facet_scale | facet_scales | |
get_expression_violinplot(), get_expression_lineplot() |
value_transform
| log_transform |

return_type values are unified on c("plot", "data", "both"). The
legacy
spellings still work and warn: "heatmap"/"clusters" (both heatmaps),
"matrix" (get_celltype_heatmap()), "genes" (get_pathway_heatmap()).
Arguments that select the shape of a purely tabular result --
get_pathway_genes(), get_genes_by_regulation(), read_vista_counts(),
derive_vista_metadata() -- keep their own vocabularies, because they
have no plot component.

Undocumented gene caps (20 for embeddings, 15 for lollipop, 25 for
barplot) are now the max_genes argument, with the existing values as
defaults.

Testing

- Added label/value integrity tests covering every exported function
that accepts a gene set. They assert two properties the 1.0.0 defect
violated: results do not depend on the order genes were supplied in,
and the value reported for a gene is that gene's own value, checked
against an independent recomputation from the object. The previous
suite asserted shape -- is.matrix(), nrow(), class -- all of which
the broken output satisfied.
- Verified by mutation testing: reintroducing the exact 1.0.0 defect
now fails five tests across three files, and replacing a name-keyed
lookup with a positional one elsewhere fails nine.
- The DE-table alignment helper is now covered end to end: identifier
resolution and its fallbacks, DESeq2/edgeR/limma column
canonicalisation, type-preserving NA padding across numeric,
integer, character, logical, factor, Date and POSIXct columns, and
the reordering guarantee itself. Both faults fixed above were found
by these tests.

Internal

- Accessor generics dispatch only on the object rather than on every
formal.
- Depends: R (>= 4.6.0); viridis dropped from Imports (unused);
BiocGenerics added. grDevices, graphics, stats, tools and utils are
now declared — all five were already used via :: without being
listed. The maintainer's ORCID iD is recorded in Authors@R.
- print.vista removed — no object could carry that class.
- Plot layer data is pinned by snapshot tests so API renames cannot
silently change output.

                        Changes in version 1.1.1                        

Bug fixes

- get_volcano_plot() now inherits log2fc_cutoff, pval_cutoff, and the
new p_value_type argument from cutoffs(x) instead of hard-coding the
raw pvalue column at 0.05. Previously the volcano could colour a
different set of genes than deg_summary(), get_deg_count_barplot(),
and get_genes_by_regulation() reported for the same object. Pass the
arguments explicitly to restore the old behaviour (p_value_type =
"pvalue", pval_cutoff = 0.05). The y-axis label now reflects which
p-value column is plotted.

- Consensus DE tables (method = "both") no longer overwrite pvalue
and
padj with 1 for every gene that is not called by both backends. Each
gene now carries the less-significant of the two backend values, so
the columns stay continuous and usable for volcano/MA plots and
ranking. Per-backend values remain available in
pvalue_deseq2/pvalue_edger/padj_deseq2/ padj_edger, and DEG calls
are unchanged.

- get_ma_plot() read its threshold fallback from the non-existent
metadata(x)$cutoffs key, silently using package defaults instead of
the object's stored cutoffs.

Reproducibility

- Pathway gene capping is now deterministic.
get_pathway_heatmap(max_genes) and get_enrichment_chord(max_genes)
truncated the pathway gene set positionally. Pathway membership is a
set, and clusterProfiler's ordering of it is arbitrary and, verified
here, differs between R sessions -- so the same call could plot a
different subset of genes on different runs. The heatmap now ranks
candidates by expression variance (most informative rows first) and
the chord by pathway participation, both breaking ties on the gene
identifier.
- Deconvolution scores are no longer aligned to samples by position
when their own labels disagree. run_cell_deconvolution() accepted
scores whose row count matched the sample count and stamped the
object's sample names onto them, even when the scores carried
different labels of their own -- which would attach every sample's
cell fractions to the wrong sample. Alignment is now by name
whenever names are available in either orientation; contradictory
labels are an error; and position is used only when the scores carry
no labels at all, with a message saying so.
- The airway vignette sets a seed. GSEA estimates p-values by
permutation and ComplexHeatmap's row k-means is unseeded, so the
rendered document previously changed on every build for reasons
unrelated to the code.

Analysis changes

- The edgeR and limma-voom backends now filter genes with the same
predicate as the DESeq2 backend — a gene is kept when at least
min_replicates samples reach min_counts. They previously ignored
min_counts at this step and used a hard-coded cpm > 1 threshold, so
the same arguments produced different feature sets across backends.

- The edgeR and limma-voom backends now filter before calling
edgeR::calcNormFactors(), per the edgeR user's guide; normalization
factors were previously estimated from genes that were about to be
discarded. Both changes shift edgeR/limma results slightly relative
to 1.1.0.

Documentation

- min_replicates is documented accurately: it counts samples across
the whole experiment, not within each group, which is what all
backends have always implemented.
- create_vista() now documents the consensus table's column
semantics,
including the support column.
- Removed a reference to get_enrichment_network() from the README; no
such function exists. Corrected the citation block and listed the
missing expression-plot entries.

Testing

- Added label/value integrity tests covering every exported function
that accepts a gene set. They assert two properties the 1.0.0 defect
violated: results do not depend on the order genes were supplied in,
and the value reported for a gene is that gene's own value, checked
against an independent recomputation from the object. The previous
suite asserted shape -- is.matrix(), nrow(), class -- all of which
the broken output satisfied.
- Verified by mutation testing: reintroducing the exact 1.0.0 defect
now fails five tests across three files, and replacing a name-keyed
lookup with a positional one elsewhere fails nine.

Internal

- Removed duplicate definitions of .prepare_sample_metadata() and
.filter_genes(), which existed in both utils-internal.R and
viz_related.R, with collation order silently deciding which one ran.
- Removed unreachable helpers .plot_pca(), .plot_mds(),
.prepare_mds_dataframe(), .prepare_corr_matrix(),
.plot_corr_heatmap(), and .cluster_log2fc_matrix() along with their
generated man pages.
- pkgdown-only articles under vignettes/guides/ and
vignettes/workflows/ are no longer shipped in the source tarball.

                        Changes in version 1.8.0                        

SIGNIFICANT USER-VISIBLE CHANGES

- importBugphyzz() defaults to data release v1.2.0
  (10.5281/zenodo.24166279): 477,741 annotations for 93,900 taxa, 36
  attributes and 19 sources.

  include annotations derived from Wikipedia; earlier releases are CC
  BY 4.0. The package stays Artistic-2.0.

  numeric attributes (#292).

  kappaThreshold and r2Threshold (#271).

  BacDive, The Microbe Directory and NCBI RefSeq assemblies (#275).

- New source Wikipedia_2026 (confidence medium, evidence nas): traits
  stated in English Wikipedia introductions, with the new attributes
  halophily class, temperature class and ph class; skin is also a
  habitat (#296).

- attribute_synonyms.tsv maps source terms to the controlled
  vocabulary (#264).

- New arguments kappaThreshold, r2Threshold and asrScoreThreshold; a
  threshold below its default also loads the imputations the export
  left out (#292).

- Validation scores per attribute and per state ship as
  validation_attributes.tsv and validation_states.tsv.

BUG FIXES AND MINOR IMPROVEMENTS

- Cell length and width no longer collapse to the lower bound of their
  range (#275).

- Downloads are cached per version.

- Typos and missing terms in attributes.tsv are fixed (#281).

- Tests that download data skip when offline (#266).

[curatedMetagenomicData](/packages/curatedMetagenomicData)
----------------------

                       Changes in version 3.22.0                        

SIGNIFICANT USER-VISIBLE CHANGES

- mergeData() and returnSamples() return a sparse assay (dgCMatrix)
  for gene_families, as curatedMetagenomicData() already does for a
  single study, instead of a dense matrix. For 48 samples from two
  studies the assay is 0.95 GB rather than 2.5 GB. Code that needs a
  dense matrix can call as.matrix() on the assay (#304, @amsegura;
  #318, @adamsorbie)

- rownames = "NCBI" gives bare NCBI Taxonomy IDs as row names, without
  the species: and genus: prefixes. Rows that share an ID are summed,
  with a message naming them. For "short" and "NCBI", clades that NCBI
  resolves no further than genus are dropped with a warning; rownames
  = "long" keeps every row (#316, @LiNk-NY)

BUG FIXES AND MINOR IMPROVEMENTS

- returnSamples() no longer mislabels columns. When a requested sample
  had no assay match and sampleMetadata was not in study order, the
  returned columns carried the names and colData of other samples
  (#354, @lwaldron)

- returnSamples() no longer drops a sample whose sample_id also occurs
  in another requested study (#354, @lwaldron)

- mergeData() returns a SummarizedExperiment input unchanged, instead
  of failing with subscript is out of bounds when given the result of
  returnSamples() (#321, @BinhongLiu)

- returnSamples() keeps only the requested samples of each study
  before merging, and mergeData() no longer builds intermediate data
  frames. Peak memory for four gene_families samples from two studies
  fell from 10.3 GB to 3.6 GB (#304, @amsegura)

- mergeData() and returnSamples() stop with a clear error when the
  merged gene_families assay would hold more than the 2^31 - 1
  non-zero values that a sparse matrix can store, instead of failing
  with p[length(p)] cannot exceed 2^31-1. The 5,474 samples from 45
  studies requested in #304 are over this limit (#304, @amsegura)

- rownames = "NCBI" keeps its row tree with mia 1.21.30 and later.
  Rows that share an NCBI Taxonomy ID are summed in this package
  instead of with mia::agglomerateByVariable(), which now removes the
  tree (#356, @lwaldron)

- The curatedMetagenomicData() help page and the vignette explain how
  the "long", "short" and "NCBI" row names differ (#342, @lwaldron)

- The vignette builds when packages in Suggests are not installed, and
  OmicsMLRepoR is removed from Suggests while it cannot be installed
  on Bioconductor 3.24 (#339, #340, @lwaldron)

- methods and Matrix are declared in Imports (#353, #355, @lwaldron)

- Unit tests updated for changes in mia (#314, @TuomasBorman)

- Added CITATION.cff (@LiNk-NY)

- Continuous integration uses the Bioconductor reusable GitHub
  workflow, with a coverage report (#338, #344, @lwaldron)

[hapmapsnp6](/packages/hapmapsnp6)
----------

                       Changes in version 1.55.1                        

- The data is no longer distributed inside the package. It is deposited
  on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23990454) and served through
  ExperimentHub, which brings the source tarball down from 264 MB to a
  few kilobytes.

- USER VISIBLE CHANGE: data(crlmmResult) no longer works, because the
  package ships no data directory. Use crlmmResult() instead, which
  returns the same SnpSet. The first call downloads the object and
  stores it in the local ExperimentHub cache; later calls read from
  that cache.

  ```
  ## before
  data(crlmmResult)
  ## now
  crlmmResult <- crlmmResult()
  ```

- USER VISIBLE CHANGE: the three CEL files are now obtained through
  celFiles(), which returns their paths on disk. Code that used
  system.file("celFiles", package = "hapmapsnp6") should use
  celFiles(asDir = TRUE), which returns a directory holding the files.

  ```
  ## before
  path <- system.file("celFiles", package = "hapmapsnp6")
  cels <- list.celfiles(path, full.names = TRUE)
  ## now
  cels <- celFiles()
  ```

- crlmmResult(metadata = TRUE) and celFiles(metadata = TRUE) return the
  resource metadata without downloading anything.

- Both accessors pass further arguments on to ExperimentHub(), so that
  an alternate hub location can be used.

- The maintainer address was updated, and authorship now uses the
  Authors@R field.

[macrophage](/packages/macrophage)
----------
                       Changes in version 1.29.1                        

- Reduced package size. The source tarball is now under 100 MB 
  The following files were removed. All of them are archived, with the full
  Salmon output for all 24 samples, on Zenodo:  The `with-inf-reps` branch
  on GitHub is a frozen snapshot of the package that still includes them.

  - The Gibbs inferential replicates
    (`inst/extdata/quants/*/aux_info/bootstrap/`, ~393 MB).
    `tximeta()` / `tximport()` on the files in `inst/extdata/quants` no
    longer imports inferential replicates.
  - `aux_info/ambig_info.tsv.gz` for each sample.
  - The full Gencode v29 GTF, `inst/extdata/gencode.v29.annotation.gtf.gz`.

- new files and datatsets

  - `inst/extdata/gencode.v29.annotation.slim.gtf.gz`: a slim Gencode v29
    GTF with only gene and transcript lines and 6 attributes (5 MB instead
    of 38 MB). It has no exon lines, so `tximeta::addExons()` will not
    work with it. It has a different filename from the full GTF on purpose:
    tximeta caches TxDbs by GTF filename, so this avoids clashing with a
    TxDb built from the full Gencode v29 GTF. Code that called
    `makeLinkedTxome(gtf=...)` with the full GTF path should switch to the
    slim filename. Built by `inst/scripts/makeSlimGTF.sh`.
  - `data(macro_txp_se)`: a transcript-level `SummarizedExperiment` with
    20 inferential replicates, for all transcripts of 2000 random expressed
    genes plus GBP1-GBP7. The `counts` and `infRep` assays are rounded to
    1 decimal. This is now used by the fishpond `swish` vignette.
  - `data(macro_tx2gene)`: a transcript-to-gene table for all Gencode v29
    transcripts, for use with
    `tximeta::summarizeToGene(se, skipRanges=TRUE, tx2gene=macro_tx2gene)`.
  - Both datasets are built by `inst/scripts/makeSumExp.R`. The script
    needs a macrophage install that still has the inferential replicates
    (<= 1.29.0, or the `with-inf-reps` branch).

[sesameData](/packages/sesameData)
----------

                       Changes in version 1.31.3                        

- The eight objects added in 1.31.1 now come from ExperimentHub, which
  assigned their ids on 2026-10-20: HM450/EPIC/EPICv2/MSA.address
  (EH10648-EH10651) and KYCG.<platform>.Mask.20261008
  (EH10652-EH10655).
  sesameDataGet() no longer falls back to Zenodo for them, and
  sesameDataCache() caches them with the rest.

                       Changes in version 1.31.2                        

- Documentation fixes from a review of the vignette. The setup chunk
  also caches genomeInfo.hg38, Mammal40.address and probeIDSignature,
  which the probe and annotation examples need. A sentence about a
  decoy = TRUE option in a
  function that does not exist is removed.

- metadata.csv describes EPIC.5.SigDF.normal as its five normal SigDFs
  (PrEC.Rep1, PrEC.Rep2, NAF.A, NAF.B, NAF.C), not an LNCaP
  segmentation. The ExperimentHub record is unchanged.

- The Zenodo fallback in sesameDataGet() downloads the file first, with
  a 600 s timeout. On a slow link (about 80 kB/s from HPC compute
  nodes)
  R's default 60 s cut the download short, so titles without an EHID
  (e.g. HM450.address, MSA.address) failed with "cannot read from
  connection".

                       Changes in version 1.31.1                        

- Added KYCG.{HM450,EPIC,EPICv2,MSA}.Mask.20261008, built from the
  InfiniumAnnotation v8.2 masks, so sesame's quality mask reads the
  same
  M_* tracks as SeSAMe2 on all four human arrays (sesame >= 1.31.6,
  zhou-lab/sesame#1).

- Rebuilt HM450.address, EPIC.address, EPICv2.address and MSA.address
  from the InfiniumAnnotation v8.3 orderings, so sesame reads the same
  probe design table as SeSAMe2. With these and the masks above, R's
  default QCDPB betas equal SeSAMe2's to ~1e-15 on all four arrays.

[systemPipeRdata](/packages/systemPipeRdata)
---------------

                       Changes in version 2.17.1                        

- Large example data resources, including FASTQ files, annotation
  resources, and precomputed BAM files, are no longer distributed
  directly with the systemPipeRdata package. These resources are now
  hosted on Zenodo and downloaded and cached locally using
  BiocFileCache.

- Added getSPRdata() for retrieving the external example data
  resources. FASTQ and annotation resources are retrieved by default,
  while precomputed BAM files can optionally be retrieved with
  getSPRdata(bam = TRUE).

- Updated genWorkenvir() and genWorkdata() to retrieve the required
  example data through getSPRdata(). Their existing workflow setup
  behavior is otherwise unchanged.
  NEW FEATURES

- Command-line interface uses now Common Workflow Language (CWL)

- Introduction of new SYSargsList control class for managing workflows

- Seamless processing of R code sections as workflow steps

- Added technical reports to scientific reporting infrastructure

- Auto-generation of CWL files from command-line strings

- Plotting of workflow topology graphs

[tximportData](/packages/tximportData)
------------

REDUCED PACKAGE SIZE

- The package's example data has been cut from ~593 MB on disk (~388 MB
  compressed) to ~171 MB on disk (~96 MB compressed). The built tarball is
  now ~96 MiB.

  The full data as it was before this change (commit `02887f7`) is kept on
  the `with-inf-reps` branch and tag at
  https://github.com/mikelove/tximportData and archived on Zenodo:
  https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22982575

  - Removed

    - `salmon_gibbs/`: Salmon 0.8.1 output with Gibbs samples (Ensembl v87,
      6 samples)
    - `kallisto_boot/`: kallisto 0.43.0 output with bootstraps (Ensembl v87,
      6 samples)
    - `tx2gene.ensembl.v87.csv`
    - `gencode/gencode.v48.annotation.gtf.gz`. tximeta can now link
      transcripts to genes with a DataFrame, so it no longer needs a GTF.
    - `alevin/{mouse1_unst_50,mouse1_LPS2_50}/alevin/bfh.txt` and
      `raw_cb_frequency.txt`
    - `kallisto/*/abundance.h5` (no bootstraps). `abundance.tsv.gz` is kept.
    - GEUVADIS samples `ERR188297`, `ERR188329`, `ERR188288` and `ERR188356`
      from `kallisto/`, `rsem/`, `salmon/` and `sailfish/`. `samples.txt` and
      `samples_extended.txt` now have 2 rows: `ERR188088` and `ERR188021`.

  - Kept

    - `salmon_ec/*/aux_info/eq_classes.txt` (used by fishpond)
    - `alevin/mouse1_unst_50_boot/` (used by eds)
    - `cufflinks/`, still with all 6 samples

  - Changes needed in downstream code

    - Code that reads `samples.txt` now gets 2 samples instead of 6. For example,
      replace `paste0("sample", 1:6)` with `paste0("sample", seq_along(files))`,
      and replace `rep(c("A","B"), each=3)` with `factor(c("A","B"))`.
    - For example data with inferential replicates (Gibbs samples or
      bootstraps), use the Zenodo record above or another data package such as
      `macrophage`.
